items.title: README.md › Anton Ernstsson · data portfolio
items.text:
A portfolio site with analytical products built on Swedish and EU public data, and the data
platform that produces them. Live at https://antonernstsson.com, hosted on Cloudflare
(Workers static assets; see [hosting](docs/deploy.md)). Swedish is the default language,
English one click away.

items.title: README.md › What is on the site
items.text:
The homepage contains the profile, experience and project index. The shared header groups
projects into Labs and Engineering; labs use continuous reports and section links. The
observatories are withdrawn: their addresses lead to the chart feed at
`#what-does-it-even-mean`. See [site structure](docs/site-structure.md)
and the [design system](docs/design-system.md).

items.title: README.md › How the data flows
items.text:
Public sources → Python ingestion (raw files kept with provenance) → dbt on DuckDB (bronze,
silver, gold) → JSON and Parquet in Cloudflare R2 → React. Heavy text and ML work runs once in
Python and ships as compact files; the browser computes only cheap, testable metrics. See
[platform/README.md](platform/README.md), [storage and serving](docs/storage-and-serving.md)
and the [data dictionary](docs/data-dictionary.md). One command runs every subject,
`python platform/pipeline.py`, locally and in GitHub Actions: jobs, news and public data are
refreshed every morning, the whole warehouse is rebuilt every Saturday, and each run publishes
a versioned release to R2 ([pipeline](docs/pipeline.md)).

items.title: README.md › Politics metrics
items.text:
**Definitions.**

| Metric                   | Definition                                                                                                                                                                          |

| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Party position           | The vote most of the party's members cast in a roll call, as Riksdagen reports it.                                                                                                  |

| Party cohesion           | Cast votes (yes, no, abstain) by the party's members that match the party position, of all their cast votes.                                                                        |

| Party similarity         | Of the roll calls where both parties had a position, the share where it was the same.                                                                                               |

| Polarisation (roll call) | 1 − (members in the largest group of parties with the same position) / (members of all parties with a position). 0 when all parties agree, about 0.5 at an even split.              |

| Polarisation (area)      | The mean polarisation of the roll calls prepared by that committee.                                                                                                                 |

items.title: README.md › Politics metrics
items.text:
| Close vote               | A roll call where \|yes − no\| / (yes + no) < 10 %.                                                                                                                                 |

| Topic share              | The learned issue lexicon (log-odds with an informative Dirichlet prior, about two thirds right on held-out speeches) applied to the words; each topic's share of the scored words. |

| Distinctive words        | tf-idf per party and party-leader debate: term frequency per 10,000 words × log(documents / documents with the term); names left out.                                               |

| Term growth              | Per 10,000 words in the issue debates, the latest riksmöte against the three before; ratio smoothed by +0.5 per 10,000 words; stems in at least 25 speeches.                        |

| Member deviation         | Cast votes that differ from the party position, of the cast votes where the party had one. Absence and deviation are not opposition by themselves.                                  |

| Voting map               | PCA of the parties' positions over the roll calls (yes 1, no −1, abstain 0), centred per roll call.                                                                                 |

items.title: README.md › Politics metrics
items.text:
**Data quality.** Before any metric, `cleanVotes` drops duplicate decision points, roll calls
where no party had a position, and roll calls with fewer than 100 cast votes, and the page
reports how many of each it found. Members who changed party are compared with the party they
belonged to at each vote.

**Design decisions.** Heavy text processing runs once in Python and ships as compact JSON;
vote metrics are cheap enough to compute in the browser from the per-session indexes, so they
stay transparent and testable. Party colours and logos come from one config
(`parties/identity.tsx`). Every chart has a text alternative, a table or labelled values, and
never relies on colour alone. The party, debate and member chosen are kept in the address.

items.title: README.md › Run locally
items.text:
```bash
npm ci
npm run dev        # http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

During development:

```bash
npm run verify:quick   # types, formatting and unit tests; no browser or live-data validation
```

Run the tests for the behavior you changed as well. Before integration, run
`npm run verify:full`; delivery changes also require `npm run verify:delivery`.
See [development workflow](docs/development.md) for scopes, logs, resource checks
and safe workspace retirement. GitHub runs complete CI for pull requests and main.

A snapshot of the site's JSON is checked in, so the site builds with Node alone. To rebuild a
subject, install `platform/requirements.txt` and run it:

```bash
python platform/pipeline.py list            # every subject, its group and schedule
python platform/pipeline.py run welfare     # fetch, build, test, export (npm run welfare)
python platform/pipeline.py check           # the four data contracts (npm run data:check)
```

`npm run data:build` runs the builders that are not yet in dbt.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › AI Act diffusion clock: pre-registration
items.text:
Written 2026-10-22, before any term was extracted or counted. It fixes the question, corpora,
term rule, adoption rule and null of H3 (idea I-1, with I-9 alongside) in roadmap item P1.5.
The commit that adds this file is the record. The code comes in later commits, and any
departure from this text is listed in the export's `method` block with its reason.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Question
items.text:
After each AI Act milestone, how many months pass before the Act's own vocabulary appears in
Riksdag speeches and in job ads? Which of the two corpora takes a term up first?

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Corpora
items.text:
The two corpora are never pooled. Each has its own months, denominators, thresholds and nulls.

- Riksdag: every speech in the chamber from Riksdagen's speech archives
  (`int_riksdag_speeches`, from September 2016). The document is one speech, its full text.
- Job ads: every ad in JobTech's historical archives from January 2020, about 2.79 million. The
  document is one ad, its headline and description, with duplicate ad ids counted once as in
  `ingest_governance_terms.py`. The scan runs in GitHub Actions.
- Month: the speech date or the ad's publication month.
- Partial months are excluded. A corpus's first or last month counts only when its records
  cover the month to its first or last day. In practice the last month is dropped because
  each archive ends mid-month.
- 2026 is a partial year. Yearly figures and labels mark it with the months it covers
  (expected: January to September).

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Milestones
items.text:
The milestones are those of `ai-act/timeline` that fall in or before a corpus's last full month.
Each is tested separately. The milestone month is the month that contains its date. A milestone
needs at least 12 earlier months in a corpus to be tested there, so the Commission's proposal
(April 2021) is tested in both corpora and nothing earlier exists.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Term extraction
items.text:
The terms come from the Act's text, not from a hand-picked list.

- Act corpus: the Swedish article texts in `ai-act/article-text-sv` (one document per article).

- Reference corpus: the 209,787 paragraphs of `silver.silver_sfs_corpus_paragraphs` in

  `sfs.duckdb`, Swedish statute law.

- Text is lower-cased. A token is a run of letters or digits, and hyphenated compounds such as

  "ai-system" are one token. N-grams have one to four tokens and do not cross a line break.

- Candidates occur at least 10 times in the Act and in at least 3 articles. No candidate starts

  or ends with a stopword, and no token is only digits.

- Score: weighted log-odds with an informative Dirichlet prior (Monroe, Colaresi and Quinn

  2008). The prior for each n-gram is its pooled count in both corpora. Counts and totals are

  taken per n-gram length. The z-score is δ / √(1 / (y_act + α) + 1 / (y_sfs + α)).

- Candidates with z ≥ 3.29 are ranked by z, and the top 60 go to review.

- Review keeps a term only if it names an AI Act concept. A dropped term gets one of these

  reasons, which are fixed before review:

  - `eu_boilerplate`: EU institutional or legal drafting language that is not about AI

    ("kommissionen", "denna förordning", article references);

  - `fragment`: no meaning on its own;

  - `nested_duplicate`: inside a longer kept candidate with the same count in the Act;

  - `general_language`: a common phrase that is often used outside AI regulation.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Term extraction
items.text:
- English counterpart (I-9): for each kept Swedish term, the English n-gram of

  `ai-act/article-text-en` (one to five tokens, the same filters) whose counts over the

  articles have the highest cosine with the Swedish term's counts. Review checks each pair. A

  wrong pair loses its English side with the reason `misaligned`.

- The output is `platform/seeds/cross_domain/ai_act_terms.csv`: every reviewed candidate with

  its scores, its decision and, for a dropped term, its reason.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Matching and shares
items.text:
- A term matches a document when its tokens occur in order, case-insensitively, separated by
  white space or a hyphen. The last token may take up to four more letters (Swedish
  inflection, "ai-systemet") and must end at a word boundary.
- Swedish and English terms are counted in both corpora.
- Monthly share: documents that contain the term over all documents in the month. Rolling
  share: the sum of matches over the sum of documents for the month and the two before it, as
  in `mart_ai_governance_timeline`.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Adoption rule
items.text:
For each corpus, term and milestone:

- Threshold: the 95th percentile (linear interpolation) of the rolling share over all months
  of the corpus before the milestone month. If every earlier value is zero, the threshold is
  zero and adoption means the first month with any match in its window.
- Adoption month: the first month, from the milestone month on, whose rolling share is above
  the threshold.
- Lag: months from the milestone month to the adoption month (0 or more). If no month up to
  the last full month passes, the lag is censored and has no value.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Placebo null
items.text:
- 200 placebo months per corpus, term and milestone, drawn with replacement from the months of
  that corpus that have at least 12 earlier months and at least L later months up to the last
  full month, where L is the observed lag. So every placebo date could have shown a lag of L.
- The same rule gives a lag at each placebo month. A censored placebo lag counts as longer
  than any observed one.
- One-sided p = (1 + placebo lags ≤ L) / 201. A censored observed lag gets no p.
- Seed 20261022. Each corpus, term and milestone starts its own generator from the seed and
  its key, so the order of computation does not change a result.
- The export lists every p with the number of tests. No adjustment for multiple tests decides
  anything. The result is descriptive: a lag shorter than at random dates, not an effect of
  the Act.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › I-9, if cheap
items.text:
- Swedish share of each term pair per corpus and month: Swedish matches over Swedish plus
  English matches, only in months with at least one match.
- The EN–SV cosine per article from the existing bge-m3 vectors, if they are stored. No new
  embedding is made for it.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › What cannot be concluded
items.text:
That the Act caused a term to spread. Generative AI reached the public in late 2022, and the
Act was negotiated and published at the same time, so many terms rise from 2023 whatever the
milestone. Milestones close together (July and August 2024, July and August 2026) share most
of their windows. A term in an ad shows that the words were written, not that the job requires
compliance work.

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Amendment, 2026-10-22 (after review, after the first Riksdag counts)
items.text:
Added after the primary analysis had run and its result was known. Nothing above this heading
has changed. The primary list and matching stay as written and are reported in full; the
amended list is reported beside them, never in their place.

Why: review dropped `ai-system`, `ai-modeller`, `ai-modell` and the sandbox terms as
`general_language`. That reason covers common phrases with uses outside AI ("hög risk",
"testning"). An AI-specific compound is not one, so these terms did not fit their own reason.
With them gone, the four kept terms matched one speech in ten years, and the lags rested on that
single match.

What changes, for the amended list only:

items.title: docs/ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md › Amendment, 2026-10-22 (after review, after the first Riksdag counts)
items.text:
- Re-review: the 56 dropped terms of the top 60 are read again against the reason definitions.
  The re-review admits only Act-derived candidates and adds no hand-picked words such as
  "AI-förordningen" or "högrisk". Result: `ai-system` and `ai-modell` come back. `ai-modeller` and
  `ai-modellen` are forms of `ai-modell` and are kept as `nested_duplicate`. `sandlådor`,
  `sandlådan` and every other drop keep their reason. The `amended_*` columns of
  `ai_act_terms.csv` record the result.
- Matching: every token, not only the last, may take up to four more letters, so
  "ai-systemet med högre risk" matches "ai-system med hög risk".
- Precision: for each re-admitted term and language, up to 50 random matched speeches (seed
  20261022) are read by hand. A match counts as on topic if it means the AI concept the
  Act names. An AI sandbox counts; a regulatory sandbox for energy, or a child's sandbox, does not.
  A term stays only at a precision of 0.8 or more. A term that fails gets the reason
  `precision`. Only the counts go to `ai_act_term_precision.csv`, never the speech text.
- Reporting: each lag shows `window_matches`, the matches in its three-month adoption window. A
  lag with 5 or fewer is labelled uninformative, whatever its p, and the diagnostics count those
  lags per list. The adoption rule and the placebo null are unchanged.

Precision in the Riksdag speeches (October 2016 to July 2026; ads follow with the ad scan):

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › EU AI Act Observatory
items.text:
`#ai-act` asks: **what does the EU AI Act actually mean for organisations building or deploying
AI?** It is a source-traceable map of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689's articles, actors, obligations,
application dates and changes, built from official EU sources only. It is a navigation aid, not
legal advice.

```
npm run ai-act            # ingest + dbt build + publish
npm run ai-act:ingest     # python platform/ingest/eu_ai_act/run.py
npm run ai-act:build      # dbt build --select tag:ai_act (models, seeds and tests)
npm run ai-act:publish    # python platform/publish/eu_ai_act/export_ai_act.py
npm run architecture:build  # the Data Constellation picks the domain up
```

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Official sources
items.text:
| Source | What | How |
|---|---|---|
| Publications Office of the EU, **Cellar** (the repository behind EUR-Lex) | The documents related to the Act: amending acts, corrigenda, consolidated versions, proposals to amend it, acts based on it | SPARQL endpoint `publications.europa.eu/webapi/rdf/sparql` (`platform/legal/cellar.py`) |
| Cellar content negotiation | The text of the Act (Official Journal), of each consolidated version and of each amending act, as XHTML, in English and Swedish | `publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` with `Accept: application/xhtml+xml` and `Accept-Language` |
| European Commission | Guidelines, codes of practice, templates, the AI Act policy page and the AI Act Service Desk | The pages listed in `platform/ingest/eu_ai_act/sources.py` |

EUR-Lex pages are what a reader follows (every row carries its `source_url`); they are not
fetched, since EUR-Lex answers automated requests with a browser challenge. No secondary source
(law firms, blogs) is used for legal data.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Ingestion and versioning
items.text:
`platform/ingest/eu_ai_act/` writes to `warehouse/raw/eu_ai_act/` through `lib/rawstore.py`, so
every file has a provenance line in `_manifest.jsonl`: URL, request headers (format, language),
fetch time, SHA-256 and size.

```
warehouse/raw/eu_ai_act/
  acts/<CELEX>.<en|sv>.xhtml         one file per published text; a CELEX number names one text,
                                      so a new consolidated version is a new file
  cellar/related@<sha12>.json        every distinct Cellar answer, kept (store_version)
  cellar/fetched.json                which texts the last run asked for and whether Cellar had them
  guidance/<id>@<sha12>.html         every distinct version of each Commission page
  guidance/sources.json              the page list
  _manifest.jsonl
```

Nothing is overwritten: texts are immutable per CELEX number, and pages and query answers that
change in place are kept per version (`rawstore.store_version`). A run is a handful of requests
spaced two to three seconds apart, so it is safe to schedule (weekly is plenty); a scheduled run
detects a new amendment, corrigendum or consolidated version as a new Cellar answer and fetches
the new text.

Fetched on 6 October 2026: Cellar listed 28 related documents; set aside the consolidations of
other acts and 20 documents remain, the Act included. Six texts were fetched; one (the English
rendering of the first consolidated version) is not held by Cellar and is recorded as unavailable.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › The versions
items.text:
The Act was amended by **Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)** of 8 July 2026, and
Cellar holds a consolidated text of 27 July 2026 (`02024R1689-20260727`). The site reads that
text as current and compares it with the text published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024
(`32024R1689`). `dim_ai_act_document` gives each consolidated version a validity window (from
its date until the day before the next); exactly one is current (a test checks it).

The comparison (`int_ai_act_provision_changes`) is provision by provision. A consolidated text
marks amended passages with ▼ markers naming the amending act (`32026R1744: REPLACED`), each
holding until the next marker; the parser carries them forward. A provision is **inserted**,
**deleted**, **amended** (texts differ and a marker names the act) or **unchanged**. When the
texts differ but no marker names an act, it is **text_differs**, never called an amendment: that
can be a corrigendum or a difference in rendering. Result: 38 provisions amended, 7 inserted,
1 text_differs (Article 108), 87 unchanged.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › The parser (`platform/legal/parse.py`)
items.text:
Both the Official Journal and the consolidated rendering mark structure with ELI ids:
`cpt_III` (chapter), `cpt_III.sct_2` (section), `art_6`, `rct_12`, `anx_III`, each with a
`.tit_1` title. The parser follows those ids in document order, so it does not depend on either
rendering's styling, and keeps the text verbatim apart from white space: one line per block,
list markers joined to their item, footnote calls left out (their numbering differs between
renderings), powers written as `10^25`. It is written for any EU act; the AI Act is the first.
Tests: `platform/tests/legal/`.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Data model
items.text:
| Layer | Model | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| bronze | `stg_ai_act_texts`, `stg_ai_act_related`, `stg_ai_act_guidance_pages`, `stg_ai_act_fetches` | file as fetched, with provenance |
| silver | `int_ai_act_documents` | document (Cellar), with document type from the CELEX scheme and version validity |
| silver | `int_ai_act_provisions` | version × language × provision (article, recital, annex), verbatim |
| silver | `int_ai_act_definitions` | Article 3 point: term and definition verbatim |
| silver | `int_ai_act_provision_changes` | provision: change between the OJ text and the current text |
| silver | `int_ai_act_guidance` | Commission page: title and date read from the page |
| silver | `int_ai_act_article_actors` | article × actor: mentions and "shall" sentences (derived) |
| gold | `dim_ai_act_document`, `dim_ai_act_guidance` | documents and guidance |
| gold | `dim_ai_act_article`, `dim_ai_act_annex`, `dim_ai_act_recital` | the current text, English and Swedish |
| gold | `dim_ai_act_actor`, `dim_ai_act_risk_class` | actors with Article 3 definitions; risk classes |
| gold | `bridge_ai_act_article_actor`, `bridge_ai_act_article_reference`, `bridge_ai_act_article_guidance` | many-to-many links |
| gold | `mart_ai_act_obligations` | actor × obligation × article |
| gold | `mart_ai_act_timeline` | milestone (application dates, deadlines, document dates) |
| gold | `mart_ai_act_changes` | change (documents, guidance, provisions) |

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Actors
items.text:
Eleven, under the Act's own terms (`seeds/eu_ai_act/ai_act_actors.csv`): provider, deployer,
provider of a general-purpose AI model, downstream provider, authorised representative,
importer, distributor (operators); notified body; market surveillance authority, national
competent authority, AI Office (authorities). Each carries its Article 3 definition verbatim.
A provider of a general-purpose AI model has no definition of its own; it is a provider under
Article 3(3), and the row says so.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Application dates
items.text:
Each article gets the date from which it applies under Article 113 as amended
(`seeds/eu_ai_act/ai_act_application_rules.csv`): the most specific rule wins (article, then
section, then chapter, then the general date). Every rule carries the sentence of Article 113 it
rests on. Where only part of an article has a different date (Article 5's prohibitions added in
2026), the article carries a second date and is shown as *partly applying* in between.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Obligations
docs/ai-act.md › Source, derived, interpretation
items.text:
Every published file and every block on the page is one of three kinds, and the page marks it:

| Kind | What |
|---|---|
| **Source** (official text) | Article text, definitions, quoted sentences, document titles and dates, as published |
| **Derived** | Computed from the text by a stated method: actor mentions and "shall" sentences (term patterns), cross-references (patterns), what changed between versions (comparison) |
| **Interpretation** | Written for this site: obligation summaries and classification, risk-class descriptions, the navigator's questions and rules |

No summary replaces legal text; no LLM output is used anywhere in this product.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Tests
items.text:
- `assert_ai_act_quotes_in_current_text`: every curated sentence (obligations, milestones,
  application rules, risk classes) appears verbatim in the current English text of the article
  it cites. If the law changes under a quote, the build fails.
- `assert_ai_act_sources_are_official`: every public row links to EUR-Lex, the Publications
  Office or the Commission.
- `assert_ai_act_dates_valid`, `assert_ai_act_one_current_version`, and unique, not-null,
  accepted-values and relationship tests on every model (115 dbt nodes and tests in all).
- Python: `platform/tests/legal` (parser, comparison, markers, Cellar, ingest selection).
- Unit: `frontend/tests/unit/aiact.test.ts` (files hang together, Article 113 dates, status on a
  day, navigator rules). End to end: `frontend/tests/aiact.spec.ts`.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › The page
items.text:
`frontend/src/aiact/`. The overview (`#ai-act`) answers practical questions first and leaves
the legal modelling for later:

1. **Today:** the latest application date as the main finding, with its article.
2. **Next:** the next milestone, and the latest official change. Each carries its source label.
   A line says when the source was last verified (`summary.latest_retrieval`).
3. **Who are you?** The startup navigator first, then one link per operator role to its
   obligations (`#ai-act-obligations?actor=<id>`).
4. **In Sweden:** links to the AI governance timeline, the Riksdag and job ads. The page says
   that these signals happen in the same period and that this does not show causation.
5. **This month:** the snapshot, sized for a screenshot, with "copy as text".
6. Folded: what the Act is, the latest guidance and the amendment. Then *Quality in brief*
   (accuracy, currentness, traceability, validity, each with its evidence), *How it was built*
   and *Trace this result*, which opens the lineage from the timeline file back to the
   Publications Office.

The project navigation follows the same order: overview, today, who it applies to, startup
navigator, timeline, obligations, risk classes, changes, the Riksdag, job ads, the governance
timeline, sources. `#ai-act-article?a=<n>` opens an article with its official text in the
reader's language. The reader's date decides what applies; `?idag=YYYY-MM-DD` previews another
day.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › The page
items.text:
Every obligation shows three layers that are never merged: the plain-language summary
(interpretation), the verbatim sentence (official text), and, folded, how it is stored in
`mart_ai_act_obligations` (derived). A changed document lists the actors its changed articles
name as "may affect" (derived).

The navigator's rules live in `platform/publish/eu_ai_act/navigator.json` and are checked
against the obligations and articles when published. Its result lists role considerations,
risk classes, topics, articles and the official source, says "navigation aid, not legal
advice", and never classifies anyone.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › The Riksdag and AI
items.text:
`#ai-act-politics` reads every Riksdag speech since 2016/17 against the Act: how often AI comes up,
with which words, by which party, and which speeches sit closest to which articles by semantic
similarity. See [ai-politics.md](ai-politics.md).

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Job ads and the AI governance timeline
items.text:
`#ai-act-jobs` counts AI governance, compliance and model-risk words in every job ad since 2020
([ai-jobs.md](ai-jobs.md)). `#ai-act-signals` puts the Act's milestones, the Riksdag series and the
job-ad series on one time axis, each in its own panel ([ai-governance-timeline.md](ai-governance-timeline.md)).
Both state under the chart that temporal overlap does not prove causation.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Limitations
items.text:
- A navigation aid, not legal advice. Recitals, annexes, delegated and implementing acts,
  standards and national law all matter for whether a provision applies.
- The obligations are a curated selection; the "shall" signal per article is a pattern, not a
  legal reading.
- Application dates are per article; paragraph-level exceptions (Article 6(5), Article 5's new
  points) are noted, not modelled per paragraph.
- Corrigenda are listed from Cellar's metadata (Cellar gives no English title for them); their
  text is not compared separately.
- Guidance pages without a publication date on the page keep none.
- Quotes and the version comparison use the English text; the Swedish text is shown as the
  official Swedish language version.

items.title: docs/ai-act.md › Built for more EU law
items.text:
Nothing in `platform/legal/` is specific to the AI Act: another act (GDPR, the DSA, the Data
Act, NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act) needs its CELEX number, a source list, and its own seeds
for actors, obligations and application rules.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › The AI governance timeline (cross-domain)
items.text:
`#ai-act-signals` is a view in the EU AI Act Observatory. It is the first cross-domain analysis:
it places three domains on **one time axis**:

- the AI Act's milestones, from Cellar;
- how often the Riksdag talks about AI and names the Act (`docs/ai-politics.md`);
- how often job ads use the words (`docs/ai-jobs.md`).

It answers **when** things changed together. It does not answer why.

```
npm run ai-governance-timeline   # dbt build --select tag:cross_domain, then publish
```

It needs the AI Act, Riksdag AI and job-ad governance models built first.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › Data
items.text:
`gold.mart_ai_governance_timeline` has one row per month and series. Each row keeps:

- numerator and denominator;
- the monthly share;
- a three-month rolling share (sums over the window);
- the gold model it comes from.

The series are defined in `seeds/cross_domain/ai_governance_series.csv`:

| Series | Numerator / denominator | From |
|---|---|---|
| `riksdag_ai` | speeches mentioning AI / all speeches | `mart_ai_politics_monthly` |
| `riksdag_ai_act` | speeches naming the Act / all speeches | `mart_ai_politics_monthly` |
| `jobs_ai_any` | ads mentioning AI / all ads | `mart_job_ai_governance_terms` |
| `jobs_ai_act` | ads naming the Act / all ads | `mart_job_ai_governance_terms` |
| `jobs_ai_governance` | ads mentioning AI governance / all ads | `mart_job_ai_governance_terms` |

Tests check that each series and month appears once, that shares lie between 0 and 1, and that
no numerator exceeds its denominator. The publisher writes `ai-act/signals.json`.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › How it is drawn
items.text:
Each series has its own panel with its own y-scale. All panels share one x-axis and the same
numbered milestone lines (*small multiples*). There is never a second scale in one chart, and
series are never added together. Their levels differ by orders of magnitude: about 1 % of
speeches mention AI, while a few ads in a hundred thousand name the Act. A shared scale would
flatten all but one series.

Months before a series' data begins are shaded. The job ads start in January 2020 and the
Riksdag in September 2016. A table gives each series per year, with the count beside the share.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › What it can and cannot say
items.text:
It can say that a series rose or fell in the same period as a milestone. That is
`temporal_overlap` in the concept layer's relation types.

It cannot separate the Act's effect from everything else that happened at the same time. Above
all, generative AI was launched publicly in late 2022, a few months before both the Riksdag and
the job ads begin to rise. The page says so under the panels.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › Results (6 October 2026)
items.text:
- **Riksdag:** the share of speeches mentioning AI stayed under 0.4 % a year until 2022, then
  rose to 0.65 % (2023), 0.97 % (2024), 1.12 % (2025) and 1.65 % (2026, to August). Speeches
  naming the Act are few (26 in all): the first in June 2023, a cluster of three-speech months
  around its publication in 2024, and the largest month, five speeches, in May 2026, while the
  amending regulation was negotiated.
- **Job ads:** the share mentioning AI was flat at 0.7–0.9 % from 2020 to 2023, then rose to
  1.2 %, 2.0 % and 2.8 % (2024–2026). Ads naming the Act appear from 2024 (25), 2025 (95) and
  2026 (95 to July).
- **Together:** both series rise from 2023. That follows the public launch of generative AI
  (November 2022) and also the Act's negotiation, publication and first application dates.
  The data cannot separate the two. What it does show is that ads *naming* the Act appear
  only after its publication and grow as its first obligations apply. That is still temporal
  overlap, not evidence that the Act changed hiring.

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › The diffusion clock
items.text:
`gold.mart_ai_act_term_diffusion` sits beside the timeline and asks a narrower question: after
each milestone, how many months pass before the Act's own terms show up in Riksdag speeches and
in job ads? The method was fixed before any counting, in
[ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md](ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md).

```
python platform/nlp/ai_act_terms.py                  # candidate terms, for review
python -m ml.ai_act.diffusion speeches               # Riksdag counts, local
gh workflow run cluster-jobs.yml -f job=module \
  -f args="ml.ai_act.diffusion ads" -f path=ai_act/diffusion   # ad counts, Actions
python platform/pipeline.py run ai_act_diffusion     # mart and ai-act/diffusion.json
```

The terms come from the Act, scored against Swedish statute law by weighted log-odds. Of the 60
best-scoring n-grams, review kept four: *AI-system med hög risk*, *AI-byrån*, *AI-modeller för
allmänna ändamål* and *testning under verkliga förhållanden*. The other 56 are listed in
`seeds/cross_domain/ai_act_terms.csv` with their reasons. Most are EU drafting language or
common Swedish.

The mart has one row per corpus, term, language and whole month. The export works out each
lag and tests it against 200 random months (the placebo null).

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › The diffusion clock
items.text:
Results for the Riksdag (22 October 2026, speeches from October 2016 to July 2026). With the
primary list, the four terms occur in one speech in all, in January 2025. The result is
uninformative (1 match): each of the four uncensored lags rests on that one speech, so its p
says nothing, and the other 50 lags are censored. It is neither a null result nor a
counter-example.

An amendment added the same day ([pre-registration](ai-act-diffusion-preregistration.md#amendment-2026-10-22-after-review-after-the-first-riksdag-counts))
re-admits *AI-system* and *AI-modell*, which review had dropped by a misread reason, and lets
every token inflect. Both terms passed a precision check (19 of 19 and 12 of 12 matched
speeches on topic). The export reports both lists side by side in `lags_side_by_side`:

| term | milestone | primary lag (matches) | amended lag (matches) | amended p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| AI-system med hög risk | proposal, Apr 2021 | 45 (1) | 45 (1) | 0.31 |
| AI-system med hög risk | prohibitions, Feb 2025 | 0 (1) | 0 (1) | 0.04 |
| AI-system | publication, Jul 2024 | – | 2 (2) | 0.24 |
| AI-system | amending regulation, Jul 2026 | – | 0 (7) | 0.14 |
| AI-modell | publication, Jul 2024 | – | 0 (2) | 0.16 |
| AI-modell | high-risk guidelines, Feb 2026 | – | 0 (5) | 0.12 |

items.title: docs/ai-governance-timeline.md › The diffusion clock
items.text:
Of the 22 amended lags with a p, 19 rest on 5 matches or fewer, and only the three July 2026 lags
of *AI-system* rest on more (7, with p from 0.14 to 0.16). The Riksdag rarely uses the Act's own
words, even with the amended list. The job-ad lane follows once the scan has run in Actions.
Each archive is written when it is done, so a run that hits the Actions timeout still keeps the
archives it finished.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › AI governance in job ads
items.text:
`#ai-act-jobs` is a view in the EU AI Act Observatory. It asks: **how often do Swedish job ads
talk about AI, AI governance, compliance and model risk, and how does that line up with the AI
Act's milestones?** It counts words in ads. It does not measure demand for skills, and it does
not say that the Act changed hiring.

```
npm run job-ai-governance   # ingest (count every archive), dbt build, publish
```

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › Source
items.text:
Arbetsförmedlingen publishes every ad from its platform in JobTech's historical archives
(`https://data.arbetsformedlingen.se/annonser/historiska/`): one zip per year, and quarters for
the current year. `platform/ingest/jobtech/ingest_governance_terms.py` streams each archive
once and keeps no ads. Per archive it stores four things:

- ads per publication month and occupation field (the denominator);
- ads matching each term;
- a few masked examples per term;
- a manifest with the archive's URL and SHA-256 and the dictionary's SHA-256.

An archive is counted again only if it or the dictionary has changed. A test requires all
archives to have been counted with the same dictionary. Ads that repeat within an archive are
counted once.

A few ads carry impossible publication dates (2051, 2099). Months after the build date are left
out in bronze.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › The dictionary
items.text:
`seeds/job_ai_governance/job_ai_governance_terms.csv` holds 13 regular expressions, matched in
an ad's headline and description. The page prints them verbatim.

| Family | Terms |
|---|---|
| Context | AI (any mention: upper-case *AI*, *artificiell intelligens*, *maskininlärning* …) |
| The Act | the AI Act by name (*AI Act*, *AI-förordningen*, *AI-akten* …) |
| AI governance | AI governance, responsible / trustworthy AI, AI compliance, AI safety |
| Model operations | model risk, model monitoring, MLOps |
| Data | data governance, privacy and data protection (GDPR …) |
| General | compliance, risk management |

A match means the words are in the ad. It does not mean the job requires them: an ad can name
GDPR in its privacy notice, or name AI as a feature of the employer's product. The page shows
example ads per term so a reader can judge what each pattern catches.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › Data model
items.text:
| Layer | Model | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| bronze | `stg_job_gov_totals`, `stg_job_gov_terms`, `stg_job_gov_examples`, `stg_job_gov_manifests` | as counted, per archive |
| gold | `mart_job_ai_governance_terms` | month × occupation field (and ALL) × term: mentions, ads, share, 3-month rolling share, year-on-year change in percentage points |
| gold | `mart_job_ai_governance_yearly` | year × field × term |

Every share has its denominator. Rolling and yearly shares are sums over the window, not
averages of monthly shares.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › The view
items.text:
- One term at a time (`?term=`), as a three-month rolling share of all ads, with the Act's
  milestones as numbered lines. The caveat that temporal overlap does not prove causation sits
  under the chart.
- A table per year with ads, matches and share.
- The occupation fields where the term is most common in the latest year.
- Example ads, and the dictionary with the archives' sizes and hashes.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › Results (6 October 2026)
items.text:
Eight archives (2020 to 2026-Q2), **4,925,716 ads** from January 2020 to July 2026.

| Share of all ads | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI (any mention) | 0.77 % | 0.94 % | 0.80 % | 0.73 % | 1.18 % | 1.97 % | 2.80 % |
| The AI Act by name | 0 | 0 | 1 ad | 3 ads | 0.003 % | 0.016 % | 0.033 % |
| AI governance | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.001 % | 0.002 % | 0.007 % | 0.016 % |
| Responsible / trustworthy AI | 0.001 % | 0.001 % | 0.001 % | 0.001 % | 0.004 % | 0.014 % | 0.034 % |
| MLOps | 0.003 % | 0.006 % | 0.007 % | 0.006 % | 0.017 % | 0.036 % | 0.056 % |
| Compliance | 0.45 % | 0.51 % | 0.51 % | 0.52 % | 0.83 % | 1.25 % | 1.33 % |
| Privacy and data protection | 2.19 % | 3.21 % | 3.45 % | 3.34 % | 3.73 % | 4.85 % | 5.39 % |

- Mentions of AI were flat at under 1 % of ads until 2023, then rose to 2.8 % in 2026. In 2025,
  11 % of Data/IT ads mentioned AI.
- The Act by name is rare: 1 ad in 2022, 3 in 2023, 25 in 2024, 95 in 2025 and 95 in the first
  seven months of 2026. The governance terms are rarer still and rise from 2024.
- The broad terms (compliance, privacy) rise too. Privacy matches include GDPR notices about
  how the employer handles applications, so their level says little about the job itself.

items.title: docs/ai-jobs.md › Limitations
items.text:
- Words, not requirements. English and Swedish patterns only.
- *AI* in upper case also matches some unrelated uses (for example, AI as a company name).
  The examples show how often.
- Platform coverage changes over time: the archives hold ads published on Arbetsförmedlingen's
  platform, not the whole labour market.
- The current year is incomplete. Its shares are comparable, but its counts are not.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › The Riksdag and AI
items.text:
`#ai-act-politics`, inside the EU AI Act Observatory, asks: **how has Swedish political language
about AI changed as the AI Act developed?** It counts which words the Riksdag uses about AI, by
whom and when, puts that next to the Act's milestones, and adds a separate, derived layer of
semantic similarity between speeches and the Act's text. It describes language; it does not infer
motives or claim that the Act caused anything.

```
npm run ai-politics              # all of the below
npm run ai-politics:ingest       # every speech archive since 2016/17 (rawstore)
npm run ai-politics:build        # dbt build --select tag:ai_politics
npm run ai-politics:similarity   # embeddings and nearest pairs, then the similarity mart
npm run ai-politics:publish      # frontend/public/data/ai-act/politics/*.json
```

The AI Act models must be built first (`npm run ai-act:build`): the similarity stage reads the
Act's Swedish text from them.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Source
items.text:
Riksdagen's open data publishes every speech in the chamber, one archive per riksmöte
(`anforande-201617.json.zip`). `platform/ingest/riksdagen/ingest_speeches.py` reads the list from
Riksdagen's open-data page and stores each archive as served under
`warehouse/raw/riksdagen/speeches/`, with URL, time and SHA-256 in the Riksdagen fetch log.
The default start, 2016/17, gives more than four years before the Commission's proposal
(21 April 2021).

Fetched on 6 October 2026: ten sessions, **129,110 speeches** from 13 September 2016 to
13 August 2026.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › The dictionary
items.text:
`seeds/ai_politics/ai_politics_concepts.csv`: each group of words is a regular expression with a
description and, where needed, a caveat. The page prints every pattern verbatim.

- **Gate** (`ai`): a paragraph is about AI when it contains upper-case *AI* (also in compounds
  such as *AI-system*), *artificiell intelligens*, *maskininlärning*, *djupinlärning*,
  *språkmodell…*, *ChatGPT* or *generativ AI*. Upper case only for the abbreviation, so words
  containing the letters do not count.
- **The Act by name** (`ai_act`): *AI-förordningen*, *AI-akten*, *AI Act*, *förordningen om
  artificiell intelligens*.
- **Framing groups** (15): innovation; competitiveness and growth; *säkerhet*; security and
  defence; risk and threat; privacy and data protection; surveillance and biometrics; fundamental
  rights; transparency; responsibility; human oversight; automation and algorithms; work and
  jobs; regulation; disinformation and democracy.
- **Pairs** (`ai_politics_framing_pairs.csv`): innovation vs *säkerhet*, privacy vs security,
  regulation vs competitiveness.

Matching is **per paragraph**: a speech is about AI when one of its paragraphs passes the gate,
and the framing groups are looked for in those paragraphs only. A budget speech that mentions AI
once therefore does not count its other paragraphs. Code: `platform/nlp/text/concepts.py`;
tests with examples that must and must not match: `platform/tests/ai_politics/`.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › The dictionary
items.text:
Swedish has one word, *säkerhet*, for both safety and security; that group cannot tell them
apart, and the page says so. The narrower security group (cybersecurity, national security,
defence) is a separate concept.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Data model
items.text:
| Layer | Model | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| bronze | `stg_riksdag_speeches` (Python) | speech: metadata as written, text as plain paragraphs, archive hash |
| silver | `int_riksdag_speeches` | speech with a normalised party (none for the chair and speakers without a party) |
| silver | `int_ai_speech_paragraphs` (Python) | paragraph passing the AI gate, with the framing terms found in it |
| silver | `int_ai_speech_concepts` | speech × concept |
| gold | `fct_ai_speech` | speech: mentions AI, names the Act; the denominator for every share |
| gold | `mart_ai_politics_monthly` | month: speeches, AI speeches, AI Act speeches, share, three-month rolling share |
| gold | `mart_ai_politics_party_year` | party × year |
| gold | `mart_ai_politics_concepts` | party (or ALL) × period × concept, among AI speeches |
| gold | `mart_ai_politics_framing` | pair × party × period: counts and balance |
| gold | `mart_ai_politics_examples` | example paragraphs per concept, and every paragraph naming the Act |
| gold | `mart_ai_act_speech_similarity` | AI Act article × rank: the closest Riksdag AI paragraphs |

Shares always carry their denominator; rolling shares are sums over the window, not averages of
monthly shares. Periods are calendar years and three phases: before the proposal (to
20 April 2021), proposal to publication (to 11 July 2024), after publication. The phase dates are
Cellar's: the Act's original proposal (`52021PC0206`) is now fetched with the Act.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Data model
items.text:
A framing **balance** is (A − B) / (A + B) over the AI speeches using either side, and is left
empty below ten such speeches.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Semantic similarity
items.text:
`platform/nlp/ai_politics/similarity.py` embeds, with one multilingual model
(`sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, shared in
`platform/nlp/text/vectors.py`):

- every paragraph of the current consolidated AI Act in its **official Swedish version**
  (1,077 passages; Articles 102–110, which only amend other acts, are left out);
- every Riksdag AI paragraph (1,256).

Both sides are Swedish, so the model compares like with like. For each article the eight closest
speech paragraphs are kept (three are published), and for each speech paragraph the three
closest passages of the Act. `run.json` records a chance baseline: 5,000 random speech–article
pairs have mean similarity 0.32 and a 95th percentile of 0.58; only pairs above that percentile
are published. A test checks that the mart rests on one model.

This is **semantic similarity**: the passages use related language. It is not influence, a
response to the Act, or shared meaning, and the page says so where the pairs are shown.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Results (6 October 2026)
items.text:
- 711 of 129,110 speeches mention AI in at least one paragraph (1,256 paragraphs); 26 name the AI
  Act (27 paragraphs).
- The yearly share of speeches mentioning AI stayed under 0.4 % every year from 2016 to 2022, then
  rose to 0.64 % in 2023, 0.97 % in 2024, 1.12 % in 2025 and 1.65 % in 2026 (to August).
- Among AI speeches, the most frequent groups over the whole period are innovation (16 %),
  regulation (14 %), risk (12 %), work and jobs (10 %) and *säkerhet* (10 %); human oversight
  is rare (under 1 %).

The rise coincides with the Act's negotiation and application and also with the public launch of
generative AI; the data cannot separate the two, and the page's caveat says that temporal overlap
does not prove causation.

items.title: docs/ai-politics.md › Limitations
items.text:
- A dictionary counts words, not meaning: a paragraph can use a word to reject an idea, and AI can
  be discussed without the words in the gate.
- Party codes are as Riksdagen records them; ministers speak with their party code, so a
  governing party's counts include its ministers.
- Small denominators: a party with fewer than 20 AI speeches in a period is shown faded.
- Examples are the most recent paragraphs per concept, not a representative sample.
- Similarity depends on the model; scores are comparable within this run only.

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Analysing the welfare data
items.text:
What to use for which purpose, how each measure may be aggregated, and the traps. The model
itself is described in [welfare-data-model.md](welfare-data-model.md).

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Pick the table by purpose
items.text:
| Purpose | Use | Grain | Why this one |
|---|---|---|---|
| BI dashboards (Power BI, Tableau, Superset) | the star schema: `dim_*` + `fct_*` | one fact per source and grain | BI engines are built for a star; a wide table is slower and less flexible there |
| Metrics that must agree everywhere | the dbt semantic layer (MetricFlow) | `sweden_month`, `county_year` | ratio and stock rules are declared once, so every tool gets the same number |
| Regression, correlation, maps | `mart_county_year_panel` | county x year (+ country) | one row per unit and year, each column already aggregated by its rule, with numerators and denominators |
| Municipal comparison | `mart_municipality_year_panel` | municipality x year | Kolada figures with population and county |
| Time series, forecasting, nowcasting | `mart_national_month` | Sweden x month | seasonally adjusted and raw series, rolling twelve-month flows |
| Cross-country comparison | `mart_ess_country_round` | country or group x ESS round | weighted means per country, pooled Nordic and EU-27 rows |
| Machine learning | `mart_county_year_features` | county x year | lags, changes and gaps to the country, backward-looking only |
| Anything across sources, exploratory | `fct_indicator` | indicator x region x period x sex x age | every headline value on one grain |

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Pick the table by purpose
items.text:
Star schema as the core and wide tables as a serving layer on top is the usual division of
labour: the star answers questions nobody has asked yet, the wide tables answer known ones fast.

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Aggregation rules
items.text:
Every indicator in `dim_indicator` states how it may be combined:

- `measure_type`: `count_flow`, `count_stock`, `rate`, `share`, `mean_score`, `median`
- `time_rule`: `sum`, `mean_of_periods`, `end_of_period`, `recompute_from_components`, `not_aggregable`
- `space_rule`: `sum`, `recompute_from_components`, `population_weighted_mean`, `recompute_from_microdata`, `not_aggregable`
- `components`, `weight_indicator`, `aggregation_note`

The principle is Kimball's: a ratio is non-additive, so store its additive components, sum
those, and divide last. In this model:

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Aggregation rules
items.text:
| Measure | Over regions, sexes, ages | Over time | Proven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| AKU unemployment rate | sum unemployed and labour force, then divide | mean of monthly levels, then divide | `assert_aku_annual_is_mean_of_months`: within 0.07 points of SCB's published annual rate, 2001-2025 |
| Sjukpenningtal | sum `sick_pay_days` and `insured_persons`, then divide | December (rolling twelve months) | `assert_sick_pay_rate_recomputes_from_components`: counties from municipalities within 0.014 days |
| Started sick-leave cases | sum | sum | `assert_additive_counts_sum_to_country` |
| Ongoing cases, population | sum | never sum: last or mean | |
| Kolada rates | use Kolada's own county and national values | not across years | reported crime: a population-weighted mean of municipalities misses the county value by 15% on average, because crime is counted where it happened |
| Medians (income) | not at all: use published values | | |
| Survey shares (FoHM) | population-weighted mean approximates; prefer published | pooled periods cannot be split or added | |
| ESS means | only from respondents: `pspwght` in a country, `pspwght x pweight` when pooling | not across rounds with different modes | |

Two structural rules:

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Aggregation rules
items.text:
- **Sum only complete sets.** A sum over parts where some are suppressed (`..` at SCB, `rojd` at
  FK) is a lower bound. AKU county levels add up to the country within 0.4 thousand when all
  21 counties are published, and fall far short when they are not.
- **Facts carry published totals.** `sex_key = 'T'`, `age_group_key` totals such as `15-74`
  and `region_code = '00'` sit beside their parts, because the parts do not always add up. Always
  filter a dimension to one member or to the parts; never sum over a dimension that contains its
  own total. The semantic layer and the panels do this for you.

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › The semantic layer
items.text:
Declared in `platform/models/gold/welfare/serving/schema.yml`, validated in CI with MetricFlow's
own validator (`platform/publish/validate_semantic_layer.py`), time spine `dim_date`.

```bash
pip install "dbt-metricflow[dbt-duckdb]"
cd platform
mf query --metrics unemployment_rate,sick_pay_rate,psychiatric_share_of_started \
         --group-by metric_time__year --start-time 2021-01-01
mf query --metrics county_unemployment_rate,county_sick_pay_rate --group-by county_year__nuts2_code
```

Checked against published figures: `unemployment_rate` for 2024 is 8.37% (SCB: 8.4), for 2025
8.86% (8.8); `sick_pay_rate` for 2024 is 12.33, FK's December value; the county metrics summed
over all counties give 8.40% and 12.33 again.

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Reading the data
items.text:
The exports are Parquet, one file per table, listed with row counts and column descriptions in
`frontend/public/data/welfare/datasets.json` and served from object storage.

```python
import duckdb
base = "https://<object-storage-base>/parquet/welfare/"   # delivery.json "parquet" base
panel = duckdb.sql(f"select * from '{base}mart_county_year_panel.parquet'").df()
```

Power BI: Get data → Parquet (or Web) per `dim_*` and `fct_*` file, relate on `region_code`,
`period_key`, `sex_key`, `age_group_key`, `indicator_key`; mark `dim_date` as the date table.
Databricks: `spark.read.parquet(...)` per file, or copy them to a volume first.

Locally, after `npm run welfare`, the whole warehouse is `warehouse/portfolio.duckdb`.

items.title: docs/analysis-guide.md › Before you conclude anything
items.text:
- **Ecological fallacy.** Correlations between counties describe counties. They do not say that
  unemployed people are more often on sick leave, and group-level correlations are usually
  stronger than individual-level ones.
- **21 counties is a small sample.** Weight by population where a county's weight matters,
  report intervals, and prefer changes within counties over time to comparisons across them.
- **Margins.** AKU county rates carry ±1-2 points; FoHM county values have intervals in
  `fct_health_survey`; ESS intervals here ignore the design and are too narrow.
- **Different definitions of the same idea.** AKU unemployment (survey, 15-74) is not Kolada's
  open unemployment (Arbetsförmedlingen register, 18-65). Sjukpenningtal 2.0 (FK) is not 1.0
  (Kolada). Keep them apart.
- **Breaks.** ESS10 in Sweden was self-completed; SCB population from 2025 carries cell-key
  noise; FK suppresses small counts.
- **Lags.** Sources publish months to years after the period. `mart_county_year_features` only
  looks backwards, but a model scored today must still use what was published by then.

items.title: docs/budget-provenance.md › Budget years, party proposals and decisions
items.text: `frontend/public/data/gold/marts/budget-context.json` is the small navigation model behind the budget report. It covers the twelve annual central-government budgets for 2015–2026 (parliamentary sessions 2014/15–2025/26). It is built by dbt (`platform/models/gold/politics/mart_budget_context.sql`, delivered by `platform/publish/export_politics.py`) from the checked-in FiU1 coverage, corrected budget frames, decision points, citations, reservations and votes; who governed and which budget was adopted each year is the reviewable seed `platform/seeds/politics/budget_governance.csv`. CI rebuilds it on every push and fails unless the output is byte-identical to the delivered file. Every year links to its official FiU1 document. It is **not** a history of every supplementary budget, every appropriation decision or every Swedish budget ever adopted.

items.title: docs/budget-provenance.md › Budget years, party proposals and decisions
items.text:
The government column represents the **submitted collective proposal**. It must not be copied into a separate M, KD, L, SD, S or MP party column. The 2023–2026 proposals came from the M/KD/L government under its SD budget agreement; missing separate columns for these parties are therefore not zeros. The 2020 and 2021 proposals from the S/MP government were agreed with C and L. [Riksdag: 2020 agreement](https://data.riksdagen.se/dokument/H701FIU2), [Riksdag: 2021 agreement](https://data.riksdagen.se/dokument/H801AU1), [Government: Tidö cooperation](https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2026/05/regeringen-och-sverigedemokraterna-presenterar-bokslut-over-tidoavtalet/).

For budget years **2015, 2019 and 2022**, the submitted government proposal was not the adopted frame. The adopted alternatives were the Alliance (M/C/L/KD), M/KD, and M/SD/KD respectively. Therefore a chart of the government's proposal for those years cannot be titled “the adopted budget.” This exception list is supported by the [government's review of the budget process](https://www.regeringen.se/contentassets/c3c8d6e9fa074489a0424e84d87e04f9/budgetprocessen-i-det-finanspolitiska-ramverket-sou-202393.pdf) and the linked FiU1 decisions.

The site has complete numeric 27-area frames for 2017–2020 and 2023–2026. They are parsed by `platform/ingest/riksdagen/budget_ingest.py` and refreshed with `python platform/legacy/politics_budget.py`. The parser:

items.title: docs/budget-provenance.md › Budget years, party proposals and decisions
docs/budget-provenance.md › Budget years, party proposals and decisions
items.text:
The exact imported chain currently exists for two years: **FiU1 budget frame point 2 → vote ID → eight party positions**, for budget years 2025 and 2026. The site also lists explicitly cited propositions/motions and reservations at that point. A citation does not mean a party endorsed the document. Only one candidate speech was retrieved for the 2025 point and none for the 2026 point; that similarity is a discovery link, not an exact speech-to-motion relationship or evidence of why anyone voted No. Older FiU1 decisions are linked as documents, but historic member-level votes are not yet imported. [Riksdag: budget 2025](https://data.riksdagen.se/dokument/HC01FiU1), [Riksdag: budget 2026](https://data.riksdagen.se/dokument/HD01FiU1).

Party alignment is useful context, but “the right voted No because the left proposed it” is a hypothesis, not something a ballot proves. In the two imported recent government budget votes, M, KD, L and SD voted **Yes** to the committee proposal. To examine opposition behaviour fairly, a later analysis should distinguish government/committee proposals, rival whole-budget alternatives and individual motions, then compare only like-for-like votes across changes of government. It should quote a party's stated reason when making a claim about motive.

items.title: docs/budget-provenance.md › Budget years, party proposals and decisions
items.text: Regenerate and check this layer with `npm run data:build` and `npm run data:check`. The context validator checks all twelve years, original frame counts and every imported party position against its source fact row.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Diagram och KPI-vyer: öppna fynd och diagramval
items.text:
Tre genomgångar från 11–12 oktober 2026 är sammanförda här: alla grafer och KPI-vyer,
politikens vyer samt Labour Market, Wellbeing och EU AI Act. Kodfynden kontrollerades på nytt

nya rapportsidorna (`JobsReport`, `WelfareReport`, `AiActReport`), som byggdes efter

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Diagramform efter fråga
items.text:
| Fråga                                  | Form                                         | Villkor                                                                                                  |

| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Ett tal för senaste läget              | Stort värde med enhet, period och jämförelse | Ett fristående antal behöver ingen graf.                                                                 |

| Ett mått mot en verklig referens       | Bullet: värde med referensmarkör             | Referensen är en baslinje, en tidigare period eller ett mål. Hitta inte på mål eller statuszoner.        |

| Två mättillfällen för flera kategorier | Dumbbell: två sammanbundna punkter per rad   | Behåll staplar kring noll när bara förändringen ska rangordnas. Jämför inte delår mot helår.             |

| Rangordning av kategorier              | Horisontella staplar (`RankBars`)            | Samma skala där raderna ska jämföras.                                                                    |

| Små skillnader mellan kategorier       | Rangordnat punktdiagram                      | Punkter tål en avgränsad skala. Staplar från en kapad nollpunkt förstorar skillnaden.                    |

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Diagramform efter fråga
items.text:
| Sammansättning av en total             | 100 % staplade staplar                       | Bara när delarna summerar. Kategorier som kan överlappa, som teknikomnämnanden, får separata staplar.    |

| Utveckling över tid                    | Linjer                                       | Direktetiketter och en vald serie.                                                                       |

| Många överlappande tidsserier          | Små separata linjegrafer                     | När läsaren ska följa varje trend. En gemensam graf passar när nivåerna ska jämföras vid samma tidpunkt. |

| Mönster över många kategorier och år   | Heatmap                                      | Ordnad skala från ljus till mörk, färgnyckel, markering för saknade värden.                              |

| Avvikelse från en referens             | Staplar kring noll                           | Vattenfall först när vägen från startsumma till slutsumma är frågan.                                     |

| Förutsagt mot observerat               | Punktdiagram med diagonal                    | Kalibreringens kvartilspann är inget konfidensintervall.                                                 |

| Närhet i en representation             | Projektion, med en lista bredvid             | Visa klusterstorlek, exempel och kvalitetsmått. Kartavstånd är ingen KPI.                                |

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Diagramform efter fråga
items.text:
Nära varje huvudgraf: frågan, måttet och enheten, perioden, jämförelsen och en kort tolkning.
Visa nämnaren för andelar och skilj procent från procentenheter. Saknade värden skrivs
"saknas", aldrig noll. En uppgång färgas inte som bra: fler jobbannonser, högre skatt och fler
sjukfall betyder olika saker.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Förslag per produkt
items.text: Förslagen var inte genomförda 12 oktober 2026.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Politik
items.text:
- Väljare: föregående mot senaste mätning som dumbbell per parti. Senaste stöd som punkter med
  osäkerhetsintervall.
- Röster: 100 % staplade staplar för ja, nej, avstod och frånvaro per parti som översikt.
  Behåll heatmap för alla partipar.
- Skatter: Sverige mot jämförelsesnittet som dumbbell, gärna en rad per skattetyp. I det
  granskade lokala urvalet var Sveriges skatter 41,4 % av BNP, plats 8 av 36, 7,4
  procentenheter över snittet, och Danmark högst med 45,2 %.
- Partiledardebatter: rangordnade staplar för repliker per parti. Behåll heatmap för vem som
  replikerar på vem.
- Utredningar: ledtid till lag som punktdiagram eller boxplot när observationerna finns. En
  ensam median säger mindre.
- Röstmodell: i det granskade urvalet var träffsäkerheten 68,9 %, majoritetsbaslinjen 56,0 %
  och ROC AUC 0,769. ROC AUC har en annan skala och visas separat.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Labour Market
items.text:
- Yrken och län mellan två perioder: dumbbell med föregående och aktuellt antal på samma rad.
- Villkor: skilj anställningsform, arbetstid och erfarenhet åt. De har olika nämnare.
- IT-rapporten visade fyra nyckeltal i det lokala urvalet: 35 726 annonser, 2 862 unika
  arbetsgivare, −52,6 % utvecklarannonser och 4,1 % juniora annonser. Visa
  utvecklarförändringen med basår och jämförelseår som sammanbundna punkter.
- Klusterkartan: behåll den för utforskning. Rangordnade staplar för annonser per kluster ger
  den kvantitativa jämförelsen.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Wellbeing
items.text:
- Regionala skillnader: punktdiagram per indikator med samma länsordning mellan panelerna, och
  osäkerhetsintervall där de finns.
- Förändring mellan två år: dumbbell per län och indikator.
- Mot länssnittet: avvikelse kring noll.
- Lägg inte värden från olika perioder i en gemensam rangordning. Mått med olika enheter får
  egna skalor.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › EU AI Act
items.text:
- Artikelstatus: segmenterad stapel för helt gällande, delvis gällande och kommande artiklar,
  en stapel per kapitel vid jämförelse. Den visar modellens statusfördelning, ingen
  organisations efterlevnad.
- Roller och skyldigheter: rangordnade staplar för antal skyldigheter. En skyldighet kan
  beröra flera roller, så rollantalen summeras inte till 100 %.
- Tidslinjen: egna rader för tillämpning, frister och dokument när händelser sammanfaller.
- Undvik mätare som antyder "procent färdig lag" eller "procent efterlevnad".

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Drug Synergy Lab
items.text:
- Anrikning bland topprankade par: punkter eller linje med baslinje på en numerisk axel.
- Vävnader: behåll kroppskartan som ingång och lägg rangordnade staplar för mätantal och
  synergiandel bredvid.

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Visuell migrering till v2, 16 oktober 2026
items.text:

items.title: docs/chart-review.md › Political Observatory v2 follow-up ? 16 October 2026
items.text:
The main political routes now use the five-area workspace. The similarity heatmap uses a
fixed 0?100% scale and exposes comparable counts by focus, hover and table. Survey lines use
calendar spacing, break across missing observations and show published uncertainty; isolated
intervals use whiskers. Party-pair history retains a 0?100% scale. Cohesion, participation
and PM-party alignment have separate denominators. Source totals with incomplete seat
coverage are flagged. Desktop/mobile screenshots and axe scans were performed on the five
new areas. Older detailed builders/readers remain available; this does not close unrelated
chart findings in other projects. See [visualization inventory](political-observatory-v2-audit.md).

items.title: docs/cluster-batches.md › Clustering batches 0-2: results
items.text:
Code: `platform/publish/clusters/`. Statuses come from `stats.diagnostics`:

- `counter_example`: the mean bootstrap ARI is under 0.6, or the same fit on two periods agrees at an ARI under 0.6.
- `descriptive`: fewer than 50 units.
- `unvalidated`: there is no stability check.

Only `finding` may be posted as a finding. Every k is picked by silhouette over 2-8 (2-10 for the labour-market types). The pick is flagged when it sits at an end of the sweep or when the runner-up is within 0.005.

items.title: docs/cluster-batches.md › Fits of 2026-10-22, after review round 1 of PR #94

items.text: Every k above that comes from a silhouette sweep is 2, the low end of the sweep, and is flagged. items.title: docs/cluster-lab.md › Cluster Lab
docs/cluster-lab.md › Konfiguration
items.text:
- `configs/cluster_lab/test.yaml`: två verkliga smoke-körningar, 400 observationer
  vardera. Jobbtestet använder det uttryckligen valda arkivet `2026-Q3`, inte hela
  2023–2026. Atlas-testet väljer ur alla tillgängliga verk.
- `jobs_2023_2026.yaml`: hela den tillgängliga jobbmarknaden, datum från och med
  2023-01-01 och före 2027-01-01. Ingen tech-, titel- eller kompetensavgränsning.
- `symbolic_atlas.yaml`: förekomster, unika passager och experiment per symbol.
- `overnight.yaml`: båda dataseten och alla tre Atlas-familjerna i en ändlig plan.
- `layouts_only.yaml`: nya kartor från redan sparade klusteretiketter.

`datasets` väljer adaptrar, källor, datum och familj. `max_symbols: null` tar alla
symboler som klarar `min_occurrences` och `min_works`. Nattkonfigurationen tillåter
20 symboler; antalet kvalificerade symboler bestäms ur den inlästa korpusen.
`source_archives` är ett uttryckligt källurval för test, aldrig en dold gräns.

Ändra basparametrar direkt i YAML eller använd en override:

```powershell
python -m ml.cluster_lab.cli validate --config configs/cluster_lab/overnight.yaml --set clustering.min_samples=10
```

Datasetets egna YAML-inställningar har företräde framför gemensamma inställningar.
CLI-overrides tillämpas sist, även efter datasetets baseline.
För Atlas ändras alltså dess `representation`, `clustering` eller `sweep` i
datasetblocket i nattkonfigurationen. Alla defaults och overrides sparas i
varje körnings `config.json`.

items.title: docs/cluster-lab.md › Konfiguration
items.text:
Sökområden finns i `sweep.search`. Enskilda värden, listor och ändliga intervall:

```yaml
sweep:
  coarse_candidates: 24
  search:
    - parameters:
        reduction.method: [none, pca, svd, umap]
        clustering.min_samples: [3, 5, 10, 20]
        clustering.min_cluster_size: [100, 300, {fraction: 0.005}]
    - when: {reduction.method: umap}
      parameters:
        reduction.n_components: [5, 10, 20, 30]
        reduction.n_neighbors: {range: {start: 15, stop: 120, step: 15}}
```

`fraction` räknas mot det faktiska antalet observationer i försöket. Det använda
heltalet sparas separat. Villkor väljer metodens sökområde. En reproducerbar,
begränsad slumpmässig sökning väljer kandidater; den kör inte hela produkten.
Ogiltiga nycklar, tomma listor, modellrevisioner och parameterkombinationer ger fel.

items.title: docs/cluster-lab.md › Inläsning och täckning
items.text:
Verktyget använder repots JobTech-arkivhämtare med ett nytt fulltextläge. Den
befintliga filtrerade IT-pipelinen och aggregerade marknadsrapporten behåller sina
uppgifter. Samma hämtare används av Cluster Lab, med återupptagbara Range-hämtningar,
retries för throttling/serverfel och checkpointade Parquet-block. ZIP-importen kan
skanna tillbaka till senast färdigskrivna block efter ett avbrott. Stabilt annons-ID
deduplicerar versioner mellan arkiv. Olika annonser slås inte ihop på textlikhet.

Årsarkiv 2023–2025 och kvartalsarkiv 2026 hämtas från den
[officiella arkivkatalogen](https://data.arbetsformedlingen.se/annonser/historiska/).
JobStreams [officiella API-schema](https://jobstream.api.jobtechdev.se/swagger.json)
beskriver `/v2/snapshot` som alla **aktiva** annonser.
