items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/README.md › Job Intelligence: compliance subsystem
items.text:
The executable foundation is
[`schema.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/schema.sql) and
[`contracts.py`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/contracts.py). It creates
13 empty tables in an isolated, in-memory DuckDB database. It also defines an
original-document interface. The Phase 1 CLI acquires register data only;
the separate Phase 2 CLI collects authority documents into a private database.
Run the offline checks:

```sh
python -m pytest platform/tests/compliance_intelligence -q
```

No company violation or reviewed legal outcome has been asserted by these tasks.
Phase 2 has observed real source documents without interpreting their outcomes. Test
records are synthetic and use temporary test directories. Private compliance
processing is separate from scheduled public data publishing. The explorer and
canonical company routes reuse the existing frontend; the job/company projection
uses the existing jobs delivery group. The homepage and intro animations are
outside this change.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/README.md › Job Intelligence: compliance subsystem
items.text:
The schema now supports a private Phase 1 registry database. The application creates
immutable cohort bundles, verifies their hashes and provides conservative identity
resolution. It is not a production warehouse migration or publication gate.
Phase 3 adds private evidence review and gated release staging. Actual human
approvals and public delivery remain pending; the real pilot has no approved rows.
Phase 4 has built six private analytical tables against the real frozen cohort.
The 50 company summary rows have unassessed metrics; legal fact tables are empty
because no real decision has been approved. Empty facts do not mean no sanctions.
Phase 5 adds `#compliance` to the portfolio, with an explicit public unavailable
state. Exact-artifact human approval is required to replace that state with real
company observations. Aggregate collection/review progress can be shown separately
without publishing company findings. No actual outcomes were approved or uploaded.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Architecture
items.text:
Status: Phase 0 design, 2026-10-16. The subsequent
[Phase 1 implementation](phase-1.md) adds register acquisition, identity resolution
and private frozen-cohort bundles. [Phase 2](phase-2.md) now implements private
source acquisition and candidate extraction in a separate Bronze/Silver/Gold
database. [Phase 3](phase-3.md) adds scoped extraction, decision links, human review,
reverification and approved release staging. Actual approvals and public deployment
remain pending. Production legal-domain tables are not populated from parser output.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Storage and execution boundaries
items.text:
| Stage | Intended contents | Boundary and existing reuse |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Acquisition | Register snapshots and original authority/court documents | Separate private store and private DuckDB file outside repository/public warehouse upload roots. Reuse `rawstore` retry, exact-byte hash and manifest semantics after supporting this private root. |

| Bronze | Immutable fetch versions with URL, request, timestamp, original-byte digest and response metadata | Never put unreviewed evidence in `warehouse/raw` with its current publishing configuration. Credentials, personal identifiers and authentication headers must be excluded from manifests/logs. |

| Silver | Legal entities, aliases, dated relationships, cases, decisions and claim-level evidence | Typed tables in a private database; verified organization numbers anchor identity. Keep extraction candidates and reviewed assertions distinguishable. |

| Review | Identity decisions, legal interpretation, privacy clearance, publication authorization | Private audit trail tied to exact record/evidence versions. Human decisions cannot be inferred from a successful parser or dbt test. |

| Gold | Approved, minimized entity/outcome facts and coverage observations | Future dbt subject follows existing bronze/silver/gold conventions, but reads approved projections only into the public warehouse. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Storage and execution boundaries
items.text:
| Export | Cohort/methodology CSV and JSON; later Parquet analytical facts | Explicit column allowlist, source links, status/as-of dates and release manifest. Exclude raw PDFs, personal details, reviewer IDs, extraction text and private object references. |

| Delivery | Immutable reviewed release and compatible snapshot pointer | Reuse `platform/publish/release.py` and `configs/delivery/`; publication must be a separate authorized operation after tests/review. Add no live group now. |

The Phase 0 namespace `compliance_intelligence` describes domain contracts, not a
fourth production medallion layer. `open_contract_database()` always uses
`:memory:`. Never copy its DDL into the publicly backed-up `portfolio.duckdb`.
Phase 1 may persist reviewed registry data only after confirming reuse terms and
the private/public boundary. Before any enforcement acquisition, private storage
must be provisioned with separate credentials and no public access. A private prefix
inside the existing public R2 bucket is insufficient.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Company identity and group scope
items.text:
`dim_company` represents one registered entity identity. A Swedish legal entity
keeps its `company_id` through a legal-name change; a newly registered successor has
a distinct identity. Proposed Swedish ID: `se:orgnr:<10 normalized digits>`.
Phase 1 must validate length, permitted legal-entity number class and Luhn checksum
against register evidence; format alone is not verification. Sole traders and
natural-person identifiers are excluded from the cohort.

Registered branches can be represented with `entity_kind=registered_branch`, linked
to their legal operator by `branch_of`. They are excluded from the initial cohort
of Swedish limited companies. A foreign parent has its own local registry number,
registry authority and registration country. Its Swedish `organization_number` is
null. Never invent a Swedish organization number for a foreign parent.

`country_code` means country of registration, not customer market, tax residence,
ownership nationality or country of alleged conduct. `legal_case.jurisdiction_country`
is separate. `authority` identifies the issuing authority/court, not the issuer of a
security. A securities issuer is a company with role `issuer`; it can be different
from the sanctioned shareholder. A natural-person sanctioned party remains outside
the public company identity model, even if a company is named in the document.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Company identity and group scope
items.text:
Aliases are evidence-backed and dated. A brand may have multiple legal operators;
identical names can return multiple candidates. Relationships record
`subsidiary_of`, `merged_into` or `branch_of` with effective intervals and evidence.
A corporate group is derived from a reviewed, dated ownership graph; it is not a
legal entity or an alias. A future group display can reference the parent identity
and relationship version without collapsing member identities.

Only a verified exact organization-number match supports automatic identity
confirmation in Phase 1. A contradictory name, historic name outside its valid
period, unclear operator or multiple candidates requires review. Fuzzy/name matches
are candidates with evidence and reasons, never silent assignments. Confidence is
a category with reasons (`verified`, `ambiguous`, `unverified`), not an invented
probability. Store candidate sets and match-method provenance privately in Phase 1.

Decisions attach through `decision_company` to directly documented parties. Group
membership never propagates a sanction. Joint liability needs explicit decision
evidence identifying each liable legal entity and scope. A merger preserves the
original case party and adds the succession relationship; it does not rewrite history
or establish transfer of liability by itself. An issuer, customer or contextual
mention cannot enter sanctioned-party metrics.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Fixed cohort design
items.text:
The proposed population is active, Swedish-registered limited companies (`AB`,
legal entities) with a primary SNI 2025 code in the six segments in
[source feasibility](source-feasibility.md). Foreign-owned Swedish subsidiaries
qualify; foreign parents, branches and pure holding entities do not qualify merely
because their groups operate IT businesses. Multiple qualifying subsidiaries may
appear because the unit is a legal entity, not a corporate group.

Select 50 entities by descending SCB employee-size-class order, then ascending
normalized organization number. Freeze the codebook for class ordering and exclude
unknown/missing class values with counts and reasons. This is a size-class-based
sample, not a claim to identify the 50 largest firms by exact employment. If the
50th position falls within a broad class, the tie-break is deterministic but
economically arbitrary; publish that limitation and boundary class size. Avoid
mixing group turnover with entity employee classes. If a complete eligible population
or 50 verified entities is unavailable, fail selection and document the gap.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Fixed cohort design
items.text:
`cohort_definition` records a population document/hash, actual snapshot as-of date,
methodology JSON/version and selection code SHA. Do not backdate a current register
snapshot to the audit date. `compliance_cohort` stores the selected identities,
original SNI and size-class attributes, source and ranks. Freeze a canonical
membership hash and original export. Re-running against the same snapshot and code
must reproduce the same ordered 50 identities and hash.

After freezing, dissolution, mergers and changed names are longitudinal annotations.
There are no replacements or silent sample refreshes. A later cohort receives a new
ID and remains comparable only with its own methodology. Exploratory company search
is a separate read-only population query; its results cannot change cohort membership
or denominators. Selection must be completed independently of enforcement searches.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Cases, events and decisions
items.text:
One `legal_case` is one authority/court docket, namespaced by issuing body and
reference number. An administrative file and an appeal court file are separate
cases. Multiple documents and decisions can belong to a case. A later `case_link`
relation must record `appeal_of`, `remittal_of` and `related_to`, with source evidence.
A separate `decision_link` records which act upholds, varies, quashes or supersedes
another act. Both are designed here and intentionally absent from the Phase 0 DDL.

`case_event` is an observed procedural occurrence. Preserve allegation,
investigation, regulatory finding, administrative sanction, judgment, final judgment,
criminal conviction, acquittal and closure without finding as different categories.
These are not ordinal severity levels. An allegation does not imply that an
investigation exists, and a closed case does not imply a violation.

`legal_decision` is an authority/court act with its own status, source, legal basis,
date and monetary remedy. `decision_kind` states the forum/type; `outcome_type`
states its result. A criminal conviction requires a criminal judgment and separate
legal review. A corporate fine must retain its actual legal basis and party; it
must not be relabeled as a natural person's conviction. The initial product should
exclude personal criminal-history records entirely.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Cases, events and decisions
items.text:
Decision date, publication date, event date and retrieval time answer different
questions and may be missing independently. Never fill an absent date from another
field. `decision_status`, `appeal_status`, `finality_status` and `stay_status` are
separate. A sanction may be issued, appealed and stayed at the same time. Default
appeal/finality values are `unknown`; the passage of a nominal appeal period or a
missing appeal search result is insufficient to assert finality. Use court/authority
confirmation with field-level evidence and a verification date.

Appeal outcomes preserve the original decision and link a new decision with the
upheld, varied, quashed or remitted disposition. Do not overwrite amounts/history or
count the same proceeding twice. Later analytical rules must choose either original
orders or effective outcomes as of an explicit date. Joint amounts remain at the
decision grain; joining multiple parties must not multiply the amount.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Evidence and review
items.text:
Each source version has a URL, original-byte SHA-256, publisher, fetch time,
publication date where known, content type, size and access/reuse/privacy status.
Content-addressed private storage retains changed versions; equal bytes at different
URLs can share a blob without collapsing fetch provenance. HTTP validators are
cache hints, not document identity. Hash derived/OCR text separately, never in place
of the original document. Pin extraction tool/model version, language and page/section
locators. A model-generated summary is an unreviewed derivative, not authority text.

`source_evidence` links each material assertion to a document and locator: identity,
party role, date, legal basis, amount, appeal and finality all need support.
`record_hash` is SHA-256 over a canonical JSON representation of the full reviewed
record plus ordered evidence IDs and document hashes. Future serialization must use
sorted keys, UTF-8, stable ISO dates/UTC timestamps, decimal strings and no NaN.
The original-document hash and the structured-record hash have different meanings.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Evidence and review
items.text:
Workflow: unreviewed extraction enters identity review; unresolved identities are
held. A legal reviewer verifies categories, amounts and current appeal/finality.
Privacy/reuse review clears the actual public projection. A different publication
reviewer approves that exact record/evidence version and export artifact. Record
reviewer, time and rationale for every action. Corrections or new source versions
invalidate relevant approvals and reopen review. Rejected/withdrawn records are
held, with reasons preserved privately. Publication requires all required approvals,
no open identity conflict and fresh verification. There is no Phase 0 exporter that
could bypass this workflow.

The Phase 0 SQL implements default-unreviewed states, named/timestamped final review
actions, typed keys, monetary constraints and several legal category guards.
It does not enforce independent reviewers, evidence completeness, all cross-table
semantics, immutable cohorts or actual publish rights. Phase 1 now adds identity
validation and application-level cohort freezing. Enforcement evidence and publication
controls now have a separate private [Phase 3 implementation](phase-3.md). Passing
SQL tests is insufficient approval to publish; its human gates, source freshness
and release validation must also pass.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Coverage and uncertainty
items.text:
Maintain one observation per company/source/search window/run. Its query manifest
records identifiers, aliases and effective periods searched, filters, pagination,
terminal-page proof, retrieval failures and document-request outcomes. A complete
search means complete execution against that source within that window, not complete
knowledge of all proceedings. Record source-selection bias separately.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Coverage and uncertainty
items.text:
| Measure | Definition | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cohort integrity | Verified unique members / target 50 | Must be 50/50 before cohort freeze; no records implies not measured. |
| Search execution coverage | Complete applicable company/source/window cells / all applicable planned cells | Always show numerator, denominator and restricted/failed/partial cells; curated sources remain incomplete histories. |
| Identity ambiguity | Unresolved candidate-party matches / all candidate-party matches | Show candidates held from publication; zero denominator gives null. |
| Evidence completeness | Supported required assertion fields / all required assertion fields | Required fields include party, category, amount when present, and claimed appeal/finality. |
| Review completion | Required approved record-version reviews / required reviews | Unknown or rejected reviews do not pass; no averaging across review kinds. |
| Verification freshness | Eligible records verified within policy interval / eligible records | Proposed policy: 30 days for open/appealed records, 90 days for final records; show max age. These are project policies, not statutory limits. |
| Finality uncertainty | Decisions with unknown finality / decisions assessed | Display alongside separate final/non-final counts. |
| Document accessibility | Retrieved readable primary documents / identified relevant documents | Show request-required, withheld, unavailable and OCR-limited counts separately. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Coverage and uncertainty
items.text:
Use a proposed analysis window beginning 2018-05-25 and ending at the declared
analysis as-of date, while retaining older related decisions needed to explain an
appeal. This improves comparability with GDPR-era IMY publication but does not
equalize authority coverage. Review the window before enforcement work. Use the
wording "no matching published record found in the searched sources/window" only
when a documented search supports it. Never derive a company innocence/risk rating
or sanction probability from missing results.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Phase 4 analytical boundary
items.text:
The [analytics CLI](phase-4.md) reads only current-valid Phase 3 approved Gold and
a verified fixed 50-member Phase 1 cohort. It rechecks legal-entity identities and
original-document hashes/excerpts before writing six isolated `gold` tables as
DuckDB, JSON and Parquet. No private candidate becomes an analytical fact. A status
dependency may validate an approved row without becoming a separate public fact.

Explicit reviewed decision links define sanction lineages before date or status
filters apply. Native case/issuer IDs remain distinct. Appeals and duplicate
documents cannot create another obligation; cross-company links and ambiguous
branches hold the build. Original and final-effective amounts have separate roles
and native currencies. Cohort-member group aggregation retains legal attribution
on every fact. Criminal-law scope stays separately unmeasured under the current
Swedish Gold contract.

Private analytical bundles include the cohort definition, filters, status snapshot,
source reconciliation, unknown coverage denominators and observation-only metric
warnings. A query validates current approvals and recomputes SQL/Parquet/JSON
agreement; withdrawn/expired Gold makes an older analytical release invalid.
This is not a public publisher or a change to whole-warehouse R2 backup. Public
delivery must run the same gate and carry the [methodology](phase-4-methodology.md).

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md › Phase 5 public explorer boundary
items.text:
The explorer producer stages an allowlisted public projection from live-validated
Gold, cohort and analytical bundles. Per-lineage measures reuse the Phase 4 Python
transform; browser filtering sums those reviewed contributions with exact native-
currency cents. Direct entity facts stay separate from group membership. A final
independent human review binds the sealed projection and presentation-source hash.
Promotion rechecks current approvals and writes only the designated public JSON
envelope. Original documents, excerpts and review-store records remain private.

The static portfolio reads this same-origin envelope without the private warehouse
or a new R2 delivery group. Its build gate and browser validate approval, integrity
and expiry. Pending, invalid, unavailable and expired data never fall back to mock
company metrics. Active pages poll the current envelope and check it on focus;
operators must withdraw/redeploy when underlying reviews are revoked. Offline
copies and exported images cannot be recalled through that mechanism.

Research graphics come from structured aggregates rendered as SVG and canvas PNG.
CSV and methodology exports retain filters, source references and fingerprints.
See [Phase 5](phase-5.md) for review operations, cache boundaries and limitations.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/completion.md › Current completion and review handoff
items.text:
Checked 2026-10-17. This report supersedes the input-readiness statements in the
earlier phase validation reports. Implementation and real processing have advanced;
public legal publication remains held. No company outcome has been approved by
the assistant or by a human reviewer.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/completion.md › Phase status
items.text:
| Phase | Implemented and exercised | Remaining acceptance work |

| --- | --- | --- |

| 1, cohort and identity | Authenticated SCB acquisition, complete six-segment traversal, canonical registry, conservative resolution and a verified frozen 50-company export. | Human clearance of source reuse/publication. Historical aliases, ownership and foreign parents remain absent unless separately evidenced; current SCB observations cannot supply their history. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Conventions
items.text:
All IDs are strings with stable namespaces. Organization numbers are identifiers,
never numeric measures. Dates use ISO calendar dates; timestamps use timezone-aware
UTC values. Validity intervals are `[valid_from, valid_to)`; a null endpoint means
unknown/open, so it cannot prove that a relationship existed on an arbitrary date.
Code and registry snapshots must be versioned outside the table contents as well.

Every SQL column declared `not null` is structurally mandatory; primary keys are
non-null. Other columns are nullable. Null means unknown/not supplied, except where
an explicit status documents not applicable or no monetary remedy. Null amounts
must never be coerced to zero. A `sanction_type=none` is an affirmative source-backed
statement; `unknown` is the default. Enum values must be preserved in exports or
mapped through an explicitly versioned label dictionary.

Common fields:

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Conventions
items.text:
| Field | SQL type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_document_id` / `document_id` | varchar, FK where declared | Exact primary-source version supporting the row; additional field evidence goes in `source_evidence`. |
| `last_verified_at` | timestamptz, required where present | When the represented information was checked against the supporting source, distinct from download/build time. Reverification also needs an audit entry. |
| `review_status` | review_state, required, default unreviewed | `unreviewed`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`. A row flag cannot replace record-version approval evidence. |
| `record_hash` | varchar, required | Lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 of canonical record content plus supporting evidence versions; see architecture. It is not a document hash. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Source document
items.text:
`source_document`: one fetched document/response version from one source context.
Primary key: `document_id`. Matching bytes across sources do not merge provenance.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `document_id`, `source_id` | varchar | Internal version ID and source registry key, such as `imy` or `scb_company_register`. |

| `source_url`, `publisher` | varchar, required | Public primary-source HTTPS URL and publishing body; authority identity remains separately attached to the case. |

| `publication_date` | date, nullable | Publisher's date, unknown if absent; not inferred from retrieval or PDF filesystem metadata. |

| `fetched_at` | timestamptz, required | Retrieval time. Future manifests also record request/filter, redirects, response headers/status and collection completion. |

| `document_hash` | varchar, required | SHA-256 of original response/document bytes, lowercase 64 hex. No newline normalization, OCR or reserialization before hashing. |

| `content_type`, `byte_count` | varchar / bigint, required | Response media type and original byte length greater than zero. |

| `storage_ref` | varchar, nullable/private | Private content-addressed object reference. Excluded from public exports. |

| `access_status` | varchar | `public`, `request_required`, `restricted`, `unknown` (default). Public retrieval is independent of reuse approval. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Source document
items.text:
| `reuse_status`, `terms_url` | varchar / nullable varchar | `unverified` (default), `permitted`, `restricted`; supporting policy/license URL, with its dated evidence retained privately. |

| `privacy_status` | varchar | `unreviewed` (default), `cleared`, `redaction_required`, `blocked`; applies to this source version, not automatically to every derivative. |

| `last_verified_at` | timestamptz | Common verification field. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Company registry
items.text:
`dim_company`: one current registered identity. Primary key `company_id`; unique
Swedish `organization_number` and unique `(country_code, registry_authority,
registry_number)`. Historic names and identity changes remain in aliases/evidence.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Company registry
items.text:
| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `company_id` | varchar | Stable legal-identity ID, proposed Swedish form `se:orgnr:<digits>`. Does not change with brand or legal-name changes. |
| `organization_number` | varchar, nullable for foreign identities | Exactly ten normalized Swedish digits; Phase 1 must add legal-entity class/checksum/register verification. Swedish records require it and match `registry_number`; foreign records leave it null. |
| `registered_legal_name` | varchar, required/nonblank | Register name, retaining diacritics and legal suffix. Search normalization must retain the original. |
| `country_code` | varchar, required | Two-letter country of registration. No inference about headquarters, parent nationality or case jurisdiction. |
| `registry_authority`, `registry_number` | varchar, required | Register namespace and its entity identifier, also usable for foreign parents. |
| `legal_form`, `entity_kind` | varchar | Register legal form; `legal_entity` (default) or `registered_branch`. A registered branch has a distinct register identity but is not a separate legal person. |
| `identity_status` | varchar | `unverified` (default), `verified`, `ambiguous`. Verified requires reviewed register support; no probabilistic score is inferred. |
| `source_document_id`, `last_verified_at` | common | Identity evidence and verification time. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Company registry
items.text:
`dim_company_alias`: one evidenced name/operator association over a validity interval.
Primary key `alias_id`; `company_id` references `dim_company`. Aliases are deliberately
not globally unique. Multiple legal entities may operate the same brand.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alias_id`, `company_id`, `alias` | varchar, required | Association ID, operator identity and nonblank original name. |
| `alias_type` | varchar | `brand`, `trading_name`, `historic_legal_name`. A brand never becomes an independent legal entity merely through this row. |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | nullable date | Effective dates supported by the source, not dates a crawler first saw a name. |
| `source_document_id`, `review_status`, `last_verified_at` | common | Support, review and freshness. |

`company_relationship`: one directed relationship assertion over a validity interval.
Primary key `relationship_id`. Self-links are rejected; no group-level case merge
or sanction inheritance is implied.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Company registry
items.text:
| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `relationship_id` | varchar | Stable assertion ID. |
| `company_id`, `related_company_id` | varchar, FKs | Child/predecessor/branch and parent/successor/operator respectively. |
| `relationship_type` | varchar | `subsidiary_of`, `merged_into`, `branch_of`. |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | nullable date | Effective relationship interval; unknown dates require manual temporal review. |
| `source_document_id`, `review_status`, `last_verified_at` | common | Relationship evidence, review and freshness. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Cohort
items.text:
`cohort_definition`: one versioned selection. Primary key `cohort_id`.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cohort_id`, `as_of_date`, `target_size` | varchar / date / integer | Cohort version, actual population snapshot date and fixed target of 50. No real sample exists yet. |
| `methodology_version`, `methodology_json` | varchar / json | Version plus population filters, SNI/class codebooks, ordering/tie-breaks, exclusions and source references. JSON structure validation belongs to Phase 1. |
| `population_document_id` | varchar, FK | Representative original source document for the selected population. For a multi-page API snapshot, full population provenance is bound by `population_manifest_hash`. |
| `population_manifest_hash` | varchar, required | SHA-256 of the canonical population manifest containing metadata and every original document/request/hash. Added in Phase 1 so a single source page cannot be mistaken for the entire population. |
| `selection_code_sha` | varchar | Git SHA or SHA-256 of selection code. Must identify exact executable selection logic. |
| `frozen_at`, `membership_hash` | nullable timestamptz / varchar | Both null for draft; both present for frozen. Membership hash covers ordered membership and selection attributes using a documented canonical serialization. |

`compliance_cohort`: one selected company in one cohort. Primary key `(cohort_id,
company_id)`; unique rank per cohort.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Cohort
items.text:
| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cohort_id`, `company_id` | varchar, FKs | Cohort and legal-identity membership. |
| `selection_rank` | integer | Deterministic rank 1 through 50. |
| `primary_sni_code`, `sni_version` | varchar | Five-digit primary code at selection and `2007` or `2025`. The proposed first cohort uses 2025. |
| `employee_size_class`, `size_class_order` | varchar / integer | Original class code and explicit codebook ordering, not an estimated exact employee count. |
| `selection_document_id` | varchar, FK | Evidence for this entity's selection attributes. |

The DDL limits membership to 50 ranks. The Phase 1 builder validates population
scope, reviews, eligibility and exactly 50 members before its database transaction.
Sealed, create-once output directories and read-only queries preserve the original
bundle through the supported interface. Hash verification detects file/database
changes; it is not a cryptographic signature or a replacement for filesystem access
control. Exploratory search never inserts memberships.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Case and decision
items.text:
`legal_case`: one authority/court docket. Primary key `case_id`; unique
`(authority, authority_case_number)`.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | varchar | Stable namespace-qualified docket ID. Not a company or corporate-group ID. |
| `authority` | varchar | Stable issuing-body identity, including the specific court. Never a securities issuer company. |
| `authority_case_number` | varchar | Official docket/reference, preserving the source representation. |
| `jurisdiction_country` | varchar | Country of the legal proceeding, separate from party registration country. |
| `case_type` | varchar | `data_protection`, `competition`, `procurement`, `financial_regulation`, `civil`, `criminal`, `other`. |
| `lifecycle_status` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `open`, `closed`, `remanded`; closure is not a substantive finding. |
| `source_document_id`, `last_verified_at` | common | Docket support and verification. |

`legal_decision`: one act within a case. Primary key `decision_id`; multiple acts may
exist in one docket. Authority is obtained by joining `legal_case`; primary source
URL/hash are obtained by joining `source_document`. No denormalized copies are needed.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `decision_id`, `case_id` | varchar / FK | Decision identity and issuing docket. |

| `decision_kind` | varchar | `administrative`, `administrative_judgment`, `civil_judgment`, `criminal_judgment`, `procedural`. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Case and decision
items.text:
| `outcome_type` | varchar | `regulatory_finding`, `administrative_sanction`, `criminal_conviction`, `acquittal`, `dismissal`, `no_finding`, `other`. A criminal conviction/acquittal requires `criminal_judgment`. |

| `decision_date`, `publication_date` | nullable date | Legal act date and source publication date. Independently unknown if absent. |

| `legal_basis` | nullable varchar[] | Cited legal instrument/version and provisions, with source locators; null is unverified, an empty list does not establish legality. |

| `decision_status` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `issued`, `corrected`, `varied`, `overturned`, `withdrawn`. Historical versions remain auditable. |

| `appeal_status` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `not_appealed_verified`, `appealed`, `pending`, `decided`, `withdrawn`, `not_appealable`. No appeal found is not verified non-appeal. |

| `finality_status` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `not_final`, `final`. Final requires an appeal state compatible with finality and separate source evidence. |

| `stay_status` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `not_stayed`, `stayed`. Enforcement stay is distinct from finality. |

| `sanction_type` | varchar | `unknown` (default), `none`, `administrative_fine`, `corporate_fine`, `coercive_fine`, `damages`, `costs`. These financial remedies are not interchangeable metrics. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Case and decision
items.text:
| `sanction_amount` | nullable decimal(20,2) | Nonnegative amount exactly stated in the source; decimal arithmetic, no floating-point rounding. A decision with several remedies needs later remedy-item rows; do not combine types here. |

| `currency` | nullable varchar | Three-letter currency, e.g. SEK; required exactly when an amount is present. Validate against the applicable ISO codebook later, not only format. |

| `source_document_id`, `review_status`, `last_verified_at` | common | Primary act, review and verification. |

An upheld administrative sanction remains an administrative-sanction outcome in an
administrative judgment. A final judgment is a judicial decision with verified finality;
it may concern a finding, acquittal or another outcome. It is not a synonym for conviction.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Events and parties
items.text:
`case_event`: one evidenced occurrence. Primary key `event_id`. An optional linked
decision must belong to the same case via a composite foreign key.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event_id`, `case_id`, `decision_id` | varchar / FK / nullable FK | Event identity, docket and relevant act. |
| `event_type` | varchar | `allegation`, `investigation`, `regulatory_finding`, `administrative_sanction`, `judgment`, `final_judgment`, `criminal_conviction`, `acquittal`, `appeal_filed`, `appeal_decided`, `remittal`, `closure_without_finding`, `correction`. |
| `event_date`, `recorded_at` | nullable date / required timestamptz | When it occurred and when it entered the system. |
| `source_document_id`, `review_status` | common | Occurrence evidence and review. |

Findings/sanctions/judgments/convictions/acquittals require a decision link. Future
cross-table validation must also verify matching event/outcome category and that a
`final_judgment` links a judicial decision with evidenced `finality_status=final`.
These cross-table semantics are not all implemented by the Phase 0 DDL.

`decision_company`: one company role per decision. Primary key `(decision_id,
company_id, party_role)`; same entity can have multiple documented roles.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Events and parties
items.text:
| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decision_id`, `company_id` | varchar, FKs | Act and directly documented legal identity. |
| `party_role` | varchar | `sanctioned_party`, `regulated_entity`, `claimant`, `respondent`, `issuer`, `contextual_mention`. |
| `attribution_scope` | varchar | `context_only` (default), `direct_legal_entity`, `documented_joint_liability`; group membership is never a default liability scope. |
| `identity_status` | varchar | `unverified` (default), `verified`, `ambiguous`. Sanctioned-party rows require verified identity and a liability scope. |
| `source_document_id`, `review_status` | common | Party-role evidence and review. |

Amounts belong to the decision, not each party. A joined party table must not
duplicate sums. Multi-remedy allocations, group displays and natural-person parties
are outside this minimal contract and require later design/review before publication.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Assertion evidence and review
items.text:
`source_evidence`: one source locator supporting one field of a record version.
Primary key `evidence_id`. Generic target references need later referential checks;
SQL only enforces the linked document FK.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evidence_id`, `target_table`, `target_id` | varchar, required | Assertion ID and target record, including canonical serialized composite IDs where needed. |
| `record_hash`, `field_name` | varchar, required | Supported version and field. |
| `document_id`, `locator` | varchar, required | Exact document FK plus PDF page/paragraph, HTML section or structured JSON path. |
| `extraction_method`, `extractor_version` | varchar | `manual`, `structured`, `text`, `ocr`, plus parser/tool/model or human procedure version. |
| `observed_at` | timestamptz | When the assertion was extracted/checked. |

`record_review`: one review action on one record version. Primary key `review_id`.
The audit trail is append-only by workflow policy; SQL alone does not enforce that.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Assertion evidence and review
items.text:
| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `review_id`, `target_table`, `target_id`, `record_hash` | varchar | Review action and exact reviewed version. |
| `review_kind` | varchar | `identity`, `legal`, `privacy`, `publication`. Privacy review includes reuse and the actual proposed projection. |
| `review_status` | review_state | Common states; approved/rejected/withdrawn actions require a nonblank reviewer and timestamp. |
| `reviewer_id`, `reviewed_at` | nullable varchar / timestamptz | Internal actor and decision time, withheld from public data. |
| `rationale` | varchar, required | Evidence checked, unresolved issues or reason for approval/rejection/withdrawal. |

Approvals bind to the current evidence set and record version. No rows in this table
automatically trigger export. Later publication validation must reject stale approvals
and require a publication reviewer independent of extraction/legal preparation.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Coverage
items.text:
`coverage_observation`: one company/source/window/search-run observation. Primary
key `coverage_id`; keep successive observations to explain changes in coverage.

| Fields | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coverage_id`, `company_id`, `source_id` | varchar | Search observation, entity FK and source identifier. |
| `window_start`, `window_end` | date, required | Inclusive requested search window; end cannot precede start. |
| `searched_at` | nullable timestamptz | Actual execution time, absent before searching. |
| `search_status` | varchar | `not_started` (default), `complete`, `partial`, `failed`, `not_applicable`, `restricted`. Not applicable needs a documented reason. |
| `query_manifest` | nullable json | Identifiers, time-valid aliases, filters, paging, terminal proof, source versions and retrieval errors. Complete status requires it and a search time. |
| `candidate_count` | nullable integer | Nonnegative candidate hits; zero is valid only after an actual search. Not-started rows require null count/time. |
| `limitations` | varchar, required | Source-selection, inaccessible history, redaction, identity and parsing limitations for this observation. |

Metrics and denominators are defined in [architecture](architecture.md). Empty
observations produce not-measured/null values, never a fabricated 0% or 100%.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Minimum requested field mapping
items.text:
| Required field | Canonical home |
| --- | --- |
| `company_id`, `organization_number` | `dim_company`; the `decision_company` bridge preserves every documented company role. |
| `case_id`, `case_type`, `authority` | `legal_case`. |
| `decision_date`, `publication_date`, `legal_basis` | `legal_decision`; source versions independently retain their publication date. |
| `decision_status`, `appeal_status`, `finality_status` | `legal_decision`. |
| `sanction_amount`, `currency` | `legal_decision`, at one monetary-remedy grain in this contract. |
| `source_url`, `document_hash` | `source_document`, reachable through document FKs and field evidence. |
| `review_status` | Reviewed record plus version-bound `record_review`. |
| `last_verified_at` | Company, source document, relationship, alias, case and decision where freshness is material. |

Future logical relations `case_link`, `decision_link`, remedy items, identity-match candidates and
release manifests are described in the architecture/handoff, not silently implied to
exist in the executable schema. Add them when their phase needs an implementation.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 2 acquisition tables
items.text:
The following tables are implemented by `ingestion.sql` in a separate private
database. They contain observations and extraction candidates. They do not create
rows in `legal_case`, `legal_decision`, `case_event` or `decision_company`.

| Table | Key and fields | Meaning |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `bronze.ingestion_run` | `run_id`; `started_at`, `finished_at` timestamptz; `configuration`, `report` JSON | Acquisition interval, bounds, seed URLs, collector code SHA, extractor version, manifest/policy hashes and optional verified cohort ID/membership hash. |

| `bronze.document_version` | `document_id` PK; unique `source_id`, `source_url`, `document_hash`; `authority`, `content_type`, `byte_count`, `first_fetched_at` | A source/URL/byte-version identity. `document_id` hashes the canonical source/URL/digest tuple; `document_hash` is the original fetched response body's SHA-256 after HTTP transfer decoding, never an extracted-text hash. |

| `bronze.document_version` retention fields | Nullable `storage_ref`, `copy_review` JSON; `reuse_status`, `privacy_status` | `reference_only_unverified` by default, with original URL as the reference. An approved scoped private-copy assessment can set `private_copy_reviewed` and a content-addressed blob. Privacy remains unreviewed and public release is not authorized. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 2 acquisition tables
items.text:
| `bronze.resource` | PK `source_id`, `source_url`; `document_id`, nullable `etag`, `last_modified`; `last_verified_at` timestamptz | Current observed version and HTTP cache hints for the URL. Older document versions stay available. Verification here means retrieval/cache verification, not legal verification. |

| `bronze.fetch` | `fetch_id` PK; `run_id`, `source_id`, `source_url`, `fetched_at`, `attempt`, nullable `status_code`; `response_metadata` JSON | One request attempt, including robots, redirects, retries and denials. Only selected response headers are retained; credentials/cookies are omitted. |

| `bronze.fetch` change fields | Nullable `document_id`, `previous_document_id`, `changed`, `error_code` | Successful content observations link current/previous identities. `changed` signals byte change, including reversion, without determining correction or supersession. HTTP errors and policy denials have no document identity. |

| `bronze.robots_observation` | PK `run_id`, `source_id`; `source_url`, `checked_at`, `document_hash`, `status_code`, `rules` JSON | Robots fetch, hash, matching allow/disallow rules and crawl delay. Failed requests also appear in the fetch log. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 2 acquisition tables
items.text:
| `silver.document_extraction` | PK `document_id`, `extraction_version`; `extracted_at`; nullable `publication_date`, `decision_date`, `case_reference`; `review_status`, `payload` JSON | One parser result per exact document version. Parser version incorporates its code, registry normalizer code and installed pypdf version. Conflicting singular fields remain null; review defaults to unreviewed. |

| `silver.discovery` | PK `run_id`, `source_id`, `source_url`, `kind`, `parent_document_id`; `label`, `status` | Discovery edges retain their parent evidence and anchor text. Seed parents use an empty string. Kind is listing/record/document; status records observation, duplicate discovery, failure or deferral by bound/manifest/source halt. Edge counts are not distinct document counts. |

| `silver.company_mention` | PK `run_id`, `document_id`, `mention_index`; nullable `company_id`; `candidate_ids`, `resolution` JSON; `review_status` | Number/name candidates resolved against the supplied canonical registry. A company ID can confirm registry identity only; scope remains contextual and unreviewed. No relationship traversal or sanctioned-party attribution. |

| `gold.ingestion_coverage` | View grouped by `run_id`, `source_id`; `fetch_attempts`, `failed_attempts`, `observed_versions` | Request-level operational counts. Retries count as attempts; robots fetches have no document version. These are not case or sanction counts. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 2 acquisition tables
items.text:
The Silver payload retains selected HTML/PDF `source_metadata`, plural
`case_references`, literal `named_legal_entities`, validated `organization_numbers`,
date `field_evidence`, discovery `links`, `revision_markers`,
`revision_link_candidates` and extraction `limitations`. Evidence carries a page or
main-content locator; extracted dates also retain their source fragment. A singular
case reference is null when multiple dockets are present. Correction markers and
links are candidates requiring review, not established legal relationships.

Private Gold JSON adds per-source attempted pages/records/documents, observed
URLs/hashes, independent dates, deferred-discovery counts, errors, terminal-list
state and limitations. A pinned manifest adds baseline hash comparisons. With a
verified cohort it adds each member's candidate document IDs and
`partial_publication_scan` status. Without a cohort, size and coverage fractions
are null and status is `not_measured_registry_missing`. The private Parquet file
contains per-run/source operational counts and the same unknown denominators.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 3 evidence and review model
items.text:
Private `legal_review.sql` extends the ingestion database without populating the
Phase 0 legal-domain tables. Source observations become versioned candidates.
The exact proposal schema is available through `review_cli.py schema` and is
implemented in `legal_extraction.py`.

| Table/view | Grain and fields | Guarantees and limits |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `review.candidate` | `record_hash` PK; `record_id`, `document_id`, nullable `case_id`, `created_at`; `payload`, `identity_match`, `completeness` JSON; nullable `registry_hash` | Immutable serialized candidate version. Record hash binds proposal, source URL/hash, publisher, preparer, identity result, registry hash, completeness and pending-link diagnostics. Record ID hashes original document bytes plus decision slot. |

| `review.current_record` | `record_id` PK, `record_hash` | Current candidate version, without deleting earlier candidates or reviews. It does not imply an approved decision. |

| `review.decision_link` | PK source record hash / target record ID / relation; exact target record hash and evidence JSON | Directed proposed appeal/upholding/modification/annulment/supersession/remittal/related/duplicate relationship. Target docket excerpt, disposition, chronology and cycles are checked; legal review is still required. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 3 evidence and review model
items.text:
| `review.pending_link` | PK source record hash / target record ID; target record hash, reason, evidence | Possible follow-ups with ambiguous or unconfirmed targets. They hold affected decisions and require a scoped proposal before legal approval. |

| `review.action` | `action_id` PK; record/context hashes, review kind, disposition, reviewer ID, review time; nullable verification time/due date; rationale, full action JSON, audit sequence | Human approval/rejection/withdrawal. Latest action per review kind governs that exact version. Service principals and unauthorized roster roles are refused. |

| `review.audit_log` | Sequence PK; UTC event time/type/payload, previous hash and event hash | Append-only application audit for candidate creation, source-access policy/request observations and human actions. Chain and record/action consistency are checked. Full database administrators can rewrite the chain; protect storage and retain external backups if stronger assurance is required. |

| `review.evidence_access` | Access ID, document ID, check time, method, nullable matched-hash flag, result | Original availability, retained/local/reference-refetch method, verified original hash or explicit hold/failure. It does not grant reuse rights. |

| `review.case_groups` | Provisional issuer/docket ID and distinct decision count | Exact normalized docket grouping. Different acts on the same docket remain distinct; court/authority cases remain separate namespaces. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 3 evidence and review model
items.text:
Proposals carry `document_id`, `decision_slot`, `scope_pages`, producer kind/version/
model, strict typed `claims` and directed `links`. Each claim has `value` plus
`evidence` entries with physical page, normalized character start/end and literal
quote. `null`, `unknown` and empty arrays preserve uncertainty. Extra keys, approval
claims, invented excerpts and unsupported values are rejected.

The claim set includes authority, case number, legal entity, optional organization
number, case type, legal basis, independent dates, original outcome, monetary
sanction, appeal information, status, party role and attribution scope. Status
values are `investigation`, `alleged`, `decided`, `appealed`, `final`, `modified`,
`annulled`, `unknown`. The original outcome is distinct from status and finality.
Monetary values use decimal strings with explicit SEK/EUR and administrative-fine
type; unsupported remedies remain unclassified. See [extraction rules](phase-3.md#extraction-contract).

Review context binds source/record heads, registry snapshot hash, decision links
and incoming legal-review heads. New evidence or dependency reviews invalidate
matching approvals. Publication must follow current identity/legal/privacy reviews
and use an independent reviewer. Verification deadlines are project policy: 30 days
for non-final/uncertain records and 90 for explicitly final records.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 3 evidence and review model
items.text:
Gold is produced through the gated exporter, staged privately as JSON and nonempty
Parquet. It includes canonical company/case/decision-version IDs, source authority
and docket, reviewed direct party, original outcome/amount/status, derived current
status and finality, subsequent-decision references, source URL/hash, review context
hash, verification/due dates and status-as-of time. Effective amount stays null
without a confirmed final unchanged order. Quotes, original documents, reviewer
IDs, model metadata and private paths are excluded. `validate-release` checks the
projection and current approvals again before future public promotion.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 4 analytical model
items.text:
Typed definitions are in
[`analytics.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.sql). These
tables are created in a separate private `analytics.duckdb`, not migrated into the
existing publicly backed-up warehouse. Counts refer to filtered approved evidence.
See the [public methodology](phase-4-methodology.md) for exact inclusion rules.

| Table | Grain / identifier | Fields and meaning |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `gold.fact_compliance_cases` | `(company_id, case_family_id)` | Origin authority/docket, earliest originating decision date, count of approved decision acts. `case_family_id` is the originating native case ID; distinct orders on one docket share this case row. |

| `gold.fact_compliance_decisions` | `decision_id` | Approved `record_hash`, direct `company_id`, native case ID, family and originating decision IDs; native/origin authorities; case category, original outcome, current legal status and finality; independent decision/publication dates, legal-basis list and origin date; origin/administrative/GDPR/competition flags; exact source URL and document hash. Flags count each sanction lineage once on its origin row. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 4 analytical model
items.text:
| `gold.fact_compliance_amounts` | `amount_id`, SHA-256 of origin/decision/kind | Decision, origin, entity and case IDs; decimal(20,2) amount, native currency, original or final_effective kind; originating date/authority/category, conversion method, source URL/hash. Nonnegative amounts, no currency conversion. Only final_effective contributes to totals. |

| `gold.mart_compliance_company_summary` | `entity_id` within one filtered bundle | Legal entity/group label and scope, cohort ID, member ID list/count, SNI and employee-class lists; employee interval bounds; observed approved decisions/case families; nullable sanction/GDPR/competition/appeal/modified/annulled counts; separate nullable criminal metric and explicit scope status; distinct reviewed documents; final totals by currency; exploratory count and currency-specific amount rate bounds; metric/coverage status and period/group dates. |

| `gold.mart_compliance_rankings` | Entity/scope/metric/currency in one bundle | Observed decimal-string value, nullable descending dense rank, assessed comparison count, explicit observation-only basis and null coverage fraction. Separate metrics only; currency is null for counts. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 4 analytical model
items.text:
| `gold.mart_compliance_source_coverage` | `(authority, period_start, period_end, period_role)` | Requested-window or subsequent-context role, approved decision and distinct document counts, known/assessed assertion fields, approved-row field completeness; nullable source-population denominator and population/search coverage fractions, explicit population-unknown status. |

Summary `entity_id` equals `company_id` for legal-entity scope or a reviewed dated
group root for group scope. `cohort_member_ids` always lists the actually aggregated
members. Group IDs do not replace defendant IDs in the facts. Employee bounds are
register class limits, not headcounts; rate bounds are decimal strings. Final
amount maps use currency keys and decimal strings, never a mixed-currency scalar.

`observed_approved_decisions` and `reviewed_source_documents` can be zero while
sanction metrics remain null (`not_assessed`). With selected approved evidence,
zero is an observed count within that evidence only. An empty final-amount map is
not a comprehensive zero-liability assertion. `criminal_convictions` is null under
the present contract, with a separate explanation in `criminal_metric_status`.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 4 analytical model
items.text:
Bundle `methodology.json` binds cohort/member hashes, as-of dates, selection rules,
filters, status snapshot, approved-Gold manifest hash, transform/SQL code hash,
dataset row counts/hashes and warnings. `cohort-definition.json` repeats the cohort
context; `reconciliation.json` lists checked source/record hashes and URLs.
Parquet, SQL and JSON project the same rows. The sealed artifact manifest binds
physical files; canonical dataset hashes provide logical reproducibility.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 5 public projection
items.text:
`explorer.py` produces one sealed private stage and, after final human review, one
same-origin public `release.json`. `state=unavailable` contains no company payload.
`state=approved` has publication status, actual review/deadline timestamps, a SHA-256
of the exact UTF-8 `payload_json` string and that string. The browser verifies the
bytes before parsing the projection. The fingerprint is not an identity signature.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 5 public projection
items.text:
| Projection field | Grain and scope |
| --- | --- |
| `context` | Approved analytical cohort, membership hash, selection/date/filter metadata, warnings and status snapshot. Original membership is 50; interactive filters select within it. |
| `presentation_sha256` | Hash binding the reviewed module's model, exports, component and stylesheet sources; the build gate checks the same order. |
| `companies` | Allowlisted canonical identity and register-source fields for cohort members and reached related entities; membership flag, employee interval bounds and explicitly null financial metadata. Private identity-review objects are excluded. |
| `relationships` | Reviewed directed entity IDs/type/validity and source URL/hash. Does not move legal liability. |
| `families` | One approved originating sanction/decision lineage, with company/native case/origin IDs, authority, category, originating date, operative status, separate metric contributions, amounts by kind/currency, approved decisions and reviewed status-document references. |
| `coverage` | The full approved release's Phase 4 authority/year/role cells, preceding interactive filters. Unknown source/search denominators stay null. |
| `evidence_valid_until` | Earliest selected decision's legal reverification deadline, conservatively normalized to UTC midnight. Final public approval cannot extend it. |
| `methodology_markdown` | The exact public method text examined with the staged payload. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/data-dictionary.md › Phase 5 public projection
items.text:
The decision CSV has one row per selected approved decision, with its own monetary
row array, native legal identity/status, source hash/URL and release/filter context.
The chart CSV instead has one row per plotted aggregate; its grain is different.
Methodology Markdown carries complete exact references and cohort/release hashes.
Graphic metadata embeds the same context; PNG carries the visible subset and needs
the companion Markdown for complete machine-readable references.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › IT jobs and canonical company identity
items.text:
Implemented and source-checked 2026-10-17. Readers can open a verified advertising
entity from an IT advertisement and return to its related current advertisements.
Unknown identities remain visible as advertisements, without company-level data.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Repository audit
items.text:
The checkout had aggregate job reports, occupation/technology analyses and ad
clusters, but no individual-ad section named "Veckans IT-jobb" and no canonical
company profile route. `JobsReport.tsx` and `JobsProduct.tsx` remain the existing
job product. The new list is a deep dive at `/#jobb-it`, reached from that report
and its topic navigation. The four existing report tabs remain intact.

`ingest_jobs.py` already provides immutable `raw.job_ads` payload versions,
deduplication and a retrying JobSearch client. `weekly_jobs.py` uses that same
client and writer. The daily market pipeline retains its archive/stream counts;
its new export step collects current advertisements. The existing market
export contains aggregate counts. Legacy hashed
`gold.dim_employer.employer_id` values remain legacy identifiers, not canonical
company IDs. No existing historical ads are rematched by name.

The existing compliance registry supplies organization-number validation, legal
identity records, reviewed aliases, dated relationships, private snapshot storage,
sealing and DuckDB schemas. `populate_database` can now materialize those same
registry tables without freezing a cohort. Job identity bundles use the same
`dim_company`, `dim_company_alias`, `company_relationship` and ID namespaces.
They are versioned materializations of this registry, not another company ID
system. The original frozen cohort is never changed by a job refresh.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Repository audit
items.text:
No usable company financial history, client/contract, repository-ownership or
issuer mapping dataset was found. The profile exposes these gaps and accepts
reviewed, directly attributed context observations when available. Public legal
data comes exclusively from the existing approved Compliance Explorer release.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Sources and access
items.text:
JobSearch's [official OpenAPI document](https://jobsearch.api.jobtechdev.se/swagger.json)
declares advertisement reuse under [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/deed.sv).
The collector uses the API, not website scraping: Data/IT occupation field
`apaJ_2ja_LuF`, publication window, publication-date sort, 100 records/page,
offsets below 2,000, four requests/second, retries/backoff on throttling and server
errors. Larger result sets split the publication interval, with overlapping
boundaries deduplicated by native advertisement ID. Different IDs remain distinct
even when titles match. Changing totals, repeated/missing pages and an unresolved
dense interval fail the collection. Equal page totals cannot prove an immutable
snapshot: the API offers no snapshot token. Copies and request parameters remain
private, so the observed batch can be reproduced offline even after ads disappear.
Client query wall times use Europe/Stockholm; OpenAPI does not specify upstream
offset semantics. Publication timestamps retain their source representation.
Daily hiring counts use the source calendar-date text, without an inferred UTC
conversion. Split windows overlap by one second to avoid losing boundary records.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Sources and access
items.text:
[SCB documents](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/avgiftsfria-uppgifter-i-foretagsregistret/)
current legal-unit/workplace data, employee size classes, a personal API key,
5 requests/second and no historical or changes-only endpoint. The existing
SCB client stays below that limit. Targeted requests use the documented v1 legal
unit endpoint with `16` followed by the validated ten-digit organization number.
The key is read from `SCB_API_KEY` and sent only in `X-API-Key`.
The authenticated endpoint and its returned identity were checked live. A 404
remains missing; unsupported foreign-legal-person records are held with their
evidence for identity review. A current snapshot
does not establish when a company changed its name or employee count.

The employer population includes employers in all industries advertising IT jobs.
It is not the eligible IT-company population or the fixed 50-company cohort.
SCB lookup snapshots explicitly set `population_complete=false`. Company ID,
registration country, securities issuer and workplace remain separate.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Resolution contract
items.text:
1. A validated legal-person organization number in the canonical registry verifies
   the advertised identity, provided its name is not contradictory.
2. A unique explicitly reviewed alias can verify an entity without a number.
   Brand, trading and historic names require source evidence and a dated validity
   interval covering the advertisement publication date.
3. Normalized current names and conservative similar-name candidates remain in
   the review queue. Confidence is evidence strength, not a calibrated probability.
4. Contradictory names, invalid numbers, multiple candidates and unsupported
   identities remain ambiguous, awaiting review or unresolved. An invalid supplied
   number never falls back to a name match.

An automatic link means **advertised employer**. It does not identify a recruiter
or an undisclosed end client. `recruiter` and `actual_employer` require explicit
human-reviewed role evidence. Workplace text and job descriptions do not establish
those roles. Parent ownership, merger edges and brand resemblance do not transfer
ads, finances or compliance decisions to another legal entity.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Resolution contract
items.text:
Manual review is bound to both `job_payload_hash` and `registry_hash`. A changed
ad or registry version requires a new review. The input JSON array requires:
`job_id`, `relationship_type`, `company_id` (nullable for rejection), both hashes,
`disposition` (`approved`/`rejected`), `reviewer_id`, UTC `reviewed_at`, HTTPS
`evidence_url`, SHA-256 `document_hash`, `source_locator` and `rationale`.
`--reviewers` names an explicit JSON array of authorized human reviewer IDs.
Conflicting role reviews are rejected. This CLI is a private operator tool, not a
public review endpoint; reviewer access must be controlled by its operator.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Tables and analytical grain
items.text:
The extension lives in [`job_links.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/job_links.sql).

| Table/view | Grain and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Existing `dim_company` | One legal entity per canonical registry snapshot. |
| Existing `dim_company_alias` | Reviewed, sourced and dated alias of one entity. |
| Existing `company_relationship` | Dated, sourced relationship; no automatic aggregation. |
| `job_observation` | One native job ID and pinned payload hash per collection, with publication time. |
| `job_company_link` | One job ID × relationship type per resolved snapshot. |
| `company_resolution_review` | One immutable human review, bound to both input versions. |
| `company_registry_observation` | Current sourced SNI and employee class, by exact company ID. |
| `company_context_fact` | Reviewed, directly attributed measure/event observation, with period, unit and source. |
| `mart_company_hiring_daily` | Company × role × publication day; distinct observed advertisements. |
| `mart_company_hiring_context` | Daily hiring rows joined to register context and each reviewed financial observation. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Tables and analytical grain
items.text:
`job_company_link` contains `job_id`, nullable `company_id`, `relationship_type`,
`match_method`, `match_status`, `match_confidence`, nullable `verified_at`, original
employer name/number/workplace, both version hashes and JSON match evidence.
SQL constraints enforce non-null company/verification time only for verified
links. Private Parquet exports include links, reviews and the two hiring marts.

The financial join is one row per financial observation; **do not sum repeated
ad counts across financial measures or periods**. Units/currencies are retained,
never converted or summed implicitly. The same canonical ID enables size/activity
and financial/activity comparisons, but current size classes are intervals and
the observed weekly ad population is not hiring volume. Historical ads outside
this window, withdrawn ads and company workforce history are not reconstructed.
Neither financial nor legal outcomes establish a cause for recruitment changes.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Public API and routes
items.text:
This is the existing static Worker/R2 architecture; no duplicate API server is
introduced. `jobs/company-intelligence.json` is part of the existing `jobs` delivery
group, excluded from `jobs-analysis` to give it one owner. The existing pinned
delivery loader serves the same dataset to the list and every company profile.
Semantic checks reconcile IDs, payload hashes, evidence, status counts and match
percentage; Node validates the browser contract during the production build.
The production publisher also checks official live JobSearch provenance and
withholds fixture/historical batches. Private audit files retain implementation
hashes and the resolution version.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Public API and routes
items.text:
The version-1 response has `state=available` or `state=unavailable` with a reason.
Available responses include `generated_at`, `valid_until`, `registry_hash`,
`coverage`, `metrics`, `jobs`, `links`, `companies`, `relationships` and `context`.
The [delivery schema](../../configs/delivery/schemas/company-intelligence.json)
and [browser model](../../frontend/src/companies/model.ts) define the fields.
Ad fields include native ID, title, original employer/workplace, validated public
organization number or null, location, structured skills, publication/deadline,
original URL and canonical payload hash. "Technologies" means skills explicitly
mentioned in ads, not an asserted deployed stack. No raw descriptions or contacts
are published. Natural-person organization identifiers are withheld.
The advertisement hash is SHA-256 of the existing writer's sorted-key UTF-8 JSON
serialization (`ensure_ascii=False`, default separators), not a digest of the
linked HTML page. Original API-response byte hashes and request parameters are
retained separately in the sealed private collection.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Public API and routes
items.text:
| Route | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `/#jobb-it` | Current ads, coverage, search and verified company links. |
| `/#jobb-it?company=<encoded canonical ID>` | Jobs explicitly linked to that entity; no group rollup. |
| `/#jobb-it?q=<search>` | Search card metadata; this does not resolve identities. |
| `/companies/:companyId` | Canonical legal profile; the complete ID is URL-encoded as one segment. |
| `/#compliance-company?company=<encoded ID>` | Existing reviewed decision detail/evidence. |

Profiles show overview, financial/workforce context, observed recruitment,
documented decisions, corporate events/relationships, clients/contracts, technology,
repositories/issuer context and related jobs. Missing IDs return a missing-profile
state; no similarly named company is substituted. Back/forward, reload and native
open-in-new-tab work. Site-root data/assets and Cloudflare's documented
[SPA fallback](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/single-page-application/)
support deep links. Existing hash routes and home navigation remain available.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Missing legal data and publication safeguards
items.text:
Only the existing approved, unexpired public Gold release can supply legal records.
The join is exact `company_id`; family-level metrics prevent multiple judgments
from becoming multiple sanctions. A parent receives no subsidiary decisions.
Appeal/finality statuses and subsequent source decisions remain visible. The
public approval fingerprint now also includes company-profile presentation code.
No legal ingestion, rankings or new legal conclusions occur in the job pipeline.

An unavailable/expired legal release means **not assessed**, not zero sanctions.
Approved records with no company decision also do not establish a negative search.
The requested wording "No documented sanctions identified in the covered sources
and period" needs an actual reviewed company-scoped search record defining those
sources and dates. None exists yet, so the implementation displays the narrower
truthful unavailable/incomplete-coverage state. It never says zero violations.
Company-scoped complete-search coverage remains null; reviewed documents and
complete authority/company search coverage must not be confused.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Local operation and deployment
items.text:
Keep the real key in the existing ignored root `.env` or process environment.
[`.env.example`](../../.env.example) declares the key and local register fallback.
Local CSV/Parquet extracts still use the Phase 1 provenance-sidecar ingestion;
pass that sealed snapshot directory with `--registry`. Missing API access is
supported: ads are collected, but unmatched identities remain unresolved.
Authentication failures with a configured key fail the refresh; they do not
silently downgrade an allegedly verified company.

```powershell

python platform/publish/job_companies.py refresh
# Same operation, atomically replacing the designated local public projection.
python platform/publish/job_companies.py refresh --publish
# Offline rebuild / human review from exact preserved inputs (new output path).
python platform/publish/job_companies.py resolve --collection .research/run/collection --database .research/run/job-market.duckdb --registry .research/run/registry --output .research/run/reviewed --reviews .research/reviews.json --reviewers .research/reviewers.json --context .research/context.json --publish
# Targeted SCB lookup: private JSON array, validated legal-person numbers only.
python platform/publish/job_companies.py lookup --numbers .research/numbers.json --output .research/new-registry
python platform/publish/job_companies.py check
npm run jobs:check
npm run build
```

items.text:
Optional `--identities` uses the existing reviewed identity supplement. Context
inputs accept only the enumerated financial, workforce, event, contract, technology,
GitHub and stock observation kinds, exact company ID, `entity_scope=legal_entity`,
approved human review, period/label/string value/unit, verification time and
precise source URL/hash/locator. Stock observations additionally require their own
`issuer_id` and country. Human reviewer identity/rationale remain private. Legal
findings are not a context-fact kind and must use the Gold release instead.
Reviewed context may include a verified registry entity with no observed current
ads; its profile shows that context without inventing recruitment records.

The daily `market` subject runs the new refresh/export step. Set `SCB_API_KEY` in
the existing `anton-portfolio` GitHub environment; the workflow references that
secret without embedding it. The local key does not configure GitHub or Cloudflare.
No SCB secret is needed in the browser or static Worker. Build and deploy through
the existing process, then publish the updated versioned `jobs` R2 group. An old
active delivery manifest lacks the new file: the UI truthfully reports unavailable
until that group is published; it never substitutes unrelated local production data.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md › Local operation and deployment
items.text:
Private raw responses, SCB snapshots, review queues, DuckDB/Parquet and audit logs
stay under `.research/job-company/` (or an explicitly chosen private output).
They are excluded from the warehouse upload roots and Git. CI currently discards
these private working files with its runner; operators needing retained manual
review must archive the sealed bundle in access-controlled private storage, not
the public R2 data prefix. Refreshes do not automatically carry human decisions
to changed input versions. Use the offline resolve command for a reviewed batch.

Jobs expire after 48 hours; the UI withholds stale records. A failed refresh keeps
the previous artifact, which still expires. Daily refresh and failure monitoring
are therefore required. The build checks structure even for expired snapshots,
while the browser enforces freshness. This prevents an unrelated site build from
publishing stale ads as current or depending on a private API credential.

No deployment or external secret change was performed by this implementation.
The homepage and intro animations were not changed for this integration.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/kkv-alternative.md › Discovery and access assessment
items.text:
The existing HTTP client checks robots before targets and redirects, restricts
origins, serializes requests with a minimum delay, bounds response size, retries
transient failures with exponential backoff and halts on 401/403. A 404 robots
response is a hold under this project's policy. It is not described as an explicit
prohibition by the host. Publication selections and higher-court precedents omit
many investigations, lower-court cases, appeals and unpublished documents.

No blanket open licence for entire websites or attachment collections is asserted.
Public access, the statutory treatment of official decisions, private retention
and public reuse are separate questions. See [source feasibility](source-feasibility.md)
and [risks](risks.md). Full PDF bodies are processed in memory; the default persisted
evidence is a stable official reference, original-byte hash, metadata and exact
private excerpts. Local import does not confer private-copy or public approval.
