items.text:
Run from the repository root. Existing Python dependencies are sufficient.

Generate a plan without making network calls:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/public_documents.py plan --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort-se-it-50-2026-10-17-v2 --output .research/compliance-intelligence/NEXT_PLAN.json
```

The actual pinned public court batch can be rechecked with:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/public_documents.py fetch --root .research/compliance-intelligence/completion-decisions-2026-10-17 --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort-se-it-50-2026-10-17-v2 --manifest .research/compliance-intelligence/kkv-alternative-2026-10-17/court-batch-pinned.json --max-documents 4
```

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/kkv-alternative.md › CLI and manifest contract
items.text:
Automatic collection accepts only explicitly listed HTTPS PDF publications on the
independent `www.domstol.se` host. It does not crawl links or fetch any KKV host.
Manifest fields are `schema_version: 1` and `documents`, whose entries contain
`source_id: court_publications`, `source_url` and `expected_sha256` (a 64-character
hash, or null for a deliberate first observation). Unknown keys are rejected.
The whole manifest is validated before network activity. A changed pinned hash
is held for review. Verified live bytes become the current source reference,
invalidating the old review context, without generating new legal claims. A local
file with a mismatched declared hash is rejected without replacing source state.
Use a deliberately revised manifest before extracting the changed live version.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/kkv-alternative.md › Manual local import
items.text:
Use an original PDF obtained through an ordinary permitted public download.
Do not use this command to launder a blocked, authenticated, encrypted or
restricted document. No file from an access-control bypass qualifies.

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/public_documents.py import-local --root .research/compliance-intelligence/completion-decisions-2026-10-17 --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort-se-it-50-2026-10-17-v2 --manifest .research/compliance-intelligence/YOUR_LOCAL_BATCH/manifest.json --max-documents 10
```

The local manifest uses the same top-level shape and adds these entry fields:

| Field | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source_id` | `kkv` for a KKV publication host, or `court_publications` for the independent court host. |
| `source_url` | Exact official public reference. Local KKV imports allow the explicitly documented `www`, `information` and `prod` publication hosts; no network request is made to them. |
| `expected_sha256` | Actual original-file SHA-256, required for local import. |
| `local_file` | Relative path within the manifest directory; path escape is rejected. |
| `acquired_at` | Actual UTC download time, not in the future. |
| `acquired_by` | Actual operator ID, kept private. |
| `public_download_without_bypass` | Explicit true only after checking the actual acquisition method. This is provenance, not legal/publication review. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/kkv-alternative.md › Manual local import
items.text:
A PDF is required, bounded to 25 MiB and 250 extracted pages. Encrypted, corrupt,
textless or unsupported documents remain held; no passwords or OCR bypass are
attempted. The pipeline stores an original reference/hash, fetch/import audit,
extraction version, uncertain observation fields, contextual matches and a
schema-validated review candidate. Case number, legal entity, decision/publication
dates, case type, status and any supported sanction amount use the existing
Phase 3 evidence schema. An unknown amount stays null, never zero. Publisher is
stored separately from the extracted deciding authority. Human-scoped corrections
use the existing `review_cli.py import-proposal` command and exact page excerpts.

Repeated URL/hash imports do not duplicate documents or candidate records.
Different URLs keep provenance while identical decision bytes share decision
identity. Changed source versions invalidate prior review context. Logs and
per-run `gold/runs/RUN_ID/supplement-coverage.json` distinguish candidates, hash
changes, extraction holds and deferred documents after a source access failure.
Exit codes: 0 for a completed candidate batch/report, 1 for held/deferred documents,
2 for invalid input or an unrecoverable command error. Reports refuse overwrite.

Rebuild detailed coverage from the recorded public search receipts:

The proposed population/ranking policy is in [architecture](architecture.md).
Primary SNI 2025 codes: `62100`, `62201`, `62202`, `62900`, `63100`, `58290`.
Qualify active Swedish AB legal entities. Rank known employee-size classes descending,
then verified normalized organization number ascending. Use the source codebook's
explicit class order; do not sort display strings lexically. This is a deterministic
size-class sample, not an exact-employment league table.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1-handoff.md › Required inputs
items.text:

   register snapshot with the required legal-unit, activity, primary-SNI/version and

   Bolagsverket HVD files for corroboration before acquiring broader access.
2. Complete snapshot/query manifest, source terms and timestamps. Preserve all pages
   or a content-addressed manifest with their hashes and verified terminal condition.
   Current-only API data cannot reconstruct an arbitrary historic cohort date.
3. Official SNI and employee-class codebooks pinned to the snapshot, including

4. Register/company-report evidence for names, aliases and dated relationships.

   even though enforcement data is not acquired in this phase.

If access, reuse rights or population completeness cannot be established, implement
offline selection against an explicitly supplied verified snapshot and report the
remaining input dependency. Do not invent 50 companies, approximate SNI codes,
employee counts, parent links or historic names to complete the file.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1-handoff.md › Implementation sequence
items.text:
1. Add a bounded register loader or snapshot-import interface under

   `platform/compliance_intelligence/`. Keep raw snapshots outside public backup roots

   until their contents/terms are cleared. Reuse byte hashes, request manifests and

   collection checkpoints; never place API secrets in provenance.

2. Implement organization-number normalization/checksum and entity-country validation.

   Populate `dim_company`, `dim_company_alias` and `company_relationship` with evidence

   and effective dates. A name change preserves identity; a merger links distinct

   identities. Foreign parent identifiers stay in their own register namespaces.

3. Implement conservative identity resolution: exact verified register identity;

   time-valid name/brand candidates; conflict/ambiguity hold with candidate IDs,

   match method and evidence. Avoid fuzzy auto-acceptance and group-based case merging.

4. Implement complete-population filters/ranking, draft `cohort_definition` and

   `compliance_cohort`, then validate exactly 50 verified unique eligible entities.

   Freeze the original selection and hash transactionally. Persist exclusions and

   counts, including the size-class boundary/tie-break limitation.

5. Add separate exploratory search over registry candidates. It must return match

   reasons/ambiguity and optional cohort membership without modifying the frozen

   sample or its denominator. A CLI/library interface is sufficient; no frontend.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1-handoff.md › Implementation sequence

   directory. Do not publish to R2 merely because an export succeeds. Propose dbt

items.text:
Produce a reproducible CLI invocation documented next to the code, a cohort CSV and
JSON, `methodology.json`, `population-manifest.json` and an exclusions/ambiguities
report. These are specified outputs for Phase 1, not files produced in Phase 0.

Every selected row must carry `cohort_id`, `as_of_date`, `selection_rank`, `company_id`,
`organization_number`, `registered_legal_name`, `country_code`, `registry_authority`,
`registry_number`, `primary_sni_code`, `sni_version`, `employee_size_class`,
`size_class_order`, `identity_status`, `source_url`, `document_hash` and
`last_verified_at`. Relationships/aliases belong in separate exports with their
own evidence and dates. Never flatten foreign parents into Swedish cohort members.

Methodology must include snapshot time versus effective source dates, exact filters,
source/terms references and hashes, classification/class ordering versions, full
eligible population count, exclusions by reason, boundary-class population, tie-break,
code SHA, schema version and canonical membership hash. Preserve original sample
attributes even when a later name or ownership annotation changes.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1-handoff.md › Acceptance checks
items.text:
- Rebuild from the same archived snapshot and code yields the same ordered 50
  organization numbers and membership hash, regardless of input order or duplicate
  observations. Fail on fewer than 50 verified eligible identities or incomplete pages.
- Test formatted numbers, invalid checksums, natural-person identifiers, duplicate
  IDs, conflicting legal names and the same brand used by different operators.
- Test a renamed entity before/after the effective date, a Swedish subsidiary with
  a foreign parent, multiple qualifying subsidiaries, an excluded holding parent,
  a registered branch and a merger with preserved predecessor identity.
- Ambiguous or contradictory matches stay unresolved with a candidate set; no
  parent/sibling receives another entity's identity or case association by default.
- Frozen membership rejects replacement/mutation. Exploratory queries cannot alter
  it; current identity annotations do not rewrite the original selection export.
- All selected identities/attributes have source evidence, true snapshot dates and
  review status. No synthetic company rows enter exports.
- Run focused pytest checks and the required repository checks. Record existing
  failures separately; do not edit unrelated frontend/workflow work to hide failures.

Phase 1 completion hands off a verified frozen cohort and identity graph. Enforcement
source pilots, legal-case linkage, review tooling and publication remain later work.

cohort bundles. On 2026-10-17 the real SCB population was acquired and the 50-member

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Activate SCB access
items.text:
Register through the portal linked by
[SCB's current API information](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/avgiftsfria-uppgifter-i-foretagsregistret/),
accept its terms and obtain your authorized key. The key is personal to the issued
API access. Set `SCB_API_KEY` in the process environment or an ignored local `.env`.
The CLI uses the repository's existing `load_env` helper. Existing environment
values take precedence over `.env`. Add variables from
[`.env.example`](../../.env.example) to an existing `.env`; copy the example only
if no `.env` exists. Keep production credentials in the authorized secret store.

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py status
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py ingest --source scb --output .research/compliance-intelligence/register-2026-10-16 --reuse-reviewed-by YOUR_REVIEWER_ID
```

The output directory name is illustrative. Actual `as_of_date` comes from retrieval,
not the directory name. `--reuse-reviewed-by` records your review of source reuse
terms; omit it to keep source reuse unreviewed. The explicit `build --private-only`
option permits private selection from a complete directly acquired SCB population
while preserving that unreviewed state. It cannot approve a local extract or a
public release. `--reuse-reviewed-by` does not
approve public publication. A key is never supplied as a command-line argument,
written to provenance or printed in an error message.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Activate SCB access
items.text:
The implementation follows the
[official AFR v1 OpenAPI specification](https://apiafr.scb.se/swagger/v1/swagger.json),
retrieved without authentication for inspection on 2026-10-16:

- HTTPS origin `https://apiafr.scb.se/v1`, header `X-API-Key`; redirects are refused.
- `GET /juridiskaenheter/naringsgren/{code}` for each eligible primary SNI code,
  with `limit` and subsequent `cursorId`.
- Read `jes`, `pagination.hasMore` and `pagination.nextCursorId`; traverse every
  page through the terminal response. The default page size is 5,000, with a
  configurable hard page bound of 1,000 per industry.
- Check each industry's `/count` before and after acquisition, received record count,
  repeated IDs/cursors, returned primary industry, field types and requested page size.
  Errors or a reached page bound leave no completed snapshot.
- Issue requests sequentially at no more than four per second. Existing HTTP
  retry/backoff handles throttling and transient server errors. Record original
  response bytes/hashes, query parameters and retrieval timestamps without headers.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Activate SCB access
items.text:
The API has no point-in-time snapshot token. Equal before/after counts cannot prove
that all values remained unchanged during retrieval. The manifest records the
acquisition interval and this limitation; acquisition crossing a UTC date is
rejected. Authenticated production acquisition passed those checks on 2026-10-17.
The API provides current register observations, not historical identity evidence
for a company at an older legal decision date.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Local CSV or Parquet fallback
items.text:
Provide the actual extract and a JSON provenance sidecar. CSV supports UTF-8/BOM
and comma, semicolon or tab delimiters; Parquet uses the existing PyArrow dependency.
No fabricated or bundled example companies are supplied.

| Canonical column | Accepted SCB column | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `organization_number` | `OrgNr` | Ten digits, hyphenated ten digits, or SCB's 12-digit legal-person form beginning `16`; checksum and legal-person number class validated. |
| `registered_legal_name` | `Namn` | Registered legal-unit name. Empty names are held. |
| `primary_sni_code` | `PrimarNaringsgren.naringsgren` | Five digits, optionally dotted; only the primary industry qualifies. |
| `active` | `FtgStat` | `true`/`1` means active; `false`/`0`/`9` means inactive. Missing activity remains unknown. |
| `employee_size_class` | `AnstKl` | SCB class code, not a headcount or an interval label. Missing/zero class is excluded from selection. |
| `legal_form` | `Jurform` | `49` or `AB` qualifies. This extra field is required to exclude non-AB entities and branches. |
| `sni_version` | supplied in metadata if absent from the file | Must explicitly be `2025` to select the initial cohort; there is no silent 2007 crosswalk. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Local CSV or Parquet fallback
items.text:
Headers are case-insensitive and must be unique. See the
[official JE layout](https://www.scb.se/contentassets/8a8eb5c3d45f461ea93482f8e8d4de4f/postbeskrivning-je.pdf)
and [variable descriptions](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/variabelbeskrivning/).
The codebook and selected six industry segments are pinned in
[`policy.json`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/policy.json).

Sidecar structure below is an unfilled configuration template. Replace the marked
values with facts about the real extract. Leave completeness/reviews unset until
actually checked; exploratory import works without declaring a complete population.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "source_id": "scb_company_register",
  "publisher": "SCB",
  "source_url": "https://apiafr.scb.se/v1/juridiskaenheter",
  "as_of_date": "ACTUAL-SNAPSHOT-DATE",
  "fetched_at": "ACTUAL-UTC-TIMESTAMP",
  "source_sha256": "ACTUAL-EXTRACT-BYTE-HASH",
  "row_count": "REPLACE-WITH-INTEGER",
  "sni_version": "2025",
  "primary_sni_codes": ["58290", "62100", "62201", "62202", "62900", "63100"],
  "population_complete": false,
  "terms_url": "https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/avgiftsfria-uppgifter-i-foretagsregistret/",
  "identity_review": null,
  "completeness_review": null,
  "reuse_review": null
}
```

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Local CSV or Parquet fallback
items.text:
Each completed review has the shape
`{"reviewer_id":"ACTUAL-REVIEWER","reviewed_at":"ACTUAL-UTC-TIMESTAMP"}`.
Identity review attests that the names and numbers came from the documented register.
Completeness review attests that the extract covers the whole declared eligible
population across all six primary industries, including all size classes and known
exclusions. A hand-picked list of 50 names is insufficient. Reuse review records
assessment of the actual dataset terms. Dates/timestamps must be ISO values with
explicit UTC timestamps; a population cannot be dated after retrieval.

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py ingest --source file --input /private/companies.csv --metadata /private/companies.metadata.json --output .research/compliance-intelligence/register-snapshot
```

Replace `.csv` with `.parquet` for a Parquet extract. Alternatively set
`COMPLIANCE_COMPANY_FILE` and `COMPLIANCE_COMPANY_METADATA` in the environment.
`ingest --source auto` prefers that configured file; otherwise it uses `SCB_API_KEY`.
If neither input exists, the command exits with an actionable error and creates no
empty dataset. HTTP failures also create no completed snapshot.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Identity enrichment and matching
items.text:
Both acquisition modes accept `--identities /private/identity-evidence.json`.
This optional supplement has `documents`, `companies`, `aliases` and `relationships`
arrays. It supplies verified evidence for foreign parents, historic names, brands,
mergers and dated parent/operator links. A source file path is relative to the
supplement, stays within that directory and has its original-byte `document_hash`
checked before import.

| Supplement collection | Required fields |
| --- | --- |
| `documents` | `document_id`, `path`, `document_hash`, `source_id`, `source_url`, `publisher`, `fetched_at`, `content_type`. |
| `companies` | `registered_legal_name`, `legal_form`, `country_code`, source document ID/locator and a `review`. Swedish identities need `organization_number`; foreign identities need `registry_authority` and `registry_number`, with no Swedish number. Optional SNI/activity/class fields affect eligibility. |
| `aliases` | `company_id`, `alias`, `alias_type`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, source document ID/locator, `review_status=approved` and `review`. Alias types: `brand`, `trading_name`, `historic_legal_name`. |
| `relationships` | `company_id`, `related_company_id`, `relationship_type`, effective dates, source document ID/locator, `review_status=approved` and `review`. Types: `subsidiary_of`, `merged_into`, `branch_of`. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Identity enrichment and matching
items.text:
Swedish IDs are `se:orgnr:<normalized-number>`; foreign IDs are
`<lowercase-country>:<escaped-registry-authority>:<escaped-registry-number>`.
Country means registration country. Registry namespaces and foreign numbers retain
their source values. The supplement is a manually reviewed input, not an automatic
ownership inference engine. Unknown effective dates are retained and cannot prove
historic alias validity. Unreviewed supplements are rejected. An unsupported
foreign entity is not silently manufactured from its Swedish subsidiary's name.

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py resolve --snapshot .research/compliance-intelligence/register-snapshot --number ACTUAL-ORGANIZATION-NUMBER --name "ACTUAL REGISTERED NAME" --on-date YYYY-MM-DD
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py resolve --snapshot .research/compliance-intelligence/register-snapshot --country GB --registry-authority ACTUAL-REGISTRY --registry-number ACTUAL-FOREIGN-NUMBER --subject-role issuer
```

Only a verified exact registry identity can return `status=verified`. A supplied
name must agree with the current name or a documented alias valid on the requested
date. Names alone return candidates needing review. Shared names/brands, conflicting
observations and inconsistent dates are held with reasons and candidate IDs.
Suffixes and diacritics are retained; normalization only applies Unicode NFKC,
case folding and whitespace. Future dates cannot be verified from an older snapshot.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Identity enrichment and matching
items.text:
A legal-name change preserves the Swedish ID. A merger retains predecessor and
successor IDs and a separate relationship. Parent or sibling links are never
followed for identity confirmation or liability attribution. `subject_role=issuer`
is retained separately from company identity and registration country. No case or
sanction attachment is performed by this phase.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Freeze and export
items.text:
```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py build --snapshot .research/compliance-intelligence/register-snapshot --cohort-id se-it-v1 --output .research/compliance-intelligence/se-it-v1
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py verify --bundle .research/compliance-intelligence/se-it-v1
```

The builder requires reviewed source reuse, complete scope and at least 50 verified
eligible Swedish AB legal entities. It orders the known employee classes descending,
then organization numbers ascending. Conflicting register observations or unexpected
malformed rows block freezing because a held entity could change the selection
boundary. Natural-person identifiers and foreign legal persons without local registry
identity are excluded with provenance locators; inconsistent AB/person identifiers
block freezing. Exclusions and size-class boundary counts are reported.

The output is a size-class-based legal-entity sample. It does not establish the
50 largest companies by exact headcount, or represent 50 independent groups.
Qualifying subsidiaries can be selected separately; pure holding firms and foreign
parents do not qualify just because their groups operate in IT.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Freeze and export
items.text:
Each bundle contains `registry.duckdb`, `cohort.csv`, `cohort.json`, `methodology.json`,
`population-manifest.json`, `exclusions.json`, `identity-ambiguities.json`,
`aliases.json`, `relationships.json`, the full normalized `snapshot.json`, original
evidence blobs and `artifact-manifest.json`. The four requested identity/cohort
tables are materialized in `compliance_intelligence`; case/decision tables remain
empty. Original registry SNI/activity/class attributes remain in the full snapshot;
selection attributes remain in `compliance_cohort` and its original exports.

Methodology records actual population date, retrieval interval/limitations, codebook,
policy and code hashes, eligible/excluded counts, duplicate observations, tie-break,
boundary class, freeze time and membership hash. The population manifest binds all
source responses/documents and their request parameters, not just one API page.
The supported builder refuses existing output directories; corrections use a new
snapshot/cohort version. Read-only queries and manifest verification preserve the
original bundle. These hashes detect changes, but are not digital signatures or
protection against someone rewriting both data and manifests with filesystem access.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Freeze and export
items.text:
All output is private. Inside this repo only ignored `.research/` or `tmp/` output
is allowed; public/frontend/warehouse/source roots and configured backup roots are
rejected. An external directory must also be protected by the operator's filesystem
permissions. Raw SCB responses may include non-cohort/personal records and must not
be committed or placed in public R2. No exporter, schedule or deployment publishes
these bundles.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Separate exploratory search
items.text:
```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/cli.py search --snapshot .research/compliance-intelligence/register-snapshot --query "SEARCH TEXT" --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/se-it-v1
```

Search returns registry candidates and optional original-cohort membership. It reads
the entire imported population, including companies outside the selected 50, and
never changes membership. A later register snapshot can be searched while labeling
membership from the original bundle through `--cohort`. Search results do not inherit
cases or sanctions through brands or group links.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-1.md › Remaining activation work
items.text:
Provide the authorized key or actual CSV/Parquet and provenance, inspect the first
real snapshot's conflicts/exclusions, complete source reviews, then build and verify
the real cohort. Confirm actual API behavior under credentials and the population's
coverage before treating the 50 as selected. Existing Phase 0
[source limitations](source-feasibility.md) and [publication controls](risks.md)
still apply. Enforcement ingestion and dashboard construction remain out of scope.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Phase 2 operation and source assessment
items.text:
Implemented and checked on 2026-10-17, Europe/Stockholm. The module collects public
source observations into private storage. It does not determine violations, case
outcomes, party liability, appeals, finality or rankings. The canonical Phase 0
legal tables remain unpopulated by this collector.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Official sources and access
items.text:
| Source | Interface checked | Access observed | Scope and restrictions |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| IMY | [Published sanction index](https://www.imy.se/om-oss/beslut-publikationer-och-remisser/beslut-om-sanktionsavgift/), linked case pages and PDFs | HTTP 200 through the collection client. No documented supported bulk decision API or downloadable decision dataset located in the official pages checked. | Index has year sections 2019–2026. Entries are discovery candidates; GDPR applicability, appeal documents and legal category require review. It is not an exhaustive register. |

| IMY | [Supervision and decisions](https://www.imy.se/tillsyner/) | Official public HTML selection, separate from the implemented sanction index | Describes a selection from 2018 onwards. This broader list is not silently substituted for sanction-index coverage. |

| Konkurrensverket | [Published competition cases](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/konkurrens/tillsyn-arenden-och-beslut/arendelista) | Direct client received HTTP 403. The source was halted. Official browser-indexed content was usable for researching the list and adapter shape. | Selected cases include open investigations, closures, authority acts and court attachments. Live pagination and PDF collection remain unverified because of the access response. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Official sources and access
items.text:
| Konkurrensverket | [Public diary](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/diarium/sok-i-Konkurrensverkets-diarium/) and [search help](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/diarium/sok-i-Konkurrensverkets-diarium/sokhjalp/) | Researched as an alternative official route; no diary adapter or supported bulk API established | Registered cases since 1998 have broader scope than the published selection. Document availability and publication delays remain separate coverage limits. |

No search-engine cache is used as ingestion evidence. Internal browser search
endpoints and alternative hosts are not treated as supported APIs or used to work
around the 403. The KKV adapter is implemented and tested against synthetic HTML;
production response validation is still required after ordinary access is available.

The [IMY robots file](https://www.imy.se/robots.txt) returned HTTP 200 and disallowed
paths matching `/*?query=` and `/*&query=`. The
[Konkurrensverket robots file](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/robots.txt) returned
HTTP 200 with a sitemap and no disallow directives. These observations permit no
inference about document reuse rights or continued future access. Every run checks
robots again. Missing, redirected, non-plain-text or denied robots responses stop
collection. Source and redirect URLs must remain on the configured HTTPS origin.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Reuse and privacy
items.text:
[IMY's reuse policy](https://www.imy.se/om-oss/vart-uppdrag/vidareutnyttjande-av-data/)
says that release and reuse require consideration of each document, including
personal data and secrecy, and identifies decisions as documents normally available
electronically for reuse. It does not grant a blanket open license for the website.

[Konkurrensverket's material policy](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/om-oss/om-webbplatsen/anvanda-och-lanka-till-vart-material/)
permits reproduction subject to conditions. It identifies protected material,
restricts reproduction for sale without permission, requires source/retrieval-date
attribution and recommends links for electronic redistribution. No blanket CC0 or
CC BY license is asserted. Check actual attachment authorship and conditions.

Default retention is a stable official reference, retrieval metadata, exact-byte
SHA-256 and limited extracted candidates. Bodies are processed in memory and are
not persisted. Extracted names, references and evidence fragments stay private.
Nothing is sent to a language model or an external OCR service. A scanned PDF
receives `no_extractable_text_ocr_not_run`; encrypted PDFs are rejected.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Reuse and privacy
items.text:
Optional original-byte retention requires a documented private-copy review JSON
via `--copy-policy`. Each source entry must contain `reviewer_id`, `reviewed_at`
(UTC), its exact `terms_url`, a `rationale` and HTTPS `allowed_prefixes` ending in
`/`. Scope the prefixes to the actual cleared documents. This records the operator's
assessment; it grants no new right and does not approve publication. For example,
the structure is `{"imy": {"reviewer_id": "...", "reviewed_at": "...",
"terms_url": "...", "rationale": "...", "allowed_prefixes": ["..."]}}`.
Fill it with actual reviewed facts; no approval is supplied by this task.

Public source availability does not resolve processing grounds, retention periods,
redaction or publication risk. Raw evidence may contain complainants, employees,
contact details or other personal data. Set the private directory's access and
retention controls before retaining copies. Public R2 and its whole-warehouse
backup must never receive this database or its evidence directory.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Run the pilot
items.text:
Use the existing Python requirements; no dependency was added. The entry point is
[`decision_ingest.py`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/decision_ingest.py).
It reads `.env` through the existing helper and honors `COMPLIANCE_PRIVATE_ROOT`
from [`.env.example`](../../.env.example). Authority collection uses no API key.
SCB credentials remain confined to the Phase 1 register client.

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/decision_ingest.py --source all --root .research/compliance-intelligence/decisions --max-pages 1 --max-records 2 --max-documents 2
```

Bounds apply separately to each source. Requests are serial with at least two
seconds between starts, increased by robots crawl delay. Four attempts use
exponential backoff for network errors, 429 and transient server errors. HTTP
`Retry-After` is honored. A delay exceeding 60 seconds defers the source to a later
run instead of making an early request. HTTP 401/403 halt that source immediately.
There is no proxy rotation, CAPTCHA bypass or automatic alternative-host fallback.
Responses are limited to 25 MiB; timeouts and extraction errors are reported.

The CLI exits 0 for a successful bounded batch, 1 for recorded source failures,
and 2 for configuration or fatal execution errors. A successful small batch does
not mean complete source coverage. INFO logs contain source, document ID and change
state; source bodies, cookies and credentials are omitted from logs.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Run the pilot
items.text:
The original pilot's five fixed resource URLs and baseline hashes are in
[`phase-2-pilot-manifest.json`](phase-2-pilot-manifest.json). To keep that exact URL
sample when the public index changes:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/decision_ingest.py --source imy --root .research/compliance-intelligence/decisions --batch-manifest docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot-manifest.json --max-pages 1 --max-records 2 --max-documents 2
```

Manifest mode follows only listed resources. Newly discovered URLs are recorded
as `deferred_manifest_scope`. Each observation compares its hash to the baseline.
Live responses can change. The HTML contains per-response nonces, and its hashes
changed between pilot runs; no legal correction was inferred.
Reference-only mode reproduces URL membership and comparison, not offline original
bytes. Reproducing extraction offline requires an authorized retained original and
the recorded extractor/dependency version. Never replace a baseline with new bytes
without preserving the earlier manifest.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Storage and update behavior
items.text:
[`ingestion.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/ingestion.sql) runs in a
separate `ingestion.duckdb` under the private root. It uses the existing
Bronze/Silver/Gold layer names without registering a public dbt subject or job.
`private_path`, `relative_file`, canonical JSON and byte hashes reuse Phase 1 and
`lib.rawstore`. The normal rawstore writer targets the public warehouse, so this
collector supplies a private writer and does not change that writer's global root.

| Layer | Contents and grain |
| --- | --- |
| Bronze | One run configuration and report; one fetch row per HTTP attempt; robots observations; immutable content identities per source/URL/hash; current URL pointers and optional private content-addressed blobs. |
| Silver | One extraction per document/version; per-run discovery edges, including parent document, anchor label and deferred/failure state; contextual company mentions with registry candidates. |
| Gold | Per-run ingestion counts and coverage reports in private JSON/Parquet. There are no outcome aggregates or public releases. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Storage and update behavior
items.text:
The acquisition configuration pins the collector code hash, extractor version,
source seeds, bounds, optional copy-policy hash and frozen-cohort membership hash.
Every successfully observed document has URL, authority, exact-byte digest, MIME
type, size, retrieval time and permitted copy reference or stable original URL.
Selected HTTP validators and source HTML/PDF metadata are preserved. Publication
and decision dates are extracted independently with field evidence. Missing or
conflicting values remain null. A source update date stays in source metadata.
IMY's first-page decision template can supply its explicitly labelled `Datum`
only when the expected decision heading and decision-document path are present.

Published pagination links are followed and deduplicated. The IMY sanction index
is currently a single page with year sections. KKV list pagination uses published
page links; if a rendered result range indicates more records but supplies no
usable links, the report records `pagination_links_missing`. An unrecognized
layout fails extraction and requires a source-layout check. Repeated URLs do not
loop. Duplicate bytes share one blob when copies are
retained; distinct source URLs keep distinct document identities and provenance.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Storage and update behavior
items.text:
Re-running the same root retains previous document versions and records new fetches.
ETag/Last-Modified requests use 304 only when an extraction for the current parser
is available. Otherwise the body is fetched again. Same URL/hash/parser produces
one extraction; changed bytes or parser code produce new evidence or extraction
versions. A new byte version records the previous document ID. Reverted content
also retains its fetch history. Rights/privacy review state stays unapproved.

Words concerning corrections or replacement, and labelled links to replacement
documents, create review candidates. A changed hash is not a confirmed corrected
decision; a source mention of an appeal is not a verified appeal outcome. Human
review must establish any `supersedes`, appeal or finality relationship later.
This phase does not merge dockets, create legal decisions, interpret amounts or
populate sanctioned-party links. Multiple docket references remain a candidate
set with a null singular reference.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Expand to the frozen cohort
items.text:
A verified real 50-company cohort became available on 2026-10-17. The broader IMY
run now has 50 dated member observations against collected mentions; KKV remains
blocked. The original pilot's `not_measured_registry_missing` status is historical.
See [completion](completion.md) for the current batch and unknown coverage limits.

When the Phase 1 frozen bundle exists and verifies, add it to a broader bounded
publication scan. Increase these bounds deliberately after inspecting the pilot:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/decision_ingest.py --source all --root .research/compliance-intelligence/decisions --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/YOUR_FROZEN_COHORT --max-pages 100 --max-records 500 --max-documents 1000
```

Use a fresh scan without `--batch-manifest` to discover beyond the fixed pilot.
The bundle is read and hash-verified without changing sample membership. A search
for each member is an assessment against collected publication mentions, not an
automated assertion of no cases. Coverage remains partial even at the end of a
selected website list. A missing mention is not a legal clearance.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Expand to the frozen cohort
items.text:
Organization numbers use the existing legal-entity validation and exact registry
resolver. Name candidates use the registry's aliases and effective dates. Names
and numbers are not paired from text proximity. With no document decision date,
the snapshot date is only a search hint and automatic confirmation is withheld.
All mentions have `contextual_mention`/`context_only` scope and require review.
The resolver does not follow parents, subsidiaries or mergers. Neither an issuer
nor a foreign parent receives another entity's case. A registry search country's
value does not determine the document subject's registration country.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-2.md › Handoff
items.text:
1. Supply and freeze the verified Phase 1 cohort using the existing SCB or local
   register workflow. Preserve its original population, date and membership hash.
2. Establish ordinary permitted KKV access or an official supplied extract. Recheck
   robots/terms and validate real list, pagination and attachment layouts before
   expanding. Do not treat the synthetic adapter tests as production verification.
3. Inspect private pilot failures, date evidence and candidate names. Add source
   layout fixtures when real templates differ. Record unresolved extraction and
   scan/OCR gaps with their evidence versions.
4. Run the larger bounded scan with the verified cohort and inspect per-source
   failures, deferred discoveries and member candidate sets. Keep unknown source
   denominators and search coverage as null.
5. A later interpretation phase may review identities, classify distinct legal
   events and link appeals/corrections with evidence. Privacy, reuse and publication
   approvals must bind to exact evidence versions before any public export.

No rankings, dashboard, homepage or intro-animation change is part of this phase.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3-validation.md › Phase 3 validation and review coverage
items.text:
Historical validation run. The later authenticated population, frozen cohort and expanded evidence batch are recorded in [current completion](completion.md). Counts and input-status statements below refer to this report's original run.

Checked 2026-10-17, Europe/Stockholm. The aggregate machine-readable result is
[`phase-3-summary.json`](phase-3-summary.json). UTC timestamps fall on the preceding
calendar date because the pilot ran shortly after local midnight.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3-validation.md › Existing evidence and real pilot
items.text:
The private Phase 2 database contained 14 byte-version identities and five current
source references. Two of those references were decision PDFs; no original-body
copy had been retained. Phase 3 read this database and re-fetched only those two
existing PDF references with robots/access checks. Both original SHA-256 values

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3-validation.md › Checks and adversarial cases
items.text:
- Similar names, contradictory organization numbers and unique brand aliases
  cannot verify another legal operator. Exact legal-name-only identity needs a
  separate authorized human review.
- Swedish thousands/million/billion units, decimal commas and SEK/EUR remain
  explicit. Wrong units, missing currency, negative/grouped ambiguous amounts and
  fabricated LLM amounts fail or abstain.
- Appeals and annulments retain the original order and amount. A pending reversal
  blocks publication; a reviewed annulment has no inferred effective fine. A
  reversal of a reversal becomes unknown until its appellate chain is resolved.
- Several decisions on a docket and several judgments in one file remain distinct.
  Ambiguous follow-up targets and possible duplicate byte representations are held.
- LLM extra approval fields, fabricated pages/quotes, unsupported finality and
  document prompt injections cannot approve records. Allegations and proposed fines
  do not become regulatory findings through the deterministic pattern match.
- Human/service roles, explicit attestation, preparer independence, separate
  publication reviewer, privacy/reuse clearance, review expiry and rejection are
  enforced. Reapproval needs a new publication approval.
- Changed source versions/context, altered candidate/action data, timezone changes,
  stale releases and rehashed Gold value substitutions cannot bypass verification.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3-validation.md › Handoff
items.text:
Provide actual verified registry input, re-extract with `--registry`, inspect each
record with `show`, and create scoped corrections through `import-proposal` where
needed. Supply authorized human reviewer identities and record their actual
decisions. Complete current appeal/finality searches before approving that status.
Validate each staged release again before future public promotion. Commands,
trust boundaries and remaining template limits are in [Phase 3 operation](phase-3.md).

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Phase 3: evidence extraction and review
items.text:
Implemented 2026-10-17. The Phase 2 private ingestion database now supports
evidence-bound extraction candidates, docket grouping, decision links, human review,
reverification and approved Gold export. There is no public deployment or automatic
approval. Current results are in [the validation report](phase-3-validation.md) and
the aggregated [coverage and review summary](phase-3-summary.json).

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Read and extract existing evidence
items.text:
The collector reuses the canonical registry resolver, original SHA-256 identities,
private-path restrictions and Bronze/Silver source records. The current pilot has
five source references, including two decision PDFs. It retained no original-body
copies. A reference alone cannot support new full-document extraction offline.

The default extraction command reads only permitted retained originals. Missing
originals become held observations; it does not invent text from URLs or previous
metadata. To re-read the existing reference-only PDFs, explicitly enable reference
refresh. Every response must match the exact Phase 2 document hash. Changed bytes
are held for Phase 2 reingestion and a new document identity.

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot extract --refresh-references --max-documents 2
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot summary
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot queue
```

The CLI honors `COMPLIANCE_PRIVATE_ROOT` from the existing `.env.example` when
`--root` is omitted. Add `--registry PATH_TO_VERIFIED_PHASE_1_SNAPSHOT_OR_BUNDLE`
to `extract` or `import-proposal` once actual registry evidence is available.
The snapshot's hashes are verified and its identity status is preserved.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Read and extract existing evidence
items.text:
Reference refresh reuses Phase 2's same-origin HTTPS client, robots checks,
serial pacing, bounded retries and access denials. It reads only existing document
references, retains no new original copies, and records fetch/policy observations
in the review audit. A hash mismatch needs a new Bronze version, not an exception
to evidence validation. No court requests, alternate-host bypass or external OCR
service is used.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Extraction contract
items.text:
[`legal_extraction.py`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/legal_extraction.py)
provides the strict JSON Schema and deterministic extractor. Existing installed
`pypdf`, `jsonschema`, DuckDB and PyArrow are reused; no dependency was added.

| Claim | Extraction and uncertainty rule |

| --- | --- |

| `authority` | Issuing-body evidence in the first scoped page's header. The hosting authority is separately preserved as `source_publisher`; a court PDF hosted by IMY does not become an IMY judgment. Unsupported or conflicting issuers stay null. |

| `case_number` | Literal Swedish authority/court references. Multiple distinct references stay uncertain until a reviewer scopes the act. Docket grouping uses normalized issuer plus reference, never company or group name. |

| `legal_entity`, `organization_number` | Literal operative subject and valid legal-person number when present. Missing numbers stay null. Context mentions are not paired into a legal operator from proximity. |

| `case_type`, `legal_basis` | Document-supported category and literal law/regulation references. Current deterministic rules cover GDPR, competition and public procurement terminology; other supported categories require documented proposals or abstention. |

| `decision_date`, `publication_date` | Independently labelled dates with exact excerpts. Conflicts remain null; URL year, update date and retrieval date cannot fill them. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Extraction contract
items.text:
| `original_outcome` | Supported outcome candidate, separate from current status. Administrative sanctions, regulatory findings, dismissal, no finding, procedural acts and judgments remain distinct. Criminal conviction requires separate explicit evidence and a criminal forum; a fine does not imply conviction. |

| `monetary_sanction` | Decimal amount string, explicit currency and sanction type. The current parser handles administrative fines. It does not classify damages, costs or corporate/coercive fines as administrative sanctions. |

| `appeal_information` | `unknown`, `instructions_only`, `filed`, `pending` or `decided`, with supporting excerpts. Instructions explain how to appeal; they do not establish that an appeal was filed. |

| `status` | Proposed status of the scoped act. Conflicting issue/history/finality statements abstain to unknown. Dispositions affecting another act belong in a directed decision link. |

| `party_role`, `attribution_scope` | Direct liability requires the named subject of the operative clause. An issuer or contextual mention cannot receive another entity's sanction. Parent, subsidiary and merger links are not traversed. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Extraction contract
items.text:
Swedish grouping spaces, decimal commas, `miljon/miljoner`, `miljarder`, `tkr`,
`mkr` and `mnkr` are parsed using Decimal. Examples of supported units are
`1,8 miljoner kronor` and `35 000 euro`. Missing currencies/units, negative amounts,
ambiguous dotted/grouped decimals and conflicting currency abbreviations abstain
or fail proposal validation. Amounts remain at the decision grain.

Each known claim has `evidence`: physical PDF page number, `start`, `end` character
offsets and a literal `quote`. Offsets address normalized page text: whitespace is
collapsed and soft hyphens are removed. They are not byte offsets or printed court
page labels. Imports check every excerpt against a freshly hash-verified original.
The extractor version hashes its code and pypdf version. Unsupported text layouts,
encrypted PDFs, empty text and scans require review; no OCR is invented.

One proposal represents one scoped act and one directly attributable primary legal
entity. Several operative parties or ambiguous joint liability stay held. A document
containing several judgments needs separate `decision_slot` values and scoped page
sets, with field-specific offsets for each act. The whole-document extraction
abstains on conflicting dates or parties. It does not split an amount across parties.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Optional structured LLM assistance
items.text:
Deterministic extraction is the default. There are no provider calls, API keys,
model-generated summaries or automatic document uploads in this implementation.
An operator can supply a manual or LLM-assisted proposal through the same strict
validation boundary:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py schema
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT import-proposal --proposal PRIVATE_PROPOSAL.json --original-file MATCHING_ORIGINAL.pdf --registry VERIFIED_REGISTRY --prepared-by PREPARER_ID
```

Use `--refresh-references` instead of `--original-file` for a reference-only source.
The imported file must identify an existing Bronze document. The CLI verifies its
original hash before checking excerpts. `document_pages()` exposes the normalized
page representation to a trusted local model integration; the importer never accepts
LLM-supplied text as the evidence corpus. Any external model processing needs a
separate assessment of data egress, privacy and source terms. No such clearance is
asserted here.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Optional structured LLM assistance
items.text:
The `schema` command outputs JSON Schema and instructions for treating document
text as untrusted data. Proposals must declare producer kind, version and model
when LLM-assisted. Unknowns are `null`, `unknown` or empty arrays. Additional keys,
including approval fields, are rejected. Fabricated excerpts, page numbers, amounts,
unsupported status claims and allegation-to-finding substitutions fail validation.
Literal evidence is necessary but cannot prove semantic truth: quoted older orders,
multi-column extraction and hostile text can still mislead. Human review remains
mandatory for every public record, including every negative finding about a company.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Cases, links and status
items.text:
Case groups use an issuer namespace and normalized docket. An authority decision
and its court appeal remain separate cases. A decision identity uses original-byte
hash plus decision slot; identical copies do not become new decisions. Separate
acts on one docket remain separate decisions. Different byte representations with
the same docket/date/party/outcome are held as possible duplicates, not summed.

Directed links point from a later act to the earlier act's exact record version:
`appeal_of`, `upholds`, `modifies`, `annuls`, `supersedes`, `remands`, `related_to`
and `duplicate_of`. Link evidence must name the target docket and support the
disposition. Chronology, target identity and cycles are checked. Exact unambiguous
references can produce deterministic link candidates. Several possible judgments
on the referenced docket create pending links and hold all affected decisions.
An explicit scoped proposal resolves those targets before legal approval.

Only a current, legally reviewed follow-up can affect the earlier act's derived
status. Unreviewed/stale links, competing lifecycle effects or an additional
appellate stage produce unknown status and hold publication. The current conservative
graph reducer requires a reviewer to resolve complex appellate chains explicitly;
it does not infer that the last timestamp restores or cancels a sanction.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Cases, links and status
items.text:
| Status | Meaning in this module |
| --- | --- |
| `investigation` | Supported investigation stage; no finding implied. |
| `alleged` | Supported allegation/claim stage; no finding implied. |
| `decided` | A documented act has been issued; outcome and finality remain separate. |
| `appealed` | An actual appeal is supported, distinct from appeal instructions. |
| `final` | Explicit finality evidence has been reviewed; age alone is insufficient. |
| `modified` | A reviewed subsequent act changes, supersedes or remands the targeted act. |
| `annulled` | A reviewed subsequent act annuls the targeted act. |
| `unknown` | Insufficient, conflicting, stale or unresolved evidence. |

Original outcome, original amount and original stage are retained. Current status
and finality are separate: an annulment or modification may have unknown or confirmed
finality. An upheld order does not automatically become final. Gold includes
subsequent decision source references supporting its current-status projection.
Effective monetary sanction remains null for non-final, modified, annulled or
uncertain states. It is not populated by overwriting the original amount.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Cases, links and status
items.text:
[Sveriges Domstolar's appeal guidance](https://www.domstol.se/hogsta-domstolen/amnen/missnojd-med-dom-eller-handlaggning/overklaga-en-dom/overklaga-till-kammarratten/att-overklaga-till-kammarratten/)
describes appeals and finality. Courts can supply
[finality certificates](https://www.domstol.se/stockholms-tingsratt/om-tingsratten/ta-del-av-allman-handling-och-arkivinformation/bestallningsformular-for-intyg-om-laga-kraft-ej-skilsmassa/).
This implementation does not determine finality by calculating statutory deadlines
or treat absence of an appeal in the collected selection as proof.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Human review
items.text:
The private `queue` command shows record/context hashes, identity ambiguity,
completeness, approval states and publication blockers. Inspect the concrete
evidence and proposed public projection before reviewing:

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT show --record-hash RECORD_HASH
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT review --request PRIVATE_REVIEW_REQUEST.json --reviewers PRIVATE_REVIEWER_ROSTER.json
```

`show` labels its projection `preview_not_approved`. Queue/show output contains
private evidence and reviewer details; do not publish it or copy it to public logs.

The operator-maintained roster maps real reviewer IDs to `kind: human` and a list
of permitted roles: `identity`, `legal`, `privacy`, `publication`. Service principals
are refused. A request must contain exact `record_hash`, current `context_hash`,
`review_kind`, `disposition` (`approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`), `reviewer_id`,
`rationale`, `human_attestation: true` and `examined_evidence: true`.

Additional requirements for approval:

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Human review
items.text:
- Identity: exact verified register number/name or a unique, time-valid exact
  registered legal name checked by the human reviewer. Brand-only, conflicting,
  foreign-parent and ambiguous matches remain held.
- Legal: complete supported legal fields and resolved lifecycle targets;
  explicit `verified_at` UTC and `reverify_by` date. Court follow-ups can receive
  legal review without company attribution, but cannot become company Gold rows
  without separately verified direct identity/scope.
- Privacy: both `privacy_cleared: true` and `reuse_cleared: true` for the actual
  projection, source excerpts and dependency evidence.
- Publication: all prerequisite approvals must be current. The reviewer must
  differ from the preparer and identity/legal/privacy approving reviewers.

No actual reviewer or approval is supplied in this task. The assistant did not
approve the real candidates. The roster/request files are trusted local operator
inputs protected by filesystem permissions, not an authentication service. Before
remote or multi-user deployment, authenticate principals and protect the roster
and database server-side. A client-supplied reviewer name is insufficient there.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Human review
items.text:
Every action is append-only through the application and records its exact evidence
context. Changes to source versions, record versions, registry versions, lifecycle
dependencies or incoming legal reviews invalidate applicable approvals. New
prerequisite reviews require a later publication approval; a rejection followed
by reapproval cannot revive an older publication approval automatically.

Reverification policy: at most 30 days for open, appealed, uncertain or non-final
records and 90 days for explicitly final records. These are project freshness
limits, not legal deadlines. Future verification times and excessive intervals are
rejected. Expired legal review blocks export until a new human legal review and
publication approval.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Audit, Gold and release validation
items.text:
[`legal_review.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/legal_review.sql) adds
private `review` tables to `ingestion.duckdb`. Candidate record versions and review
actions are retained. The audit chain binds sequence, UTC time, event payload and
previous hash. Verification checks candidate hashes and review-action payloads
against their audit entries. It is tamper-evident under trusted storage, not an
externally anchored signature system; an administrator able to rewrite the whole
database and chain is outside that guarantee.

```sh
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT verify-audit
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT export-gold --output PRIVATE_NEW_RELEASE_DIRECTORY
python -X utf8 platform/compliance_intelligence/review_cli.py --root PRIVATE_ROOT validate-release --bundle PRIVATE_NEW_RELEASE_DIRECTORY
```

Gold export checks every gate again and emits only an allowlisted public projection.
It omits raw excerpts, original PDFs, reviewer identities, rationale, model metadata
and private paths. JSON, optional nonempty Parquet, release metadata and integrity
manifest are staged in a new private directory. Zero eligible records produces an
empty JSON dataset and manifest, not fabricated rows.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Audit, Gold and release validation
items.text:
`validate-release` rechecks approval freshness, current source/graph context, exact
projection values, unique decisions and JSON/Parquet agreement. Even a rehashed
bundle cannot substitute a new amount under an approved record hash. Run it against
the live private review database immediately before any future public promotion.
An older bundle is an as-of snapshot, not a permanent permission to serve stale
records. Revocation/expiry requires removal from any future current release.

This phase adds no public dbt subject, warehouse migration, R2 group or scheduled
publisher. Phase 0 legal-domain contracts remain separate from candidate observations;
no parser inserts unreviewed decisions or sanctioned-party links there. Public
delivery integration must preserve these gates and the private storage boundary.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-3.md › Remaining work
items.text:
The real frozen SCB cohort was supplied and 55 unique PDF byte versions were
checked on 2026-10-17. There are 53 private candidates and two textless documents
held for OCR; none has human approval. Inspect and correct the scoped proposals in
the [current review packet](completion.md). Current register identity cannot prove
a historical legal name without dated evidence. Establish ordinary
KKV access before expanding its document coverage. Real authorized human reviewers
must resolve legal-status ambiguity, party scope and current appeal evidence before
any approval. Broader court templates, unsupported remedies, OCR and complex
multi-party/appellate chains remain held until supported and reviewed.

No rankings, dashboard, homepage or intro-animation changes are included.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Compliance analytics methodology
items.text:
Version 1, checked 2026-10-17. These metrics describe reviewed public evidence for
a fixed sample of Swedish IT legal entities. They measure the approved records
represented in a release. They do not estimate all violations, a company's ethics
or its probability of receiving a future sanction.

At the implementation baseline on 2026-10-17, no actual 50-company cohort or
human-approved legal outcomes were available in this workspace and no real company
benchmark had been produced. Later releases declare their own approval and coverage
metadata. Synthetic regression fixtures must be distinguished from measured results.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Population and dates
items.text:
The population and selection rule are fixed by [Phase 1](phase-1.md). Eligible
active Swedish limited companies must have a primary SNI 2025 code in 58290,
62100, 62201, 62202, 62900 or 63100. Selection takes 50 companies by descending
employee size class, then organization number within a class. This orders size
classes; it does not establish the largest 50 companies by exact employment.
Only a complete, source-reviewed register population can produce the frozen sample.

Every analytical bundle includes the cohort ID, snapshot date, membership hash,
selection order, eligible codes and selection limitations. Filtering never changes
the original membership. Industry and employee-class filters select a subset of
that membership. No replacement companies are drawn.

The default window starts 2018-05-25 and ends at the register snapshot date.
Explicit windows can differ. Dates are inclusive and select the originating
approved decision's decision date. Publication dates remain separate and do not
substitute for decision dates. `--year` intersects an explicit date window.
Follow-up decisions remain attached even when dated outside the window. Current
status means status known in the approved Gold snapshot, not status reconstructed
at the window end. `status_snapshot_at` records that distinction. Historical
point-in-time legal status is not inferred from a later release.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Population and dates
items.text:
Authority and case-category filters apply to the originating decision. Native
court issuers, docket IDs and dates remain visible in decision facts and coverage.
Status filters use the latest supported sanction act in the approved linked chain.
Changing a filter produces another versioned bundle with its own context.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Unit of observation and approval
items.text:
All decision facts come from Phase 3 Gold records, validated again against the
current private review store. An exact reviewed legal entity and direct attribution
are required. Expired, withdrawn or stale approvals prevent reuse of an old release.
Original documents and private candidates supply validation evidence; they never
add unapproved company findings to these metrics.

An authority/docket identifies a native case. Multiple separate orders within that
case remain distinct acts. Explicit approved appeal, upholding, modification,
annulment, remittal and supersession links identify one sanction lineage across
authorities and courts. A related-case link alone does not merge sanctions.
Ambiguous multi-origin appeals, branching obligations, cycles and cross-company
liability links stop the build. A later document date alone cannot resolve them.

The case fact has one row per legal entity and originating native case ID. The
decision fact has one row per approved decision record ID, retaining native and
originating IDs. Confirmation flags occur only on the originating row of each
sanction lineage. Two separate orders on a docket can therefore produce one case,
two sanctions and several documents without counting an appeal as a new sanction.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Metric definitions
items.text:
| Metric | Definition within the selected approved evidence |

| --- | --- |

| Confirmed administrative sanctions | One per explicit sanction lineage whose operative approved act is an administrative sanction against the direct sanctioned party, with current status decided, appealed or final. Alleged, investigation, unknown, unresolved modified and annulled states are excluded. |

| Total final monetary sanctions | Sum of approved operative administrative fine amounts with explicit finality, separately for each native currency. A modified order needs a separately approved replacement act and amount. An annulled or unresolved modified order contributes no final amount. |

| GDPR sanctions | Confirmed administrative sanction lineages categorized as data protection with an explicit GDPR, dataskyddsförordningen or 2016/679 legal basis. |

| Competition law sanctions | Confirmed administrative sanction lineages categorized as competition with an explicit konkurrenslagen or 2008:579 legal basis. |

| Cases under appeal | Distinct originating native cases with current appealed status or a supported pending/filed appeal that has not been resolved by a substantive follow-up. |

| Modified / annulled decisions | Separate counts of approved decision records with the respective current known status. These counts describe records and must not be added to sanction counts. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Metric definitions
items.text:
| Reviewed source documents | Distinct original document hashes represented by selected approved decisions and their approved status dependencies. Multiple decision slots or URLs for identical bytes count once per summary. |

| Criminal convictions | Currently null with an explicit unmeasured status; see legal scope below. |

Original amounts remain in `fact_compliance_amounts` with `amount_kind=original`
for traceability. Only `final_effective` rows contribute to final totals. Adding
both kinds would double-count the same obligation. SEK and EUR remain separate;
`conversion_method=none_native_currency`. There is no exchange rate, inferred
conversion or total combining currencies. Other currencies and remedy types are
held until their upstream evidence contract is supported.

An issued administrative fine may be under appeal. Its count and its non-final
amount must be read separately. Original findings are preserved when a decision is
subsequently modified or annulled; the original amount does not silently become a
current final liability. IMY explains that GDPR sanction amounts depend on factors
including turnover and the circumstances of the infringement. [IMY supervision outcomes](https://www.imy.se/om-oss/vart-uppdrag/sa-arbetar-vi-med-tillsyn/vad-kan-tillsynen-leda-till)

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Metric definitions
items.text:
KKV's decision-making powers and the decision forum changed in March 2021. A
historical dataset must retain the actual issuer and court history; it must not
relabel older court decisions as newly issued KKV sanctions. Its fine calculation
also depends on case-specific circumstances and turnover. [KKV competition fines](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/konkurrens/tillsyn-arenden-och-beslut/sanktioner/konkurrensskadeavgift/)

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Criminal-law scope
items.text:
A Swedish företagsbot must not be relabeled as a criminal conviction of the legal
entity. Corporate fines and a natural person's criminal responsibility require
separate legal treatment. [Swedish Prosecution Authority glossary](https://www.aklagare.se/ordlista/),
[current Swedish Criminal Code](https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/brottsbalk-1962700_sfs-1962-700/)

The current Gold contract supports Swedish administrative/court sources without
a reviewed jurisdiction-specific legal-person conviction scope. Consequently
`criminal_convictions` is null and
`criminal_metric_status=not_measured_separate_legal_entity_criminal_scope_required`.
An incoming criminal conviction/acquittal record is held for a separate scope
contract. A future legally appropriate conviction metric requires
an explicit upstream jurisdiction, legal-person defendant, outcome and finality
contract, its source adapter and human legal/publication approval. A foreign parent,
brand, director's conviction or reference to a corporate fine cannot supply that
missing contract. This metric is unavailable, not zero.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Entity and corporate-group views
items.text:
The default view describes individual legal entities by canonical ID. Corporate
groups aggregate only the selected cohort members linked through reviewed
`subsidiary_of` relationships valid at the declared `group_as_of` date. The date
must not exceed the identity snapshot. Unknown start dates and cyclic structures
stop grouping. Merger history, brands, branches and similar names do not imply
group membership.

A foreign parent may label a group if its identity and relationship are documented.
The parent receives no attributed sanction in the facts. Companies outside the
frozen cohort contribute neither sanctions nor employees. Group figures are
therefore cohort-member aggregates, not complete consolidated group exposure.
Industry/size filters apply to members before grouping, and the output lists their
IDs and count. Legal facts retain the original defendant regardless of view.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Size and financial metadata
items.text:
Use the register's dated employee size classes as intervals. SCB distinguishes
legal units from workplaces and publishes employment in classes for the register;
an interval must not be presented as an exact headcount. [SCB variable descriptions](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/variabelbeskrivning/)

For count N and employee bounds L and U, exploratory sanctions per 1,000 employees
have bounds `1,000*N/U` and `1,000*N/L`. Final monetary amounts use the same formula
separately per currency. With L=0, both bounds are null. An open upper employee
class yields a null lower rate bound; the finite upper rate bound is retained.
No midpoint or invented precise employment is used. Group denominators sum only
selected member bounds and do not assume consolidated employment is known.

These intervals are arithmetic bounds for the snapshot, not statistical confidence
intervals. Current company size may differ from employment during the decision
period. Employees are not the number of affected people, processing activities,
transactions, relevant market sales or legal obligations. Enforcement selection,
publication practices, industry and case severity differ. The ratios cannot be
read as violations per employee, causal effects or comparative compliance quality.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Size and financial metadata
items.text:
No verified revenue or financial statements are available through the current
registry contract. This phase adds no revenue-adjusted metric. Adding financial
normalization requires approved, sourced, dated entity-level values, native
currency, accounting-period and consolidation scope; group revenue must not be
paired silently with one subsidiary's fine.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Missingness, coverage and comparisons
items.text:
Companies with no selected approved decision have `metric_status=not_assessed`,
null sanction/appeal/outcome metrics and no ranking row. Their represented document
and decision counts are zero. A company with approved evidence can have zero
confirmed sanctions within that evidence, for example after an annulment. Neither
case establishes an absence of violations. An empty final-amount map means no
qualifying amount in the approved records, not an established zero financial risk.

Coverage has one cell per authority/year/period role. IMY and KKV receive explicit
cells for every requested year, including empty years. Courts and follow-up years
appear when represented. Follow-ups outside the requested window have
`period_role=subsequent_context`, including follow-ups in the same calendar year.
Document counts are distinct within each cell; a document covering several
companies or periods is not additive across summaries/cells.

Field completeness counts known values among these nine fields for approved
decision rows: record hash, authority, company ID, decision date, publication date,
legal basis, case category, original outcome and finality. Null, unknown and empty
legal-basis lists are missing. With no rows the fraction is null. This measures
field availability in approved rows only. Status-reference documents without an
independently published decision row contribute to document counts, not field counts.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Missingness, coverage and comparisons
items.text:
The number of all relevant authority publications and the number of completed
company/source searches are not established by the current pilot. Population and
search-coverage denominators and fractions remain null. An empty year is not a
completed negative search. Operational collection status comes from the Phase 3
coverage report and remains separate from approved-record field completeness.

`mart_compliance_rankings` supplies separate descending dense ranks for observed
administrative, GDPR and competition counts and final amounts per currency.
KKV and combined-source rankings are currently disabled because reliable KKV
collection is unavailable. The ranking mart is populated only for an explicitly
IMY-scoped analysis with no competition category. The explorer requires that same
authority filter before enabling metric sorting or ranks. Individual approved
evidence remains inspectable. An IMY-only observation does not turn missing
competition coverage into zero competition sanctions.
It records the comparison count and its observation-only basis. Fewer than two
assessed entities gives a null rank; unassessed entities are excluded. These are
transparent orderings of the selected evidence. There is no combined score,
severity weighting, criminality scale, ethics scale, population percentile or
ranking based on the employee intervals. Unequal and unknown coverage limits
comparisons even where an ordinal value can be computed.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-methodology.md › Missingness, coverage and comparisons
items.text:
Consumers must present the cohort definition, date/status snapshot, filters,
coverage limitations and warnings alongside any result. The CLI returns this
context with query results. A future public page must display these conditions
before comparative values and link to this methodology.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4-validation.md › Delivered scope
items.text:
All six requested analytical datasets have typed private DuckDB schemas, JSON and
Parquet exports. The build uses only live-validated approved Gold and a frozen,
verified 50-company cohort. It implements separate administrative/GDPR/competition
counts, final native-currency amounts, appeal and modified/annulled counts,
reviewed-document counts, authority/year coverage, requested filters, dated group
aggregation and exploratory employee-interval normalization. Separate observed
metric ranks carry comparison counts and coverage limitations; no universal score
is implemented.

The criminal metric is explicitly null/unmeasured because the current Swedish Gold
contract has no legally cleared legal-person criminal-conviction scope. Corporate
fines and administrative sanctions cannot fill it. No verified revenue data exist,
so normalization uses documented employee class bounds only. These limits are
explained in the [public methodology](phase-4-methodology.md).
