items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Phase 4 operations
items.text:
Implemented 2026-10-17. The entry point is
[`analytics.py`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.py), with typed
tables in [`analytics.sql`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.sql).
It uses the existing DuckDB, Parquet, canonical JSON and sealed-directory helpers.
No additional dependency, public warehouse migration, scheduled ingestion,
dashboard, R2 upload or frontend change is introduced.

Read the [public methodology](phase-4-methodology.md) before using any comparative
values. Current inputs are not ready: the real register/cohort is missing and the
pilot has zero human-approved Gold records. Commands below use illustrative path
names for inputs that must first be created through the existing gated workflows.
Do not create fake records to satisfy these paths.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Inputs and commands
items.text:
1. Acquire a real SCB or permitted CSV/Parquet register and freeze the 50-company
   cohort using [Phase 1](phase-1.md). Preserve that bundle and its identity evidence.
2. Complete source evidence, identity/legal/privacy and independent publication
   review in [Phase 3](phase-3.md). Export an approved sealed Gold release. Reviews
   must still be fresh; source and identity dependencies must remain unchanged.
3. Check collection/readiness without generating company metrics:

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.py status --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot
```

Build into a new private directory. Existing output directories are never replaced:

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.py build --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --release .research/compliance-intelligence/approved-gold --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort --output .research/compliance-intelligence/analytics-release --year 2025 --authority Integritetsskyddsmyndigheten --category data_protection --scope legal_entity
```

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Inputs and commands
items.text:
Other filters are repeatable `--authority`, `--category`, `--status`, `--industry`
(eligible primary SNI code) and `--size-class` (SCB class code); inclusive
`--date-from`, `--date-to`; `--scope corporate_group` and `--group-as-of`.
Omitted categorical filters include all values. Invalid enum values, dates or
future group dates fail explicitly. Year and date filters intersect. See the
methodology for originating-authority and originating-decision-date semantics.

The build revalidates Gold and the frozen cohort before deriving metrics. It then
checks selected decisions and status dependencies against the exact original
document SHA-256 and every supported claim's precise normalized page excerpt.
This is a reconciliation check, not a new extraction or approval step. Changes to
source bytes, evidence or current approvals hold the build without a completed
output. Unapproved candidates are never included in analytical facts.

Retained permitted originals are read privately. Reference-only evidence cannot
be reconciled offline. Use `--refresh-references` only when permitted fresh source
access is appropriate. This reuses the source policy/robots, host, rate, retry and
audit controls from Phase 2/3 and requires the original hash to match. Restricted
or changed originals cause a hold; this flag cannot override source restrictions.
No unrestricted copy of a reference-only document is written into the bundle.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Inputs and commands
items.text:
Validate before delivery or query, with the live review store still available:

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.py validate --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --release .research/compliance-intelligence/approved-gold --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort --bundle .research/compliance-intelligence/analytics-release
python platform/compliance_intelligence/analytics.py query --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --release .research/compliance-intelligence/approved-gold --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort --bundle .research/compliance-intelligence/analytics-release --table mart_compliance_company_summary
```

Validation checks sealed files and current Gold/cohort eligibility, recomputes all
six projections, checks methodology and code versions, compares exact JSON rows
with SQL and checks Parquet against SQL in both directions. A resealed changed
metric does not pass. Query performs this validation and returns `{context, rows}`.
Withdrawal or expiry invalidates existing analytics; regenerate only after the
reviewed release is valid again. CLI failures return exit code 2 with a bounded
error code. Private source bodies are excluded from errors. Directly opening exported
files bypasses live validation, so public delivery must use this validation gate.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Storage and reproducibility
items.text:
The build creates the six required tables under `gold` in an isolated
`analytics.duckdb`, plus typed Zstandard Parquet and canonical JSON for each table,
including empty tables. `methodology.json` contains input manifest/membership
hashes, code hash, row counts and canonical dataset hashes. `cohort-definition.json`
and `reconciliation.json` preserve the cohort context and original-document checks.
The artifact manifest binds the actual files.

Canonical row hashes are stable for identical approved inputs, filters and code.
Physical DuckDB/Parquet bytes and creation timestamps are not claimed to be
byte-identical across executions. The code hash binds this transform and its SQL;
the Gold and cohort manifests bind the upstream versions. Python package versions
remain those of the existing project environment, not a new hermetic runtime.

These are private release candidates under `.research/` or `tmp/`. Do not copy the
private evidence database or use the existing whole-warehouse R2 backup path.
There is no automatic public promotion. A future publisher must revalidate inputs,
carry methodology/coverage alongside metrics, apply the existing public projection
rules and handle withdrawal/replacement of published artifacts.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-4.md › Next implementation handoff
items.text:
Once authorized register data and human reviews exist, freeze and verify the real
50 members, build the selected approved release, reconcile its originals and run
`validate`. Inspect currency-separated totals and review-status lifecycle links
against the corresponding official publications before public delivery. Record
the real authority-publication regression checks in the validation report.

Keep KKV's blocked access as missing coverage until permitted access works. Do not
replace it with inferred zeros. Expand financial metadata or criminal-law scope
only through separately evidenced upstream contracts and human legal approval.
No score, public dashboard or broader ingestion is part of this change.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Phase 5 explorer and research export
items.text:
Implemented 2026-10-17. Open `#compliance` from the portfolio's Projects menu.
The explorer has four persistent hash routes, with filters in the query string:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `#compliance` | Cohort observations, approved decisions by issuer, timeline, final amount distribution and full-release source coverage. |
| `#compliance-rankings` | The frozen 50-member table, separate administrative-count and currency-specific monetary comparisons, legal identities and expandable evidence. |
| `#compliance-company?company=CANONICAL_ID` | Direct legal-entity information, individual decisions, current appeal/reversal context, register provenance, workforce intervals and reviewed relationships. |
| `#compliance-stories` | Deterministic comparisons with structured CSV, methodology Markdown and social graphic exports. |

The public legal artifact is an explicit unavailable state. A verified real
company cohort now exists privately; no real Gold decision has human approval.
An independently validated aggregate progress artifact reports the frozen sample,
dated source processing and review counts. It contains no company findings.
See [current completion](completion.md). Production
contains no test companies, invented chart points, sample amounts or implied clean
company counts. Every route remains navigable and explains the missing inputs.
The public methodology can be downloaded even when company data are unavailable.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Design and interaction
items.text:
The intended reader is a researcher or portfolio visitor checking what public
decisions establish about a particular legal entity. The interface supports
comparison followed by inspection of exact sources. It reuses `ReportShell`, the
shared navigation, `ChartCard`, `DashGrid` and `RankBars`. Helvetica comes from
`--font`; neutral surfaces, spacing and borders use existing tokens. Muted violet
uses the existing `--series-3` token. No second theme or font package is added.

The fixed cohort/verification notice is the main visual marker: named legal
identity, dated approval and source coverage stay beside the comparison. There is
no score gauge, severity-colored leaderboard or decorative motion. The homepage
intro and animation sources were not edited. Only the shared project registry and
route integration expose this project through the existing navigation.

Filters select originating authority, case category, operative known legal status,
inclusive originating-decision dates, SNI industry and employee size class. The
date window must remain inside the reviewed published window. Later court context
stays attached to the originating lineage. The original sample is never redrawn.
Entity scope switches between individual companies and dated cohort-member group
aggregates. Group labels link to that root's own identity. A foreign parent does
not acquire a subsidiary's legal outcomes on its company detail page.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Design and interaction
items.text:
Administrative sanctions can be appealed. Final amounts are a separate metric;
SEK and EUR have separate sorting and totals. Unassessed entities stay null and
have no observed rank. Counts and ranks are observations within approved evidence,
not risk or ethics measures. Criminal convictions remain separately unmeasured
under the current upstream contract. Verified revenue metadata are unavailable;
the detail view says so and uses register employee intervals without a fabricated
headcount. See the [public methodology](phase-4-methodology.md).

Full-release authority/year coverage is labeled as preceding interactive filters.
Field completeness in approved rows is distinct from source-population or search
coverage; the latter denominators remain unknown. Selected decision/document counts
on the overview and narrative follow the interactive filters. Native issuer and
originating authority are deliberately named separately.

Native form controls, disclosure elements and tables support keyboard use. Scroll
regions keep wide tables local on phones; links, source hashes and company names
wrap. Headings, focus indicators, live selection counts and chart text alternatives
are provided. Charts use a zero baseline and visible numeric labels. The module
adds no animation and follows the existing site's responsive report layout.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Stage and review the public projection
items.text:
The producer is
[`explorer.py`](../../platform/compliance_intelligence/explorer.py). It requires
the real verified cohort, a current approved Gold release and a validated Phase 4
analytics bundle. The analytics input must use legal-entity scope without
categorical filters. Its reviewed time window bounds browser exploration.
Use the actual private paths produced by Phases 1–4; the names below are examples.

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/explorer.py stage --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --release .research/compliance-intelligence/approved-gold --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort --analytics .research/compliance-intelligence/analytics-release --output .research/compliance-intelligence/explorer-stage --prepared-by ACTUAL_PREPARER_ID
```

Staging writes a sealed private bundle with `review_status=pending` and returns the
exact stage-manifest SHA-256. It does not write a public file or grant approval.
It revalidates current Gold/cohort/analytics eligibility and recomputes per-lineage
measures through the Phase 4 transform. No private candidate is a metric input.
The projection includes only cohort companies and reachable reviewed relationships,
approved decision facts, allowed public source references and method/coverage
metadata. Original bodies, excerpts, reviewer IDs and private paths are excluded.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Stage and review the public projection
items.text:
An authorized human publication reviewer must inspect the exact staged projection,
its identity/relationship reuse and the deterministic presentation/export behavior.
The final reviewer must differ from `prepared_by`. The operator-maintained roster
has the same human/role structure as Phase 3. The approval JSON requires:

| Field | Required value or meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `reviewer_id` | Actual roster principal with `kind=human` and the `publication` role. |
| `disposition` | `approved`. |
| `human_attestation`, `examined_evidence` | Explicit true after the human examination. |
| `privacy_cleared`, `reuse_cleared` | Explicit true for this registry, relationship, decision and export projection. |
| `stage_manifest_sha256` | Exact hash returned by staging. |
| `reviewed_at` | Actual UTC timestamp, at or after stage creation and not in the future. |
| `valid_until` | Actual UTC deadline after review, no more than 30 days after that review and no later than any selected evidence deadline. |
| `rationale` | The reviewer's substantive reason for approving this projection. |

No actual human approval file is generated by this task. After a real review:

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Stage and review the public projection
items.text:
```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/explorer.py promote --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --release .research/compliance-intelligence/approved-gold --cohort .research/compliance-intelligence/cohort --analytics .research/compliance-intelligence/analytics-release --staged .research/compliance-intelligence/explorer-stage --approval .research/compliance-intelligence/final-approval.json --reviewers .research/compliance-intelligence/reviewers.json
npm.cmd run compliance:check
npm.cmd run build
```

Promotion revalidates all inputs, regenerates and compares the exact staged
projection, enforces the independent final review and records its private audit
event. Only then does it atomically replace
`frontend/public/data/compliance/release.json`. There is no arbitrary production
output argument and no upload. The review binds the public payload and the exact
module/model/export/CSS source fingerprint, with line endings normalized to LF.
Changing those presentation files
requires restaging and another final review. The build gate rejects corruption,
missing approval, an expired release or a changed presentation fingerprint.

The envelope's SHA-256 is an integrity check, not a digital signature. The security
boundary includes the authorized private roster, approval-file handling, protected
repository/deployment and operator permissions. A repository administrator who can
rewrite the application and its checks is outside this local gate's trust model.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Withdrawal and freshness
items.text:
The browser validates the envelope hash, 50-member identity shape, allowed source
protocols, attribution, metric types and approval/evidence deadlines before showing
company results. It stops displaying expired results and checks freshness before
downloads. It reloads the current release at least once per minute while active
and on focus. Failed validation hides results; it does not fall back to cached
fixture values. The specific release URL uses `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The earliest deadline includes legally reviewed status dependencies, even when
they have no independently public company decision row. Date-only Phase 3 evidence
deadlines become UTC midnight at the start of that date
for public expiry, a conservative boundary. A final projection review cannot
extend underlying legal verification. Legal changes before the deadline still
need an operator action; this static application has no connection to private
review-store changes. Withdraw locally and redeploy the replacement through the
normal site delivery process:

```sh
python platform/compliance_intelligence/explorer.py withdraw --root .research/compliance-intelligence/phase-2-pilot --reason review_withdrawn
```

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Withdrawal and freshness
items.text:
Other supported reasons are `evidence_changed` and `reverification_required`.
Withdrawal writes only an unavailable state and records a private audit entry.
It cannot erase already downloaded files or social posts. Deployment propagation,
offline browsers and copies remain publication risks; retract or replace shared
graphics when a decision is reversed or the evidence changes. Never describe the
polling interval as immediate global revocation.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Research exports
items.text:
The research page has reproducible issuer counts, decision timelines and native-
currency final amount distributions. Text describes the selected approved records;
there is no LLM-written company narrative or inferred allegation/finding. More than
eight issuer categories are grouped as other issuers; long year ranges use labeled
adjacent year intervals. The underlying decision CSV preserves every selected
approved decision and its native monetary rows; the chart CSV preserves the exact
plotted aggregates.

SVG is generated from structured values at 1200 × 1200 or 1200 × 1500. PNG draws
that same SVG onto an exactly sized canvas. Nothing is extracted from a screenshot
or the DOM chart. Both exports include title, originating-decision period, cohort
snapshot, filters, current-status snapshot, review expiry, release identifier and
visible exact source URLs that fit the reference area. SVG metadata contains all
source URLs and hashes. The companion Markdown includes every exact reference,
the full release/membership hashes, filters and the public methodology. PNG is
inherently a raster image; download the Markdown for complete machine-readable
references and clickable links.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Research exports
items.text:
Native currencies are never summed together. Final-effective monetary rows alone
enter distributions; original amounts remain traceable in the decision CSV. Money
sorting and totals use integer cents (`BigInt`) to preserve decimal precision.
CSV fields are quoted and formula-like cells are neutralized before spreadsheet
use. SVG text/attributes are XML-escaped; there are no external images, scripts or
font requests. Helvetica falls back to Arial where unavailable. PNG decode or
canvas failures report an error and leave SVG/CSV available.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/phase-5.md › Acceptance still requiring real inputs
items.text:
The authorized register and frozen 50 members now exist privately. Obtain real
record-level human approvals and complete original-publication reconciliation.
Then stage the public projection, inspect the four views and exports privately,
obtain the independent exact-stage approval and promote. Run the build/security/
browser checks and deploy through the existing site process. Nothing in this
phase approves the existing real candidates or publishes company outcomes.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/risks.md › Risks and publication controls
items.text:
Assessed 2026-10-16. These controls are product requirements for later work, not a
claim that the unimplemented publication system already enforces them.

| Risk | Consequence | Required control | Owner / release condition |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Public warehouse backup | Raw PDFs, personal details or reviewer data can leak even when omitted from JSON exports. | Private storage/database outside current upload roots, separate credentials and explicit export allowlist. Test that sentinel private content cannot reach either public releases or whole-database backup. | Data engineer; block enforcement acquisition until isolation exists. |

| Wrong legal entity or brand | A subsidiary, parent, issuer or customer receives another party's finding. | Register-backed numbers, dated aliases, separately reviewed party role and explicit liability scope. Group membership cannot authorize attribution. | Identity reviewer; unresolved/conflicting matches held. |

| Incomplete publication | Selected public decisions create false claims of no cases or unfair company comparisons. | Publish search windows, source selection, failures, withheld documents and verification dates. No company compliance/innocence ranking. | Analytics reviewer; coverage denominator visible. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/risks.md › Risks and publication controls
items.text:
| Procedural misclassification | Complaint or administrative fine is described as a conviction. | Separate event/outcome types, forum checks, legal-basis locators and human legal review. | Legal reviewer; category evidence required. |

| Appeal or correction missed | Overturned decisions or reduced amounts are presented as current. | Separate appeal/finality/stay state, linked court dockets, preserve original versions and invalidate affected approvals. | Legal reviewer; proposed 30/90-day freshness policy applied. |

| Personal data in company evidence | Complainants, employees, witnesses, defendants or sole traders become identifiable. | Minimize collection; exclude natural-person identity rows and criminal-history search. Redact derivatives, inspect OCR/PDF metadata and avoid public raw documents. | Privacy reviewer; projection-specific clearance. |

| Legal reuse assumed | Public access is mistaken for blanket licensing or lawful republication. | Retain dated source/dataset terms; apply statutory decision-text rules with exceptions; distinguish attachments and personal data. | Privacy/reuse reviewer; unresolved rights block publication. |

| Sample drift and selection bias | Replacing merged firms or choosing famous sanctioned brands invalidates the study. | Freeze population snapshot, code, methodology, selected rows and hash before any enforcement search; no replacements. | Analytics engineer; exactly 50 verified unique members. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/risks.md › Risks and publication controls
items.text:
| Group amount multiplication | One joint fine is counted for each party or for both first instance and appeal. | Decision/remedy grain, explicit latest-effective-outcome policy and deduplication tests before aggregates. | Analytics engineer; reconciled sums and exclusions. |

| Extraction/translation error | OCR decimal, currency, Swedish wording or legal basis changes the meaning. | Keep original-byte evidence and page locators, pin extractor versions, manually compare material fields and review translations. | Legal/data reviewers; uncertain fields remain unknown. |

| Approval becomes stale | A changed record reuses approval of an older version. | Bind reviews to record/evidence hashes and the final export; independent publication approval; withdrawn records removed in the next corrected release. | Publisher; deny publication when any required review is absent. |

| Credentials or query logs leak | Personal API keys, tokens or person numbers reach git, R2 or CI logs. | Secrets managed in authorized secret stores, redact auth/request metadata, use least-privilege source and storage credentials. | Data engineer; secret scan and log inspection before operationalization. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/risks.md › Privacy assessment before collection
items.text:
[GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679) distinguishes personal information
from legal-entity information; company documents can contain both. Determine the
controller, purpose and lawful basis for actual personal-data processing, document
minimization/retention, and assess whether a DPIA is required before processing that
may present high risk. Evaluate any storage or processing outside the EEA. These
are assessments of the real processing arrangement, not permissions implied by this
architecture.

[IMY's article 10 guidance](https://www.imy.se/globalassets/dokument/rattsligt-stallningstagande/imyrs-2021-1-lagovertradelser.pdf)
covers more than convictions. A person-level offence/suspicion database is excluded
from this company outcome module. Company fines and proceedings must be described
using the documented legal category; publish no criminal label based on an
administrative decision or on a named employee's conduct. Public-interest or
journalistic exemptions and an issuing authority's own publication do not establish
this project's legal basis automatically. Resolve material legal questions with a
qualified reviewer before the affected release.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/risks.md › Publication workflow
items.text:
1. Preserve primary evidence privately and classify access/reuse/privacy status.
2. Resolve the exact party identity and effective-period conflicts. Hold ambiguity.
3. Review event category, forum, legal basis, amount and procedural status.
4. Review the intended public fields, source links and wording for privacy/reuse.
5. Obtain independent publication approval for the record/evidence and artifact hashes.
6. Validate the allowlisted export and release manifest before activation.
7. Handle correction/removal requests through the same versioned review path, recording
   reasons privately and updating public outcome/freshness information promptly.

Current policy proposal: reverify open/appealed outcomes every 30 days and final
outcomes every 90 days, or sooner on new evidence. The data owner must set raw
evidence, rejected-candidate and reviewer-log retention periods before collection;
indefinite retention is not an approved default. Immutable releases need a specific
withdrawal/purge and cache-handling process for accidental personal disclosure.
Removing a current manifest pointer alone does not erase a public object.

The Phase 0 SQL rejects some structurally impossible states but is not an access
control or legal-review engine. Its tests cannot establish publication permission.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Source feasibility
items.text:
Official-source desk research checked 2026-10-16. This is an access assessment;
no company population or enforcement corpus was collected. Availability of a web
page does not establish completeness, bulk access permission or publication rights.

The [Phase 2 access assessment](phase-2.md) supersedes this desk assessment for
IMY/KKV collection: current robots checks, KKV reuse conditions, its direct-client
403 response and the reference-only pilot are documented there. Other sources
below remain future connectors.
The later [KKV alternative assessment](kkv-alternative.md) documents ordinary
independent court-PDF access, the API robots-policy hold, the fixed-cohort index
search and the local public-document import. It does not establish complete KKV
coverage or replace human evidence/publication review.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text:
| Source | Access and format | History and gaps | Reuse and restrictions | Phase decision |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| [IMY tillsyner och beslut](https://www.imy.se/tillsyn) | Public list of ongoing/completed supervision, detail pages and linked decisions, commonly PDF. Search dates and status are discovery aids. No documented bulk decision API verified. | IMY explicitly describes a selection from 2018 onward. Unpublished cases, older Datainspektionen material and redactions require separate checks or document requests. | [IMY reuse policy](https://www.imy.se/om-oss/vart-uppdrag/vidareutnyttjande-av-data/) notes privacy/confidentiality limits; no blanket CC license established here. Formal Swedish authority decisions have a statutory copyright rule, with exceptions noted below. | Feasible for a bounded manual pilot after identity and document review. Record selected-publication coverage. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [Konkurrensverket diarium](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/diarium/sok-i-Konkurrensverkets-diarium/), [search help](https://www.konkurrensverket.se/diarium/sok-i-Konkurrensverkets-diarium/sokhjalp/) | Searchable case metadata, parties and downloadable decisions. Browser-facing search is not a verified supported bulk API. | Help states all registered cases from 1998, updates daily, decisions usually about a day after dispatch. Many closed cases have a decision online; this does not promise every document. Case-type numbering changed in 2013. Curated competition lists are only selections. | Personal names omitted from web diary; missing/secret documents need authority review. No blanket open license or automation quota verified. Use statutory decision-text treatment only where applicable. | Feasible, with case-type and docket normalization. Keep complaints, merger clearances and procurement outcomes distinct from infringements. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [Domstolsverket open data](https://www.domstol.se/om-webbplatsen-och-digitala-kanaler/oppna-data/), [Sök rättspraxis](https://www.domstol.se/tjanster-och-blanketter/sok-rattspraxis/) | Public search/RSS; official open-data page links technical YAML. Its download was not retrievable through the research tool. A stable machine API and its terms must be verified in the pilot. | Open-data overview says reports from 1981 and judgments/decisions from March 2025. Start years vary by court/series. This is mainly higher-court precedent, not a national company-case register or complete lower-court history. | Published parties' personal names are omitted. An explicit machine-readable license was not independently verified; do not label the feed CC0 from secondary-site claims. Decision text has statutory treatment below. | Feasible as precedent/discovery evidence; inadequate alone for appeal/finality coverage. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [Individual Swedish courts](https://www.domstol.se/domar-och-beslut/bestall-domar-beslut-eller-handlingar/) | Contact the court holding a case to obtain judgments or case documents. Each release is reviewed; some requests incur copying/scanning or delivery charges. | Court-specific websites and registries are needed for unpublished/older judgments, appeals and finality confirmation. Anonymization can prevent organization-number matching. | Public access is assessed per document. Access is not automatic permission to build a personal criminal-history index. Preserve redactions and delivery restrictions. | Manual supplement in a later phase. This task sends no requests to courts or other authorities. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [FI sanctions](https://www.fi.se/sv/publicerat/sanktioner/), [financial firms](https://www.fi.se/sv/publicerat/sanktioner/finansiella-foretag/), [market information](https://www.fi.se/sv/publicerat/sanktioner/marknadsinformation/) | Separate category/year lists and linked decisions. No supported bulk sanctions API established. Appeals go to court; administrative findings and closure letters differ. | Lists expose current years and older archives. Earliest complete coverage, removals and category consistency were not established. Securities cases may sanction a shareholder or natural person while naming an unrelated issuer. | [FI open-data policy](https://www.fi.se/sv/om-fi/om-webbplatsen/oppen-data/) permits reuse without fee/agreement, with FI and date as attribution. Document privacy/third-party limits still require review. | Feasible for directly identified legal entities. Sparse applicability for IT firms is possible; preserve issuer and sanctioned party separately. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [SCB company register](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/avgiftsfria-uppgifter-i-foretagsregistret/) | Free current register API; current documentation specifies a personal API key, registration and terms, 5,000 rows/call and 5 calls/second. Employee figures are size classes. | Current information only; no historical endpoint or free delta feed. Snapshot data to reproduce a sample. Companies/legal units and workplaces/CFAR are different units. | Key must not be shared. Record accepted terms; free access does not establish all redistribution conditions. Old certificate instructions describe a replaced interface. | Preferred Phase 1 population, subject to actual authorized access and complete paging. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Feasibility matrix
items.text: | [Bolagsverket high-value API](https://bolagsverket.se/apierochoppnadata/hamtaforetagsinformation/vardefulladatamangder/apiforvardefulladatamangder.5513.html), [download files](https://bolagsverket.se/apierochoppnadata/hamtaforetagsinformation/nedladdningsbarafiler.2517.html) | HVD API requires issued credentials/OAuth2; page specifies no agreement and 60 queries/minute. Downloadable HVD files are free/no agreement, updated weekly. Full company-information API is a separate service. | Digital annual-report file collection is stated to cover digital filings from 2020. Digital filing is incomplete; accounts are lagged and entity/group figures differ. Verify file columns before substituting for the SCB population. | Save dataset-specific terms and attribution evidence. [Full-information API](https://bolagsverket.se/apierochoppnadata/hamtaforetagsinformation/apiforatthamtaforetagsinformation.3988.html) has a separate access/contract process. Do not infer free unrestricted access to every registry field. | Corroborate legal names, registration and relationships; evaluate available HVD files before acquiring broader access. |

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Industry classification
items.text:
Use a versioned classification from the
[official SNI 2025 publication](https://www.scb.se/contentassets/b06d75cd13f8423595b4ba8290c9ea55/sni-2025.pdf)
and [SCB register variable descriptions](https://www.scb.se/vara-tjanster/bestall-data-och-statistik/foretagsregistret/variabelbeskrivning/).
Proposed eligible primary codes: 62.100 programming; 62.201 IT consultancy;
62.202 computer facilities management; 62.900 other IT/computer services;
63.100 data infrastructure, processing and hosting; 58.290 other software publishing.
Persist five digits without punctuation and the classification version.

This intentionally excludes telecom carriers, hardware manufacturing/resale,
holding companies, general web portals and game publishing. It defines an IT
services/software cohort, not the whole ICT sector. Secondary codes alone do not
qualify a company under the proposed rule. A 2007-coded input requires a documented
crosswalk and separate review; never replace 2007 codes with 2025 labels silently.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Applicable legal and reuse baseline
items.text:
[Swedish Copyright Act 1960:729, section 9](https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/lag-1960729-om-upphovsratt-till-litterara-och_sfs-1960-729/)
excludes authority decisions and some other official texts from copyright, with
specified exceptions for included works. This is a statutory rule, not a CC0
license covering an entire website, database, photo collection or attachment set.
Assess the actual document and any third-party content.

[DIGG's guidance on making data available](https://www.digg.se/kunskap-och-stod/oppna-och-delade-data/vagledning-om-oppna-datalagen/krav-vid-tillgangliggorande-av-data-for-vidareutnyttjande)
and IMY's reuse policy require attention to information protection and personal
data. The Open Data Act does not itself create a right to disclosure of secret
documents. Robots rules, technical quotas and published terms must be checked
again before any automated collector is enabled. No attempt to bypass access
controls or infer an unpublished endpoint is part of this design.

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Applicable legal and reuse baseline
items.text:
[GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679) recital 14 and articles 5, 6, 9,
10 and 35 inform the privacy design. Legal-entity data differs from information
about identifiable employees, complainants, sole traders or defendants.
[IMY's article 10 position](https://www.imy.se/globalassets/dokument/rattsligt-stallningstagande/imyrs-2021-1-lagovertradelser.pdf)
explains that protected criminal-offence information can extend to suspicions and
proceedings, including acquittals. Publishing a company record must not expose a
natural person's criminal history by implication. See [risks](risks.md).

items.title: docs/compliance-intelligence/source-feasibility.md › Unknowns and pilot evidence required
items.text:
The pilot must retain terms/robots verification time, actual API specification
version, request parameters, pagination/terminal evidence, server response metadata,
original-byte hashes and gaps for each source. For HTML/PDF sources, manually test
ordinary decisions, changed decisions, appeals and redacted documents. Establish
minimum/maximum observed dates separately from any authority's advertised coverage.
No observed row count, complete-history date or access permission has been invented
to fill these unresolved checks.

items.title: docs/concept-constellation.md › Concept Constellation
items.text:
`#concept-constellation` is an experimental meaning atlas. It asks: **where do the same ideas
appear as they move from stories to philosophy, politics and law?** The data comes from the
shared concept layer (`docs/concept-layer.md`). This page shows what that layer can defend and
nothing more.

```
npm run concepts      # build, dbt and publish the concept layer
```

items.title: docs/concept-constellation.md › Views
items.text:
| Address | Shows |
|---|---|
| `#concept-constellation` | The 28 concepts on a circle by family, the four corpora inside in chain order, and typed relations. `?begrepp=<id>` selects a concept and `?visa=` picks the relation types. |
| `#concepts-profiles` | Concept × corpus: how often each concept is a passage's closest, against chance (3.6 %). |
| `#concepts-method` | Sample, model, dominance metrics, editorial choices. |
| `#concept-<id>` | One concept, for example `#concept-autonomy` or `#concept-risk`. It shows the profile across corpora, the closest passages per corpus with source links, cross-corpus pairs above baseline, related concepts, and links to measures elsewhere on the site. |

items.title: docs/concept-constellation.md › Relation types
items.text:
Every line has one type, drawn in its own colour **and** stroke pattern, so colour is never the
only cue. The legend states each type's content type.

| Type | Drawn as | Content type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `semantic_similarity` | blue, solid, width by strength | derived | Two concepts' anchors are among each other's three nearest, in both languages. On a concept page, two passages from different corpora are closer than 95 % of random pairs. Similar wording; not influence. |
| `shared_tension` | orange, dashed | interpretation | The two concepts are the poles of one Philosophy Atlas tension. This is an editorial choice. |
| `shared_concept` | neutral, width by lift | derived | Shown as "prominent in corpus": the concept is a passage's closest at least twice as often as chance in that corpus. |
| `documented_reference` | green, dotted | source | Riksdag speeches that name the AI Act. This is a corpus-to-corpus link counted from the speeches' own text. |
| `temporal_overlap` | grey, dashed | derived | Two series change in the same period. Used on the AI governance timeline (Phase 8). Temporal overlap does not prove causation. |

The three hues (`#3987e5`, `#d95926`, `#199e70`) pass the dataviz palette validator on the
site's dark surface, including the colour-vision-deficiency checks. Corpora are identified by
position and label, not colour.

items.title: docs/concept-constellation.md › What a concept page includes, and leaves out
items.text:
A concept page shows another domain's data only where a measure of the same idea exists there
(`seeds/concepts/concept_links.csv`). For example, *risk* links to the Riksdag framing group
"risk", the job-ad terms `risk_management` and `model_risk`, the AI Act risk classes, and the
progress ↔ precaution tension. *Autonomy* links only to the autonomy ↔ paternalism tension. Its
page says that no Riksdag word group and no job-ad term measures autonomy, rather than filling
the gap with a near match.

items.title: docs/concept-constellation.md › Limitations
items.text:
- The concept list, anchor sentences, tensions and links are editorial. Different anchors would
  give different profiles.
- The four corpora differ more from each other than their subjects do: 93 % of nearest
  neighbours are from the same corpus. Passages are therefore never placed on one map across
  corpora.
- "Closest passages" are what the model ranks highest. No reader has judged them to be about
  the concept.
- The constellation's layout is fixed by family. The distance between two nodes on the circle
  carries no meaning; only the lines do.

items.title: docs/concept-journey.md › Concept Journey
items.text:
`#concept-journey?begrepp=<id>` follows one idea through four kinds of text: myths and folk
tales (stories), philosophy (ideas), Riksdag speeches (public debate) and the EU AI Act
(rules). It is the reading view of the concept layer ([concept-layer.md](concept-layer.md));
the constellation and the concept pages ([concept-constellation.md](concept-constellation.md))
stay as the exploring views.

The page says at the top what it shows and what it does not: passages with similar language
are placed closer together, and that is semantic similarity, not historical influence.

items.title: docs/concept-journey.md › Concepts
items.text:
It opens with five concepts (`JOURNEY_CONCEPTS` in `frontend/src/concepts/logic.ts`):

| Concept | Why it is included |
|---|---|
| Risk | A Philosophy Atlas tension, a Riksdag word group, job-ad terms and the AI Act risk classes |
| Transparency | A tension, a Riksdag word group and the AI Act's Article 50 obligations |
| Control | A tension, the Riksdag's human-oversight group and Article 14 obligations |
| Responsibility | A Riksdag word group and a job-ad term; it stands out most in the Riksdag |
| Autonomy | Strong in philosophy, almost absent in law and politics; the page says so |

All 28 concepts remain on the constellation.

items.title: docs/concept-journey.md › What the page shows
items.text:
1. The concept, its description and a small constellation on a dark plate. Each domain is a
   star sized by how often the concept is a passage's closest, against chance
   (`profiles.json`). Lines appear only where the data has a relation: semantic similarity
   between two domains' passages above the 95th percentile of random pairs (`pairs.json`), and
   the documented reference from Riksdag speeches that name the AI Act (`relations.json`).
   Domains differ by tone, shape and label, so colour is never the only cue. Positions mean
   nothing beyond the order of the domains.
2. *Why this matters*: generated from the same figures (where the concept stands out most and
   least) plus the editor's notes from `seeds/concepts/concept_links.csv`. Marked derived and
   editorial.
3. One section per domain: how often the concept is the closest there, two representative
   passages with their source link, similarity and rank, and the measures elsewhere on the site
   that count the same idea (`links.json`). Where none exists, the page says so instead of
   filling the gap.
4. *What connects them?* The closest cross-domain pairs, each with its value and the random
   baseline.
5. *What does not follow from this*, *Quality in brief*, *How it was built* and *Trace this
   result*.

items.title: docs/concept-journey.md › Relation types and status
items.text:
Every link is labelled with its relation type and status:

| Type | Used for | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Semantic similarity | A passage close to the concept's anchor; two passages from different domains closer than random pairs | derived |
| Shared concept | A Riksdag word group, job-ad term or AI Act view that measures the same idea | derived or editorial |
| Shared tension | The concept is a pole of a Philosophy Atlas tension | editorial |
| Documented reference | Riksdag speeches that name the AI Act | derived from the speeches' text |

No passage-to-concept mapping has been reviewed yet, and no reviewed Symbolic Atlas cluster is
tied to a concept (`summary.reviewed_cluster_links` is 0). The stories section says so and shows
the model's closest passages among the 101 books of the Symbolic Atlas corpus (v4).

items.title: docs/concept-journey.md › Limitations
items.text:
- The concepts, anchors, tensions and links are editorial. Different anchors would give
  different results.
- 93 % of nearest neighbours come from the same corpus, so passages are only compared within a
  domain and through the concepts, never on one shared map.
- The myth corpus samples about four passages from each of the 101 v4 books, so one book's
  passages rarely carry a concept on their own; it is still a sample, not every passage.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › The shared concept layer
items.text:
The portfolio's text corpora sit at four stages of one chain: **stories** (myth and folklore),
**ideas** (philosophy), **contestation** (Riksdag speeches) and **codification** (the EU AI Act).
The concept layer reads a balanced sample of all four against one editorial list of concepts,
with one embedding model, so that the Concept Constellation (`docs/concept-constellation.md`)
and the concept pages can show where an idea such as *autonomy* or *risk* is prominent, and in
what words, without pretending that one corpus caused another.

```
npm run concepts                # all of the below
npm run concepts:build          # platform/nlp/concepts/build.py -> warehouse/features/concepts
npm run concepts:dbt            # dbt build --select tag:concepts
npm run concepts:publish        # frontend/public/data/concepts/*.json
```

It reads the warehouse built by the Symbolic Atlas, the Philosophy Atlas, the AI Act and the
Riksdag AI models; build those first.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Content types
items.text:
Every row is marked:

- **source**: a chunk's text, exactly as it stands in the source, with its URL;
- **derived**: similarity, rank, z-score, shares, pairs; computed, reproducible, model-dependent;
- **interpretation**: the concepts, their anchor sentences, the tensions and the links to other
  measures; chosen by a person, and named as such.

No label is produced by a language model. A link between an atlas cluster and a concept exists
only in `seeds/concepts/cluster_concept_reviews.csv`, written by a reviewer; it is empty now.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Concepts
items.text:
`seeds/concepts/concepts.csv`: 28 concepts in six families (moral, political, regulatory,
epistemic, social, symbolic), each with a one-line description and an **anchor sentence in
English and in Swedish**. Status `curated`, created by the portfolio's editor; the method column
names how the concept is read (the anchor embedded with the shared model).

`concept_tensions.csv` pairs concepts with the Philosophy Atlas tensions they are poles of (or
nearest to). `concept_links.csv` links a concept to a measure elsewhere on the site only where
the target measures the same idea: a Riksdag framing group, a job-ad term, an AI Act view or a
tension. *Autonomy* has no Riksdag group or job term, and gets none.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Corpora and sampling
items.text:
| Corpus | Stage | Language | Chunks | Documents | Read from |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| myth | stories | en | 404 | 101 books (v4) | `silver.int_symbol_occurrences` (context windows) |
| philosophy | ideas | en | 494 | 13 works | `silver.int_philosophy_passages` |
| politics | contestation | sv | 495 | 495 speeches | `silver.int_riksdag_speeches`, one paragraph per speech |
| law | codification | en | 500 | 121 provisions | `silver.int_ai_act_provisions`, `02024R1689-20260727` |

At most 500 chunks per corpus, spread evenly over its books, works, calendar years
(2016–2026, 45 speeches each, party speeches only) or the Act's provisions in reading order
(Articles 102–110, which only amend other acts, are left out). A speech's paragraph is chosen
by a hash of its id, never by its content. Every chunk keeps corpus, document, location, source
URL, the hash of the source version it was read from and its retrieval time
(`gold.dim_text_chunk`; tests require all of them).

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Method
items.text:
`platform/nlp/concepts/build.py`, with `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`
(the shared model in `platform/nlp/text/vectors.py`):

1. Every chunk is embedded; each concept's anchor is embedded in both languages, and a chunk is
   compared with the anchor in its own language.
2. **Alignment** (`gold.fct_concept_alignment`, chunk × concept): cosine similarity, the
   concept's **rank** among the 28 for that chunk, and a **z-score** against the same concept in
   the same corpus.
3. **Profiles** (`gold.mart_concept_profiles`): how often a concept is a chunk's closest
   (rank-1 share; chance is 1/28 ≈ 3.6 %) and among its three closest.
4. **Representative passages** (`gold.mart_concept_passages`): chunks where the concept ranks
   in the top three, ordered by z-score within the corpus; eight per concept and corpus.
5. **Cross-corpus pairs** (`gold.fct_cross_domain_similarity`): per concept and pair of
   corpora, the closest pair among the representatives, kept only above the 95th percentile of
   4,000 random pairs between those corpora.
6. **Concept relations** (`gold.mart_concept_relations`): `semantic_similarity` where two
   anchors are among each other's three nearest in both languages; `shared_tension` from the
   editorial seed.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Why ranks and z-scores, not raw similarity
items.text:
Raw similarity depends on the corpus as much as on the concept: the mean chunk–anchor
similarity is 0.10 for myth, 0.15 for politics, 0.17 for law and 0.21 for philosophy, because
abstract prose is closer to every abstract anchor sentence. A rank compares concepts *within* one
chunk and a z-score compares chunks *within* one corpus, so neither carries that offset.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Evaluation (`run.json`)
items.text:
- **Corpus dominance.** 93 % of each chunk's ten nearest neighbours come from its own corpus
  (chance 25 %); with each corpus's mean removed, still 80 %. The four corpora differ in genre,
  period and language far more than in subject, so the layer never places chunks from different
  corpora on one map or clusters them together. It compares them only through the concepts.
- **Language.** 98 % of neighbours share the chunk's language (chance 63 %); Swedish is one
  corpus, so this is mostly the corpus effect again.
- **Anchor agreement.** Each Swedish anchor's nearest English anchor is the same concept for 28
  of 28 concepts: the two languages' anchors say the same thing to the model.
- **Concentration.** No corpus is absorbed by one concept: the largest rank-1 share is death in
  myth (38 %); normalised entropy of rank-1 concepts is 0.68–0.82.

items.title: docs/concept-layer.md › Results (7 October 2026)
docs/concept-layer.md › Limitations
items.text:
- An anchor sentence is one way of putting a concept; another wording moves the scores. The
  anchors are published so they can be argued with.
- The model reads at most 128 tokens (about 100 words); longer chunks, mostly philosophy, are
  read from their beginning.
- Translations: myth and philosophy are read in English translations, the Riksdag in Swedish,
  the Act in English. The model is multilingual but not equally good in both.
- Riksdag paragraphs are a sample of all speeches, not of AI speeches; the AI-specific analysis
  is `docs/ai-politics.md`.
- Representative passages are what the model finds closest, not passages a reader has judged
  to be about the concept.
- Scores are comparable within one run of one model only.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Data Constellation
items.text:
The page is retired from the website: `#data-constellation` and `#data-catalogue` now lead to
the project index ([site-structure.md](site-structure.md)). The graph is still generated
(`npm run architecture:build`) and still feeds *Trace this result* on the product pages. The
rest of this document describes the map as it was built.

`#data-constellation` showed the whole data platform as one interactive map: where the data
comes from, how it is ingested, how dbt models it, which files are published and which
products read them. The point it makes is that the portfolio is one shared platform with
several products on top, not separate dashboards; and for a reviewer, that any product can be
traced back to its sources.

The map is generated from the repository. Nothing in React lists a model or an edge.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › How the graph is built
items.text:
```
npm run architecture:build     # python platform/architecture/build_graph.py
```

writes `frontend/public/data/architecture/graph.json` and registers it in the delivery
catalogue. It reads:

| Input | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `platform/target/manifest.json` (dbt; `dbt parse` is run when missing) | every model, seed and source, their paths, descriptions and materialisation, and lineage from `depends_on` |
| `frontend/public/data/schema/er.json` (`export_er.py`) | table kinds (fact, dimension, mart, bridge, seed), primary keys, columns, row counts, and relationships between tables, each measured in the data or backed by a dbt relationships test |
| `platform/architecture/registry.py` | what dbt cannot see: origins, ingesters, ML stages, publishers and their output patterns, products and shared infrastructure |
| the publisher scripts | the dbt tables each one reads, found in its source (`gold.fct_x` or a quoted name) |
| frontend code | the data paths each product's folders name; a product consumes a delivery node when one of its paths matches one of the node's files |
| files under `frontend/public/data` and `catalog.json` | which files each delivery pattern covers (including Parquet that lives only on R2) |

`validate()` refuses the graph on duplicate ids, unknown types, layers or domains, edges to a
missing node, or a data-flow edge that runs right to left. The build fails if a registry entry
names a file that does not exist.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › How the graph is built
items.text:
A new dbt model appears on the next build without any frontend change. A new source, ingester,
publisher or product needs one registry entry.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Domains
items.text:
| Domain | Assigned from |
|---|---|
| Politics | dbt folders `parliament`, `politics`, `news`, `taxes`; the politics product |
| Job market | dbt folders `jobs`, `market`; seeds at the root of `seeds/` (role and technology patterns) |
| Shared platform | `models/gold/shared` (date, period, region, indicator … dimensions), SCB, and the infrastructure |
| Sweden | dbt folder `welfare` |
| Symbolic Atlas | dbt folder `symbolic` |
| EU AI Act | dbt folders `eu_ai_act` and `ai_politics` (the Riksdag's speeches read against the Act); the Publications Office and the Commission as sources |

Smaller standalone projects (DrugComb, DiVA, Homie) are not in the map: they do not
run on the dbt warehouse.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Node types
items.text:
| Type | Id | Meaning | Marker |
|---|---|---|---|
| source | `src:<id>` | an external system (Riksdagen, SCB, Gutenberg …) | large star with a ring |
| ingestion | `ingest:<id>` | a `platform/ingest/<dir>` loader | small square |
| raw | `raw:<dbt source>` | a dbt source: raw landing tables | small diamond |
| seed | `dbt:<name>` | reference data in `seeds/` | hollow circle |
| bronze, silver, gold | `dbt:<name>` | dbt models by layer | dots, gold larger and brighter |
| ml | `ml:<id>` | analytical stages outside dbt (embeddings, clustering, experiments) | four-pointed star |
| delivery | `out:<pattern>` | a set of published files under `frontend/public/data` | hollow square |
| frontend | `app:<id>` | a product | large planet |
| shared | `infra:<id>` | rawstore, the EU legal parser, dbt + DuckDB, the delivery catalogue, Cloudflare R2 | double ring |

Models dbt switches off by default (the job-ad clustering marts, enabled by a dbt variable) are
included, marked `enabled: false` and drawn faded.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Edge types
items.text:
| Type | Meaning | Drawn as |
|---|---|---|
| `lineage` | data built from data: origin → ingester → raw → models → ML | solid line |
| `delivery` | a published file written from a table (or ML output) by a publisher (`via`) | accent line |
| `frontend-consumption` | a product reads a published file | accent line |
| `relationship` | a key joins two tables (cardinality, basis) | dashed, Data model view only |
| `infrastructure` | a stage runs on shared infrastructure (an ingester that stores through rawstore, a dbt Python model or ingester that imports `platform/legal`) | dotted, only on a selected path |

Physical lineage, logical relationships and product consumption are separate edge types and
are never drawn the same way: a join is not a build step.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Graph JSON
items.text:
```json
{
  "nodes": [{ "id": "dbt:mart_symbol_atlas", "label": "mart_symbol_atlas", "type": "gold",
              "layer": "gold", "domain": "symbolic",
              "path": "platform/models/gold/symbolic/mart_symbol_atlas.sql",
              "description": "…", "materialized": "table", "kind": "mart",
              "keys": ["occurrence_id"], "rows": 4804, "columns": ["…"], "enabled": true }],
  "edges": [{ "source": "dbt:int_symbol_occurrences", "target": "dbt:mart_symbol_atlas",
              "type": "lineage" }],
  "domains": [{ "id": "symbolic", "label": "Symbolic Atlas", "lane": 4,
                "counts": { "sources": 1, "models": 5, "gold": 2, "delivery": 9 } }],
  "layers": ["source", "ingestion", "raw", "bronze", "silver", "ml", "gold", "delivery", "frontend"],
  "generated_at": "…", "dbt_version": "…"
}
```

Delivery nodes add `files`, `formats`, `examples` and `published_by` (script paths, `legacy`
for the pre-warehouse politics builder); sources add `url`; products add `href`; raw nodes add
their `tables`.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › The page
items.text:
- **Layout.** x is the stage (source → ingestion → raw → bronze → silver → ML → gold → delivery

  → product), y the domain lane, shared infrastructure in the middle lane. Inside one lane and

  stage, nodes sit on a small sunflower spiral, deterministic per graph. No force layout.

- **Views.** Platform (the architecture), Data model (gold tables and seeds by kind, joined by

  their keys) and Lineage (opens on a product; choose any node).

- **Filters.** Domain (others fade; shared nodes on the domain's paths stay), layer chips (hide

  stages), and search over labels, ids and paths.

- **Selection.** A click, a search result or a button in the list selects a node: everything

  upstream and downstream lights up, the rest fades, and the panel shows layer, domain,

  repository path, materialisation, key, rows, files and publishers, joins, what it is built

  from and what it feeds, and for a product a link to it.

- **Address.** `?view=`, `?domain=`, `?hide=` and `?node=` keep a view shareable.

- **Accessibility.** The canvas has a text description; "Architecture by domain" below lists

  every node by domain and stage as keyboard-selectable buttons. Markers differ in shape, not

  only colour; only the bronze, silver and gold layers keep their tones, the rest are greys.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › The page
items.text: - **Phone.** Below 700 px the map stands upright and fills the screen's width: stages run top to bottom, domains become columns, stage names run up the left edge, and only products, the selection and short paths are labelled. No sideways scrolling; the details follow below, and the layer chips sit in one swipeable row.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Trace this result and the data catalogue
items.text:
The graph also serves two lighter views.

- **Trace this result** (`frontend/src/ui/Trace.tsx`): a fold under a figure that lists, stage
  by stage, where it comes from: the page, the published file, the gold model, silver, bronze,
  seeds, the raw copy, the ingestion and the official source (`tracePath` in
  `frontend/src/constellation/graph.ts`, unit-tested). It is used on the AI Act timeline and
  obligations, the politics overview, the job market, welfare and the Concept Journey, and links
  to the full lineage here (`#data-constellation?view=lineage&node=<id>`).
- **Data catalogue** (`#data-catalogue`, `frontend/src/catalogue/`): every delivery node as a
  dataset, with the gold models it is published from (description, grain, columns, rows), its
  files from `catalog.json` (format, size, rows, download), its sources, the pages that read it
  and the quality checks registered on its models. Above it, the platform's status: when the
  graph was built, the export run, how many quality checks pass, and each domain's own record
  of when it was last built or checked. A domain without such a record is left out.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Adding things
items.text:
- **A source:** add an `ORIGINS` entry and list it in its ingester's `origins`.
- **An ingester:** add an `INGESTION` entry with the dbt sources (`raw`) it fills.
- **A publisher:** add a `PUBLISHERS` entry with its output patterns; inputs are detected, or
  set `inputs` per output when the script reads delivery files or ML output instead.
- **A product:** add a `PRODUCTS` entry with its route and the frontend folders that hold its
  data loading.

Then run `npm run architecture:build`; the Python tests (`platform/tests/architecture`) and the
unit tests (`frontend/tests/unit/constellation.test.ts`) check the result.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Limitations
items.text:
- Publisher inputs are found by name in the script source; a table read through a variable
  name would be missed, and `inputs` must then be set by hand.
- Product consumption is matched from string literals in frontend code; a path assembled at run
  time in several parts may not be found (the welfare Parquet partitions are matched by prefix).
- Some politics files are still built by `platform/legacy/build_gold.py` from raw Riksdagen data
  without the warehouse; they are marked legacy, with an edge from the ingester.
- Row counts come from the ER export and exist only for tables built in the local warehouse.
- The map shows the architecture, not run state: whether a build last succeeded is on the
  status page.

items.title: docs/data-constellation.md › Quality view
items.text: `#data-constellation?view=quality` keeps the platform layout and adds a small mark beside each product and model that has registered quality checks: its weakest measured result (● pass, △ warning, × fail, ○ not measured, – not applicable). The marks use the site's ink, never traffic-light colours, and the legend names every mark. Choosing a node shows its checks by dimension and, for a product, its main validity analysis, with a link to `#quality`. See [quality-and-validity.md](quality-and-validity.md).

items.title: docs/data-dictionary.md › Datakatalog: portfolio
items.text:
Genererad från filerna i `frontend/public/data/` och utvalda källsnapshot under `data/` med `python platform/legacy/generate_data_dictionary.py`.
Kolumnerna nedan är **observerade fältnamn på tabellnivå** (och för den kuraterade voteringsvyn även underlistorna), inte en påstådd databasspecifikation.
JSON-filer med `schema_version`, `generated_at` och `data` listas som tabellen inuti `data`.
CSV-exporter som speglar JSON och riksmötespartitioner är inte nya observationer.

items.title: docs/data-dictionary.md › Överblick
items.text:
- `politics/parliament/`: upstreams publika export av tal, analyser, beslut, aktiviteter, budget och lagkandidater.
- `politics/decisions/` och `politics/laws/`: materialiserade läsvyer byggda ur ovanstående data respektive Allegorias lagtextpooler; dubletter av källobservationer.
- `debates/`: äldre ämneskörning samt aktiva korrigerade budgetramar. Ämnes-ID här får inte sammanfogas med nyare `politics/parliament/topics/`.
- `reports/`: RFC-mätning och två separata textkorpusars budgetordträffar.
- `jobs/`: fem aggregerade CSV-tabeller. Inga annonsrader finns i detta repo.
- `gold/`: materialiserat semantiskt lager; räknas inte som nya källobservationer. Se `docs/gold-semantic-model.md` för dess schema och mått.
- `platform/sources/allegoria/` utanför `public/` innehåller källsnapshotfiler och utkastannotationer; dessa är inte färdiga politiska riktningsmått. `data/budget/` innehåller lexikonets källa.

**Nyckelnotation:** `+` anger sammansatt nyckel, `→` en kontrollerad referens, och ordet *kandidat* betyder att kopplingen inte är ett fastslaget sakförhållande.

items.text:
```mermaid
erDiagram
    DEBATE_PROTOCOL ||--o{ DEBATE_SPEECH : protocol_id
    ISSUE_SESSION ||--o{ ISSUE_SECTION : session
    ISSUE_SECTION ||--o{ ISSUE_SPEECH : path_and_speech_range
    DEBATE_SPEECH ||--o{ UMAP_POINT : speech_id
    DECISION_POINT ||--o{ CITATION : point_id
    DECISION_POINT ||--o{ RESERVATION : point_id
    DECISION_POINT ||--o| ROLL_CALL : vote_id
    ROLL_CALL ||--|{ PARTY_VOTE : vote_id
    ROLL_CALL ||--o{ MEMBER_VOTE : vote_id
    ROLL_CALL ||--o{ SPEECH_LINK_CANDIDATE : vote_id
    DEBATE_SPEECH ||--o{ SPEECH_LINK_CANDIDATE : speech_id
    DECISION_POINT ||--o{ PROPOSITION_LINK : point_id
    BUDGET_PROPOSAL }o--|| BUDGET_YEAR_AREA : budget_year_and_expenditure_area
    LAW_SNAPSHOT ||--o{ LAW_PROVISION : pool_and_document_id
```

**Validerat i de här exporterna:** 4 407 unika `point_id`; 1 436 av dem har ett `vote_id`.
Varje importerad votering har åtta partirader (11 488 rader).
Alla 18 505 citat och 7 503 reservationer refererar en befintlig `point_id`.
Samtliga 393 proposition–utskott-kopplingar refererar en befintlig punkt men gäller endast **dokumentnivå**.

items.title: docs/data-dictionary.md › Sammanfogningsregler
items.text:
1. `point_id` är den säkra nyckeln från beslutspunkt till citat, reservation och propositionskandidat. `vote_id` kopplar beslutspunkt till registrerad votering och därefter till parti- och ledamotsröster. En ja-röst gäller utskottets förslag, inte automatiskt varje citerad proposition eller motion.

2. `speech_id` kopplar partiledartal till UMAP-punkter och semantiska besluts-kandidater. En semantisk likhet är inte stöd, motsägelse eller samma persons röst. Sakdebattens avsnitt använder `path` plus `first_speech_number`–`last_speech_number` för att välja rätt tal ur ett helt protokoll.

3. Budget: koppla `session + actor (= party) + expenditure_area` till `session + party + expenditure_area` i textmatchningen. Koppla budgetförslag till årsutfall på `budget_year + expenditure_area` först efter kontroll av områdets historiska definition. `GOV` är ett kollektivt förslag, inte ett individuellt partiförslag.

4. Lagtextpoolerna `v1` och `v2` överlappar. Använd `pool + document_id + provision_id` och snapshotversionen. Ett omnämnande av en lag är en lexikal kandidat; den parlamentariska lagtextsnapshoten är inte verifierad som gällande på talets datum. Inga validerade votering→skärpning/uppluckring-par finns.

5. Jobbtabellerna kan kopplas på `year/month + role` efter månads-/årshärledning. `cohort + technology` är ett separat aggregat och kan inte kopplas till enskilda annonser eller arbetsgivare i dessa exporter.

items.title: docs/data-dictionary.md › Sammanfogningsregler
items.text:
6. Riksmötesfiler under `sessions/` och partiämnesfiler under `parties/` är partitioner/aggregat av samma politiska material. Räkna dem inte ovanpå globala summeringar. De gamla och nya ämneskörningarna har olika klustertilldelningar: den gamla visar 49,7 % ogrupperade ord och den nya 59,4 %. Sammanfoga inte på enbart `topic_id`.

7. Den aktiva budgetrapporten läser `debates/budgets/summary.json`, där rätt budgetår valts. Den oförändrade upstreamkopian och `politics/parliament/budgets/execution.json` måste årskontrolleras innan deras förslag–utfall-differenser används.

8. `data/budget/keywords.csv` är källlexikonet till språkrapportens lexikonposter. Koppla på `expenditure_area + keyword`; betrakta inte lexikonrader som observerade anföranden.

items.title: docs/data-dictionary.md › Övriga metadata och filformat
items.text:
- `frontend/public/data/politics/catalog.json`: källrevisioner, filstorlek och SHA-256 per fil; inte en observationstabell.
- `frontend/public/data/politics/overview.json` och `politics/parliament/overview.json`: globala räknare och metodmetadata.
- `frontend/public/data/reports/manifest.json`: hash för indata/utdata till rapportexporterna.
- `frontend/public/data/politics/meaning.json`: motortest och **utkast** till politiska annotationer; inte validerad parti-KPI.
- `frontend/public/data/politics/parliament/manifest.json`: filregister. JSON- och CSV-varianter av samma `summary`, `topics` osv. är samma tabell i två format.
- `frontend/public/data/debates/budgets/coverage.json` och `year-selection-audit.json`: importtäckning och reparation av tabellår.
- `frontend/public/data/reports/rfc-drift.json` har dessutom `matched_changes: []`; inga verkliga kravpar klarade den strikta matchningen. Syntetiska `scenarios` är motorexempel.
- `platform/sources/allegoria/sources-v1/source/` och `sources-v2/source/` är rå XML/RFC-källdokument, inte relationella tabeller. `sources-v2/failures.json` är en lista med strängar, och `platform/sources/allegoria/corpus/*.yaml` är motor-/annotationskonfigurationer. Bronze-snapshot och de publika lagbestämmelserna är olika nivåer av samma källmaterial.
