items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › Data storytelling
items.text:
The portfolio is an editorial data publication first and an analytical tool second. Every
flagship page answers in this order:

**question → answer → one main visual → interpretation → explore → method**

The first four are what everyone should read; the last two are there when someone asks for
them. Depth is never removed, only moved to the level where it belongs.

items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › Three levels
items.text:
| Level | What | How it looks |
|---|---|---|
| 1. What everyone should understand | The question, the answer, why it matters | Large type, short paragraphs |
| 2. The evidence | One main chart, one comparison, one key number | `ChartSection`, `FindingHero` |
| 3. Depth | Filters, tables, diagnostics, downloads, method, quality, sources | `ExploreSection` (folded), `MethodSummary`, `.story-diagnostic` |

Level 3 never competes with level 1: no grid of key figures beside the answer, no filters
before the first chart, no model metrics beside a research conclusion.

items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › The pieces
items.text:
`frontend/src/ui/Story.tsx`, styled in `frontend/src/ui/story.css`:

- **DataQuestion**: number or eyebrow, the question, one line of context.
- **FindingHero** (major finding): a number that tells the story on its own, one sentence,
  an optional comparison and source.
- **ChartSection** (supporting finding): question, a title that states the finding, a
  subtitle with definition and period, the chart, a one-line finding and its source.
- **Interpretation**: *What this means* in one to three short paragraphs, with an optional
  *What it does not mean*.
- **SourceCaption**: source · period · definition, quiet, under the figure.
- **ExploreSection**: folded until opened; its children render only then, so the overview
  stays light.
- **StoryNext**: where to go next, as editorial links rather than cards.
- **MethodSummary**: the lineage in one line with a link to Data Constellation, the one quality
  point that matters for the project with a link to Quality & Validity.

Data Constellation carries the engineering depth and Quality & Validity the methodology, so a
project page shows one lineage line and one quality point, not the whole platform.

items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › Audit of the flagships
items.text:
| | Politics `#politik` | AI Act `#ai-act` | Job market `#jobb` | Symbolic Atlas `#symbolic-atlas` | Welfare `#sweden` |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Kind | Information product | Information product | Market analysis | Research | Civic statistics |

| Main question | What separates the parties in practice? | What applies now, to whom, and when? | How is demand for labour changing? | Can recurring symbolic meaning emerge without predefined categories? | Which parts of Sweden do well or poorly, measure by measure? |

| Main answer | The most divided policy area and the most and least alike pair, from the roll calls | The latest application date, what it brings, and its article | The change in new ads against the same months a year earlier | The first model clustered books, not meaning (the baseline's largest-book share) | The highest and lowest county on the chosen measure |

| Main visual | Polarisation per policy area | What applies now, next and the latest change | Ads per month | The atlas map, read with a three-line key | The 21 counties as small multiples |

| Explore | Who votes with whom; More analyses; the theme pages | Roles, startup navigator, timeline, obligations | Growing roles, the clustering, treemap, counties, terms | Filters, cluster panels, corpus explorer, experiments | Headline values, county table, indicator explorer |

items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › Audit of the flagships
items.text:
| Method | Sources, method and data quality (folded); `#politik-kallor` | `#ai-act-sources` | `#jobb-kallor` | Method with diagnostics (trustworthiness, silhouette, noise, membership) | Data quality (folded), pipeline status, data model |

| Validity note | Figures keep their source and definition | Derived obligations stay traceable to the official text | Ads are a proxy for demand, not the labour market | Good clusters did not at first mean symbolic meaning | Relationships are descriptive only |

items.title: docs/data-storytelling.md › Rules
items.text:
- A large number only when the number tells the story; diagnostics go under Method.
- One question, one main visual; supporting charts go below, under Explore or on a deep-dive
  page.
- Chart titles state a finding; the subtitle gives definition, denominator and period.
- Every primary figure has its source, period and definition in a caption.
- Filters sit directly above the chart they change and every page has a meaningful default.
- Research pages (Symbolic Atlas, Philosophy Atlas, Concept Constellation) show question,
  experiment, finding, validity and limitations, negative findings included; information
  products show current state, navigation, exploration and source.
- Deep links keep working: earlier views become deep dives, never dead addresses.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › Semantisk kontroll före dataleverans
items.text:
`platform/publish/validate_refresh_delivery.py` kontrollerar innehållet i jobb-,
nyhets- och DiVA-leveranserna innan `release.py` publicerar dem. Offentliga data
har sin egen kontroll i `validate_public_data.py`. Publiceringens regler står i
[r2-delivery-contract.md](r2-delivery-contract.md).

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › Anrop och resultat
items.text:
`--root` är katalogen som innehåller `jobs/`, `parliament/` och `diva/`, inte
repositoryroten. Varje grupp kontrolleras separat:

```sh
python platform/publish/validate_refresh_delivery.py --group jobs --root frontend/public/data
python platform/publish/validate_refresh_delivery.py --group news --root frontend/public/data
python platform/publish/validate_refresh_delivery.py --group diva --root frontend/public/data
```

Jobs kan dessutom kräva färsk streamtäckning:

```sh
python platform/publish/validate_refresh_delivery.py --group jobs --root frontend/public/data --stream-state warehouse/raw/jobtech/stream/state.json
```

Grupperna `jobs` och `diva` kör kommandot i sitt publiceringssteg i
`platform/pipeline.yml`. Alla tre grupperna har det dessutom som `checks` i sin
spec under `configs/delivery/`, så `release.py` kör det före uppladdningen.
Validatorn läser JSON med repositoryts `read_json` och använder i
övrigt standardbiblioteket. Den skriver inga dataset, fyller inga luckor och gör
inga API- eller R2-anrop. Det finns inga nya beroenden.

Exitkod 0 och JSON-status `validated` betyder att kontrollerna passerade.
Fel i data eller filer ger exitkod 1 och JSON-status `failed` med ett kort `error`.
Felaktiga CLI-argument ger argparse-standardens exitkod 2. De koderna gäller
validatorn; sammanfattarens separata kontrakt använder kod 2 för valfria AI-fel.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › Jobs
items.text:
Kontrollerna följer `export_market.py`:

- Alla numeriska JSON-värden måste vara ändliga. NaN och Infinity avslås.
- `monthly` och `daily` har rader `[datum, annonser, vakanser]`. Datum måste vara
  kalendergiltiga, unika och strikt stigande inom varje fältserie. Månader måste
  vara avslutade; dagar måste ligga före dagens datum i Stockholm.
- Annons- och vakansräknare måste vara icke-negativa heltal. Boolean, decimaler
  och negativa värden avslås även i occupations, regions, conditions och archives.
- `last_month` är sista `monthly.all`-månaden. Dess år och månadsnummer ska stämma
  med `latest_year` och `ytd_months`. `years` ska vara den sorterade unika årlistan
  från `monthly.all`. Årsräknare får inte referera till andra år.
- Fältvärden får inte överstiga motsvarande `all`-värde när båda finns. Jämförelsen
  gäller månads- och dagsräknare, regionernas års-/YTD-räknare och conditions per
  år, kategori och etikett. YTD får inte överstiga motsvarande helårsräknare.
- Fält-, occupations- och regionidentifierare ska vara unika. Preliminary-månader
  ska finnas i den exporterade totala månadsserien.

Fält summeras inte till en tvingad totalsumma. Kontrollen kräver inga rader för
varje månad eller dag och skapar inga nollrader. `ytd_months` betyder senaste
kompletta månads kalendernummer enligt `int_market_periods`, inte antalet
observerade månadsrader. Utan `--stream-state` är detta en innehållskontroll av en
daterad leverans; den påstår inte att dagens stream har hämtats.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › Streamtäckning
items.text:
Kontrollen bygger på ingestionens eget state: `complete_from` och `fetched_until` skrivs till state först efter
framgångsrika hämtfönster. Ingen ny `verified`-markör behövs.

`complete_from` ska vara ett giltigt kalenderdatum senast gårdagen i
`Europe/Stockholm`. `fetched_until` ska ha datum och klockslag, ligga från dagens
lokala midnatt till nu och aldrig i framtiden. Offsetlösa tidsstämplar tolkas som
Stockholmtid, precis som `ingest_stream.py`; offsetförsedda värden konverteras
till samma tidszon. Senaste kompletta dag är `fetched_until`-datum minus en dag.
Om filen dessutom har `last_complete_day` måste den stämma med den härledda dagen.
Exporterade dagsrader får inte ligga efter täckningens slut.

En senast observerad annons från förrgår godkänns när vattenmärket täcker gårdagen.
Noll annonser är alltså inget bevis på avbrott. Stale, saknat, ogiltigt eller
framtida vattenmärke avslås när `--stream-state` begärs. Detta verifierar det
angivna vattenmärkets struktur och färskhet, inte råfilernas hash, extern
fullständighet eller att state hör till just de exporterade bytesen.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › News
items.text:
`parliament/news.json` måste ha unika artikel-id:n, giltiga publiceringstidsstämplar
med tidszon och källreferenser som finns i `sources`. Framtida tidsstämplar och
icke-ändliga numeriska värden avslås. Sammanfattningsfilen är valfri; om den finns
kontrolleras genereringsdatum, originalperiod, text och citerade artikel-id:n.
Kända citerade artiklar måste ligga inom sammanfattningens originalperiod, och
partinoteringar måste stödjas av de citerade artiklarnas partitaggar.

En aktuell sammanfattning med okända citat avslås. En tidigare daterad
sammanfattning vars period börjar före de synliga artiklarnas första dag får
behålla äldre id:n som saknas i det nuvarande exportfönstret. Det kräver att
sammanfattningen genererades före nyhetsexporten och ger en uttrycklig varning om
att dessa citat behöver verifieras mot arkiverade poster. En period som delvis
överlappar det synliga fönstret kan också ha sådana äldre citat. Giltiga, kända
citat kontrolleras fortfarande.

Från ett begränsat exportfönster går det inte att bevisa att ett saknat historiskt
id fanns i arkivet. Validatorn redovisar den begränsningen och tar aldrig bort en
gammal sammanfattning eller ändrar dess datum. Den verifierar inte språkmodellens
tolkning av artikeltext eller att alla relevanta artiklar har arkiverats.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › DiVA
items.text:
`diva_clusters.py` exporterar unika heltals-id:n för kluster och punkter med
`x`, `y`, `c` och `t`. Validatorn kräver ändliga numeriska koordinater, unika
kluster-id:n och punktreferenser till befintliga kluster. Exporten har inget
enskilt post-id i punkterna, så punktunikhet kan inte verifieras. Upprepade
titlar eller koordinater avslås inte som påstådda dubblettposter. Statusen
redovisar detta som en varning. Gruppen är verifierad med exportens form som
testfixture, inte mot en verklig DiVA-fil.

items.title: docs/delivery-validation.md › Tester
items.text:
`platform/tests/python/test_refresh_delivery_validation.py` täcker falska
deltotaler, dubbla eller oordnade perioder, framtida datum, negativa räknare och
räknare som inte är heltal, NaN och Infinity, stale eller framtida täckning,
Stockholms dygnsgräns, giltiga glesa dagsserier, sammanfattningens citat,
bevarande av äldre citat och period samt DiVA-koordinater. Tiden är fixerad i
CLI-testerna, så de fungerar oavsett maskinens datum.

```sh
python -m pytest platform/tests/python/test_refresh_delivery_validation.py -q
```

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Hosting: Cloudflare
items.text:
The site is static files (`npm run build` → `dist/`) served by Cloudflare Workers static
assets at `https://antonernstsson.com`, plus a small Worker script (`worker/index.ts`) for the
two Workers AI demos ([workers-ai.md](workers-ai.md)). Requests to `/api/*` run the script
first; every other request is served from the files as before, and a request that matches no
file is handed back to the files by the script. The site's JSON
is part of those files. Parquet marts and document shards are served from the R2 bucket
`anton-portfolio` on the same Cloudflare account, which also holds the versioned data releases
the site does not read ([storage-and-serving.md](storage-and-serving.md)).

Cloudflare builds the site itself from this repository (Workers Builds): pushes to `main`
deploy code and static assets. Data workflows publish validated R2 releases and update
`manifests/current.json`; they do not create data commits or deploy the site. The frontend
connection is enabled once after the complete R2 bundle is verified.

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Branches: main and a preview per pull request
items.text:
`main` is production. New work never lands there directly:

1. Work happens on a feature branch, with a pull request into `main`; CI must be green.
2. Cloudflare attempts a branch preview (`npx wrangler preview`, using the
   `[previews]` block in `wrangler.toml`). Check its actual build result before relying
   on a preview. Its origin also needs the bucket's CORS permission.
3. The owner looks at the preview and approves the merge; merged, it is live.
4. Data refreshes validate, upload and activate their own R2 groups. Once the frontend
   connection is enabled, the site reads the approved version without a code commit or deployment.

items.title: docs/deploy.md › In the repository
items.text:
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wrangler.toml` | Worker name, `dist/` as its static assets, the script for `/api/*`, the Workers AI and rate-limit bindings |
| `worker/index.ts` | `/api/embed` and `/api/answer`; tests in `worker/index.test.ts`, run by `npm run test:unit` |
| `.node-version` | Node 22 for Cloudflare's build image |
| `frontend/public/_headers` | Security headers; long cache for hashed assets, short for data. It does not apply to responses the Worker script makes: `/api/*` sets its own `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy` |
| `platform/publish/r2-cors.json` | Origins allowed to read the bucket: the domain, `www`, `workers.dev`, the branch preview, local dev |
| `frontend/index.html` | Canonical URL `https://antonernstsson.com/` |
| `infra/` | Terraform for the R2 buckets, CORS, the Worker's custom domains, the `main` ruleset and environments ([infra/README.md](../infra/README.md)) |

The site uses relative paths (`base: './'` and hash routing), so it works at the domain root,
on `workers.dev` and in previews without configuration.

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Setup, once
items.text:
Terraform in `infra/` now owns part of this setup; its bootstrap checklist is in
[infra/README.md](../infra/README.md). Once it is applied, CORS and the Worker's custom domains
change through Terraform, not the dashboard.

1. **Domain.** Cloudflare → Domain Registration → register `antonernstsson.com`. Its DNS is
   then on Cloudflare, which the custom domains below need.
2. **Workers.** Workers & Pages → Create → Import a repository → `korv9/anton-portfolio`, once
   for production:
   - project name `anton-portfolio` (must match `name` in `wrangler.toml`)
   - build command `npm run build`
   - deploy command `npx wrangler deploy`
   - preview command: the default, `npx wrangler preview`
   - path `/`, API token: create new

The build publishes to `https://anton-portfolio.anton-ernstson.workers.dev`, which is
   also allowed in `r2-cors.json`. Check under Settings → Build that the production branch is
   `main`.

Under Settings → Build, turn on builds for non-production branches, so every pull request

   gets its preview link.

3. **Domain on the site.** The Worker → Settings → Domains & Routes → Add → Custom domain:

   `antonernstsson.com`, and `www.antonernstsson.com`. To send `www` to the bare domain, add a

   redirect rule: Rules → Redirect Rules → hostname equals `www.antonernstsson.com` → dynamic

   redirect to `concat("https://antonernstsson.com", http.request.uri.path)`, status 301,

   preserve query.

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Setup, once
items.text:
4. **Domain on the data.** R2 → `anton-portfolio` → Settings → Custom Domains →

   `data.antonernstsson.com`. Then:

   - apply the CORS policy: R2 → the bucket → Settings → CORS policy → paste

     `platform/publish/r2-cors.json` (with Terraform applied, `infra/cloudflare` does this);

   - set the repository variable `R2_PUBLIC_BASE` to `https://data.antonernstsson.com/`

     (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables);

   - run *Bootstrap versioned data delivery in R2* first with

     `manifest_key=manifests/pipeline-smoke.json`, then verify the real files and browser

     reads before running it with `manifests/current.json`;

   - enable `manifest_url: https://data.antonernstsson.com/manifests/current.json`

     in the committed delivery file, or set `VITE_R2_MANIFEST_URL` for the site build.

     `R2_MANIFEST_URL` / `R2_LIVE_DELIVERY=1` also configure the catalogue generator.

     Once set in the delivery file, the generator preserves that connection;

   - retain historical copies until versioned reads, rollback and reproduction pass.

5. **Scheduled refreshes.** Each morning (UTC): `refresh-jobs.yml` at 04:23 (new archives and

   the day's job ads from JobTech's stream), `refresh-welfare.yml` at 04:37 (welfare, taxes

   and parliament: roll calls, reports, polls, elections, government, studies) and

   `refresh-news.yml` at 05:17. Each publishes a validated R2 group: jobs, public-data

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Setup, once
items.text:
or news. They run in the `anton-portfolio` environment, whose secrets

   hold the R2 credentials, and can also be run by hand from the Actions tab. To pause one,

   comment out its `schedule:` lines. Riksdag speeches and the analyses built on them

   (embeddings, maps) are refreshed by *Build and store the warehouse*, run by hand.

6. **Refresh secrets.** Settings → Environments → `anton-portfolio` → Secrets:

   `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_BUCKET` (an R2 API token

   with read and write on the bucket). Without them the daily refresh stops at its first step

   and the news collection does nothing.

7. **The first release.** Actions → `publish-r2.yml` → Run workflow. It stages every delivery

   group and activates them together; give it `manifests/pipeline-smoke.json` as

   `manifest_key` to check the whole bundle apart from the production pointer, then

   `manifests/current.json`. The site is not wired to the manifest

   ([r2-delivery-contract.md](r2-delivery-contract.md)).

8. **The warehouse in R2.** Actions → *Build, store and publish the warehouse* → Run workflow. It

   fetches every public source, builds the DuckDB warehouse with dbt and stores it in the

   bucket with all its raw files (`platform/publish/warehouse_store.py`):

   `warehouse/portfolio.duckdb.gz`, `warehouse/manifest.json` (built when, from which commit,

   SHA-256, rows per schema), `warehouse/raw/` and `warehouse/features/` (the ML stages'

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Setup, once
items.text:
outputs: embeddings, maps, clusters, the concept layer). Later runs start from the stored

   files. Run by hand, the ML stages run only when their output is not stored yet; choose

   `ml: always` to rerun them (seeds are fixed, so the same inputs give the same results). The first run counts

   every JobTech archive for the AI governance terms and takes a couple of hours.

   Fetch the warehouse anywhere with `python platform/publish/warehouse_store.py pull`. The

   bucket is public, so the warehouse can be downloaded by anyone; it holds only open data.

   `platform/tests/architecture/test_pipeline_workflows.py` fails if a dbt subject, a source

   or an ML stage is added without a step here.

What lives where:

| What | Where | Kept by |
   |---|---|---|
   | Approved JSON, Parquet and document shards | R2, `releases/<group>/<id>/files/` | `release.py`, with exact-byte readback and activation last |
   | Static assets, code and committed reproduction snapshots | Git and Cloudflare Workers | code deployments; snapshots retained during migration |
   | Raw source files, ML outputs, the DuckDB warehouse | R2, `warehouse/` | *Build and store the warehouse* |

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Limits
items.text:
Free plan: 20,000 files and 25 MiB per file in a Worker's static assets; requests for static assets
are free and unlimited. Requests that run the script (`/api/*`, and addresses that match no file)
count against the Free plan's 100,000 requests a day and 10 ms CPU each; Workers AI has 10,000
neurons a day. The Worker's `[ai]` binding (`AI`) needs no secret or setup step: Workers Builds
deploys it with the Worker, and the neurons count against the account. The `[[ratelimits]]` binding
(`RATE_LIMITER`, 20 requests a minute per IP and location) passes `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run`;
whether the Free plan accepts it shows on the first preview deploy. If it is rejected, remove the
block: the neuron allocation is the hard limit either way.

`npx wrangler dev` needs a remote session for the AI binding. Wrangler reads
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` from `.env`, and that token needs the Workers Scripts permission for a
remote session; without it, run `npx wrangler login` and start dev without the token in the
environment. Until that is done, live calls go through the Node shim in
`platform/publish/workers_ai/eval_answer.ts`, which runs the Worker's code against the Workers AI
REST API ([workers-ai.md](workers-ai.md)).

`r2-cors.json` allows local dev only on port 5173 (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1`). On another port
the browser cannot read the files the site loads from R2, such as the debate shards and the SFS
`meta.json`.

items.title: docs/deploy.md › Limits
items.text:
A local build on 13 October 2026 had 950 files, the largest
5.4 MB. Check the config locally with `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` after `npm run build`.

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Design system v2 migration audit
items.text:
Audited 16 October 2026 against the existing working copy. Existing unrelated changes were
retained. This migration changes presentation and documentation; it adds no dependencies.

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Baseline and dependencies
items.text:
The existing Graphify index was queried first with a 1,000-token budget. It identifies
`main.tsx` as the entry point importing shared styles but does not describe CSS selector
precedence. Source inspection and a scan of all 51 stylesheets supplied that detail.

| Area                | Before                                                                                                                           | Migration                                                                                                                             |

| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Entry point         | `styles.css`, `pages.css`, product styles, `design-system.css`, then `tokens.css`; project CSS loaded through lazy React modules | Import order retained; semantic tokens and compatibility aliases in the existing token file                                           |

| Color roles         | Ivory, white, pastel panels and olive selection; interface styles read cluster palette names                                     | Greige canvas, secondary surface and panel; neutral selection and chart defaults; categorical cluster palette kept separate           |

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Baseline and dependencies
items.text:
| Typography          | Two Manrope font faces and a preload, Helvetica identity, monospace metadata                                                     | System Helvetica throughout the interface and canvas labels; metadata in Helvetica, code in monospace; obsolete font requests removed |

| Global overrides    | `site/editorial.css` enlarges every project heading and removes dashboard panel styles                                           | Smaller shared heading roles, compact gutters and restored panel structure; workspace-specific open figures                           |

| Navigation          | Shared header, native project-menu disclosure, breadcrumbs, topics, report tabs and project pager                                | Existing components retained, project header compacted and neutralized; no duplicate sidebar                                          |

| Reports             | Shared `ReportShell`, project-specific chart frames and high-specificity long-read selectors                                     | Existing charts and topic ordering retained; common panel, tab and metadata roles                                                     |

| Visualization stage | Three-column stage CSS despite markup placing settings below the figure; duplicate editorial overrides                           | Stage stylesheet now describes the actual full-width figure and optional two-column settings disclosure                               |

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Baseline and dependencies
items.text:
| Dark visualization  | Component-scoped `.plate`, local aliases and a decorative radial gradient in Symbol Lab                                          | Local semantic palette and aliases; gradient removed; page and global header stay light                                               |

| Controls            | Native controls, shared button states, many local focus colors                                                                   | Neutral focus tokens, consistent foreground/background pairs and existing pressed/disabled behavior                                   |

| Charts              | Party and categorical colors plus hardcoded blue defaults, olive heatmaps and tinted state comparisons                           | Party and cluster identity retained; single-measure defaults and status comparisons neutral; heatmap text contrast corrected          |

| Responsive layout   | Component-specific 320-1100px rules; existing table and figure scroll wrappers                                                   | Local breakpoints retained; shared stacking at 760px and compact header layout at 760/360px                                           |

| Accessibility       | Skip link, focus outlines, reduced motion, chart keyboard navigation, table alternatives and axe tests                           | Existing conventions retained; regression checks cover route-to-route color inheritance and isolated dark plates                      |

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Baseline and dependencies
items.text:
The shared design ownership is documented in [design-system.md](design-system.md). Existing
`DashGrid`, `ChartCard`, `Feature`, `Stage`, `ProjectHero`, `ProjectStructure` and native
controls cover the requested primitives. No parallel component library was added.

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Remaining literal colors
items.text:
Literal interface colors outside the token file were removed from project stylesheets.
The exceptions are the protected homepage and its legacy About/experience rules in
`styles.css`. The chat-window gradient is an overflow mask, not a decorative background.
Party identities, cluster palettes and reviewed/candidate marks retain their data meaning.

The old `--cv-*` palette remains in `tokens.css` for categorical renderers and the protected
homepage. Existing `--page`, `--paper`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--info`, `--negative`, `--teal`
and `--orange` names are compatibility aliases, not separate themes. `--negative` is neutral
for comparisons; actual error text can use `--color-error`.

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Review and validation
items.text:
The visual review covers desktop project entry pages and mobile examples from each workspace.
Screenshots and the computed-style inventory are in `artifacts/design-v2/`. The existing
accessibility suite checks 320, 768 and 1440 pixel widths. The migration adds regression
checks for all workspace categories, header size and palette inheritance after navigation.
The existing Concept Lab interaction test also covers the SVG node hit area: a node link
now receives pointer events throughout its bounds, including the gap between its dot and label.

The homepage source hashes match the pre-migration working copy. At 1440 by 1000 pixels,
the homepage name has the same bounds, 112-pixel type, 103.04-pixel line height and color as
before. The backdrop bounds and non-font computed properties also match. Its existing
text sizing formula and animation code were not edited. Other text can reflow with the
required Helvetica fallback stack.

The swap review distinguishes compact analytical headings from the identity display scale.
The squint review checks that surfaces group the charts while data remains the strongest
color. The signature is the common question/filter/chart/source sequence with room for the
labs' projections and engineering diagrams. The token review separates greige UI roles from
categorical data colors. Native focus, readable control states and reduced motion were
checked through the existing browser tests.

items.title: docs/design-system-audit.md › Review and validation
items.text:
Backend tests need a writable pytest temporary directory on this Windows host. The default
system pytest folder rejects access; the suite passes with a workspace-local `--basetemp`.
Live-delivery tests remain opt-in and do not validate production endpoints in the default run.

Open analytical questions in [chart-review.md](chart-review.md), including chart-form and
keyboard improvements outside this visual migration, remain separate work.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Portfolio design system v2
items.text:
A warm-grey analytical workspace for recruiters, hiring managers and readers exploring the
projects. The interface provides structure; charts, networks and source material provide
meaning. The homepage retains its existing composition and palette, with Helvetica applied.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Tokens and type
items.text:
`frontend/src/tokens.css` is the only token definition file. `main.tsx` imports it after the
base and shared styles. Project styles reference these tokens, including when loaded lazily.
Semantic names are available to new code; existing aliases resolve to the same values.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Tokens and type
items.text:
| Role                             | Token                    | Value     | Existing aliases                  |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------- | --------------------------------- |
| Canvas                           | `--color-canvas`         | `#F1EFE7` | `--page`, `--paper-strong`        |
| Navigation and secondary surface | `--color-surface`        | `#E2DFD6` | `--paper`, `--wash`, `--side`     |
| Panel and selected field         | `--color-panel`          | `#CECBC2` | `--surface`, `--select`           |
| Separator                        | `--color-border`         | `#A9A69D` | `--line`                          |
| Control edge                     | `--color-border-control` | `#858279` | `--line-strong`                   |
| Main text                        | `--color-ink`            | `#363636` | `--ink`, `--accent`, `--focus`    |
| Secondary text                   | `--color-ink-secondary`  | `#57554E` | `--muted`, `--ink-faded`          |
| Inverse text                     | `--color-ink-inverse`    | `#F1EFE7` | `--on-accent`                     |

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Tokens and type
items.text:
Secondary text is darker than the initial reference `#66645F`: that reference fails 4.5:1
on the secondary surface. `#57554E` also passes on the darker panel. Inactive data and
separator colors are not body-text colors. Native control borders use the stronger edge.

Helvetica uses the system stack `"Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif`.
There are no downloaded Helvetica files or Manrope font requests. Arial is the fallback
where Helvetica is unavailable. Body is regular, controls and chart titles medium, headings
selectively semibold. Metadata also uses Helvetica. Code uses the system monospace stack.
Charts, tables and metrics use tabular figures.

| Type role                   | Token                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Display, protected homepage | `--type-display`                 |
| Page title                  | `--type-page-title`              |
| Section title               | `--type-section-title`           |
| Chart title                 | `--type-chart-title`             |
| Body                        | `--type-body`                    |
| Label                       | `--type-label`                   |
| Caption                     | `--type-caption`                 |
| Metric                      | `--type-metric`                  |
| Technical metadata          | `--type-metadata`, `--font-meta` |
| Code                        | `--type-code`, `--font-mono`     |

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Tokens and type
items.text:
The `--h*`, `--fs-*` and dashboard names remain compatibility roles. The display scale is
reserved for identity; analytical page titles use the smaller page scale.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Composition and ownership
items.text:
The existing React components form the system. Add a component only when the existing
primitive cannot express the interaction. Use native links, buttons, selects and disclosures.

| Responsibility                             | Existing implementation                                                       |

| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| App shell and workspace identity           | `App.tsx`, `.site-shell`, `data-workspace`                                    |

| Global header and project menu             | `site/SiteHeader.tsx`, `site/header.css`                                      |

| Breadcrumbs and project pager              | `site/Header.tsx`, `site/site.css`                                            |

| Project and section navigation             | `projects/ProjectStructure.tsx`, `projects/topics.ts`                         |

| Content and workspace alignment            | `site/editorial.css`, `.ds-container`                                         |

| Project header and section header          | `ui/Project.tsx`, `ProjectHero`, `ProjectSection`                             |

| Dashboard grid and panel                   | `ui/dash/Dash.tsx`, `DashGrid`, `ChartCard`                                   |

| Analytical chart, header, source and table | `charts/feature/Feature.tsx`, `Feature`                                       |

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Composition and ownership
items.text:
| Visualization stage                        | `ui/Stage.tsx`, `Stage`, `StageBlock`, `StageFacts`                           |

| Metrics and tables                         | `KpiRow`, `Feature` table alternatives and existing native `.dk-table` tables |

| Ranked comparison and time series          | `charts/RankBars.tsx`, `MultiLineChart.tsx`, `TimeSeriesChart.tsx`            |

| Filter bar and select                      | `Pick`, `report-chips`, `SlicerSelect` and existing project filters           |

| Disclosure                                 | `ui/Disclosure.tsx`, native `details` for local methodology                   |

| Loading, empty and error states            | Existing data-page states, `site/PageBoundary.tsx`                            |

Shared layout rules live in `site/editorial.css`. Chart and stage internals live in their
own stylesheets. `tokens.css` supplies tokens, shared control states and the scoped plate.
Do not add a second theme or an override sheet for individual projects.

Dashboard grids have twelve columns; a full-width chart spans all twelve. Gutters are fluid
between 16 and 28 pixels. Project sections use `--sp-section`; local gaps use `--sp-1`
through `--sp-7`. Charts have no global maximum width. Prose keeps a 68-character measure.
Panels use thin borders, a 2-pixel radius and no elevation shadow. Navigation is compact.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Four workspace patterns
items.text:
`App` derives `data-workspace` from the existing registry groups. Changing visual layout
does not change routes, analytical calculations, topic order or data loading.

| Pattern          | Projects                                                 | Composition                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Observatory      | Political, Labour Market, Wellbeing, EU AI Act           | `ReportShell` and existing deep views; compact question, topic tabs, contextual filters, wide primary chart and supporting panels |
| Lab              | Symbol, Philosophy, Concept, Drug Synergy                | Report tabs where already present; full-width maps, compact controls, legends and optional method/settings disclosures            |
| Engineering      | IT Incident Clustering, DiVA Thesis Lakehouse, Homie API | `ProjectHero`, project sections, architecture and pipeline figures, validation, results and code links                            |
| Interactive tool | Cluster Visuals                                          | Primary visualization and its controls; no added metric row                                                                       |

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Four workspace patterns
items.text:
Ask the Law has no active route in the current site. The retired RAG address redirects to
the project index. A future focused application can use the tool pattern without restoring
retired functionality as part of this migration.

The existing section-navigation model replaces a sidebar. Do not introduce a second global
navigation hierarchy. Engineering content keeps its existing structure; metrics appear only
where the report already uses them.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Data color and dark plates
items.text:
Party identities remain in `parties/identity.tsx` and render without an interface color tint.
Categorical cluster palettes retain their values. The `--cv-*` names now belong to the
cluster palette and the protected homepage, not the project interface. Other categorical
series use `--series-1` through `--series-5` with labels and existing marks or legends.

Single-measure charts use neutral ink. Changes, vote kinds and applicability states do not
imply green or red success. Source labels, selected controls and chart defaults use neutral
tokens. Actual error messages can use `--color-error` and must include readable text.

Heatmaps retain their values, order and scales. Pale ramps stop before dark text loses
contrast; dark cells use inverse text. The technical stage inventory uses the same principle.
Existing analytical review items remain in [chart-review.md](chart-review.md).

`.plate` provides a component-scoped dark canvas (`#242422`) and locally rebinds semantic
colors, compatibility aliases and chart aliases. It does not change the page or navigation.
Canvas renderers read the local computed typography and colors. Symbol Lab retains its dark
projection; surrounding controls and content follow the warm-grey page. No decorative
radial gradient remains. Meaningful architecture-layer colors are not interface accents.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Controls, accessibility and responsiveness
items.text:
Use `.btn` for the primary action, `.btn-quiet` for an outlined action and `.btn-text` for a
text action. Existing filter groups share hover, pressed, disabled and focus states. A
selected text filter uses weight and an underline; a segmented control can use ink fill.
The dark foreground and light inverse text must travel together on filled controls.

Inputs have explicit foreground and background colors. Focus has a visible 2-pixel outline.
Existing skip links, chart keyboard navigation, table alternatives, accessible labels and
native disclosures are retained. Reduced motion disables transitions and reveal animations.

At 760 pixels shared workspace panels stack; component-specific chart breakpoints retain
local scrolling where detail cannot shrink. The header condenses at 760 pixels and stacks
its links at 360 pixels. Project topic links wrap. Wide tables scroll inside their wrappers.
No page-level horizontal overflow is allowed at 320, 768 or 1440 pixels.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › SWEDEN
items.text:
The SWEDEN pages are one exception to the single token file. Their tokens are scoped to
`.sweden` in `frontend/src/sweden/sweden.css`, they follow `prefers-color-scheme`, and their
scene panels may use translucency. Nothing in that file reaches `.home-shell` or the other
projects. [sweden-design.md](sweden-design.md) is the reference for these pages.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Protected homepage
items.text:
`:root:has(.home-shell)` in `tokens.css` retains the homepage's original legacy token values,
including its palette, heading scales, section spacing and weights. The sans stack changes
to Helvetica. Project header changes are scoped to `.project-shell`. No homepage source,
text positioning, sizing formula or animation timing is changed by this migration.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Validation
items.text:
`frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` checks navigation through every workspace type,
Helvetica, page and header colors, header height, the protected homepage name composition
and the boundary around a dark plate. Existing accessibility tests run axe on the main
pages, check overflow at three widths, keyboard focus and reduced motion. The broader
Playwright suite checks the retained interactions and analytical contracts.

See [design-system-audit.md](design-system-audit.md) for the migration inventory and review.

items.title: docs/design-system.md › Political workspace integration
items.text:
Political Observatory v2 reuses this token system and existing `Feature`, chart, control
and party-identity components. `politik/workspace/workspace.css` owns its twelve-column
layout, neutral position symbols, compact navigation and local matrix scrolling. No new
global tokens or homepage styles were introduced. See [workspace implementation](political-observatory-v2.md).

items.title: docs/development.md › Development workflow
items.text:
Start from the current accepted branch. Query the graph for the affected code, then
read the relevant source. Define the behavior to preserve or change and its check.

items.title: docs/development.md › Verification levels
items.text:
| Level | Command | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quick | `npm run verify:quick` | TypeScript, formatting, frontend and Worker unit tests |
| Full | `npm run verify:full` | Quick checks, one production build, Python suite, security browser tests and complete E2E |
| Delivery | `npm run verify:delivery` | Real data contracts, pipeline registry and politics delivery reconciliation; may use the network |

Quick checks are the local floor. Add the relevant Python or browser tests for the
behavior you change. Documentation-only edits need copy and link review. Shared
frontend, routing, security and integration changes need Full. Data export or
delivery changes need Delivery as well. GitHub retains all required checks on PRs
and main, including real delivery checks; local scopes do not replace that gate.

Use `node scripts/verify.mjs full --plan` to inspect commands without running them.
Checks stop at the first failure. Logs and each Python run's isolated temporary
directory live under ignored `tmp/checks/`. The console shows status, elapsed time
and a short failure excerpt. A local Full run reuses its build for security tests.
Successful Python fixtures are removed from that run's own directory; failed
fixtures and all logs remain available for investigation.

items.title: docs/development.md › Verification levels
items.text:
Preflight checks disk space and existing dependencies without installing or deleting
anything. Quick requires 2 GiB free; Full and Delivery require 4 GiB. These are
starting thresholds, not storage quotas. Local Playwright uses one worker; CI uses
two. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS` explicitly when resources permit. An existing browser
can be selected with `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH`.

Run expensive checks once per relevant change. Save detailed output in the logs;
do not paste successful test lists or large generated data into agent context.
Poll remote CI no more than once per minute and report only changed outcomes.

items.title: docs/development.md › Workspaces
items.text:
`npm run workspaces` reports branch, dirty state and whether each HEAD is included
in the cached `origin/main`. It flags ignored local files without reading their
contents. It does not fetch, archive, reset or remove anything.
Refresh remote references before deciding what is merged. A retirement candidate
is a review prompt, not proof that an Orca terminal or editor is inactive.

Keep one integration branch for a task. Start new tasks from accepted main; do not
start from an old dirty workspace. Existing dirty workspaces retain their owners
and must not be reset or copied wholesale into a new task.

After a merge, confirm the exact commit on remote main, stop or park the owning
terminal, and inspect `git status` in the source workspace. Only then remove a
clean, unlocked, merged worktree with `git worktree remove <exact-path>`. Preserve
branches, uncommitted work and ignored local data. Review and preserve private
profiles, `.env` files and warehouses before removal; Git's clean state omits them.
Never use force removal as cleanup. Keep the primary
main checkout and any active workspace. A dependency installation may be reused
locally only when package-lock.json is identical; CI always installs from its lock.

items.title: docs/development.md › Skills and extraction
items.text:
`CLAUDE.md` routes skills by the actual change. Keep upstream skill documents for
reference; loading every design guide is unnecessary for a markup-preserving move.
The approved visual direction remains in `docs/design-system.md` and `tokens.css`.

Split large files by responsibility as they are touched. Preserve public entrypoints,
markup, state ownership and failure behavior. For example, the projects page owns
composition while workflow history, ingestion records, pipeline tables and warehouse
inspection have their own modules. Verify the affected page on desktop and mobile.

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Gold semantic model
items.text:
The portfolio serves a **static, versioned gold layer** at `frontend/public/data/gold/`. It is rebuilt from the checked-in Parliament, budget, language, JobTech, Allegoria and RFC exports with `python platform/legacy/build_gold.py`. It requires no live API or database. `semantic-model.json` is the machine-readable contract: table paths, row counts, observed column types, grains, primary keys, relationships, metric definitions, source hashes and output hashes.

**Two builders, one definition.** dbt builds nine of the 31 tables (`fact_language_area`, `fact_language_coverage`, `mart_budget_language_gap`, `fact_topic_session_party`, `fact_activity`, `fact_budget_outturn`, `fact_rfc_version`, `mart_party_session_vote`, `mart_party_agreement`) and the vote marts in `platform/models/gold/politics/`; `platform/publish/export_politics.py` delivers them and reconciles them byte for byte (`--check`). The other 22 tables and the budget-report, jobs, debate, RFC and overview marts are still built in Python by `build_gold.py`, outside dbt. The metrics and relationships are defined once, in dbt YAML: each metric is a dbt (MetricFlow) metric whose `gold` meta is its entry here, and the relationships and the unavailable `validated_vote_direction_pairs` sit on the `gold_semantic_model` exposure (`platform/models/gold/politics/schema.yml`). `export_politics.py` writes both from the dbt manifest; `build_gold.py` carries them forward.

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Layers and ownership
items.text:
| Layer | Location | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source / bronze | `frontend/public/data/politics/parliament/`, `platform/sources/allegoria/` | Original exported snapshots and offline law documents; keep for audit. |
| Curated / silver | `frontend/public/data/politics/decisions/`, `frontend/public/data/politics/laws/`, `frontend/public/data/debates/budgets/`, `frontend/public/data/reports/`, `frontend/public/data/jobs/` | Parsed, corrected or indexed material. The exact-year budget correction lives here. |
| Gold facts and dimensions | `frontend/public/data/gold/tables/` | One explicit grain and key per table. No double-counting the source partitions or v1/v2 law overlap. |
| Gold presentation marts | `frontend/public/data/gold/marts/` | Small, stable JSON contracts consumed by the site; document and transcript details remain lazy-loaded from their curated source shards. |

**Build order:** regenerate upstream political and report exports when sources change, then run the gold builder and validator. A source hash mismatch causes validation to fail until gold is rebuilt. Gold JSON is committed so the static site builds without Python in its deployment environment.

```powershell
python platform/pipeline.py run legacy   # build_gold.py, dbt +tag:politics, export_politics.py, ...
python platform/legacy/validate_gold.py
npm run build
npm run test:e2e
```

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Main grains and keys
items.text:
| `fact_language_area` | 10,368 | `corpus + method + session + party + expenditure_area` |

| `mart_budget_language_gap` | 2,700 | Same language grain, **only** where a party has all 27 budget areas |

| `fact_job_month_role` | 192 | `month + role`; unique ad IDs, not hires |

All 31 table schemas, including the smaller job, activity, RFC and precomputed vote-measure tables, are in [`semantic-model.json`](../frontend/public/data/gold/semantic-model.json). The broader physical source inventory is in [the data dictionary](data-dictionary.md).

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Joins and measure semantics
items.text:
```mermaid
erDiagram
    DIM_PARTY ||--o{ FACT_PARTY_VOTE : party
    FACT_DECISION_POINT ||--o{ FACT_PARTY_VOTE : point_id
    FACT_DECISION_POINT ||--o{ FACT_POINT_CITATION : point_id
    FACT_DECISION_POINT ||--o{ FACT_POINT_RESERVATION : point_id
    FACT_DECISION_POINT ||--o{ FACT_PROPOSITION_POINT_LINK : point_id_document_level
    FACT_DECISION_POINT ||--o{ FACT_MOTION_VOTE_LINK : vote_id_citation_only
    DIM_ACTOR ||--o{ FACT_BUDGET_FRAME : actor
    DIM_TOPIC ||--o{ FACT_TOPIC_SESSION_PARTY : model_id_topic_id
    DIM_TOPIC ||--o{ FACT_UMAP_SAMPLE : model_id_topic_id
    DIM_LAW_SNAPSHOT ||--o{ FACT_LAW_PROVISION : pool_document_id
```

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Joins and measure semantics
items.text:
- **Party position** is the largest recorded yes/no/abstain member-vote group for that party and roll call. This normalizes a damaged `Avstår` source label without changing vote counts. A yes refers to the *committee proposal*, which may reject a cited motion.
- **Party agreement** is same yes/no position divided by roll calls where both parties recorded yes/no. Abstentions are excluded. The published ordered-party matrix contains its numerator and denominator.
- **Cohesion** is the sum of each party's largest cast-vote group per roll call divided by all its cast member votes. **Recorded attendance** is cast votes divided by cast plus recorded absences. Pairing arrangements are unknown.
- **Budget–language difference** is `keyword_share_pct - budget_share_pct` in percentage points, keyed by session, party and expenditure area, *plus* a chosen corpus and matching method. It excludes incomplete party frames and missing party proposals. It is descriptive language attention, not support, intention or causal influence; speeches can postdate proposals.
- **Topic share** belongs to one named model run. Never join old and new topics on `topic_id` alone. UMAP is a deterministic sample with axes that have no direct political meaning.
- **Law direction** has no validated vote→versioned-provision→reviewed-annotation chain. The semantic model explicitly marks `validated_vote_direction_pairs` unavailable at zero; no tightening/loosening party score is published.

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Joins and measure semantics
items.text: The frontend reads the gold vote, budget, job, UMAP and RFC marts. Original member votes, citations, law text and full speeches are loaded on demand from their versioned source files. This keeps the initial interface responsive while preserving drill-down evidence.

items.title: docs/gold-semantic-model.md › Refresh and checks
items.text:
`build-gold.py` is deterministic: it writes no wall-clock build timestamp. It refuses duplicate or missing primary keys, unknown parties, orphaned vote points, incomplete eight-party roll calls, orphaned citations/reservations, unknown topic/model pairs and provisions without law snapshots. `validate-gold.py` independently checks source/output hashes, every table's declared key and row count, key relationships, party positions, corrected budget arithmetic, eligible budget-language joins, law provision totals and monthly/yearly job-ad reconciliation. Source-text hashes normalize CRLF to LF across operating systems; checked-in gold JSON is pinned to LF.

Gold keeps **facts, dimensions and marts distinct**. Do not add their row counts together: marts are materialized views of the facts. Legacy source exports stay available for reproducibility but are not interchangeable with the corrected and versioned gold tables.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Idea Lineage
items.text:
Data lineage explains where data came from. Idea Lineage explains why the system became what it
is: which ideas appeared, what was decided and why, what was tested, what was learned, what was
set aside and what is still open.

It records how thinking changes without slowing it down. An idea is material, not an obligation:
there are no due dates, streaks, completion rates or productivity scores, and none should be
added.

Three things with similar names do different jobs. Data Constellation shows how data moves through
the platform. Concept Constellation shows how ideas appear across corpora (stories, philosophy,
politics, law). Idea Lineage shows how the project's own ideas and decisions evolved over time.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › What is stored, and what never is
items.text:
Stored: short structured events. Each has a title (at most 140 characters), an optional summary
of one to four sentences, an optional reason, project ids, tags, an importance, a certainty and
links to other events. It can also carry experiment fields (question, hypothesis, method,
result, interpretation, limitations) and implementation references (commit, PR, files, route,
artifact, run, dataset). A source note says whether the event was entered by hand or extracted
from an answer. For an extracted answer, the note keeps the SHA-256 of that answer and the date,
never the answer itself.

Never stored: prompts, user messages, full assistant answers, transcripts, hidden reasoning, tool
traces or scratchpads. The schema is a closed list of keys. Keys such as `prompt`,
`user_message`, `conversation`, `raw_response` and `chain_of_thought` are refused at any depth,
and every free-text field is capped at 600 characters. `platform/tests/idea_lineage` fails if
one slips through.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Event model
items.text:
```yaml
id: decision-2026-10-07-006        # <type>-<date recorded>-<NNN>, readable and unique
created_at: 2026-10-07T15:20:00+00:00
occurred_on: 2026-10-07            # optional: when it happened, if not when recorded
type: decision                     # idea | decision | hypothesis | experiment | finding | question
                                   # (also rejection | implementation | observation)
title: Open the concept layer with Concept Journey
summary: >
  Follow one concept at a time through stories, philosophy, Riksdag speeches and the AI Act.
reason: A reader can follow one idea more easily than read the whole constellation.
projects: [concept-constellation, symbolic-atlas, philosophy-atlas, politics, ai-act]
tags: [concepts]
importance: major                  # minor | normal (default) | major
status: active                     # as written; see "effective status" below
certainty: confirmed               # proposed | tentative | confirmed
visibility: public                 # private (default) | public
relations: {supersedes: [idea-2026-10-04-003]}
inferred_relations: {related_to: [idea-2026-10-05-002]}   # suggested, never presented as certain
implementation: {commit: 278a788}
source: {kind: manual, session_date: 2026-10-07}
```

Only `id`, `created_at`, `type` and `title` are required. Project ids are the ones in
`frontend/src/projects/projectRegistry.ts`, plus `portfolio` for work on the site as a whole.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Event model
items.text:
A relation on event E reads "E *relation* target", and new events point at older ones:
`inspired_by`, `evolved_from`, `supersedes`, `replaces`, `contradicts`, `tests`, `supports`,
`rejects`, `implements`, `answers`, `results_from`, `applies_to` and `related_to`. The passive
forms (`evolved_into`, `tested_by`, `supported_by`, `rejected_by`, `implemented_as`,
`resulted_in`) are accepted and read the other way. Links need not form a tree. Every target must
exist when the event is written.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › The journal is append-only
items.text:
```
.idea-lineage/journal/2026-10-07.jsonl          private, git-ignored
.idea-lineage/public/journal/2026-10-07.jsonl   public, committed
```

One JSON line per event, one file per day. A line is never edited. When a direction changes, a
new event says so (`supersedes`, `rejects`, `answers`, `evolved_from`), and the views derive the
earlier event's *effective status* from it: superseded, abandoned, answered or evolved. An append
writes nothing unless every event in the batch passes validation and has an unused id.

Because this repository is public, private events never enter it: `.idea-lineage/*` is
git-ignored except `public/`. Set `IDEA_LINEAGE_HOME` to keep the private journal somewhere
durable, such as a private repository. A cloud session's container is discarded, and the default
home goes with it.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Capturing events
items.text:
From a final answer, never a conversation:

```bash
npm run ideas:extract -- --input answer.txt          # review: shows candidates, writes nothing
npm run ideas:extract -- --input answer.txt --apply  # appends them
IDEA_LINEAGE_MODE=auto npm run ideas:extract < answer.txt
```

The extractor favours precision over recall and takes only what an answer marks itself:

- a fenced `idea-lineage` block holding JSON events;
- labelled lines: `Decision:`, `Idea:`, `Hypothesis:`, `Experiment:`, `Finding:`,
  `Open question:`, `Rejected:`, `Implementation:`, `Observation:`, with Swedish equivalents
  such as `Beslut:`, `Idé:`, `Fynd:`, `Öppen fråga:` and `Avfärdat:`;
- bullets under a heading with one of those names (`## Decisions`, `### Öppna frågor`).

It does not mine prose. It never makes a claim stronger than the wording:

- A "decision" with hedges ("could", "would", "maybe", "kanske", "skulle") is stored as an idea
  with certainty `proposed`.
- A finding without a number is `tentative`.
- Text after "because" or "eftersom" becomes the reason.

Projects are found by name, for example "Symbolic Atlas", "AI Act" or "Concept Journey". When an
item names none and the whole answer names exactly one, that project is used; `--project` sets it
explicitly.

It does not record every answer. An answer without marked items records nothing, so
confirmations, routine fixes and explanations leave no trace.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Capturing events
items.text:
Input that looks like a conversation export (speaker turns, or a JSON `messages` or `role`
array) is refused.

Duplicates:

- The answer's SHA-256 stops the same answer being extracted twice.
- An item that matches an event of the same type from the last 30 days is skipped. The match is
  a token Jaccard of at least 0.8 over title and summary.
- A near match (0.5 to 0.8) is kept and linked to the earlier event as an inferred `related_to`.

History is never merged.

By hand:

```bash
npm run ideas:add -- --type idea --project symbolic-atlas --title "Test translator centring"
npm run ideas:add -- --type finding --project symbolic-atlas --title "…" --results-from experiment-2026-10-07-002 --commit efe3595
```

`add.py` suggests earlier events with similar titles but never blocks saving. `--public` writes
to the public journal.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Views (derived, rebuilt whole)
items.text:
`npm run ideas:build` rebuilds every view from the journal. `ideas:state`, `ideas:diary` and
`ideas:export` rebuild one each. Each Markdown file begins with "Generated from the Idea Lineage
journal. Do not edit".

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `state/<project>.md` | Current direction (the latest of the project's own decisions, a major one first), active decisions, hypotheses, experiments, latest findings, open questions, ideas, and what was superseded or set aside and by which event |
| `state/portfolio.md` | Portfolio-wide direction, projects with lineage, themes shared by tag across projects, recent major decisions, cross-project connections, open cross-project questions |
| `context.json` | Per project: active decisions, hypotheses, open questions and recent findings (ids and titles), for an agent to read before substantial work |
| `diary/<date>.md` | One readable page per day an event happened (`occurred_on`, else recorded) |
| `digests/<year>-W<week>.md` | The same for a week |
| `idea_lineage.duckdb` | `dim_event`, `dim_project`, `dim_tag`, `fact_relation`, `bridge_event_project`, `bridge_event_tag` for descriptive analysis |
| `frontend/public/data/idea-lineage/events.json` | Public events only, publishable fields only, links only between public events |

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Questions
items.text:
```bash
npm run ideas:search -- "construct validity"     # TF-IDF over title, summary, reason, tags
npm run ideas:history -- symbolic-atlas          # dated, with linked events
npm run ideas:why -- "book centring"             # walks the links back to the origin
```

```
WHY (book centring)
  2026-10-05  Finding: Book-centring cut the largest-book share from 74 % to 57 %
  ↓ results from
  2026-10-05  Experiment: Four deconfounding variants on one shared sample
  ↓ implements
  2026-10-05  Decision: Centre the embeddings by book before clustering
  ↓ inspired by
  2026-10-05  Hypothesis: Book identity confounds the representation
  ↓ inspired by
  2026-10-05  Finding: The baseline clusters followed books, not symbols
  ↓ results from
  2026-10-05  Idea: Map symbol words in myth and folklore without predefined meanings
```

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Public and private
items.text:
Every event is private unless written with `--public` or `visibility: public`. The exporter
reads only public events and drops `visibility` and `source`. It also drops any link to a
private event, so a public page cannot reveal that a private one exists. The public journal in
this repository holds the Symbolic Atlas lineage from its published results (research history,
commits 5 to 7 October 2026), the Concept Journey decision and the decision to keep this journal.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › The page
items.text:
The page is retired from the website: `#idea-lineage` now leads to the project index
([site-structure.md](site-structure.md)). The journal and its commands are unchanged. The page
read only `idea-lineage/events.json` and showed one view at a time:

- The timeline puts events by date on a thin thread, one shape per kind (an open circle for an idea, a
  filled square for a decision, a diamond for a hypothesis, a triangle for an experiment, a
  filled circle for a finding, a dashed circle for a question). Each event lists its stored
  links. "Why does this exist?" keeps only the events it came from, following those links back
  to the origin. Filters: project and kind.
- Projects now gives the current direction, active decisions, latest findings and open
  questions per project, derived the same way as the state files.
- Set aside lists the ideas and decisions a later event superseded or rejected, with that event's
  reason.

There are no counters, scores or due dates.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › For agents
items.text:
Before substantial work on a project, read `.idea-lineage/state/<project>.md` or `context.json`.
After substantial conceptual work, write the answer's decisions, ideas, findings and open
questions as labelled lines, then run `npm run ideas:extract` on that final answer. Tiny fixes
need neither. Nothing runs automatically; extraction is something you do, so it is always
visible.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Relation to Allegoria
items.text:
The design borrows from Allegoria's own records. Like `DATA_DECISIONS.md`, decisions are
append-only and a change is a new entry that supersedes the old one. Like its `predictions/`,
expectations are written as hypotheses before results. Its `[inferred]` labels become inferred
relations. No Allegoria file is moved or read automatically; an Allegoria decision can be
recorded here as an event with `--project allegoria` and a reference.

items.title: docs/idea-lineage.md › Known limitations
items.text:
- The extractor relies on answers marking their items. Unmarked prose records nothing, by design.
- Duplicate detection is lexical; two phrasings of one idea can both be kept, linked as related
  at best.
- Project detection is by name and alias, so an unnamed project needs `--project`.
- An event cannot change visibility after it is written. To publish a private idea, write a new
  public event; the private one stays where it is.
- In a cloud session the private journal is lost with the container unless `IDEA_LINEAGE_HOME`
  points somewhere durable.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Feature engineering and clustering ensemble — 4 October 2026
items.text:
The current experiment combines **65% cleaned multilingual text embeddings, 15% title
patterns and 20% detected technology mentions**, then takes agreement from three
independent UMAP/HDBSCAN fits. It assigns **5,210 of the same 6,123 ads** to **17 groups**,
leaving **913 (14.91%)** as noise. No group has a majority from one employer. This is a
more useful grouping for technology/role exploration, with explicit tradeoffs in the
original full-text geometry; it is not a validated occupational taxonomy.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Features and ablations
items.text:
Eight feature recipes were tested with two UMAP representations (30 neighbours/5D and
60 neighbours/10D), three minimum cluster sizes (40/60/100), two minimum samples (3/5)
and eom/leaf selection: **192 fits**. The [complete candidate table](job-clustering-features.csv)
includes the exactly reused previous input vectors and configuration, not a renormalised
approximation of the baseline. All fits use the full eligible corpus; one fixed 1,200-row
sample supplies pairwise diagnostics, excluding each fit's noise.

| Single fit | Groups | Noise | Largest group | Assigned ads in majority-employer groups | Raw cosine silhouette | Clean cosine silhouette | Own feature cosine silhouette |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous raw model, 30/5, size 60, samples 5, leaf | 25 | 47.90% | 4.69% | 19.28% | .0739 | .0366 | .0739 |
| Clean text, 30/5, size 100, samples 3, eom | 9 | 49.76% | 11.35% | 0% | .0613 | .0625 | .0625 |
| Clean + title, 60/10, size 100, samples 5, eom | 21 | 13.64% | 9.95% | 0% | −.1008 | −.0988 | .1665 |
| Balanced three-view input, 60/10, size 100, samples 3, eom | 17 | 11.81% | 11.40% | 0% | −.0603 | −.0620 | .1024 |
| More skill weight, 60/10, size 100, samples 3, eom | 13 | 5.41% | 46.32% | 0% | −.0497 | −.0403 | .0548 |
| Additional lexical view, 60/10, size 100, samples 3, eom | 4 | 4.85% | 58.84% | 0% | .0957 | .0809 | .1281 |

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Features and ablations
items.text:
The lowest noise solutions restore a giant group and were rejected. Clean + title and
balanced inputs were profiled and checked across seeds. The balanced ensemble was chosen
for more coverage, a moderate largest group, diverse technology profiles and lower
weighted top-employer concentration than the reviewed title-heavy alternative. The old
ranking based on raw-vector silhouette favours the nine-group clean-only fit; it does
not automatically determine the adopted solution.

**The original and cleaned semantic-only silhouettes become negative.** The hybrid defines
similarity partly through title and technology features, so it sacrifices cohesion in
the prior full-text geometry. Own-feature silhouette is positive but modest and is partly
circular because those features construct the clusters. Increased coverage, lower employer
concentration and reproducibility justify an exploratory replacement; they do not prove
better semantic clustering under every definition of similarity. Assigned subsets also
change as noise changes, so scores are not measured on identical retained rows.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Text cleanup
items.text:
HTML is converted to text, URLs/emails are removed and descriptions are split into
segments. Repeated nontechnical segments appearing across at least 0.5% of distinct
original text inputs (minimum eight), and selected recruitment/benefit wording, are
removed. Segments mentioning any technology in the existing skill vocabulary are protected,
including negated mentions. If cleaning would empty a description, its text is retained.

3,461 ads lose segments, and 91.5% of original characters remain. Common removed text
includes application invitations, recruitment-test descriptions and repeated staffing-company
introductions. No ads, languages, employers or years are excluded. Local audit Parquet records
removed segments per job ID, and its report records examples and counts. Cleaning remains a
heuristic and may remove meaningful generic/soft-skill content or retain technical boilerplate.

The clean embedding input uses title, cleaned description and detected technologies.
Unlike the original input, it does not append JobTech's separate supplied skill labels
(nonempty in 73 ads); description text remains available. That is another representation
change, not a pure boilerplate-only ablation.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Feature models
items.text:
The same pinned multilingual MiniLM encoder is used for 384D cleaned text vectors; no
second neural encoder or paid model service is introduced. The title model uses word
unigrams/bigrams, a token pattern preserving `.NET`, `C++` and `C#`, TF-IDF and a seeded
48D SVD. The technology model reweights the existing 32-label skill bridge with TF-IDF;
it does not duplicate extraction regexes. The lexical-description ablation uses 128D SVD
but was not selected. These transformations follow the documented
[TF-IDF](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)
and [TruncatedSVD](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD.html) APIs.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Feature models
items.text:
Each view is L2-normalised, multiplied by the square root of its weight, concatenated,
then normalised again. Thus squared view contributions correspond to the declared weights;
raw block dimension/magnitude does not dominate. The selected input has 464 dimensions.
23.7% of ads have no detected technology mentions; their skill block is zero and the
remaining views are renormalised. Missing mentions are not claims that an ad needs no skills.
Role, seniority, employer, region and year are excluded from features. Title features can
still reproduce title-rule categories and language variants; role cross-tabs are descriptive
and not independent ground truth. Vocabulary/SVD are fitted on the complete exploratory corpus,
not a train/test split for predicting future ads.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Three-fit consensus and validation
items.text:
Selected parameters: cosine UMAP, 60 neighbours, 10 dimensions, minimum distance 0;
HDBSCAN minimum cluster size 100, minimum samples 3, eom. Fits at seeds **42/43/44**
are aligned using maximum overlap assignment with
[SciPy's linear assignment solver](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment.html).
Ambiguous ties are rejected; an alternate cluster must have a majority of its overlap in
its matched reference group. A point is assigned only with at least **two votes out of three**.

The reference fit determines the available consensus cluster identities, so new groups
found only in alternate fits may be rejected. Noise can gain an assignment if the other
two fits agree. A consensus group can have fewer points than its component fit's minimum
size because voting removes boundary points. This is a seed ensemble of the same model
family, plus feature fusion; it is not a bagged ensemble of independently trained neural encoders.

The delivered point support is **2/3 or 1 for assigned points, zero for noise**. It is a
vote fraction, not HDBSCAN membership or a calibrated probability that the label is true.
The UI distinguishes this meaning. Profiles use support for representative ads and retain
automatic-label uncertainty. A skill must occur in at least 15% of a group, with lift at
least 1.5, to enter its label; rarer distinctive mentions remain visible in the profile.
This avoids naming a 205-ad frontend group after 17 PHP mentions.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Three-fit consensus and validation
items.text:
| Ensemble seeds | Groups | Noise | ARI vs chosen ensemble, all rows including noise | ARI on mutually assigned ads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 42/43/44, delivered | 17 | 14.91% | 1 | 1 |
| 43/44/45 | 18 | 14.5% | .877 | .990 |
| 44/45/46 | 17 | 13.0% | .845 | .972 |
| **45/46/47, completely disjoint seeds** | **17** | **15.4%** | **.800** | **.989** |

The first two checks share seeds with the selected ensemble and are optimistic sensitivity
checks. The third uses entirely new seeds. Its common assigned core covers about 81% of
the corpus; high core agreement is not stability of every ad's assigned/noise status.
These are resampled initialisations on one corpus, not cross-year or employer-held-out validation.

Examples of delivered profiles: Python/SQL (234), Snowflake/dbt (699), React/JavaScript
(205), Kubernetes/Docker (157), C++/Linux (526 and 343) and C#/.NET (399).
Two mixed profiles (143 and 405) have weak differentiation. The 143-ad group contains
CNC/CAM and industrial-programming titles already included by the existing source role
rules; it is not silently relabelled as a precise software occupation. Groups can also
split related roles by title/language/technology coverage. Labels remain descriptive.
