items.title: docs/job-clustering-ensemble.md › Reproduce and deliver
items.text:
The display is an independent 2D UMAP of the fused features, using 60 neighbours, minimum
distance .08 and seed 42. It changes from the prior full-text map; clusters are still fitted
in 10D, not the display. Both original-text and fused-feature neighbour preservation are
reported. The fitted-cluster camera/full-map control uses genuine coordinates.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Job clustering parameter sweep — 4 October 2026
items.text:
The original five-cluster fit put 84.99% of the 6,123 advertisements in one mixed group.
The selected replacement produces **25 groups**, with the largest containing **287 ads
(4.69%)**. It assigns 3,190 ads and leaves **2,933 (47.90%)** as noise. This improves the
resolution of identifiable groups while reducing coverage; it does not establish a clean
occupational taxonomy for the whole dataset.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Search and selection
items.text:
The same corpus, 384D cached multilingual embeddings, model commit and random seed 42
were used for all **417 candidates**. No advertisements were removed, translated or
re-embedded, and no embeddings contain the title-rule role labels.

Grid: UMAP neighbours 10/30/60 × dimensions 5/15 × minimum distance 0/.1;
HDBSCAN minimum cluster size 20/30/60/100 × minimum samples 3/5/10/20 × eom/leaf.
The initial UMAP 30/15/.05 representation was also searched, and its original
HDBSCAN 50/10/eom fit was retained: 13 × 32 + 1 = 417.

Reductions and density hierarchies were reused. Cosine silhouette in original embeddings
and Euclidean silhouette in UMAP use one fixed sample of 1,200 ads, excluding noise for
each candidate. As different ads become noise, these are **not** evaluations on identical
assigned subsets. Full-corpus noise, largest-cluster share and employer concentration are
reported separately. The [complete candidate table](job-clustering-sweep.csv) contains
every setting and result; local assignments, reductions, profiles and seed checks are in
`warehouse/ml/jobs/sweeps/25820ae69496eeba/`.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Search and selection
items.text:
| Candidate | UMAP n / dimensions / min_dist | HDBSCAN size / samples / selection | Groups | Noise | Largest group | Original cosine silhouette | UMAP silhouette |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous | 30 / 15 / .05 | 50 / 10 / eom | 5 | 8.79% | 84.99% | −0.0882 | 0.2247 |
| **Selected** | **30 / 5 / 0** | **60 / 5 / leaf** | **25** | **47.90%** | **4.69%** | **0.0739** | **0.5222** |
| Finer eom fit | 30 / 5 / 0 | 30 / 5 / eom | 46 | 39.46% | 3.67% | 0.0654 | 0.5429 |
| Highest exploratory rank | 60 / 15 / 0 | 20 / 3 / leaf | 84 | 48.02% | 2.11% | 0.1185 | 0.5759 |

The exploratory rank is `original_silhouette − .3*noise_share − .5*largest_share
− .15*employer_majority_share`. It is a screening heuristic, not an accuracy metric.
Manual selection favoured a manageable number of interpretable groups, no dominant mixed
group, less than half the dataset as noise at seed 42 and stronger seed agreement than
the reviewed 46-group fit. The 25-group fit has better original-space separation and less
employer-majority concentration than the reviewed 46-group fit, although it assigns fewer ads.
The 84-group fit was not selected simply because it ranked higher.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Profiles
items.text:
Examples of the selected automatic descriptive profiles:

| ID | Label | Ads | Largest employer share |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | Databricks / dbt | 277 | 12.64% |
| 9 | Fabric / dbt | 163 | 5.52% |

| 15 | Angular / .NET | 100 | 45.00% |

| 18 | PHP / Node.js | 172 | 6.40% |

Six groups remain majority-employer groups, covering 615 ads (19.28% of assigned ads).
These include Deploja, Veritaz, Försäkringskassan, Axis and SAAB. Employer/template
concentration remains visible in the explorer. Some C++/Linux profiles repeat across
several groups: numbering and examples distinguish them, but the skill labels alone do
not establish separate occupations. Original-vector silhouette of approximately .074 is
modest despite the much stronger UMAP score; parameter tuning has not eliminated the
limitations of mean-pooled full advertisement text.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Seed sensitivity
items.text:
Both the 25-group and 46-group configurations were checked with seeds 43 and 44. UMAP
was refitted; HDBSCAN parameters were held constant. Adjusted Rand index handles
permuted cluster IDs.

| Selected fit seed | Groups | Noise | ARI vs seed 42, including noise | ARI on mutually assigned ads | Mutually assigned share of corpus |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 43 | 24 | 51.27% | .6136 | .9060 | 42.61% |
| 44 | 24 | 47.59% | .6751 | .8796 | 45.91% |

The 46-group alternative had mutually assigned ARI .7307/.7425 and all-row ARI
.5191/.5996. The selected fit has more consistent groups within the common assigned
core; membership/noise boundaries remain sensitive. The seed 43 fit puts more than half
the corpus in noise. These checks do not prove stability across years or employers.

items.title: docs/job-clustering-sweep.md › Reproduction and delivery
items.text:
These were the embedding-only defaults; the current pipeline uses the
[feature ensemble](job-clustering-ensemble.md). For this older run the independent display UMAP is 2D with 30
neighbours, minimum distance .08 and seed 42; clustering is performed in 5D. The changed
colours reflect new memberships in the same display geometry. The explorer supports
distinct colours beyond six groups and clickable numbered legend entries to isolate a
group. Noise, original-vector silhouette and the sweep/seed provenance remain visible.
The default camera fits the assigned clusters; it reports the number of ads outside the
frame and has a full-map control that includes every distant noise point. This is an
affine view change, not a refit, removal of ads or independent repositioning of groups.

The pipeline validates the chosen corpus, source metadata, model, parameters and package
versions, and checks the recomputed labels/probabilities against the reviewed assignments
before updating raw. dbt owns gold and the existing exporter supplies the map and homepage.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-graph-update.md
items.text:
﻿# Job Intelligence graph update

Updated 2026-10-18 with the installed Graphify interpreter. The local graph now contains **7,477 nodes, 18,394 edges and 661 communities**, compared with 6,289 nodes before this update.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-graph-update.md › Scope and evidence
items.text:
The update re-extracted 414 tracked code files: production frontend/platform code, selected scripts, Worker files and the canonical job-link SQL schema. The selection includes the Worker unit-test file. It also extracted 41 semantic nodes and 91 evidence-labelled edges from five public documents:

- `docs/job-intelligence.md`
- `docs/job-intelligence-report.md`
- `docs/compliance-intelligence/README.md`
- `docs/compliance-intelligence/architecture.md`
- `docs/compliance-intelligence/job-company-integration.md`

The broad repository has 947 structural candidates. This bounded update excludes unrelated ML, configuration and most tests. Tier-aware merging preserves unselected AST sources and previous semantic evidence; 3,536 prior nodes outside the selected source set remain present. Earlier document/media evidence was retained without claiming fresh verification. No CV, profile, private research, environment or raw collection file was read for this update.

New semantic edges carry exact source paths, line locations, evidence quotes and `EXTRACTED` confidence with score 1.0. No fuzzy entity merge or external model backend was used. SQL identity links retain their canonical table definition.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-graph-update.md › Verification and limitations
items.text:
Both local caches resolve these symbols to current source locations:

| Symbol              | Source                                                |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `JobIntelligence()` | `frontend/src/job-intelligence/JobIntelligence.tsx:9` |
| `rankJob()`         | `frontend/src/job-intelligence/ranking.ts:61`         |
| `useWorkspace()`    | `frontend/src/job-intelligence/useWorkspace.ts:13`    |
| `job_company_link`  | `platform/compliance_intelligence/job_links.sql:16`   |

Post-build diagnostics report zero missing/dangling endpoints and zero duplicate or collapsed edges, with **25 self-loops**. The graph has 318 isolated nodes and 343 nodes without a source path, including external-reference stubs. Community cohesion ranges from **0.026992615227909345 to 1.0**, median **1.0**; singleton communities can have perfect cohesion, so this is not an accuracy score.

The fresh extraction fragment separately reports 2,033 dangling-endpoint edges, 37 self-loops, two exact duplicates and 262 undirected same-endpoint collapses before merge. Fragment references can resolve against retained nodes or become reference stubs during graph construction. The post-build zero count does not prove that the extractor resolved every external symbol. The graph remains a navigation index; verify relationships against source before changing behavior.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-graph-update.md › Verification and limitations
items.text:
Seven entrypoints/scripts yielded no symbols. Windows multiprocessing failed and Graphify completed a sequential AST fallback. No dependency was installed. AST extraction failed-source list is empty.

AST used zero model tokens; external LLM API calls were zero. Host-session semantic input/output usage is unavailable to Graphify. Its zero counters must not be interpreted as zero session usage or a measured cost saving. No dollar-cost or token-reduction benchmark was measured.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-graph-update.md › Local outputs
items.text:
`graphify-out/graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, health diagnostics, scope receipts, manifests and cost annotations remain ignored local artifacts in both the integration checkout and the original checkout. Original-cache root metadata identifies its local query root and separately records the integration snapshot source. Previous graph/report/manifest/cost files are preserved in a timestamped local backup.

HTML was not regenerated because the graph exceeds 5,000 nodes. Any existing `graph.html` describes the earlier graph. This audit contains only generic implementation and verification information; graph contents are not added to Git.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Job Intelligence implementation report
items.text: Implementation date: 2026-10-18. The initial delivery was verified locally. Subsequent branch integration was explicitly authorised; see the integration note below.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Delivered experience
items.text:
`#jobb-it?job=JOB_ID` now opens a continuous research workspace. The desktop selector uses 22% of the layout, bounded to 220-270px; the selected advertisement uses the remaining width. Each pane scrolls independently. Mobile places the compact searchable selector above the same content. Selection stays in browser history and survives filtering, and the research pane resets to its top when switching jobs.

The right pane renders the full original advertisement, requirements, CV explanation and all nine company sections immediately. There are no mandatory tabs, expand controls or analysis buttons. Multiple independently verified employer roles produce separately attributed company sections. Unresolved identity never acquires another company's context.

Public visitors see generic analysis and newest-first jobs. Explicit local configuration enables private CV-based recommendations, best match first. The local qualification profile, evidence and recommendation export stay under ignored `.research/`; they are absent from public job payloads. The production application does not request the local profile endpoint.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Architecture and reuse
items.text:
The repository graph and repository instructions were consulted before source lookup. The graph did not cover several newer compliance/company modules, so targeted source inspection verified those relationships. The initial architecture plan was documented before implementation and is now maintained as [the architecture, contracts and methodology](job-intelligence.md).

Reused components and invariants:

- Official JobSearch ingestion, pagination/retries, time-window collection and immutable raw payload hashes.
- Existing canonical company registry, exact organisation-number/verified-alias resolution, separate recruiter/employer roles, SCB metadata and reviewed context datasets.
- Existing company loader, current jobs, source citations, Compliance Explorer, legal lifecycle and independent publication approval/expiry/withdrawal checks.
- Existing DuckDB/Parquet research outputs, versioned R2 delivery, Cloudflare infrastructure, React routing, shared chart components and grey/violet/Helvetica tokens.
- The frozen SCB 50-company compliance cohort and its sealed evidence. Its artifact manifest was verified unchanged.
- The separate Labour Market Observatory, legacy compliance links and canonical `/companies/:companyId` route.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Architecture and reuse
items.text:
Added fulltext publication packages, conservative requirement extraction, continuous presentation, a deterministic relevance engine, a local-only profile adapter and a reproducible private ranking CLI. Existing company evidence links, related-job cards and legal release rendering now have separate cohesive modules to respect the repository's code-file size rule, with their approval fingerprints retained. No backend framework, identity namespace or dependency was added.

The shared immutable staging helper now retries only bounded Windows access/sharing locks during atomic directory finalisation. Existing output is never replaced. Permanent failure and immutable-output tests remain enforced.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Ranking methodology
items.text:
The shared browser/CLI engine computes `round(100 * sum(weight * factor) / sum(assessed weights))`. Defaults are explicit-required skills 35%, preferred skills 10%, target role 20%, experience/seniority 15%, location 15% and education 5%. Configured but unassessed factors leave the denominator. An entirely unassessed weighting cannot recommend a job.

Each explicit requirement retains its original sentence, field and line. CV evidence is evidenced, partial or not evidenced; the last state does not mean the person lacks the skill. Ambiguous advertisement mentions do not become mandatory requirements. Professional years remain unknown unless explicitly documented; internships and projects are not converted into full-time years.

Unestablished required experience of at least three years, substantial required management and conflicting specified degrees cap the score at 39 and exclude automatic recommendation. Senior/lead/staff/principal and DBA/infrastructure-only roles cap it at 49. Alternative qualifications, unspecified seniority, supported remote arrangements and 0-2-year ranges are handled separately.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Ranking methodology
items.text:
Recommendation requires direct target-role compatibility, the configurable threshold and no blocking experience/degree condition. Sorting prioritises suitability, then absence of potential required-condition uncertainty, score and stable job ID. Newest-first sorting remains available. This is an explainable research estimate, without ATS or calibrated hiring-probability claims.

The local profile separates documented qualification facts from location/role preferences. It records internships and projects without inventing professional years. The initial qualification file was checked against the supplied CV and excludes personal contact fields. Public visitors never receive that profile.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Contracts and safety
items.text: Complete field contracts, source interpretation, privacy rules and API responses are documented in [job-intelligence.md](job-intelligence.md#public-data-contracts). Executable contracts are in `configs/delivery/schemas/job-workspace.json`, `model.ts`, `profile.ts` and `ranking.ts`.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Contracts and safety
items.text:
- `job_id -> job_company_link -> company_id` remains the only company join. Parent/subsidiary findings are not transferred.
- Metadata, latest-50 fulltext and disjoint remaining fulltext share release timestamps and registry identity. Each text record is bound to its original payload hash. Quotes are validated against source lines.
- Text is rendered through React as text, with no active HTML. HTTPS links reject unsafe schemes, credentials, local/private addresses, unsafe ports and malformed URLs. Dedicated contact fields are excluded; known contact names, emails and phone numbers are redacted with a disclosed count.
- Current expiry/removal signals are applied during projection and rendering. Original source wording and whitespace are preserved apart from disclosed contact redactions.
- Local profile access requires explicit non-VITE configuration, a loopback connection/host and same origin. Responses are private/no-store. There is no production/preview endpoint, upload flow, applicant persistence or external CV transmission.
- Public negative legal records still require exact attribution, review, Gold approval and independent current publication approval. New presentation files enter the publication fingerprint. Old approvals require fresh staging/review before a changed legal presentation can publish.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence-report.md › Validation receipts
items.text:
Earlier full-suite attempts exposed disk exhaustion and transient Windows staging locks. Completed test artifacts were compressed without deleting evidence; bounded lock retries were regression-tested. A simultaneous browser/security run also collided in Playwright's shared artifact directory; the final full browser run uses a separate output directory. Test assertions and publication safeguards were retained.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Job Intelligence
items.text: Job Intelligence is a continuous job research workspace at `#jobb-it?job=JOB_ID`. The reader selects an advertisement once and reads its full wording, requirements, CV explanation and company evidence in one pane. Desktop uses a 22% list capped at 270px; both panes scroll independently. Mobile puts a searchable selector above the same continuous content. Company sections have no reveal buttons or tabs.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Modes and user journeys
items.text:
Public visitors get the latest 50 unexpired advertisements in the observed JobSearch window, generic requirements and verified company context. No applicant profile or personalised recommendations are published.

Local personalisation is opt-in. A qualification-only profile in ignored `.research/` supplies documented CV facts. Location preferences, target-role weights, factor weights and the recommendation threshold are separate configuration. The browser ranks the complete fresh candidate set and displays up to 50 relevant jobs, best match first. Newest-first sorting remains available within these recommendations. Fewer than 50 qualifying ads is an explicit state.

Selected advertisements survive filters and browser history. A shared link on the public site opens the same advertisement with generic analysis. `/companies/:companyId` and all `#compliance*` links continue to work. The separate Labour Market Observatory keeps its name, routes and analytics.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Repository audit and reuse
items.text: There was no CV matching engine. This implementation adds bounded deterministic matching; it does not claim to implement an employer ATS. Financial statements, historical workforce data, contracts, verified repository ownership, corporate events and issuer/price histories are not assumed to exist.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Storage and delivery
items.text:
`JobSearch → immutable raw.job_ads → existing company resolution → public metadata + text packages → pinned jobs R2 release → React`.

The canonical join remains `job_id → job_company_link → company_id`. Automatic resolution means advertised employer, with separate evidence required for recruiter and actual-employer roles. Names, brands, parents, subsidiaries and securities issuers are never substituted for one another.

When multiple legal entities have independently verified roles in one advertisement, their company sections render separately in the same pane, with a documented actual employer first. Evidence and legal records stay scoped to each canonical ID. An unverified advertiser remains explicitly withheld.

All three job JSON files share `generated_at`, `valid_until` and `registry_hash`. Fulltext entries additionally bind to the exact advertisement `document_hash`. The publisher validates the entire batch before replacing local public files. The existing R2 release system activates the complete version together. Both text files belong exclusively to the jobs group; jobs-analysis excludes them.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Public data contracts
items.text:
| File / entity | Grain and fields |
| --- | --- |
| `jobs/company-intelligence.json` | Existing schema v1: jobs, verified/unresolved links, companies, relationships, reviewed context, source coverage and reconciling metrics |
| Job metadata extensions | Optional `normalized_skills[]`, `seniority[]` (mentions), `remote_evidence[]`; original employer, workplace, location, timestamps, source URL and payload hash retained |
| `jobs/workspace.json` | Latest 50 at publication: schema v1, state, observation/expiry, registry hash, selection rule and `jobs[]` |
| `jobs/workspace-remaining.json` | Disjoint remainder of the observed active population; loaded only for older selected jobs or opt-in local ranking |
| Fulltext record | `job_id`, `document_hash`, `source_url`, `description_text`, `text_origin`, `contact_redactions`, safe `application_url` or null, employment type, working hours, duration, salary, salary type, remote wording, analysis |
| Analysis | Version, limitations and requirements with `label`, `category`, `strength` (`required`, `preferred`, `ambiguous`), `source_field`, line and exact quote |

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Public data contracts
items.text:
Primary text is about 380 KB and the remainder about 4.3 MB for the measured batch. Metadata and canonical company summaries are fetched once. Switching jobs belonging to the same entity reuses loaded company data. Full source text is rendered as React text with an empty HTML allowlist; it is never passed to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Formatted-only source text is converted to text. Original wording and whitespace remain except disclosed email, phone and known contact-name redactions. Dedicated contact fields are excluded. Original raw payloads stay private.

JobSearch is listed as CC0 in the [official data-service catalogue](https://data.jobtechdev.se/dataservice). This does not remove privacy obligations. Expiry/removal signals are applied when collecting/projecting, deadlines are checked again in the browser, and releases expire after at most two days. Withdrawals between refreshes remain a live-source limitation. Source timestamps without offsets use the documented Stockholm client interpretation; original timestamps remain available.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Private qualification contract
items.text:
`SearchProfile` schema v1 is defined and validated in `frontend/src/job-intelligence/profile.ts`:

- `source`: `kind=candidate_supplied_cv`, SHA-256 of the reference CV.
- `facts.skills[]`: canonical skill, `evidenced` or `partial`, source reference and exact qualification excerpt.
- `facts.experience[]`: internship/project kind, label, evidenced skills, source reference and excerpt.
- `facts.professional_years`: documented number or null. Internships/projects never become invented full-time years.
- `facts.education`: documented level, credits, completion date, reference and excerpt.
- `preferences`: ordered locations, remote preference, target-role weights, six factor weights and minimum score.

Unexpected fields and email/phone patterns are rejected. The initial local profile was checked against the supplied CV and excludes contact details. There is no new CV upload, applicant database, external model call or public recommendation export. The portfolio's pre-existing CV download remains outside this feature.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Local API and ranking result
items.text:
`GET /__local/job-intelligence-profile` exists only in Vite development. It requires an explicit `JOB_INTELLIGENCE_PRIVATE_PROFILE`, loopback connection and host, same origin, GET method and a real JSON path under `.research/`. Responses are private/no-store. Remote and cross-origin requests receive 403; disabled configuration receives 404; invalid configuration receives 422 without logging its contents. Vite denies direct filesystem access to `.research/`, environment files and private lineage files. Production and preview do not install this endpoint; production JavaScript does not request it.

`Relevance` v1 contains `job_id`, bounded score, suitability, potential blockers with advertisement quotes, each explicit requirement's evidence state, six factor values/weights/explanations, matched role and version. Browser calculation is in memory. The private CLI adds source file hashes, profile configuration hash, engine hash, as-of time, original advertisement hashes/URLs/timestamps and verified canonical company IDs. Its output is restricted to `.research/`.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Relevance methodology
items.text:
The estimate is `round(100 × Σ(weight × factor) / Σ(assessed weights))`. It is a reproducible research heuristic, not a calibrated hiring probability. Missing assessed factors are excluded from the denominator. An entirely unassessed configured weighting returns zero and no recommendation.

| Factor | Initial weight | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required skill evidence | .35 | Unique explicit required skills: evidenced = 1, partial = .5, not evidenced = 0 |
| Preferred skill evidence | .10 | Same calculation for preferred skills |
| Role | .20 | Configured target-role title compatibility; indirect body-only signal is insufficient for recommendation |
| Experience / seniority | .15 | Explicit junior signal = 1; unspecified seniority = .75; senior title = .15; conflicting stated experience lowers it further |
| Location | .15 | First preferred location = 1; configured nearby location = .85; supported remote/hybrid mention = .8; outside preference = .35; unspecified = .5 |
| Education | .05 | Source requirements compared with documented qualification; equivalent-experience alternatives remain uncertain, not automatically satisfied |

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Relevance methodology
items.text:
Required skills not evidenced by the CV, citizenship/security/language conditions, degree equivalence and stated professional years appear separately as conditions to verify. They do not prove the person lacks the competence. Required experience of three or more years not established by the CV, substantial required management experience and specific incompatible degree requirements cap the estimate at 39 and exclude automatic recommendation. Senior/lead/staff/principal titles and DBA/infrastructure-only roles cap it at 49. A role without "junior" is eligible; unspecified working arrangements do not exclude it. Explicit alternative qualifications and 0–2-year ranges are handled separately.

Recommendation requires direct configured role compatibility of at least .5, the configured score threshold (initially 50) and no blocking experience/degree condition. Sorting uses suitability, absence/presence of potential hard-condition uncertainty, score descending, then stable job ID. Consequently required-condition evidence takes precedence over a small weighted-score difference. Preferred-role weights and locations are editable locally. Unknown and inferred advertisement mentions never become explicit requirements.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Relevance methodology
items.text: The vocabulary and sentence rules are bounded. Number words, ranges and negations have tests, but indirect wording, equivalent degrees and nuanced seniority still require reading the original advertisement. The model does not infer a company's ethics, legal risk or hiring decision.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Current data and missing sources
items.text:
The measured official collection was observed 2026-10-17T21:53:55Z: 601 active Data/IT source records, 600 Swedish eligible ads after excluding an explicitly Swiss workplace, 246 verified company profiles, 590 verified advertised-entity links, one ambiguous and nine unresolved links. One advertisement subsequently reached its deadline, leaving 599 current candidates at the local check. The latest 50 have readable source text; 41 have a separate validated HTTPS application URL, with original advertisement links for the others. Twenty contain disclosed contact redactions. These counts describe this snapshot and are not a permanent benchmark.

The local run selected 25 suitable advertisements from those 599, all with verified advertised-entity links. Three carry explicit conditions requiring further verification. This is intentionally fewer than 50. Named recommendations and qualification evidence remain in the private report, not in public datasets.

Missing reviewed enrichment: company financial history/ratios, exact historical employee counts, long hiring history, procurement/client evidence, verified repository ownership, corporate events and stock/issuer series. Existing context rows can render automatically when approved and directly attributed; five-year financial and workforce charts need real compatible observations first. Current hiring counts by publication day are shown where multiple days support comparison. They are observed postings, not confirmed hires or causal evidence.

Compliance remains independently gated. The current public release is unavailable pending human review. No unapproved named findings are published; missing coverage is never shown as zero violations. KKV coverage limitations and ranking holds remain. The frozen SCB compliance cohort is unchanged and independent of both the job population and private recommendations.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Run locally
items.text:
From the repository root in PowerShell, using the existing installed dependencies:

```powershell
$env:VITE_DELIVERY_MODE = 'local'
Remove-Item Env:JOB_INTELLIGENCE_PRIVATE_PROFILE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
npm.cmd run dev
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5173/#jobb-it for generic public behaviour.
```

Stop that server, then enable the prepared ignored qualification profile:

```powershell
$env:VITE_DELIVERY_MODE = 'local'
$env:JOB_INTELLIGENCE_PRIVATE_PROFILE = '.research/job-intelligence/profile.json'
npm.cmd run dev
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5173/#jobb-it for local personalised discovery.
```

Edit that private JSON to change preferences or replace documented qualifications, then reload. Keep the source references/excerpts and actual CV hash; do not add contact fields. Unset the variable to disable personalisation. The profile is intentionally not committed, so another checkout must create its own validated qualification file. CV parsing/upload UI and a production access-controlled applicant service are not implemented.

Reproduce a private selection into a new filename:

```powershell
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/rank_local_jobs.mjs --profile .research/job-intelligence/profile.json --output .research/job-intelligence/next-ranking.json
# Optional: --as-of ISO_UTC_TIME within the still-fresh source observation period.
```

Refresh the existing official job pipeline, optionally using its existing SCB key or registry fallback:

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Run locally
items.text:
```powershell
python platform/publish/job_companies.py refresh --output .research/NEXT_UNIQUE_JOB_RUN --days 7 --publish
```

Here `--publish` writes local public JSON only. It does not deploy or send data to R2. Use unique output directories and never place private profiles/reviews in `frontend/public/`.

items.title: docs/job-intelligence.md › Deployment and validation
items.text:
No deployment is automatic. Publish the complete validated jobs R2 group (market, company metadata and both text packages), preserving exclusive group ownership, before a frontend release expects these files. Use existing Workers/static assets and delivery activation. Keep `SCB_API_KEY` backend-only. Deploy public generic behaviour; local personalisation requires a separate authorised access-controlled design before any production use. Any change to the company/workspace presentation requires a new exact-artifact compliance publication approval.

Final validation results and the exact changed-file inventory are in [implementation report](job-intelligence-report.md).

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Semantic structure of selected Swedish tech advertisements
items.text:
The question is whether natural groups in advertisement language match the four existing
title-based families: Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, Data Scientist and Software Developer.
This is **not** a model of the entire Swedish labour market, a count of hires, or a validated
occupational taxonomy. The all-occupation market report remains a separate product.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Architecture and ownership
items.text:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[JobTech historical archives] --> B[Existing candidate ingestion: raw.job_ads]
    B --> C[dbt bronze.stg_job_ads]
    C --> D[dbt silver.int_job_ads_enriched]
    D --> E[ml/jobs: title + description + source skills]
    F[gold.bridge_job_skills: existing mention extraction] --> E
    E --> G[Local multilingual sentence embeddings, cached by input hash and model commit]
    G --> R[Cleaned semantic vectors + title TF-IDF/SVD + technology TF-IDF]
    F --> R
    R --> H[UMAP: higher dimensional representation, three seeds]
    H --> I[HDBSCAN fits and aligned two-of-three consensus]
    R --> J[Separate UMAP: two display coordinates]
    I --> K[Profiles, diagnostics, role cross-tab]
    J --> K
    K --> L[Parquet run artefacts and raw.job_cluster_* sources]
    L --> M[dbt gold.mart_job_clusters and dim_job_cluster]
    M --> N[Dedicated compact delivery exporter]
    N --> O[React Canvas explorer]
    N --> P[Sample of real coordinates for homepage]
```

`ml/jobs/` extends the existing separate ML environment. Ingestion, role classification,
skill extraction and dbt remain in `platform/`; React consumes delivery. Python never
creates gold marts. The three `raw.job_cluster_*` tables are the ML-to-dbt boundary, imported
transactionally only after all coordinates and probabilities validate.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Architecture and ownership
items.text:
Cluster dbt models and their tests are opt-in through `job_clusters_enabled`. An ordinary
portfolio build does not require model weights or an ML warehouse. Existing reports and
data exports are not regenerated or replaced by this analysis.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Selection and provenance
items.text:
The loader queries `silver.int_job_ads_enriched`, retains precisely the four existing role
families and excludes empty descriptions. It uses `gold.bridge_job_skills` without copying
the extraction regexes. Role, seniority, publication year, region and employment type are
metadata and never enter the embedding input. Required skill labels supplied by JobTech
are included in addition to the existing detected mentions.

The published run (`efd2e318dc1621b2`) reads the **official 2022–2025 archives**, loaded with
the existing ingestion: 3,392,438 raw records and 87,287 retained candidates. dbt
classification and nonempty descriptions leave 35,861 analysis advertisements with 26,104
distinct input texts. The first run used the 2025 archive alone (6,123 ads). The candidate
universe is broader than the classified universe because candidate retention also uses
occupation matches and dbt applies title exclusions.

Archives: `https://data.arbetsformedlingen.se/annonser/historiska/<year>.jsonl.zip` for 2022,
2023, 2024 and 2025; each month's hash is in the coverage ledger.

SHA-256: `43499d2835b607f47e9641443e160bfcab26816c4f04fa17e87bb52b48ce79c6`

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Selection and provenance
items.text:
The archive includes publication-date spillover. A publication-year filter outside 2025
does **not** imply a complete additional annual archive. The delivery manifest includes
the archive coverage ledger, source hashes and whether a hash sample was requested.
Earlier archives can be appended with the existing ingestion and the same analysis rerun.
No fixture data can pass the analysis loader.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Embeddings and reproducibility
items.text:
Default model: `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`.
It is a local multilingual model producing 384-dimensional sentence/paragraph embeddings;
its relatively small size and multilingual training make it a practical Swedish/English
baseline. See the [model card](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2)
and [multilingual model documentation](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/blob/main/docs/sentence_transformer/pretrained_models.md).
The rule for model services, from [workers-ai.md](workers-ai.md):
"Endast öppen, publicerad data skickas till Workers AI. Besökarens text loggas aldrig och sparas inte."

The model has a short token window. The implementation divides each complete semantic input
into token-sized chunks, embeds them locally, computes a token-weighted mean and normalises
that vector. This avoids silently retaining only the beginning of a long advertisement.
Mean pooling can still overemphasise company boilerplate and dilute individual requirements;
the model is a baseline, not a model validated specifically on Swedish recruitment text.

Input whitespace and skill order are normalised; languages and spelling are retained.
SHA-256 covers the text representation version and exact normalised input. The model's
Hub commit is resolved before cache lookup. Cache identity includes that commit and the
chunking representation. One vector is stored per distinct text; duplicate ads reuse it.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Embeddings and reproducibility
items.text:
`warehouse/ml/jobs/embeddings-<identity>.parquet` stores job ID, text hash, model/revision,
representation, vector and timestamp. Batch checkpoints are atomically replaced, so an
interrupted run resumes. Warehouse, weights and source text remain gitignored.

Each run stores assignments, profiles and `report.json` under `warehouse/ml/jobs/runs/`.
Its identity incorporates text, delivered metadata, parameters, dependency versions,
implementation hash and coverage. The report records the resolved model commit, seed,
dependency versions, cache reuse and diagnostics. Fixed seed is reproducible within that
environment; different library versions or hardware can change the fitted space and IDs.
Cluster IDs are run-specific, not persistent occupational identifiers.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › UMAP and HDBSCAN
items.text:
The current defaults, selected after feature ablations and consensus checks, are cosine
UMAP with 60 neighbours, 10 dimensions and `min_dist=0` for
clustering, and an independent 2D UMAP with `min_dist=.08` for display. HDBSCAN operates on
the **10-dimensional space**, using Euclidean distance there, `min_cluster_size=600` (100 in
the 2025-only run; six times the ads, six times the minimum),
`min_samples=3`, and eom selection. Aligned fits at seeds 42/43/44 assign a group only
when two agree. Noise (`cluster_id=-1`) is retained. The input combines cleaned semantic
text, title patterns and detected technology mentions with weights .65/.15/.20. See
[feature and ensemble findings](job-clustering-ensemble.md) for the 192-fit ablations,
disjoint-seed check, limitations and exact reproduction commands. The earlier 417-candidate
embedding-only search remains available as a baseline with explicit parameters.
Each of these settings is exposed by the command-line interface.

See [UMAP's clustering guide](https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html).
UMAP can alter density and manufacture apparent separation. Display axes have no
interpretable units, and global geometry is not a calibrated measure of similarity or
causality. Year filtering hides points in the same fitted space; it never refits UMAP.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Profiles and evaluation
items.text:
Profiles contain counts, shares, role cross-tabs, title frequencies, seniority shares,
regions, years, smoothed skill lift and high-membership representative advertisements.
The dbt cluster dimension joins existing employer metadata to show the five largest
employer shares. A majority from one employer triggers an explicit warning in the profile.
Skill lift is compared against the entire analysis dataset, with minimum support and a
minimum lift of 1.5 and 15% within-group support for labels. Weak skill/title differentiation is labelled as a mixed
tech group instead of suggesting a precise occupation. Skills are mentions, including
optional or negated mentions; seniority remains the existing title-rule approximation.
For single fits, membership describes the HDBSCAN fit, not the truth of the label.
For consensus, the delivered support is the agreeing vote fraction (2/3 or 1, zero for noise).
Neither is a calibrated occupational-label probability.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Profiles and evaluation
items.text:
Diagnostics include cluster counts and sizes, noise share, mean membership, silhouette
in both the clustering representation and the original embeddings (cosine), excluding noise,
trustworthiness of the display against
cosine embedding neighbours, and adjusted Rand index/cross-tabs against existing roles.
The fused-feature map also reports trustworthiness against its own feature neighbours;
the original-text diagnostic remains separate.
Silhouette is null when not defined. Expensive pairwise diagnostics use a deterministic
sample capped at 1,500 rows, and the sample size is reported.

`--compare` reruns two alternatives: half the neighbour count and half the minimum cluster
size. These are sensitivity checks, not an automatic search for the prettiest picture.
The headline result and parameter comparisons are recorded in delivery, and the website
shows the role cross-tab alongside the map. The measured results are in the generated run
report, [the parameter sweep](job-clustering-sweep.md) and [the feature
ensemble](job-clustering-ensemble.md).

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Profiles and evaluation
items.text:
Repeated advertisements are distinct records, so recruitment templates and employer
language can create dense groups. Ad distribution is also highly imbalanced across roles;
Analytics Engineer has little support in this archive. A future employer-grouped and
template-deduplicated sensitivity study would help distinguish technology from wording.
The previous embedding-only sweep configuration was also checked at seeds 43 and 44. Agreement is reported
both for all rows including noise and for rows assigned by both fits; the latter covers
only 42.6–45.9% of the full dataset and must not be presented as stability of every ad.
The current ensemble's disjoint seed check covers an 80.94% common assigned core;
see [ensemble findings](job-clustering-ensemble.md) for both all-row and core agreement.
Cross-year or employer-grouped stability remains untested.

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Parameter sweep
items.text:
`python -m ml.jobs.sweep` runs offline against the pinned embedding cache, without changing
the database or delivery. It searches neighbours 10/30/60, dimensions 5/15 and clustering
`min_dist` 0/.1, plus the initial 30/15/.05 representation. Each representation tests
minimum cluster sizes 20/30/60/100, minimum samples 3/5/10/20 and eom/leaf selection;
the original 50/10/eom configuration is included separately: **417 candidates**.

UMAP representations and HDBSCAN hierarchies are reused, with resumable candidate checkpoints.
Cosine silhouette in the original vectors and Euclidean silhouette in UMAP use the same
fixed 1,200-ad diagnostic sample, excluding noise. Reports include largest-group share,
employer-majority share and membership. An exploratory ranking penalises noise, a dominant
cluster and employer-majority groups; it is not an accuracy metric or automatic promotion.

Profiles and seed review led to choosing the 25-group leaf configuration instead of the
highest-ranked 84-group fragmentation. See [sweep findings](job-clustering-sweep.md) and
the [complete candidate table](job-clustering-sweep.csv). `--review <candidate.json>` checks
two additional seeds and saves profiles; `--sweep-candidate <candidate.json>` in the pipeline
requires matching corpus, metadata, model, parameters and dependency versions, then verifies
the recomputed assignments against the reviewed candidate before writing raw tables.

`--database` and `ML_JOBS_DB` override the ML/export database. `--model` and `--revision`

items.title: docs/job-market-clustering.md › Rerun on Windows
items.text:
The exporter writes immutable JSON point shards of 5,000 rows, an aggregate manifest and
a 1,500-point real-coordinate homepage sample. It verifies run consistency and reconciles
row counts before export. Each point includes title and skill mentions for interaction,
never descriptions or embeddings. The full explorer is a separately loaded Canvas module;
the homepage requests only the compact sample and the political project preview.

The explorer provides role/cluster/seniority/year modes, a year selector, pointer details,
keyboard point traversal (arrows, Home/End, Enter and Escape), cluster selection and an
HTML cross-tab/profile fallback. Legend text and point details accompany colour encoding.
Loading, missing-data, retry and reduced-motion behaviour are covered by browser tests.

items.title: docs/job-market.md › The job market
items.text:
The Labour Market Observatory (`#jobb`) shows every job ad published on Arbetsförmedlingen
since 2020, in all occupations. The IT report on software and data roles, which reads whole ads, is
`#job-market-tech` (see `platform/ingest/jobtech/`).

items.title: docs/job-market.md › Source
items.text:
Arbetsförmedlingen's historical ads (JobTech), one archive per year and, for the current
year, one per quarter: <https://data.arbetsformedlingen.se/annonser/historiska/>. From 2020
to mid-2026 that is about six million ads and 6 GB of compressed JSON.

After the latest archive, ads are counted every morning from JobTech's stream
(<https://jobstream.api.jobtechdev.se>, open, no key), which returns every ad created, changed
or removed in a time window, in the archives' shape.

items.title: docs/job-market.md › Pipeline
docs/job-market.md › Pipeline
items.text:
later still counts, as in the archives. The stream cannot be read backwards (a past window

   holds only the ads whose last change fell in it, and a removed ad comes back without its

   publication date), so it counts from its first run: the days before are not counted, and a

   month enters the monthly series only when the stream covers it from its first day. The

   months between the latest archive and the stream's first whole month stay empty until their

   quarterly archive is published.

2. **Model**: dbt, tag `market` (`platform/models/{bronze,gold}/market`):

   - `stg_market_ads`, `stg_market_conditions`: each archive counts only its own year or

     quarter, so an ad republished across a turn of the year counts once; the stream

     (archive `stream`) counts only the months after the archives end, so a new quarterly

     archive replaces it for its months; months before 2020 and after today are dropped; the 2020–2021 archives' upper-case codes

     (`VANLIG_ANSTALLNING`, `HELTID`) map to the later labels; ads with no county, or

     "Ospecificerad arbetsort", are an unknown county.

   - `dim_market_field`, `dim_market_occupation_group`: latest labels.

   - `mart_market_field_monthly` (with `preliminary` for stream months),

     `mart_market_occupation_yearly`, `mart_market_region_yearly`,

     `mart_market_conditions_yearly`, `mart_market_archives`, `mart_market_daily` (ads per

     day from the stream). The whole market is in its own models

items.title: docs/job-market.md › Pipeline
items.text:
(`mart_market_field_monthly_total`, `mart_market_region_yearly_total`,

     `mart_market_conditions_yearly_total`); the export adds it as field `all`.

   - `int_market_periods` (silver): the comparison period ends with the last complete month;

     `mart_market_period` is the same row in gold, for the export.

3. **Export**: `platform/publish/export_market.py` writes `frontend/public/data/jobs/market.json`,

   with `daily` (ads per day) and `preliminary` (months from the stream). *Trender* shows the

   latest days under the monthly chart, marked preliminary.

4. **Refresh**: `.github/workflows/refresh-jobs.yml`, every morning (04:23 UTC): it restores

   the stored counts, stream and provenance log from R2, counts any new archive and the stream

   since the previous run and rebuilds `market.json` (`pipeline.py run market`). It stores the

   raw files back in R2 before it validates the export, then publishes the `jobs` group as a

   versioned release ([delivery-validation.md](delivery-validation.md)). It commits nothing. Quality check `jobs_stream_currentness` warns when the stream's last

   complete day is more than two days old.

```
python platform/ingest/jobtech/ingest_market.py
python platform/ingest/jobtech/ingest_stream.py
cd platform && dbt build --select tag:market && cd ..
python platform/publish/export_market.py
```

items.title: docs/job-market.md › Reading the numbers
items.text:
- An ad is not a hire, and one ad can seek several people. Vacancies count an ad without a
  number as one.
- The latest year is partial. Every change on the page compares the same months: the
  complete months the latest year covers, in that year and the year before.
- Days and months counted from the stream are preliminary until the quarter's archive is
  published; an ad that was up for less than the time between two runs is missed.
- Occupation groups are Arbetsförmedlingen's taxonomy (SSYK 2012), in Swedish. A group's
  label and field are those of its latest month.
- Changes per occupation group are shown only where the group had at least 100 ads in the
  months compared.

items.title: docs/news.md › Political news
items.text:
`#politik-nyheter` lists political news from **SVT Nyheter**, **Sveriges Radio Ekot** and the
**Government Offices**, tagged by party and topic. The party view (`#politik-partier`) shows the
news naming each party.

items.title: docs/news.md › What is kept
items.text:
Only what the feeds themselves publish: the headline, the feed's own short summary, the time
and the link. Every item links to the article, which stays with its publisher; article text is
never fetched. SVT's robots.txt allows real-time retrieval (not AI training).

| Source | Feed |
|---|---|
| SVT Nyheter | `https://www.svt.se/nyheter/rss.xml` (RSS, about 100 latest items) |
| Sveriges Radio Ekot | `https://api.sr.se/api/rss/program/83` (Atom, 20 latest; SR's open API) |
| Government Offices | `https://www.regeringen.se/Filter/RssFeed?filterType=Taxonomy` (RSS, 100 latest, with ministry and policy area as categories) |

SVT sometimes answers 403 to automated requests. A failing source is logged and skipped; the
others are still read, and the next run tries again.

items.title: docs/news.md › Pipeline
items.text:
1. **Collect**: `platform/ingest/news/news_ingest.py` reads the feeds and merges new items

   into a monthly archive, `warehouse/raw/news/items-YYYY-MM.jsonl` (one line per item, with

   when it was first and last seen), and logs every fetch in `_manifest.jsonl`. The feeds

   hold only a day or so, so the archive is built by reading often; it starts the day

   collection started. With `--sync` the archive lives on R2 (`raw/news/`) between runs.

2. **Tag**: dbt, tag `news` (`platform/models/{bronze,gold}/news`):

   - parties by the way newsrooms write them, case-sensitive: "(S)", "S-ledaren", "SD:s",

     "Vänsterpartiet", "Tidöpartierna" (`seeds/news/news_party_terms.csv`);

   - parties by the full name of a politician in office now, for news that names a minister

     without the party ("Ebba Busch", "socialminister Jakob Forssmed"). The names come from

     Riksdagen's person list (`platform/ingest/news/people_ingest.py`, members serving,

     ministers, Speakers, MEPs). A name two people share is left out, and so is an ordinary

     member with one of the thirty most common Swedish surnames ("Johan Andersson" in the

     news is more often someone else); ministers and Speakers always count;

   - topics by keyword: forming a government and the site's 15 policy issues

     (`seeds/news/news_topics.csv`);

   - political: from the Government, naming a party, about forming a government, or using the

     words of national politics.

items.title: docs/news.md › Pipeline
items.text:
3. **Export**: `platform/publish/export_news.py` writes `frontend/public/data/parliament/news.json`:

   the political items of the last 60 days, topics, items per party in 30 days, and each

   source's last fetch.

4. **Summarise**: `platform/publish/summarize_news.py` writes

   `parliament/news-summaries.json`, a summary of the last seven days with the articles it

   cites. It runs only when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. See below for what happens when it fails.

5. **Schedule**: `.github/workflows/refresh-news.yml`, every morning at 05:17 UTC. It publishes

   the `news` delivery group to R2 and commits nothing. It needs the R2 secrets

   ([deploy.md](deploy.md)).

```sh
python platform/pipeline.py run news                 # all of it
python platform/pipeline.py run news --only dbt      # one phase
```

items.title: docs/news.md › The summary is optional
items.text:
Fetching, the archive, tagging, dbt and the export are required: a failure stops the run. The
summary is not. The summariser never changes `news.json`, and it writes a new
`news-summaries.json` only after a complete answer that passes the schema and cites known
articles. In every other case the previous summary stays byte for byte, with its own
`generated_at` and `period`. No replacement text is written when there is no earlier summary.

| Exit code | Status | What the run does |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `generated` or `skipped` | Continues. `skipped` has the reason `no_key` or `no_recent_items` |
| 2 | `degraded` | Continues and publishes the headlines with the previous summary |
| 1 | `failed` | Stops: a local input, output or status-file error, or bad arguments |

Code 2 covers `refusal`, `max_tokens`, `unexpected_stop`, `api_error`, `sdk_unavailable`,
`invalid_response` and `ungrounded_response`. A summary is ungrounded when it cites an unknown
article id, or names a party that the cited articles' tags do not support.

items.title: docs/news.md › The summary is optional
items.text:
Before it fetches, the run restores the last approved summary from R2
(`release.py materialize --prefer-active`), so a failed attempt publishes that one and not an
older copy from the checkout. `--status-file` writes the attempt's status as JSON outside the
public data: status, reason, exit code, `attempted_at`, model, items considered and the active
summary's date and period. An API error is recorded by exception type and HTTP status, without
the response body or the key. The client has a 60-second timeout and does not retry.

The citation and schema checks do not show that each sentence renders its source correctly.
The summary's wording still needs a human read.

items.title: docs/news.md › Limits
items.text:
- Keyword tagging: an item can name a party without being about it (an analysis naming five
  parties is tagged with all five), and a topic word can match in passing.
- No history before collection started; the feeds cannot be read backwards. Until the
  archive is 30 days old, the count by each party covers the time since collection started,
  and the page says so.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Parliament: elections, government and the Riksdag's decisions
items.text:
The Political Observatory (`#politik` and its themes) is built from this model. It covers the
following source periods, with additional workspace coverage limits documented below:

| Part | Source | Period |
|---|---|---|
| Roll calls, every member's vote | Riksdagen, `votering-<rm>.csv.zip` | 1993/94 to now, 33 sessions, 22,900 roll calls, 8 million votes |
| Committee reports (title, committee, decision date) | Riksdagen, `dokumentlista` | 1993/94 to now |
| Election results and seats | SCB (ME0104), Valmyndigheten for elections SCB has not yet published | 1973 to 2026 |
| Party preference survey (PSU) | SCB (ME0201, Vid10) | 1972 to the latest May or November survey |
| Governments and their agreements | `seeds/parliament/governments.csv`, a source per row | 1991 to now |
| Government-formation news | Riksdagen's own news items | since the latest election |
| Speeches | Riksdagen, the site's speech index | 1993/94 to now |
| Budget outturn per expenditure area | Statskontoret | 1997 to 2025 |

Not yet even: the government and party **budget frames** (FiU1) are machine-readable for
2007/08, 2009/10, 2012/13–2013/14, 2016/17–2019/20 and 2022/23–2025/26. For 2020–2022 the
Riksdag's HTML carries no tables, and before 2007 the comparison tables have other headings.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Layers
items.text:
```
ingest/riksdagen/history_ingest.py   votes/<rm>.csv.gz, reports/<rm>-<page>.json
ingest/elections/elections_ingest.py scb/election_*, scb/psu, val/<val>/RD_S.json, riksdagen/formation/
models/bronze/parliament/stg_*       one row per source row; the roll-call layouts of different years unified
models/silver/parliament/int_*       roll calls and each party's position on them
models/gold/parliament/              dims, facts and marts below
publish/export_parliament.py         parliament/*.json and parquet/parliament_roll_calls/
```

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Tables
items.text:
| Table | Grain | What |
|---|---|---|
| `dim_government` | government | prime minister, parties, dates, agreement, status |
| `dim_parliament_session` | riksmöte | dates, the election it followed, the government at its start |
| `dim_committee` | committee | current and former committees, each assigned to an issue |
| `dim_issue` | policy issue | committees, expenditure areas, welfare indicators |
| `fct_roll_call` | session × `roll_call_id` | report, committee, issue, yes/no/abstain/absent, outcome, the government's position and whether it won |
| `fct_party_roll_call` | session × `roll_call_id` × party | the party's votes, position, unity, role that day |
| `mart_party_session_record` | session × party | attendance, unity, winning side, voting with the government |
| `mart_party_pair_session` | session × party pair | share of decisions with the same position |
| `fct_election` | election × party | votes, share, seats, source |
| `fct_election_municipality` | municipality × election × party | votes, share |
| `fct_party_poll` | survey month × party | share, margin of error, changes |

Keys shared with the rest of the platform: `party` (one spelling: FP is L, KDS is KD),
`session` ('1999/2000' written in full), `issue_key`, and `indicator_key` into the welfare
model.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Definitions
items.text:
- **Roll call.** One vote id can carry two roll calls: on the matter (sakfrågan) and on the
  reasons given for the decision (motivfrågan). `roll_call_id` is the vote id plus `:motiv`
  for the latter; `is_substantive` marks decisions. The marts count decisions only.
- **A party's position** is what most of its present members voted; an even split is `split`.
- **The government's position** is that of the prime minister's party that day.
- **Role**: `government`, `agreement` (a written agreement with the government, such as the
  Januari- and Tidö agreements) or `opposition`, on the date of the roll call.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Tested against
items.text:
- The party vote counts of 2024/25–2025/26, built independently for the evidence layer:
  11,488 of 11,488 party results identical.
- Valmyndigheten against SCB for 2022: the same votes and seats for all eight parties.
- Every election fills 349 seats (350 in 1973) and shares add to 100.
- Every roll call lists 349 members; three in the source do not and are flagged.
- Each PSU survey adds to 100.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Caveats
items.text:
- Linking speeches to issues uses the debate title, which equals the committee report's title
  for about 45 % of issue-debate speeches; the rest are not counted per issue.
- The welfare indicators shown on an issue page describe the area. They are not effects of
  the decisions beside them.
- SCB counts Ny demokrati's votes (1991, 1994) among other parties; its seats are shown.
- PSU is a sample survey with a margin of error of about ±1 point for the largest parties.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Running
items.text:
```bash
npm run parliament          # fetch, dbt build (tag:parliament), export
npm run parliament:build    # build from the files already fetched
```

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Government studies
items.text:
`platform/ingest/riksdagen/studies_ingest.py` fetches the SOU and Ds series (from 1995) and
Riksrevisionen's audit reports, and reads every government bill since 2006/07: its committee
reports and the studies its section "Ärendet och dess beredning" names (in a budget bill, per
proposal). Each link keeps the sentence that makes it.

| Table | Grain |
|---|---|
| `dim_study` | a study: SOU, Ds, RiR, or a ministry memorandum a bill names |
| `fct_bill` | a government bill |
| `fct_bill_report` | a bill and a committee report it was dealt with in |
| `fct_bill_study` | a bill and a study it names as preparation, with the sentence |

The site shows the latest studies and what they led to on `#politik-utredningar`, and the studies
behind every decision it lists. Budget and spring bills are left out of that per-decision
link, since they name hundreds.

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › What counts as a complete session
items.text:
`platform/ingest/riksdagen/studies_ingest.py` reads every document in Riksdagen's bill list and
writes a coverage report per session, `studies/coverage/<session>.json`: each listed document
with its status, source URL and, on failure, the error. A session gets a completion record only
when the report, the preparation rows and the complete list files all match their hashes.
Missing and failed bills are kept as `pending_bills`; an attempt that leaves any ends in an
error and stops dbt and publication for the subject. Progress is saved every 25 documents, so a
restart reuses what was already read.

Two cases are handled without failing the session:

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › What counts as a complete session
items.text:
- Annexes with no status page. A 404 from `dokumentstatus` is recorded as
  `unavailable_attachment` only when the list's own metadata shows an annex: a `d` suffix with
  a number, a related main document in the same list, the same session and designation, and
  the annex marker. The main document must have valid preparation in the same attempt. The
  case that prompted the rule is 2010/11: eight listed parts, GY03101d2 to GY03101d9, of
  *Årsredovisning för staten 2010* (GY03101), all 404 while the main document answers 200. The
  annexes get no preparation row of their own and are tried again at the next historical
  revision. Any other 404, a 503, a timeout, broken JSON, a wrong document identity or empty
  text is still an error.
- Documents with no embedded HTML. Sixteen documents from 2014/15 came back with identity
  and committee links but no text. The ingest then reads the main PDF from Riksdagen's file
  host, and requires a matching document identity and title and exactly one main PDF. Empty or
  invalid PDF text is an error. The bytes, URL and hash are stored like any other raw file
  (`pypdf` is pinned in `platform/requirements.txt`).

items.title: docs/parliament-data-model.md › Parties: colours, logos and the party page
items.text:
`frontend/src/parties/identity.tsx` holds each party's identity, used everywhere a party is
shown (seat bar, party pickers and charts, vote lists, tables, BudgetLab):

- `color`: the party colour as Swedish media and Wikipedia draw it (S #E8112D, M #52BDEC,
  SD #DDDD00, V #DA291C, C #009933, KD #000077, MP #83CF39, L #006AB3), for filled areas;
- `line`: the same hue darkened to at least 3:1 against the page, for lines, text and small
  marks (V darker still, so it does not read as S);
- `ink`: the text colour on `color`;
- `logo`: the party's current mark as Riksdagen shows it on *Ledamöter och partier*
  (media.riksdagen.se, 240 px WebP), in `frontend/public/logos/parties/`.

Because every party has its own colour, charts of parties are no longer limited to five
series.

`#politik-partier` shows a card per party, sorted by the latest election. A party's page gathers
what the other pages have on one party, from the same files: `now.json` (result, poll, role),
`elections.json` and `polls.json` (support over time), `sessions.json` (governments it sat
in or supported, voting record, agreement with each other party in the latest session),
`issues.json` (record per issue, speeches) and `taxes/decisions.json` (its vote on each tax
decision).

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Philosophy Atlas
items.text:
`#philosophy-atlas` (experimental) asks: **how do recurring moral and philosophical tensions
organise texts across thinkers and traditions?** It maps passages of thirteen public-domain works
by meaning, groups them, measures how far the groups follow the works rather than the ideas, and
reads the passages through a set of tensions chosen as lenses. No group is named by a machine.

```
python platform/ingest/philosophy/ingest_corpus.py                       # Gutenberg, via rawstore
cd platform && dbt build --profiles-dir . --select tag:philosophy --exclude path:models/gold/philosophy
python platform/nlp/philosophy/pipeline.py                              # sample, embed, map, cluster, tensions
cd platform && dbt build --profiles-dir . --select path:models/gold/philosophy
python platform/publish/philosophy/export_philosophy.py
```
(`npm run philosophy` runs them in order.)

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Corpus
items.text:
`platform/ingest/philosophy/corpus.json`: one work per thinker, spread over ethics, political
philosophy, epistemology and existential thought, from Plato (*Republic*, Jowett) to Nietzsche
(*Beyond Good and Evil*, Zimmern). Each entry carries title, author, approximate year, period,
tradition, area, original language, text language (English throughout), **translator** (from the
Gutenberg file; null with a note where the file names none: Aristotle's *Ethics*, Marcus
Aurelius) and genre. Ids, titles, authors and translators were checked against each file.

**Only the philosopher's own text.** Editions open with translators' and editors' introductions,
biographies and analyses (Jowett's introduction to the *Republic* runs to thousands of lines) and
close with notes and glossaries. `text_start` / `text_end` in corpus.json mark where the work
itself begins and ends (a line matched in full, its n-th occurrence), and
`platform/nlp/philosophy/passages.py` `own_text` keeps only that span. The shared Gutenberg
cleaning (`nlp/symbolic/cleaning.py`) then removes tables of contents, indexes, footnotes.

Passages: paragraphs joined to at least 60 words and split above 220 at sentence ends; headings
dropped. 7,794 passages in all.

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Pipeline (`platform/nlp/philosophy/pipeline.py`)
items.text:
1. **Balanced sample**: at most 200 passages per work, evenly spaced through it (2,600).
2. **Embeddings**: `paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` (`nlp/text/vectors.py`), the model the
   concept layer uses for every corpus, so these vectors are comparable with the others.
3. **Two maps**, as the Symbolic Atlas learned: *raw*, and *centred per work* (each work's mean
   vector subtracted, `nlp/symbolic/transforms.py`). UMAP 2-D for the map, 10-D for HDBSCAN
   (min cluster size 25).
4. **Evaluation** of each map: groups, noise, largest-work share, groups dominated by one work,
   groups across works (≥ 3 works, none above half), and the share of each passage's ten nearest
   neighbours from the same work and with the same translator, against chance.
5. **Groups**: composition, the six passages nearest the centre, the most distinctive words
   (class-based TF-IDF). Status `unreviewed` unless `nlp/philosophy/reviewed_clusters.json` holds
   a review for the group's fingerprint (hash of its sorted members). Labels come only from there.
6. **Tensions** (`seeds/philosophy/tensions.csv`): eleven pairs (freedom ↔ control, individual ↔
   collective, duty ↔ consequence, …), each pole written as one sentence and embedded; a
   passage's position is its similarity to pole A minus pole B.

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Results (6 October 2026)
items.text:
| | Raw | Centred per work |
|---|---|---|
| Groups | 20 | 23 |
| Passages in no group | 35 % | 44 % |
| Groups across works | 6 | 19 |
| Groups dominated by one work | 2 | 0 |
| Nearest neighbours from the same work (chance 8 %) | 48 % | 32 % |
| Nearest neighbours with the same translator (chance 14 %) | 58 % | 44 % |

A well-separated group is not necessarily the structure we meant to measure: in the raw map the
work, and the translator's English, organise much of it. Centring per work reduces that a lot,
not entirely. Differences along the tensions are small; the lens is ours.

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Data model
items.text:
`stg_philosophy_documents` (bronze) → `int_philosophy_passages` (silver, Python) →
`dim_philosophy_document`, `dim_tension`, `mart_philosophy_atlas`, `mart_philosophy_clusters`,
`mart_philosophy_tensions`, `mart_philosophy_tension_poles` (gold). Published under
`frontend/public/data/philosophy/`; no embedding is published.

items.title: docs/philosophy-atlas.md › Limitations
items.text:
- Thirteen works do not stand for traditions; this is a corpus for exploring method.
- Translations: nine of thirteen works are English translations, mostly Victorian; translator
  style is measurable in the map.
- Passages are cut mechanically; a passage can join the end of one argument and the start of the
  next.
- Tension poles are single sentences we wrote; another wording would move the positions.

items.title: docs/pipeline.md › Pipeline
items.text:
How a subject gets from its source to the site, and what runs it. This is the only document
that describes orchestration. The definitions themselves are in two files:

- `platform/pipeline.yml`, the registry: one entry per subject with its steps, dbt selectors,
  raw paths, schedule and delivery group.
- `platform/pipeline.py`, the command that reads it. npm scripts, local runs and GitHub Actions
  all call this command.

![From source to site](pipeline-flow.svg)

A subject is fetched to `warehouse/raw`, built and tested by dbt into
`platform/target/<subject>`, passed through an ML stage if it has one, and exported to
`frontend/public/data`. Its delivery group is then checked and published as a versioned
release in R2 (`platform/publish/release.py`, specs in `configs/delivery/`). Each release's
group manifest records the dbt results of the group's subjects and its file row counts under
`dq` and `reconcile`; a blocking dbt result stops the upload
([r2-delivery-contract.md](r2-delivery-contract.md)). The site does not
read these releases: it serves the data committed under `frontend/public/data`
([storage-and-serving.md](storage-and-serving.md)). No workflow commits data.

items.title: docs/pipeline.md › Running a subject locally
items.text:
```sh
python platform/pipeline.py list                      # every subject: group, schedule, SLA, write modes
python platform/pipeline.py run welfare               # fetch, build, test, export
python platform/pipeline.py run welfare --only dbt    # one phase: ingest, dbt, ml, export, publish
python platform/pipeline.py run symbolic --only dbt:1 # the first dbt step of a subject that has two
python platform/pipeline.py run --all --dry-run       # print every command, check the files exist
python platform/pipeline.py check                     # the four data contracts
python platform/pipeline.py pull welfare              # its raw and feature files from R2
```

The old npm names still work and are one-line aliases: `npm run welfare`, `npm run
parliament:build`, `npm run symbolic:silver`, `npm run concepts`, `npm run data:check`.

Options for `run`:

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--only a,b` | Only these phases. `dbt:2` picks the second dbt step |
| `--full-refresh` | Sets `PORTFOLIO_FULL_REFRESH=1`: refetch history as well as current data |
| `--ml missing` | Default. Run an ML stage only when its stored output is absent |
| `--ml stale` | Also run it when its inputs changed since the stored run |
| `--ml always` | Rerun every ML stage |
| `--dry-run` | Print the commands; fail if a script, spec or dbt path they name is missing |

Rules the command keeps:

items.title: docs/pipeline.md › Running a subject locally
items.text:
- Each subject builds into its own `platform/target/<subject>`, so one subject's test results
  are never read as another's.
- An export runs only after the subject's ingest, dbt and ML steps all came through and its dbt
  tests passed.
- One failed subject does not stop the others. A subject that `needs` a failed one is skipped.
  The exit code is non-zero if anything failed.
- A group is published once, and only when every subject in it succeeded in the same run.
- Publishing changes the active release in R2. Locally it runs only with `--only publish`, and
  needs the R2 credentials in the environment. In Actions it is part of a normal run.

`pull` and `push` need the R2 credentials too. `push` deletes remote raw files that are gone
locally only for subjects marked `prune: true` (welfare, parliament, taxes).
