items.title: docs/security.md › Security checks
items.text:
The site serves static files. Production credentials belong in the GitHub
`anton-portfolio` environment and Cloudflare secrets. PR CI has no R2 credentials.
Data publication jobs accept only `main` and use the separate environment.

items.title: docs/security.md › Local checks
items.text:
```sh
npm audit --audit-level=moderate
npm run test:security
python -m pytest platform/tests/architecture/test_security.py -q
gitleaks git --redact --no-banner .
```

`test:security` builds the site and applies the built `_headers` policy to browser
responses. It checks startup, navigation, the CV dialog and blocking of injected
inline and external scripts. It does not prove that Cloudflare serves those headers.
Styles allow inline declarations because the charts and React components use them.
Scripts allow only the site's origin. Framing allows the same origin for the CV PDF;
external sites cannot embed the page.

The Security workflow runs on pushes, pull requests and weekly. It audits npm and
each Python lock, checks the upstream version of the CPU PyTorch wheel, and scans
Git history with a checksum-verified Gitleaks binary. `.gitleaksignore` contains
reviewed historical false positives for public identifiers, indicator keys and job
titles. Each exception names an exact commit, file, rule and line. Review new
findings individually. A real credential must be revoked, not added to the baseline.

items.title: docs/security.md › Updating Python locks
items.text:
The locks target Python 3.12 on Linux, matching GitHub Actions. Keep the small input
files as the dependency declarations. The ML and news inputs include the base
requirements so their locks resolve the complete environment. The ML input pins
one CPU PyTorch wheel by URL and SHA-256; check its version and hash against the
official PyTorch CPU index before changing it.

Regenerate after changing an input or when addressing an advisory:

```sh
uv pip compile platform/requirements.txt --upgrade --python-version 3.12 --python-platform linux --generate-hashes --no-emit-index-url -o platform/requirements-ci.lock
uv pip compile platform/requirements-ml.in --upgrade --python-version 3.12 --python-platform linux --generate-hashes --no-emit-index-url -o platform/requirements-ml.lock
uv pip compile platform/requirements-news.in --upgrade --python-version 3.12 --python-platform linux --generate-hashes --no-emit-index-url -o platform/requirements-news.lock
uv pip compile platform/requirements-security.in --upgrade --python-version 3.12 --python-platform linux --generate-hashes --no-emit-index-url -o platform/requirements-security.lock
```

items.title: docs/security.md › Updating Python locks
items.text:
Install the security tools with
`pip install --require-hashes -r platform/requirements-security.lock`, then run
`pip-audit --require-hashes --disable-pip -r <lock>` for each lock. The workflow
audits the upstream PyTorch version separately because pip-audit skips wheel URLs.
Run the tests before accepting dependency updates. Dependabot checks npm, Python
declarations and Actions weekly; regenerate the locks for Python updates.

items.title: docs/security.md › Hosting settings and verification after publication
items.text:
GitHub settings verified and updated on 15 October 2026:

- The `anton-portfolio` environment accepts only the `main` branch. Required
  reviewers are not enabled on this environment because scheduled data refreshes
  also use it.
- `main` requires both CI jobs, Dependency audit and Secret scan from GitHub
  Actions, an up-to-date branch and resolved review conversations. The protections
  also apply to administrators; force pushes and branch deletion are disabled.
  The Security workflow in this change must run successfully before merging it.
- No R2 access or secret key was present in repository secrets. R2 credentials
  were present in the separate environment. Their bucket permissions still need
  to be checked in Cloudflare.

Cloudflare Always Use HTTPS still needs verification or activation with a valid
Cloudflare login. `_headers` sets HSTS for one year; it does not force an HTTP
request to redirect.

After the changes have been published, verify both entry points:

```sh
python scripts/check_security_headers.py https://antonernstsson.com/
python scripts/check_security_headers.py https://anton-portfolio.anton-ernstson.workers.dev/
```

The verifier checks the HTTP redirect, HTTPS certificate validation and enforced
security headers. A blocked or failed request is a failure, not a verified result.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Site structure
items.text:
How the site is organised and which file decides what. The visual direction is in
[design-system.md](design-system.md); how a page orders its content is in
[data-storytelling.md](data-storytelling.md).

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › SWEDEN research platform
items.text:
SWEDEN (`#sweden`) is the featured research platform. It has five research products and a
Connections page, and its design is described in [sweden-design.md](sweden-design.md).

| Route | Product | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `#sweden-matning` | A Politics of Measurement | Findings (SCB and Kolada catalogues) |
| `#sweden-arbete` | B The Ideal Human | Findings for counted archive years; the full backfill runs weekly |
| `#sweden-likhet` | C The Invisible Sweden | Findings (the 2024 clustering of 280 municipalities) |
| `#sweden-tillhorighet` | D The Infrastructure of Belonging | Findings (KB library statistics, 2014 onward) |
| `#sweden-framtid` | E The Lost Futures | Findings (Riksdag speeches 1993/94–2025/26; DiVA not yet counted) |
| `#sweden-samband` | Connections | Three relationships computed, two joins rejected |

The header links to SWEDEN first. Its project menu is titled Other projects, and on the homepage and
`#projekt` a featured SWEDEN card stands above the other projects. The Wellbeing Observatory moved from `#sweden*` to `#wellbeing*`. Its old addresses
(`#sweden-health`, `#sweden-counties` and the others) redirect.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Projects and navigation
items.text:
The homepage holds the identity, profile, experience and project index. A shared header
replaces the old sidebar. Its project menu groups the twelve projects, and Cluster Visuals sits
beside them as a separate tool.

| Group         | Projects                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Observatories | Political Observatory, Labour Market Observatory, Compliance Intelligence, Wellbeing Observatory, EU AI Act Observatory, Swedish Statute Book |
| Labs | Symbol Lab, Philosophy Lab, Concept Lab, Ask the law, Drug Synergy Lab |
| Engineering | IT Incident Clustering, Homie API, DiVA Thesis Lakehouse |

Each project has an entry page. Political Observatory opens as five analytical areas, with shared party selection and
source readers behind them. The other observatories retain their report tabs, each with
an address of its own. Labs and engineering projects are continuous
reports with section addresses. Readers for one speech, debate, article or concept are separate
views. Previous and next links follow the menu's group order.

Two pages use Cloudflare Workers AI ([workers-ai.md](workers-ai.md)). Ask the law (`#fraga-lagen`)
answers questions over Swedish statutes or the EU AI Act; `?korpus=ai-act` picks the AI Act.
On `#cluster-visuals`, the card `#cv-place` places a reader's sentence on the party-leader debate
map.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Where it is defined
items.text:
| What                                                                  | File                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Project names, descriptions, addresses and menu grouping              | `frontend/src/projects/projectRegistry.ts` |
| Topic links under each project                                        | `frontend/src/projects/topics.ts`          |
| Hash routing, report tabs, deep dives and redirects for old addresses | `frontend/src/router.ts`                   |
| Shared report frame                                                   | `frontend/src/report/ReportShell.tsx`      |

Routes are `#path` with optional query parameters, so a chosen view can be shared as a link.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Layout and copy
items.text:
Observatory charts use bounded analytical panels. Labs and engineering keep wide figures
and open comparisons; filters and technical detail may have a bounded area. A
chart heading names the measure; its caption keeps source, unit, period and comparison basis.
Technical methods use native disclosures. Analytical pages have a warm-grey canvas, and the
decorative debate background stays on the homepage. Large map projections keep their reading
key.

The Wellbeing county reference is a mean of the counties weighted by total population, and is
labelled that way. Each source keeps its own population definition.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Retired views
items.text:
The platform pages (quality, data model and ER, architecture, catalogue, Idea Lineage), the RAG
assistant, the industrial pump project, DiVA topic clustering and Allegoria are off the
website. Their addresses lead to the project index (`REDIRECTS` in `router.ts`). The pipelines,
schema access, quality checks and trace data that the remaining projects use are still in the
repository, and so are their documents: [quality-and-validity.md](quality-and-validity.md),
[data-constellation.md](data-constellation.md) and [idea-lineage.md](idea-lineage.md).

Retired project ids are still accepted by the append-only idea journal, so old records stay
readable.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Visual workspace ownership
items.text:
The project groups also determine `data-workspace` on the app shell: `observatories`,
`labs` or `engineering`. Standalone views use `tool`. `ReportShell`, `Stage`, `ProjectHero`,
`Feature` and the existing dashboard kit provide the four patterns documented in
[design-system.md](design-system.md). This classification changes presentation only.
The homepage keeps its own token scope and composition; shared project styling is scoped
to `.project-shell`.

items.title: docs/site-structure.md › Political Observatory v2
items.text:
The five routes are `#politik`, `#politik-val`, `#politik-riksdag`, `#politik-budget` and
`#politik-tal`. The scoped workspace lives in `frontend/src/politik/workspace/`. Existing
research views and old aliases remain available. See [Political Observatory v2](political-observatory-v2.md)
for filter semantics, evidence relationships, retained routes and coverage. The homepage and
shared site header were not changed by this migration.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › Storage and serving
items.text:
Where the data lives and how the site finds a file. What builds and publishes the data, and
when, is in [pipeline.md](pipeline.md). The rules for a versioned release are in
[r2-delivery-contract.md](r2-delivery-contract.md).

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › What is stored where
items.text:
| What | Where | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| Code, dbt models, seeds, schemas, test fixtures | Git | Commits |
| The site's JSON, 690 files in the catalogue | `frontend/public/data/` in Git, which the site reads; also in R2 releases, which it does not | The exports; a group's publish step |
| Parquet marts (68 files) and document shards (4,586) | R2 bucket `anton-portfolio` | A group's publish step |
| Raw source files, ML features, the DuckDB warehouse | R2, under `warehouse/` | `pipeline.py push`, `build-warehouse.yml` |
| Secrets | GitHub and Cloudflare secrets | By hand |

The counts are from `catalog.json` on 13 October 2026. The bucket is public and holds only
open data. A folder called `private` in a public bucket is not an access boundary; private
originals, such as the degree project's source material, are not uploaded.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › The catalogue
items.text:
`platform/publish/build_catalog.py` (`npm run data:catalog`) writes two files in
`frontend/public/data/`:

- `catalog.json`: one entry per delivered file with `path`, `product`, `format`, `bytes`,
  `rows`, `schema_version`, `partition`, `sha256` and `run_id`. The publish step and the
  validators read it. The browser never fetches it; it is 1.8 MB.
- `delivery.json`: what the site fetches at startup. It holds the base URL per format, the
  prefixes that mark a path as a shard, and the Parquet parts per dataset.

`run_id` is a hash of the catalogued content, so an unchanged tree rebuilds byte for byte.
Entries written by catalogue version 2 carry the SHA-256 and size of the exact bytes. Entries
for files that were moved to R2 under version 1 keep a hash taken after CRLF was normalised
and are marked `sha256-crlf-normalized`; they are read back with that rule and get an exact
hash the next time they are published.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › How the site resolves a path
items.text:
Components ask for logical paths such as `gold/overview.json`, never URLs.
`frontend/src/dataSource.ts` turns the path into a URL.

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `fetchData(path, init?)` | Any fetch of a data file |
| `useData(path, root)`, `useGoldData(path)` | React hooks in `frontend/src/politics/data.ts` |
| `useDataUrl(path)`, `resolveDataUrl(path)` | A resolved URL for a link or download |

The production site reads the data committed under `frontend/public/data`. The committed
`delivery.json` has schema version 1, JSON base `data/`, and the bucket's `r2.dev` address for
Parquet and shards. It has no `manifest_url`, and `VITE_R2_MANIFEST_URL` is not used, so the
site does not read the versioned releases the workflows publish to R2
([r2-delivery-contract.md](r2-delivery-contract.md)).

`VITE_DELIVERY_MODE=local` reads everything from `data/`, for development and offline
fixtures. On localhost a missing `delivery.json` is tolerated the same way.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › Adding a delivered file
items.text:
1. Write it under `frontend/public/data/<product>/`.
2. Run `npm run data:catalog`.
3. Read it by logical path through one of the functions above.
4. Give it to a delivery group in `configs/delivery/`, or leave it to `baseline`.

A directory whose files are read one document at a time goes in `SHARD_DIRECTORIES` in
`build_catalog.py`. The site reads that list from `delivery.json`, so nothing in `src/` changes.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › Validators and remote files
items.text:
`platform/lib/delivery.py` reads a delivered path from disk when it is there and from the
delivery base when it is not, so the checks in `npm run data:check` keep their full coverage:

- `validate_politics.py` verifies every local file byte for byte, asserts that each absent
  file is a catalogued shard, and reconciles all 1,436 roll-call member totals by fetching the
  decision shards.
- `validate_gold.py` checks all 714 gold source hashes, fetching the ones that moved.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › What moved to R2, and what that cost
items.text:
On 2026-09-25 the 3,470 document shards (489.1 MB) went to the bucket and left the repository.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/public/data/` files | 4,004 | 536 |
| `frontend/public/data/` size | 652 MB | 158 MB |
| `dist/` | 655 MB | 157 MB |
| Start-page bundle | 433.5 KiB | 332.6 KiB |

The speech index under `discovery/` followed: 140 MB of JSON, one file per session, became
Parquet with one part per session under `parquet/speech_cards/` (39 MB, the same 256,498
rows). `discovery/index.json` stays on the site and lists the parts. JSON served by the site
fell from 221.6 MB to 82.5 MB.

R2 holds the only readily available copy of the shards. `platform/legacy/build_politics.py`
needs three local sources to regenerate them (`--parliament`, `--allegoria`,
`--local-corpus`), and one of those is in no repository. Git history still has the files,
because the move was an ordinary commit.

`platform/publish/upload.py` is the unversioned uploader from that move. No workflow or
delivery group uses it; releases go through `platform/publish/release.py`.

items.title: docs/storage-and-serving.md › The bucket's address
items.text:
`r2.dev` is rate-limited, and the first CI run that read from it got 429s. The production
data domain is `https://data.antonernstsson.com/`, set as the repository variable
`R2_PUBLIC_BASE`. With the variable unset, the catalogue falls back to the `r2.dev` address.
`platform/publish/r2-cors.json` lists the origins allowed to read the bucket; a request with
`Origin: https://antonernstsson.com` comes back with that exact origin. Setting up the domain
is in [deploy.md](deploy.md).

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › SWEDEN atlas
items.text:
The atlas is a second way into SWEDEN: one dark 3D space per study, with the question and
two short texts on the left. The first says what the data reveals; the second names the
Data–Reality Gap, meaning what the data cannot show. The routes are `#sweden-atlas` (start)
and `#sweden-atlas-a` to `-e` plus `#sweden-atlas-x` (Connections). You can also open the
atlas from the SWEDEN menu. The product pages under `#sweden-*` are unchanged.

Code lives in `frontend/src/sweden/atlas/`. three.js loads only on atlas routes.

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › How a page is built
items.text:
- `space.ts` is the shared stage. It holds the stars, camera, orbit controls and the
  drawing helpers: glow, thread, arc, web floor and ghost box. A ghost box is a dashed
  outline drawn where data is missing.
- `AtlasPage.tsx` is the page template. It shows the header, the space, the free text,
  a key, a source line and the DATA drawer.
- One file per page holds the data reading, the computed finding and the scene:
  `AtlasHub`, `AtlasMeasured` (A), `AtlasWorker` (B), `AtlasModelled` (C),
  `AtlasBelonging` (D), `AtlasFutures` (E) and `AtlasConnections` (×).

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › Interaction
items.text:
Every choice in the scene has a keyboard route as well:

- Start: click a municipality, or pick one from the list, to see its similarity group and
  a link to C.
- A: click a bar or a row label to light that area of life.
- B: switch between the occupation-fixed and the raw rate, and click a personal trait to
  follow it. The finding is recomputed.
- C: play, or drag the slider, to move every municipality between the map and similarity
  space. Paths can be turned off. Click a municipality, or pick one from the list, to light
  its three nearest neighbours.
- D: click a floor label to isolate that floor. Click a municipality, or pick one, to trace
  it through all four floors.
- E: click a theme in the key, or a slice, to follow it in both corpora.
- Connections: click a thread to read the relationship, its interval or the reason it was
  rejected.

A selection rebuilds the scene and keeps the reader's camera. C's slider moves objects in
place without a rebuild (`apply` in `AtlasPage`).

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › Data slots
items.text:
Each page reads its files through `slots.ts`. Every slot has a path, a role and the JSON
shape the scene expects. A slot is either filled or empty:

- A filled slot is drawn from the published file.
- An empty slot is drawn as a ghost: a dashed outline with the text "awaiting <file>". The
  page's DATA drawer lists the slot with its path and shape. Nothing is filled with sample
  values.
- The "Revealed" text is computed from the data. While its file is missing, the page says
  which file would produce it.

To fill a slot, publish the file at its path in the shape given in `slots.ts`. The scene
picks it up on the next load, and nothing else needs to change.

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › Data slots
items.text:
| Slot                     | Path                                       | Fills                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measurementOther`       | `sweden/measurement/other_catalogues.json` | A: rows for Socialstyrelsen, Brå, Folkhälsomyndigheten and others         |
| `similarityAlternatives` | `sweden/similarity/alternatives.json`      | C: the top floor, another model specification                             |
| `travelTime`             | `sweden/belonging/travel_time.json`        | D: travel time replaces area per service point on the accessibility floor |
| `belongingSurvey`        | `sweden/belonging/belonging.json`          | D: the belonging floor                                                    |
| `futuresSou`             | `sweden/futures/sou.json`                  | E: a third corpus row (SOU)                                               |

Some gaps fill themselves. In B, adding a counted year to `language/trends.json` turns its
ghost column into a bar. In Connections, publishing a tested relationship for a pair that
is now only conceptual replaces the dotted thread with a tested one.

items.title: docs/sweden-atlas.md › Rules kept from SWEDEN
items.text:
- Missing data is drawn as missing, never interpolated or treated as zero.
- Corpora with different denominators get separate rows and are never pooled.
- Colour never carries meaning alone. Every gap is also written out in words.

items.title: docs/sweden-connections-preregistration.md › SWEDEN Connections: pre-registration of candidates 3.1 and 3.2
items.text:
Written 2026-10-21, before either analysis was run. It fixes the question, data, method, seeds,
decision rule and limits of candidates 3.1 and 3.2 in
[sweden-statistical-research-plan.md](sweden-statistical-research-plan.md) (section 3, step 5).
The commit that adds this file is the record: the code that computes them comes in a later
commit, and any departure from this text is listed in the export's `method` block with its
reason.

Shared by both analyses:

- Source: `gold.mart_municipality_year_cross_subject` and `gold.fct_municipal_similarity`, read
  by `platform/publish/sweden/export_connections.py`. Nothing is read from published JSON.
- Rates as SWEDEN D publishes them: physical visits per inhabitant and staffed service points
  per 10,000 inhabitants, both over D's `library_population`. A value D set to missing stays
  missing; it is not restored.
- County is the first two digits of the municipality code.
- Seed 20261021. Each analysis starts its own generator from it, so the order of computation
  does not change a result.
- Assessment labels are the page's existing ones: `robust`, `uncertain`, `not_supported`.
  Holm-adjusted p-values are published beside the raw ones and never decide a label on their
  own.
- Every sentence says "municipalities where", never "people who".

items.title: docs/sweden-connections-preregistration.md › 3.1 Matched-neighbour comparison (C × D)
items.text:
- Question: Among municipalities that SWEDEN C finds socially alike, how much do library use

  and library supply differ?

- Data: the 280 municipalities C analysed in 2024 and their five nearest neighbours. The

  neighbours follow `export_similarity.py`: Euclidean distance over the 12 indicators of

  `gold.fct_municipal_similarity`, each standardised over the 280. Library rates for 2024.

- Measure: for each municipality, the log ratio of its own rate to the median rate of those of

  its five neighbours that have a value. A municipality needs its own value and at least three

  neighbour values; the others are counted as missing. Two measures: visits per inhabitant and

  service points per 10,000.

- Summary: the median absolute log ratio, and the share of municipalities whose rate is more

  than 1.5 times, or less than 1/1.5 times, their neighbours' median.

- Reference: each neighbour set replaced by five municipalities drawn without replacement from

  the same SKR group (excluding the municipality itself), 999 rounds. The reference shows how

  alike municipalities of one SKR type are without C's matching.

- Decision rule, per measure: `robust` if the observed median absolute log ratio is below the

  reference's 2.5th percentile (C's neighbours are more alike than SKR peers); `uncertain` if it

  is below the reference median but not below the 2.5th percentile; `not_supported` otherwise.

items.title: docs/sweden-connections-preregistration.md › 3.1 Matched-neighbour comparison (C × D)
items.text:
One-sided permutation p = (1 + rounds at or below observed) / 1,000. The family is the two

  measures; Holm over the two.

- Sensitivity, pre-stated: the same comparison with 2019 library rates against the 2024

  neighbours. The neighbour variants of plan section 2.3 belong to SWEDEN C's step and are not

  part of this run.

- Evidence class: descriptive comparison.

- What cannot be concluded: that library provision causes use; anything about residents. A

  municipality far from its neighbours may host a regional library, a university or a tourist

  season, and the 12 indicators do not cover those. Door counters differ between

  municipalities.

items.title: docs/sweden-connections-preregistration.md › 3.2 Within-municipality change (C panel × D)
items.text:
- Question: Did library visits fall more in municipalities where population fell or median

  earned income fell?

- Data: library visits from D, population and median earned income (Kolada N00906) from the

  municipal panel, in 2014, 2019 and 2024. Two periods: 2014→2019 and 2019→2024, kept apart

  because the pandemic falls in the second.

- Departure from the plan: the plan also names the dependency ratio. The yearly panel has no

  dependency ratio (only C's 2024 Kolada inputs do), so ageing is not tested. No new data is

  fetched for it.

- Model, per period: least squares of Δ ln visits on Δ ln population and Δ ln median earned

  income, with an intercept, over the municipalities that have all three values at both ends

  of the period (paired panel).

- Intervals: 95 % percentile county-cluster bootstrap of each coefficient, 2,000 resamples of

  the 21 counties.

- Permutation: the outcome vector shuffled across municipalities, 4,999 rounds; two-sided p per

  coefficient = (1 + rounds with |β*| ≥ |β|) / 5,000. The family is two coefficients × two

  periods = four tests; Holm over the four.

- Decision rule: `robust` if at least one coefficient's interval excludes zero in both periods

  with the same sign; `not_supported` if every interval includes zero; `uncertain` otherwise.

- Sensitivity, pre-stated: the balanced panel (municipalities with visits in every year

  2014–2024) beside the paired one. The 13 values D repaired cannot be restored: 12 are zero

items.title: docs/sweden-connections-preregistration.md › 3.2 Within-municipality change (C panel × D)
items.text:
visits, which have no logarithm.

- Evidence class: exploratory statistical relationship. It becomes a validated relationship

  only if this specification is committed before the first run and 2025→2026 data confirms it

  later.

- What cannot be concluded: a causal effect of demographic or income change on library use.

  Shrinking municipalities may close branches first, so the ordering can run the other way.

  Library reorganisation, changed counting methods and merged service points are not

  controlled.

items.title: docs/sweden-data-source-strategy.md › SWEDEN data source strategy
items.text:
Phase 0B, 2026-10-20. Candidate sources for the five products, as the three Phase 0 audits found
them, plus one own check (Trafiklab). Source tags are defined in
[sweden-research-alignment.md](sweden-research-alignment.md#evidence-and-status-levels).

Nothing here is ingested. No endpoint or licence is added beyond what an audit or the own check
read. "Verified" means the access route was probed or the official page read. "UNVERIFIED" means it
was not, and the cell says which part is missing. A source with a verified endpoint and an
unverified licence is marked UNVERIFIED for the licence.

Before any new source, the roadmap repairs and re-analyses existing data. Several questions below
can be answered better with data already on disk; the "existing data first" section lists them.

items.title: docs/sweden-data-source-strategy.md › Priority classes
items.text:
Essential: fills a gap that weakens a published claim, at low cost. High value: answers a research
question the product cannot answer today. Optional: useful context, or cost or access is not yet
clear. Reject: closed, personal, not reproducible, or duplicates an existing source.

items.title: docs/sweden-data-source-strategy.md › Existing data first
items.text:
These questions need no new source:

- A: measures per table from the 1,299 metadata files; keyword validation of domains from titles.
- B: label crosswalk, complete-year endpoints, sub-lexicons, co-occurrence, SSYK-4 and employer
  controls on the 2023–2026 corpus already in `warehouse/raw/jobtech/cluster-corpus/`.
- C: geographic null, permutation test, sensitivity, 2020–2023 stability, and outcome comparison
  with panel columns not used in clustering (`good_wellbeing_pct`, `low_trust_pct`,
  `serious_mental_strain_pct`, `sick_pay_rate_1_days`) [AC].
- D: zero and partial-sum handling, balanced panels, a 2019 baseline, intervals on ρ.
- E: per-word marker rate, validation sample, relative horizon, party harmonisation, Swedish-only
  DiVA abstracts.

items.title: docs/sweden-data-source-strategy.md › Cost and maintenance
items.text:
Repairs are dbt and export changes measured in minutes. B's sub-lexicon recount re-streams 23
archives over several weekly runs with `--max-new 3`, about 2–3 hours of CI in total, without
storage growth [B]. Enriched JobTech metadata adds about 1.5 GB of transient download per full pass.
SCB, Arbetsmiljöverket, Kolada and bibstat additions are kilobytes to low megabytes. SOU and
propositions mean about 1 GB streamed. Swerik (about 8.4 GB) and GTFS routing are the only sources
with high storage or compute cost, and both wait on a prerequisite.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › SWEDEN design
items.text:
SWEDEN is the portfolio's featured research platform: five research products and a Connections
page under `#sweden`. This document covers how its pages look and are built. What each product
measures is described on the product's own page, in its method drawer.

The visual direction is "Sverige i höjd": a 3D scene over the whole window is the page's main
content, and glass panels float above it. Everything else sits below the scene.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Boundary
items.text:
- Everything lives in `frontend/src/sweden/` and is scoped to `.sweden`. Its tokens never reach
  `.home-shell` or the other projects, and the homepage source is not touched.
- `App.tsx` sets `data-workspace="sweden"` on the shell for SWEDEN routes, and does not render
  `SiteHeader` there: SWEDEN pages carry their own header (`Header.tsx`).
- The site's shared chart components (`RankBars`, `MultiLineChart`) are reused. `.sweden` rebinds
  the tokens they read (`--ink`, `--muted`, `--line`, `--series-1..5`, `--color-chart-*`).

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Routes
items.text:
| Route                  | Page                              |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `#sweden`              | Hub                               |
| `#sweden-matning`      | A Politics of Measurement         |
| `#sweden-arbete`       | B The Ideal Human                 |
| `#sweden-likhet`       | C The Invisible Sweden            |
| `#sweden-tillhorighet` | D The Infrastructure of Belonging |
| `#sweden-framtid`      | E The Lost Futures                |
| `#sweden-samband`      | Connections                       |
| `#sweden-kit`          | Component states, no data         |

The Wellbeing Observatory moved from `#sweden*` to `#wellbeing*`. Its old addresses redirect in
`router.ts`. A page's state is kept in the query, for example `#sweden-likhet?vy=likhet&kommun=2584`.
Pages write it with `setHashParams(path, params, true)`, so back and forward step through the views.
`?scen=2d` shows a page's 2D view in the scene's place.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Header (`Header.tsx`)
items.text:
No band of its own: the header sits on the page and fades into the scene with a gradient, never
a hard edge.

- On the left, the name in Archivo Expanded, upper case. Below it, one row in IBM Plex Mono:
  `SWEDEN`, then each product as its letter and one word (`C Similarity`). The current page is
  underlined and has `aria-current="page"`; each link's accessible name is the full title.
- On the right, two boxed controls. `MENU` opens a native `<dialog>` from the right (Start, SWEDEN,
  More); it takes focus, closes on Escape and hands focus back. The theme control switches SWEDEN
  between dark (default) and light, remembered per reader in `localStorage`.
- On a phone the header leaves the scene and stacks above it; the product row scrolls sideways.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Tokens
items.text:
These are defined on `.sweden` in `sweden.css`. Dark is the default; `html[data-sw-theme='light']`
switches to light.

| Token                            | Dark                              | Light                             | Use                                  |

| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |

| `--sw-bg`                        | `#11100E`                         | `#E9E8E4`                         | Page                                 |

| `--sw-glass`                     | `rgba(26,24,21,.8)`               | `rgba(250,249,246,.88)`           | Scene panels only                    |

| `--sw-ink`                       | `#EDE6D6`                         | `#141416`                         | Text                                 |

| `--sw-muted`                     | `#A39E93`                         | `#55545B`                         | Secondary text                       |

| `--sw-line`                      | `rgba(237,230,214,.13)`           | `rgba(20,20,22,.14)`              | Rules, borders                       |

| `--sw-accent`                    | `#C9BCF2`                         | `#5A4A8C`                         | Links, focus, product letters        |

| `--sw-seq-lo` / `--sw-seq-hi`    | `#3A3256` / `#E3D8FF`             | `#BCB1DC` / `#2C1F5E`             | Sequential magnitude                 |

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Tokens
items.text:
| `--sw-div-neg` / `-mid` / `-pos` | `#E08A5C` / `#3A3935` / `#6FB3D2` | `#B4562A` / `#C9C7C2` / `#2F6F8F` | Deviation from a meaningful midpoint |

| `--sw-base`                      | `#2A2925`                         | `#B9B6AF`                         | The ground and map base in 3D        |

| `--sw-stamp`                     | `#E2B65A`                         | `#8A6A1F`                         | Status stamps                        |

Colour rules:

- A sequential ramp is used only for magnitude, and a diverging ramp only around a stated midpoint.
  The ramp runs dark to light in the dark theme and light to dark in the light theme, so copy
  says "taller" or "further along the scale", never "darker".
- C's four similarity groups use fixed categorical colours (`GROUP_HEX` in `SimilarityStage.tsx`).
- Party colours are used only for party data.
- Missingness, significance and status are always written out in words. Colour never carries them alone.

Type, self-hosted under the SIL Open Font License (`frontend/public/fonts/sweden/`, `OFL.txt`):

- Archivo Expanded (width 125) for the name.
- IBM Plex Mono for navigation, labels, stamps, scales and numbers.
- Newsreader for questions, headings and the hub's product names.
- The site's body stack for running text.

The scene panels are the one exception to flat surfaces: they have translucency, a 10px backdrop blur
and a soft shadow. Every other surface on the page is flat.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Page template (`template.tsx`)
items.text: Every research product renders `SwedenResearchPage`, with the sections in this order:

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Page template (`template.tsx`)
items.text:
1. Scene. The full window (`100svh`), the 3D view filling it, with four fixed panels:
   - Title, top left: product letter and title, status stamp, the research question as the
     `h1`, one sentence on what the scene shows, then the findings as numbered buttons (at
     most three). A finding that runs against the expectation is marked and sorted first. Choosing
     one opens its values, evidence stamp and source in place and, where the page supports it,
     moves the scene (`onShow`). Findings are computed from published data, never written by hand.
   - Legend, top right: the measure, its period, the scale, how to read it, and the 3D / 2D switch.
   - Main control, bottom centre: the product's own control (C's Map ↔ Similarity, a measure, a year).
   - Info, bottom right: the chosen entity with raw values, units and source.
2. Explore. The 2D and tabular equivalents of the scene, with exact values and filters.
3. Method and limitations. `MethodDrawer` holds the nine sections: question, theory, data,
   method, results, alternatives, limitations, references and reproducibility. Limitations
   open by default. Data quality and construct validity are always discussed separately.
4. Interpretations. Two to four theoretical readings. Each says what the theory would
   expect, gives a verdict (supports, challenges, or cannot decide) computed or argued from
   the evidence, and states its limits.
5. Related research. Two or three links, each with a one-line reason.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Page template (`template.tsx`)
items.text:
A product without validated data renders its scene with an `EmptyState`. The empty state says
what the page would show, what it needs, and whether that is ingestion, validation, licence
review or cloud execution. Product status (`products.ts`) is one of three: findings available;
pipeline ready, awaiting execution; or data unavailable.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Scenes and their 2D equivalents
items.text:
| Product | 3D scene                                                                                                                       | 2D equivalent (`?scen=2d`, and without WebGL) |

| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |

| Hub     | The municipalities on the map, coloured by C's similarity group                                                                | The list of pages                             |

| A       | Domain × decade bars, by the finest geography                                                                                  | The coverage matrix with exact counts         |

| B       | Category × year; skills as matte stone, personal expectations as glass. Years without a counted archive are flat, empty ground | The language matrix                           |

| C       | Municipalities lift from the map and travel to their principal components (`t`, 0–1)                                           | The SVG map / similarity dots                 |

| D       | Municipalities raised by rank on the chosen measure, libraries as lights                                                       | The choropleth with library points            |

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Scenes and their 2D equivalents
items.text: | E       | Theme × year for the Riksdag; years left out are empty ground                                                                  | The future matrix                             |

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › 3D engine
items.text:
- `stage.ts`: the shared three.js stage. 32° perspective camera, damped orbit controls,
  hemisphere light plus one directional light with soft shadows, a shadow-catching ground,
  colours read from the tokens. The view is offset so the subject sits between the panels.
  It renders on change only and caps the device pixel ratio at 2.
- `BarField.tsx`: instanced boxes for A, B and E, with projected row and column labels.
- `MunicipalityField.tsx`: SCB's municipality boundaries (SWEREF99 TM, 100 m units; one scene
  unit is 10 km) as extruded shapes over a flat map base, with an optional second position per
  municipality, drawn paths for the move, outlined and labelled selections, and point lights.
  `SimilarityStage.tsx` (C) and `BelongingStage.tsx` (D) build on it; the hub uses it directly.
- three.js is lazy-loaded on SWEDEN routes only. The homepage never loads it.
- Scenes receive normalised heights and colours. Pages keep the raw values and show
  them in the info panel and in the tables under Explore.
- C's play button animates `t`; reduced motion jumps to the end instead.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Accessibility and responsive behaviour
items.text:
- Every 3D scene has a 2D equivalent with native, labelled controls, and every chart has a table.
- Focus is a 2px accent outline. Touch targets are at least 44px.
- From 760 to 1100px the main control takes the full width at the bottom and the info panel sits above it.
- At 760px and below the header and panels leave the scene and stack: header, title with
  findings, the visual, control, info, then legend.
- Reduced motion turns off animation within `.sweden`.

items.title: docs/sweden-design.md › Adding a research page
items.text:
1. Add the product's data to `products.ts` (with a one-word `short` name for the header),
   keeping `status: 'pipeline'` until its data has run.
2. Write `<Product>.tsx`. Load the product's files with `fetchJson` from `sweden/<product>/`,
   compute the findings from them, and render `SwedenResearchPage` with a `Scene`.
3. Lazy-load it in `SwedenPage.tsx` and remove its `PENDING` entry.
4. Export the data from a dbt mart under `models/gold/sweden/` through a script in
   `platform/publish/sweden/`, and add its steps to the `sweden` subject in `platform/pipeline.yml`.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › SWEDEN E: pre-registration of the futures topic pilot
items.text:
Written 2026-10-22, before any sentence was embedded or clustered. It fixes the unit, sample,
model, clustering, selection rule, stability criterion, null models and what will count as a
finding for an unsupervised reading of what futures the Riksdag and Swedish student theses talk
about. The commit that adds this file is the record; any departure is listed in the export's
`method` block with its reason. No cluster is named in this pilot: every cluster is published as
"unreviewed cluster N" with its top terms until the owner has reviewed it.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Unit and sample
items.text:
- Unit: one sentence that contains a match of SWEDEN E's existing future marker (`future` in
  `platform/seeds/sweden_futures/future_terms.csv`). The marker decides only which sentences are
  read, never what they are about. Sentences are split on line breaks and on `.`, `!` or `?`
  followed by white space; sentences under 6 or over 80 words are left out.
- Riksdag: every speech in data.riksdagen.se's session archives, year from the speech date.
- DiVA: the Swedish abstract of student theses (`studentThesis`, first dc:language Swedish,
  `futures_theses.swedish()`), year of publication, the latest version of each OAI identifier.
  The title is not a sentence and is not read. Harvested from record month 2005-01: a record's
  datestamp is its last change, after the thesis was deposited.
- At most one sentence per speech or abstract: the matching sentence with the lowest SHA-1 of
  `seed:document id:sentence index`. One long speech cannot fill a year.
- Per year and corpus, at most 1,500 such sentences: the 1,500 documents with the lowest SHA-1 of
  `seed:document id`. Seed 20261022. Years analysed: Riksdag 1994–2025, DiVA 2005–2025 (complete
  years; DiVA has under 300 future-oriented abstracts a year before 2005).
- Text stays in ignored local storage. Published rows carry sentence id, corpus, year and cluster.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Representation
items.text:
- `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, revision
  `e8f8c211226b894fcb81acc59f3b34ba3efd5f42`, on CPU, through `ml/jobs/embeddings.py` (normalised,
  checkpointed per batch).
- Primary space: each corpus's mean vector subtracted, then re-normalised, so that the clustering
  does not split parliamentary speech from academic prose before it splits subjects.
  Sensitivity: the same selected configuration on the uncentred vectors; the corpus AMI of both
  is reported.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Clustering and selection
items.text:
- Family: UMAP (5 dimensions, cosine, `min_dist` 0, `n_neighbors` 15, 30, 50) then HDBSCAN
  (`min_cluster_size` 0.5 %, 1 %, 2 % of the sample; `min_samples` 5, 10; excess of mass).
  Each UMAP is fitted with seeds 1, 2 and 3. Baseline: k-means and a diagonal Gaussian mixture on
  the 50-component PCA of the same vectors, k = 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, seed 1.
- Eligible: coverage (share not noise) at least 50 % and between 5 and 60 clusters.
- Selection: highest mean DBCV over the three seeds among eligible HDBSCAN configurations;
  silhouette in the UMAP space is reported beside it.
- Stability, required of the selected configuration: mean pairwise ARI across the three seeds at
  least 0.6 (assigned in both), and mean ARI at least 0.5 between the full fit and three refits
  on 80 % subsamples without replacement (seeds 11, 12, 13), on common sentences. A cluster is
  stable when its best Jaccard match in each other seed is at least 0.5. If no configuration
  passes, the pilot reports that no stable topic structure was found and publishes no topics.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Null models
items.text:
- Structure: every embedding dimension permuted independently across sentences (seed 20261022),
  then the selected configuration. The real space must give a higher DBCV and more than one
  cluster with more than 1 % of the sentences; otherwise the clusters are treated as artefacts.
- Trends: years permuted within corpus, 999 rounds, for every trend and correlation p-value.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Analyses
items.text:
- Share: sentences of a cluster over all sampled sentences of that year and corpus, noise
  included in the denominator. 95 % bootstrap CI, 1,000 resamples of sentences within each cell.
- Trend: OLS slope of share on year per stable cluster and corpus; permutation p; Holm over all
  stable cluster × corpus tests.
- Riksdag vs DiVA: per stable cluster with at least 1 % of sentences in both corpora, Pearson
  correlation of first-differenced yearly shares over 2005–2025, and cross-correlation at lags
  −3 to +3 years. p from 999 permutations of the differenced DiVA series; Holm over clusters for
  lag 0 and for the largest absolute lag correlation.
- Securitisation reading: trends of clusters whose top terms concern security, defence, threat or
  crisis are listed as exploratory only, until a reviewer has named the clusters.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › What counts as a finding
items.text:
- A finding: a stable cluster whose trend, or whose Riksdag–DiVA correlation, has a Holm-adjusted
  p below 0.05 and that beats both null models.
- Not a finding: any cluster name or reading before review; unstable clusters; noise; a single
  year's spike; correlations over fewer than 10 overlapping years; a lag that is not significant
  after Holm; a corpus-specific cluster (90 % or more from one corpus) used as evidence that the
  two corpora talk about the same future.
- What cannot be concluded: what speakers or students intend or believe; anything about futures
  not voiced with the marker; that one corpus influences the other.

items.title: docs/sweden-futures-topics-preregistration.md › Changes after registration
items.text:
- 2026-10-22, storage. The first UMAP fit ran out of memory on the laptop, so the clustering
  moves to `.github/workflows/cluster-jobs.yml`. The sample (with its sentence text) and the
  embedding shards are therefore stored in the project's R2 warehouse store under
  `features/sweden/futures_topics/run/`, beside the raw speeches and abstracts they were drawn
  from. They are not part of any release, and the site still receives only sentence ids,
  corpus, year and cluster. The candidate files stay local.
- 2026-10-22, compute. The method is unchanged: UMAP runs on the full 384-dimensional centred
  vectors with the registered grid, on a 16 GB runner. The laptop memory fixes that would alter
  the method are not applied: PCA to 50 dimensions before UMAP, fewer epochs, fitting on a sample
  and transforming the rest, or fixing `n_neighbors` after a pilot. TensorFlow is kept out of the
  process, and the centred space is rebuilt from the shards for the analysis instead of being
  saved as a second copy.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › SWEDEN research alignment
items.text:
Phase 0, 2026-10-20. This document compares each SWEDEN product with its research question, using
only facts that were checked. Nothing here changes code or data. The roadmap is in
[sweden-research-roadmap.md](sweden-research-roadmap.md), the lineage and coverage in
[sweden-data-inventory.md](sweden-data-inventory.md), and candidate sources in
[sweden-data-source-strategy.md](sweden-data-source-strategy.md).

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › Evidence and status levels
items.text:
Every number carries a source tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [AC], [B], [DE] | The three Phase 0 audit reports (projects A and C, B, D and E), 2026-10-20, read-only, code at `6560478a`. They are kept outside the repository with their query scripts (`a_repro*.py`, `c_check.py`, `q1.py`–`q5.py`, `d1.py`–`d4.py`, `e1.py`, `e2.py`). The script named next to a number is the one that produced it. |
| [own] | Checked again for this synthesis, by reading the cited lines or by running Python over the committed files in `frontend/public/data/sweden/`. The command is given. |
| [CI] | GitHub Actions run `39441114070`, "Build, store and publish the warehouse", sha `37167df9`, success, 2026-10-20. |

No local `warehouse/portfolio.duckdb` exists. The audits recomputed the gold marts in memory from
raw or feature files with the repository SQL [AC, B, DE].

Five status levels are kept apart throughout:

1. implemented: the code exists
2. ran: the pipeline has run successfully, locally or in CI
3. data available: the inputs exist and their coverage is known
4. analysis verified: the published numbers reproduce and their interpretation holds
5. published: the result is live on the site

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › A. Politics of Measurement
items.text:
**Question.** What does Sweden measure, and what does it overlook?

**Intended reader insight.** Where a domain appears measured depends on which agency holds the
statistics and how the catalogue is classified.

**Verified data.** SCB Statistikdatabasen API v2 lists 4,286 tables, 4,270 public. Kolada has 5,860
distinct KPIs. Published items are 10,130 = 4,270 + 5,860 [AC `a_repro.py`, `a_repro3.py`; CI log
"SWEDEN measurement: 10130 items, 1880 coverage cells"]. `coverage.json` has 1,880 cells summing to
64,009, years 1900–2026, with zero differences on recomputation [AC `a_cov.py`]. Metadata was
fetched only for the 1,299 tables with a variable containing "region" [AC; CI log].

**KPIs and findings.** Counts per domain (`export_measurement.py:55-66`). "Current" means
`last_year >= current_year - 2` for SCB (`mart_sweden_measurement_items.sql:50`) and a non-null
`publ_period` for Kolada, two definitions under one label [AC]. Findings in `Measurement.tsx:159-245`:

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › A. Politics of Measurement
items.text:
- "Health looks unmeasured in SCB's catalogue … one of the most measured in Kolada": SCB 7, Kolada
  932. Correct and well framed [AC `a_repro2.py`].
- "SCB publishes 983 tables on employment and 6 on culture": correct for SCB [AC].
- "No published table or key figure falls under Spirituality": true of the seeds only. No seed row
  maps to `spirituality`, so the zero holds by construction. 18 item titles match
  `trossamfund|religi|kyrk|andlig` [AC `a_kw.py`].
- `frontend/src/sweden/products.ts:35` says "Culture and civic life are the thinnest measured
  domains". By SCB plus Kolada, culture (120) is fifth thinnest after spirituality 0,
  social_relationships 54, wellbeing 78 and leisure 103. It is thinnest only in SCB (6) [AC].
- `products.ts:68` says "Employment is the most densely measured domain in official statistics".
  That holds for SCB (983). With Kolada added, other 2,356, economy 2,121 and education 1,882 come
  first [AC].

**Missing analyses.** A count of measures per table; a multi-label or keyword check of the domain
mapping; a frequency × geography × currency grid per domain.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › A. Politics of Measurement
items.text:
**Scientific weaknesses.** One SCB table is not one indicator, so SCB and Kolada counts are in
different units. Single-label mapping by subject code. Projections ending in 2120 count as current
(141 tables end after 2026). The geography heuristic misses at least 21 tables whose geographic
variable is named `kommun` or `län`. Kolada `institution` strings are not normalised, so "345
institutions" is not meaningful [AC].

**Gap interpretation.** A measurement absent from SCB's database and Kolada may exist at
Socialstyrelsen, Folkhälsomyndigheten, Brå, Kulturanalys or KB. The page must say "absent from these
catalogues", never "unmeasured". Counts show availability, not importance.

**Improvements.** Fix the two `products.ts` claims and note that spirituality has no mapping. Split
`is_current` into ongoing and projection. Detect geography from `kommun`/`län` names and json-stat
roles. Count measures from the metadata already on disk. Then add Socialstyrelsen and
Folkhälsomyndigheten catalogue metadata.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › B. The Ideal Human
items.text:
**Question.** What kind of person does the Swedish labour market expect workers to be, and how does
what workers should know and do compare with what they should be?

**Intended reader insight.** Job-ad language about personal traits changed in a measurable way, and
the change has limits as evidence about work.

**Verified data.** 23 archives, 11,291,650 ads, 8,736,050 distinct texts, 2,865,052,019 words, years
2006–2026 with 2026 covering Q1–Q3 only [B `q1.py`; own: summing `ads` and `distinct_texts` in
`frontend/public/data/sweden/language/coverage.json` gives 23, 11,291,650 and 8,736,050]. County is
null in every archive 2006–2019. Occupation is missing for 99.99 % of 2006 texts and 86.4 % of 2007
[B `q1.py`]. Ads are CC0 per the source README [B].

**KPIs and findings.** Unit: distinct text per archive (sha1 of normalised headline and
description, `ad_language.py:125-129`). Main measure: matches per 1,000 words with the occupation mix
fixed (`Language.tsx:96-97`). The CONTINUITY changes 2010→2025 reproduce: passion +71.3 %,
creativity +21.3 %, competence −18.7 %, stress −33.9 % [B `q1.py`]. Published `trends.json` equals
the recomputed mart with maximum absolute difference 0 [B].

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › B. The Ideal Human
items.text:
The page computes changes from `from` = 2008 to `last` = 2026, a partial year
(`Language.tsx:153-160`), while the reading text says "between ${first} and ${last}", which is
2006–2026 (`Language.tsx:599-600`). The Han/Fisher verdict needs a mean personal change above +10 %
and gets +10.1 %. Without passion the other seven personal categories average about −2 % [B].

**Missing analyses.** Lexicon precision and recall; co-occurrence per text; SSYK-4 trends;
employer and staffing-agency controls; uncertainty on breaks.

**Scientific weaknesses.**

- The 2020 standardised values are an artefact. In 2020 old field labels hold 4–12 texts but keep
  full pooled weight (Pedagogik about 11 %). Creativity 2020 is published at 2.024 against 1.559
  harmonised [B `q3.py`, `q4.py`]. Cause: no label crosswalk and no minimum cell size in
  `mart_sweden_job_language_trends.sql:18-33`.
- In a 2025 shard of 18,653 texts, 75 % of passion matches are `engag*`, often employer
  self-description. 55 % of identity matches are "personliga egenskaper" or "personlig lämplighet"
  [B `q5.py`].
- Ads tripled in length, so per-word rates fall for terms used once per ad.
- Dedup is per archive only (`ad_language.py:114`, `:127-129`).

**Gap interpretation.** Ads show how employers write, not working conditions, hiring or lived
experience. A rising term family can be a template or applicant-tracking-system effect.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › B. The Ideal Human
items.text:
**Improvements.** Crosswalk the eight non-taxonomy labels and require a minimum of texts per
field-year. Use complete years as endpoints and show baseline sensitivity. Fix the `first`/`from`
copy. Split `engag*` from passion and the recruitment formulas from identity. Draw a manual
validation sample.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › C. The Invisible Sweden
items.text:
**Question.** How does the statistical definition of similarity change our understanding of
Sweden?

**Intended reader insight.** Municipal similarity is a construction, and the map changes with the
features and the distance chosen.

**Verified data.** 290 municipalities, 280 analysed. Seven lack social assistance and three lack
turnout [AC `c_check.py`]. The run `public-consensus-2026-10-13` sits in the local warehouse only.
In CI the export prints "is not here; committed files kept" (`export_similarity.py:114`; CI log line
4953).

**KPIs and findings.** 208 of 280 municipalities have their nearest social neighbour in another
county; median distance 180 km [AC; own: `summary` in `similarity/municipalities.json`].

The verdict for "Centre and periphery" is `challenges` whenever the share exceeds 0.5
(`Similarity.tsx:500-503`). 0.5 is the wrong reference. With 21 counties of unequal size, a random
partner lies in another county 92.7 % of the time. Observed: 74.3 %. Own check: Python over
`similarity/municipalities.json`, expected share = Σ k(n−k) / n(n−1) over county sizes k,
n = 280; observed = first neighbour's county differs. Same-county pairs occur at 25.7 %, about
3.5 times the 7.3 % chance level. The random-pair median distance is 302 km against 180 km for social
neighbours [AC]. The data therefore show social similarity clustered in space, the opposite of the
verdict.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › C. The Invisible Sweden
items.text:
Clustering: k=2 silhouette 0.352, bootstrap ARI 0.751; k=4 silhouette 0.274, AMI against SKR 0.319;
shuffled 95th percentile about 0.20 [AC, as recorded; the model was not re-run].

**Missing analyses.** Geographic null and permutation test; sensitivity to feature set and distance;
temporal stability over 2020–2024; comparison with outcomes not used in clustering.

**Scientific weaknesses.** Turnout labelled 2024 is the 2022 election value carried forward by
Kolada: panel median 88.0 for 2018–2021 and 86.0 for 2022–2025 [AC `c_check.py`]. The method copy
says "Standardise the 12 indicators for 2024" (`Similarity.tsx:390`). Employment has no 2018, 2019
or 2025 values. Neighbours use 12-D z-space while clusters use 4 PCs. k=2 ARI barely clears 0.75.
Listwise deletion leaves a hole in the far north [AC].

The source line "Kolada and SCB, ${data.year}" (`Similarity.tsx:194`) credits Kolada for derived
data. Kolada's terms say "Gör du egna bearbetningar på vår data, får inte Kolada anges som källa"
[AC, official page].

**Gap interpretation.** Clusters are constructed. SKR comparison is partly circular because
population and commuting are inputs to both. Crow-flies distance is not travel.

**Improvements.** Add the nulls and rewrite the verdict. Disclose each feature's reference year.
Reword the source line as own processing of Kolada and SCB data. Make C build in CI with a contract
test. Then run sensitivity and stability checks on the panel already on disk.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › D. Infrastructure of Belonging
items.text:
**Question.** Can access to community and public participation be measured, starting with
libraries?

**Intended reader insight.** Availability, use and belonging are different things, and library
statistics measure only the first two.

**Verified data.** KB bibstat terms `BemanService01`, `Besok01`, `Publ199`, `Aktiv99`, 2014–2025;
Biblioteksdatabasen 4,330 records, 1,223 public, 1,147 with coordinates [DE `d1.py`, `d2.py`].
Published `municipalities.json` has 3,446 municipality-years [DE `d3.py`; own: `len(rows)`]. No
term is complete for every municipality and year. Balanced 2014–2025 panels: service points 272
municipalities, visits 222 [DE].

**KPIs and findings.** Rates per 10,000, per inhabitant, per 1,000 and per 100
(`export_belonging.py:116-118`); km² per staffed service point. The paired decline 2014→2025 is
1,171 → 1,033 service points (−12 %, n = 285) and 62.67 M → 46.79 M visits (−25 %, n = 271)
[DE `d4.py`]. CONTINUITY's "1,171 to 1,054" and "63.6 to 48.7 million" are unpaired national sums.
Both are correct measures of different things; the page shows the paired one. Spearman ρ between
service points per 10,000 and visits per inhabitant, 2025: 0.144, n = 282 [DE].

**Missing analyses.** Opening hours, including staffless hours; a pre-COVID 2019 baseline;
intervals on medians and ρ; population-weighted distance.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › D. Infrastructure of Belonging
items.text:
**Scientific weaknesses.** 12 municipality-years have 0 visits with at least one staffed service
point, and one row (1498/2022) has 0 service points with 64,110 visits [DE; own: Python over
`belonging/municipalities.json` `rows` lists the same 12 and 1]. They are published as real zeros.
`export_belonging.py:110` adds each organisation's value to a cell that starts at 0, so a missing
organisation gives an undercount. The docstring promises "the share of years reported"
(`export_belonging.py:13-14`), which the output lacks. The Putnam/Habermas reading says "supports"
whenever service points fell [DE].

**Gap interpretation.** Visits include commuters and visitors; borrowers include institutions;
nothing here measures loneliness or belonging. Fewer service points may mean merged branches or
staffless opening.

**Improvements.** Treat the 13 impossible zeros as missing. Null or flag municipality-years with a
non-reporting organisation. Use paired or balanced sets for every change. Remove the "supports"
verdict. Add opening-hour terms from bibstat.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › E. The Lost Futures
items.text:
**Question.** Are we imagining different futures, or projecting the present forward?

**Intended reader insight.** Which themes accompany future talk in the Riksdag, and in student
theses, and how that changed. The page must not assume a decline.

**Verified data.** 32 Riksdag sessions, 199394–202526, 415,595 speeches [DE `e1.py`; own: summing
`speeches` in `futures/coverage.json` gives 32 sessions and 415,595]. DiVA: 322 months, 431,898
Swedish-language records with an abstract, years with at least 1,000 records published (2001–2026)
[DE].

**KPIs and findings.** Future share: speeches where the marker matches / all speeches. Theme share:
future speeches with a theme anywhere / future speeches. Recomputed marts match `trends.json` within
4.99e-5 [DE]. Five-year means 1994–1998 against 2022–2026: future share 17.9 % → 20.6 %;
alternatives 2.9 % → 0.6 %; security 27.5 % → 39.1 %, or 35.8 % for the tail without 2026 [DE].

**Missing analyses.** Length-normalised marker; validation sample with precision and recall;
uncertainty for five-year means and breaks; party harmonisation.

**Scientific weaknesses.**

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › E. The Lost Futures
items.text:
- Session 1999/2000 is never counted. The regex `anforande-(\d{6})\.json\.zip`
  (`platform/ingest/riksdagen/futures_language.py:47`) does not match `anforande-19992000.json.zip`,
  which Riksdagen lists (HEAD 200, 20,939,449 bytes) [DE]. Own check: `futures/coverage.json` jumps
  from session `199899` to `200001`. 1999 is published with the spring sitting only (8,542
  speeches). 2000 has 4,844 speeches and is dropped by the half-median rule
  (`export_futures.py:35-60`).
- 2026 is a running year and is kept, because 10,279 speeches pass the threshold of about 6,350
  [DE].
- Future share tracks mean words per speech: Spearman ρ = 0.84, p = 1.3e-9, 1994–2026 without 2000;
  ρ = 0.86 for DiVA [DE].
- The horizon pattern `(år|till|fram till|inför) 20[2-9]0` is time-asymmetric [DE].
- DiVA joins Swedish and English descriptions (`harvest.py:61`), and weekly increments will count
  changed records twice [DE].
- Copy says DiVA is "not yet counted" (`Futures.tsx:7`, `Futures.tsx:485`,
  `export_futures.py:15`, `export_connections.py:131`), but the page shows the DiVA series.

**Gap interpretation.** Word frequency does not measure imagination or opinion. Riksdagen and DiVA
are separate corpora with their own denominators. Speeches are debate; the designed futures sit in
SOU and propositions, which are not ingested.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › E. The Lost Futures
items.text:
**Improvements.** Fix the regex and recount one 21 MB archive. Exclude or mark 2026. Store the
marker count to get a per-word rate. Validate the lexicon. Harmonise KDS with KD. Keep only the
Swedish DiVA abstract and store record IDs. Fix the stale copy.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › Connections
items.text:
Connections is the analytical layer across A–E. `export_connections.py` computes three D×C
relationships and records two rejections [own: keys of `connections/connections.json`].

| Pair | Kind | Time | Geography | Method | Assessment |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| A×D | Descriptive comparison of measurement coverage | A: catalogue years 1900–2026; D: 2014–2025 | A has no municipal join; D is municipal | Catalogue items against municipal statistics | Compatible only as prose: A counts 6 SCB culture tables, while D's library statistics come from KB, outside SCB's database. This is the "measured elsewhere" case. No correlation is possible. |

| A×C | Conceptual and methodological link | A lists tables; C uses 2024 | A shows 586 SCB tables at municipal resolution and 75 at subarea | A is a pool of candidate features for C | Compatible as a source list for alternative feature sets. No statistic. |

| C×D | Statistical relationship, exploratory | Both 2024; turnout is 2022 but is not in these pairs | Municipality code, 280–282 municipalities | Spearman ρ with bootstrap CI and partial ρ on log population | Compatible in time and geography. Visits vs post-secondary education ρ −0.004, CI [−0.125, 0.118], partial 0.192, n = 281 [DE, from `connections.json`]. The 12 zero-visit rows enter n, so the D repair comes first. Descriptive only, several tests, no significance claim. |

items.title: docs/sweden-research-alignment.md › Connections
items.text:
| B×E | Untested hypothesis | 19 shared years 2008–2026, 2026 partial in both | National only | Two lexicons, two genres, both length-confounded | Rejected correctly. The recorded reason "waits for the full job-ad backfill" is stale: all 23 archives are counted. A correlation of two trending national series would reflect shared trend and text length. Keep it as a side-by-side description. |

| A×E | Conceptual link, untested hypothesis | A 1900–2026 catalogue years; E 1994–2026 speeches | National | No crosswalk between A's 13 domains and E's nine themes | Not compatible in method. "Do the futures politicians talk about match what agencies measure?" needs a documented theme-to-domain mapping first. |

Combine datasets only after time, geography and method are shown to match. No Connections claim is
causal.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › SWEDEN research roadmap
items.text:
Phase 0, 2026-10-20. Proposed order of work, for approval. Nothing here is implemented. Evidence
for each item is in [sweden-research-alignment.md](sweden-research-alignment.md),
[sweden-data-inventory.md](sweden-data-inventory.md) and
[sweden-data-source-strategy.md](sweden-data-source-strategy.md).

Each item is marked **existing** (data already on disk or in R2) or **new ingestion** (a source
not fetched today). Sections 1 and 3 to 6 need existing data only, with three exceptions marked
in place. Verified outputs that are not named in a repair stay as they are.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › 1. Repairs
items.text:

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › 2. High-value sources
items.text:
All new ingestion. Order follows research value against cost.

1. KB bibstat opening hours `Open101–106`, `Open201–206` for D. Verified definitions, same API, near
   zero cost. Essential.
2. JobTech Taxonomy for B. Already cached; the crosswalk in 1.8 uses it. Essential.
3. Kolada additional KPIs for C and D (outcomes, library and participation KPIs). Terms verified.
   Essential for C.
4. SCB regional tables including DeSO/RegSO for C. CC0, verified. Essential.
5. Socialstyrelsen catalogue metadata for A. Endpoint verified, licence UNVERIFIED; read the licence
   page before ingesting.
6. Riksdagen SOU, then propositions, for E as a third corpus. Verified, about 1 GB streamed.
7. Arbetsmiljöundersökningen and Yrkesregistret AM0208 for B. Verified, small.
8. SCB population grid for D. Partly verified.
9. Folkhälsodata HLV for A and D. Licence UNVERIFIED; county level only.

Wait for a licence or endpoint check: dataportal.se, Valmyndigheten files, Segregationsbarometern,
Swerik, SwePub, JobTech enriched ads trait fields. Defer GTFS routing until the grid distance exists.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › 3. Methods
items.text:
All existing data.

- A: count measures per table from metadata; detect geography from `kommun`/`län` and json-stat
  roles; split `is_current` into ongoing and projection (`mart_sweden_measurement_items.sql:50`);
  normalise or drop Kolada `institution`.
- B: sub-lexicons (passion into `engag*` and passion/brinner; identity into recruitment formulas and
  career); co-occurrence per text; SSYK-4 standardisation; staffing-agency share on 2023+;
  cross-archive text dedup; segmented regression or bootstrap for breaks.
- C: sensitivity without log population and commuting, on PCA-4 space, with Mahalanobis distance;
  Jaccard overlap of neighbour sets; stability over 2020–2023; neighbours on 11 indicators for the
  10 excluded municipalities, flagged.
- D: balanced or paired sets for every change; 2019 next to 2014 as a pre-COVID baseline.
- E: relative horizon marker (year above speech year plus N); report `långsiktig` separately;
  harmonise KDS with KD and separate presiding officers and the King; bootstrap for five-year means
  and a permutation null for breaks.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › 5. Validation and reproducibility
items.text:
- B and E lexicons: stratified manual samples, about 50 matches per category and period for B and
  about 200 hits plus 200 non-hits for E, coded for what the match means. Publish precision and
  recall with intervals. Existing data; older B periods need a re-stream.
- C clustering: report the null and permutation results with the groups; re-run in CI (1.17).
- Tests to add: pytest for `catalogue_ingest.py` staging, `export_belonging.py` aggregation,
  `futures_language.py` and `futures_theses.py` `count()`; dbt tests `texts_matching <= texts`,
  field labels within taxonomy plus crosswalk, year range and not_null on E marts.
- Provenance: the site serves committed files with `run_id: null`. Record which release the
  committed copy matches.

items.title: docs/sweden-research-roadmap.md › 6. Gap presentation
items.text:
Findings come before KPI cards. On each page, say what the data cannot show, once and concretely:

- A: absent from SCB's database and Kolada, not unmeasured.
- B: ads describe how employers write; they do not measure hiring or conditions. Show
  Arbetsmiljöundersökningen beside the ads once ingested, as a descriptive comparison.
- C: groups are constructed; the map changes with the definition.
- D: library supply and self-reported belonging sit on different geographies and periods, so they
  are shown side by side, never correlated across municipalities.
- E: frequency is not imagination; Riksdag and DiVA are separate corpora.
